🌎✈️ Hispanic Heritage Month in ELL World History

Ms. Dunn’s students went on a “trip around the world” without leaving the classroom! They picked up passports 🛂, ID badges 🏷️, and tour bags 🎒 before visiting stations to explore different countries, practice English 🗣️✍️, answer questions, and get their passports stamped ✅.

text:
📊😄 Statistics meets tongue twisters!

On Tuesday, Oct. 7, our Stats students put their linear regression skills to the test in a hilarious hands-on activity! Students gathered bivariate data by timing how long it took different group sizes to say tricky tongue twisters — and ended the day with the entire class joining in together.

There were lots of laughs, smiles, and data points as they learned how to analyze relationships between variables in a fun, memorable way.

Try it yourself!
🗣️ “Picky people pick Peter Pan peanut butter — it’s the only peanut butter picky people pick!”

#CHSWampusCats #StatsInAction #LearningIsFun #TongueTwisterChallenge

author: Conway High School
text:
Recently, Ms. Sinsley’s Statistics students took learning around the world—literally! Using small globe beach balls, they estimated the proportion of Earth covered by water. 🌊

In groups of 4–7, students tossed the globes and recorded whether their fingers landed on water or land. Then the whole class joined in for even more trials! 🌍

Their estimates ranged from 54% to 70% water—pretty close to the true value of 71%. That’s hands-on learning at its best! 👏📈

#WampusCatScholars  #HandsOnLearning #WampusCatPride

text: ARKANSAS ASSET BUILDERS HOSTS FREE FAFSA HELP DAY TO GUIDE STUDENTS AND FAMILIES THROUGH FINANCIAL AID APPLICATIONArkansas Asset Builders, committed to empowering Arkansans to improve their financial well-being, is hosting a free FAFSA Help Day to assist students and their families in completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). The event will provide critical, expert guidance to ensure students access the maximum financial aid available for the 2026-2027 academic year.The FAFSA is the gateway to federal grants, loans, and work-study funds, as well as many state and institutional financial aid programs. Completing the application accurately and on time is essential for paying for college, but the process can often be confusing. This event provides professional, one-on-one assistance at absolutely no cost.FAFSA Help Day Event DetailsDate: Saturday, October 25, 2025Time: 1:00 pm – 4:00 pmLocation: Faulkner County Library (1900 Tyler Street, Conway, AR 72032)Assistance Provided: Financial aid professionals from local colleges and universities will be on-site to help students and parents navigate the FAFSA, determine contributor status, and accurately complete the application."The FAFSA is more critical than ever due to recent application changes, and filing early is key to securing available funds," said Joyia Yorgey, Executive Director of Arkansas Asset Builders. "We are dedicated to removing the financial and logistical barriers that prevent students from accessing financial resources for higher education. Our FAFSA Help Day ensures families have the expert support needed to complete this vital step toward achieving their educational and financial goals."To get the most out of the event, students and parents should attend together. However, help is still available if attending individually. Attendees should bring necessary documents for the FAFSA, including: student and parent social security numbers, studentaid.gov login credentials, and information about 2024 tax return(s), any untaxed income received in 2024, and current bank and investment account balances. Appointments are highly recommended to guarantee personalized assistance.Students and parents can sign up for an appointment and find more information about the event on the Arkansas Asset Builders website at https://arkansasassetbuilders.org/event/fafsa-help-day/ or by calling 501-503-2123.About Arkansas Asset BuildersArkansas Asset Builders desires that all residents of Arkansas have the opportunity to flourish by building their household’s financial security and stability. We believe that financial education and free tax preparation are key services that empower individuals and families to break cycles of debt and financial instability and take control of their financial future. Learn more at https://arkansasassetbuilders.org

author: Conway High School
text:
💙 Behind the Blue & White: Passion. Knowledge. Dedication.

📚 Department Spotlight: English Language Arts

If the ELA Department were a book genre, they’d be classic fiction — full of timeless themes, universal truths, and creative imagination.

✨ One word that defines them: Transformative.
Every day, CHS English teachers help students find their voice, challenge their thinking, and discover the power of words.

Through stories, essays, and conversations, they connect reading and writing to students’ lives and real-world issues — showing that literature isn’t just something you study, it’s something you live.

🖋️ What they hope every student takes away: confidence in the ability to analyze, interpret, and write with purpose.

💭 Department spirit character: Atticus Finch — thoughtful, patient, and grounded in moral integrity and the belief that education can change lives.

📖 Advice from the ELA team: Don’t be afraid to make mistakes. Every draft, every reread, every misstep brings you closer to understanding and growth.

💙 Behind the Blue & White, our ELA teachers embody passion, knowledge, and dedication — empowering every Wampus Cat to think deeply, express boldly, and grow confidently.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

text:
🎉 CHS Shines at the 57th Arkansas Student Congress on Human Relations State Tournament! 🎉

Our Conway High School Student Congress team brought their A-game to this year’s state tournament, showing off their debate skills, legislative know-how, and teamwork in a competition that’s been shaping young leaders since 1968.

🏆 2025 Arkansas Student Congress Awards:

Superior in Caucus: Ian, Katharine, Amelia, Addison, Landon

Excellence in Committee: Ian, Katharine

Superior in Committee: Milina, Amelia, Addison, Landon

Excellence in Floor Debate: Milina

Superior in Floor Debate: Ian, Katharine, Addison, Landon

Superior in Parliamentary Procedure: Ian, Katharine, Addison, Landon

✨ CHS Best Delegate: Ian Lee-Kim

💡 Individual Highlights:

Highest Scoring Delegate in House I: Ian Lee-Kim

Melinda Valdez-Milloway Award: Ian Lee-Kim

House I Best Bill (2nd Place): Ian Lee-Kim (Author) & Katharine Welky (Co-author)

House I Best Delegation (1st Place): Ian Lee-Kim & Katharine Welky

House I Bill Passed in Committee: Ian & Katharine

House II Bill Passed in Committee: Milina Michel (Author) & Amelia Garrett (Co-author)

House III Elected House Clerk (2nd Year!): Addison Choate

House III Best Overall Delegate: Landon Harvey

House III Best Delegation (1st Place): Addison & Landon

House III Bill Passed in Committee: Addison (Author) & Landon (Co-author)

🏅 Overall Delegation: 2nd Place – Conway High School

The Arkansas Student Congress, the state’s oldest model legislative event, gives students the chance to experience the democratic process first-hand—writing and debating legislation, running caucuses, serving in committees, and presenting their ideas on the House & Senate floor at the State Capitol.

A huge congratulations to all our delegates for representing CHS with skill, intelligence, and teamwork! Special thanks to Mrs. Casey Griffith for coaching our talented Speech & Debate team.

text:
Congratulations to CHS Senior, Callie Wesbecher, for being named a National Speech & Debate Association’s Academic All American! 

The Academic All American award recognizes high school students who have earned the degree of Superior Distinction within the NSDA Honor Society by competing in speech and debate events at tournaments; completed at least 5 semesters of high school; demonstrated outstanding character and leadership; and earned a GPA of 3.7 or higher. Fewer than 2% of National Speech & Debate Association student members earn the Academic All American award every year. This honor is an indicator of Ian’s academic achievement and competitive success. 

Callie is a 3 year member of the CHS Speech & Debate Team. Callie competes in Congressional Debate, along with Student Congress and Mock Trial (Philadelphia). Upon graduation, Callie will be attending Central Baptist College.

author: Conway High School
text:
Congratulations to CHS Senior Ian Lee-Kim for earning Premier Distinction within the National Speech & Debate Association's Honor Society. 

Premier Distinction is the highest degree in the NSDA Honor Society! This is an outstanding achievement. Fewer than 3% of NSDA members earn Premier Distinction prior to graduation! This milestone is a celebration of the hundreds of hours Ian has spent preparing, practicing, and competing to hone his communication and leadership skills. Along with earning Premier Distinction, Ian is also an NSDA Academic All-American. 

Ian is a 3-year member of the CHS Speech & Debate team and has competed across the state of Arkansas, along with Philadelphia, Iowa, Kentucky, and Virginia. Ian competes in Congressional Debate, Mock Trial, Student Congress and Original Oratory.

🧸💉 EMR Students Bring Smiles to the Teddy Bear Clinic!

Kylee Ritchey, Ronnia Evans, Mailee Cushing, Shelby Holder, Haley McCarron, and Magnolia Smyers recently took part in HIPPY Arkansas’s Teddy Bear Clinic — a fun, hands-on event that helps young children feel more comfortable with doctor and hospital visits.

Using stuffed animals as “patients,” children learned how to check vitals, give pretend shots, and apply bandages — all with help from our EMR students, who played the role of caring medical professionals.

Through this experience, students practiced real-world communication and empathy skills while supporting community health education. 💙

Way to go, EMR team, for making healthcare learning bear-y fun! 🩺🐻

text:
Our AP Biology students had a sweet time in lab on Friday—well… until the Gymnema tea kicked in! 😅🧪
As part of their Signal Transduction Pathways investigation, students sampled all the major flavors (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami) before drinking Gymnema tea, which temporarily blocks the sweet receptors on your tongue. Mind. Blown. 🤯🍬

They also discovered that thanks to our unique DNA, we don’t all taste things with the same intensity! 👅🧬
Check out this snapshot from Friday’s flavorful (and slightly confusing!) experiment!

#APBiology #ScienceIsCool #CHSScience

text:
Congratulations to CHS Senior, Landon Harvey, for being named a National Speech & Debate Association’s Academic All American! 

The Academic All American award recognizes high school students who have earned the degree of Superior Distinction within the NSDA Honor Society by competing in speech and debate events at tournaments; completed at least 5 semesters of high school; demonstrated outstanding character and leadership; and earned a GPA of 3.7 or higher. Fewer than 2% of National Speech & Debate Association student members earn the Academic All American award every year. This honor is an indicator of Landon’s academic achievement and competitive success. 

Landon is a 3 year member of the CHS Speech & Debate Team. Landon competes in Congressional Debate, along with being on the Student Congress team.  Upon graduation, Landon will be attending the University of Central Arkansas. Landon is coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith.

author: Conway High School
text:
Our Science Department at CHS is a powerhouse of expertise, experience, and global perspective! 🌍🔬
With 158 years of combined teaching experience and a wide array of degrees—ranging from Chemistry and Biology to Physical Science and even a Doctorate in Pharmacy—our teachers bring passion and knowledge to every classroom. The CHS Science Department offers 15 different science courses, including on-level, AP, accelerated, concurrent semester, and advanced semester courses, giving students countless opportunities to explore and excel. 🧪
Many of our science teachers have traveled the world—from Costa Rica and Italy to Canada and Puerto Rico—bringing diverse perspectives into their teaching. ✈️ Beyond the classroom, our educators shine with accomplishments like running nonprofits, creating CHS spring musical costumes, winning state fiddle championships, and launching programs at CHS like Science Helper. Their dedication has earned multiple Teacher of the Year awards and other honors, making the CHS Science Department a launching pad for future scientists and innovators. 🌿

text:
🌿 Exploring Biology in the Real World! 🌄
Our Fundamentals of Biology class took learning outdoors today with a field trip to Petit Jean State Park—and what a day it was!

Students studied ecosystems and biodiversity up close, snapping photos of mosses, ferns, lichens, and mushrooms along the trail. They also got to experience some of Petit Jean’s most fascinating features: the iconic sandstone “turtle” rocks, a cave filled with ancient pictographs and petroglyphs created by Native peoples 500–1500 years ago, and even tested out some impressive echoes across the Cedar Creek canyon!

Despite the 35° temps and a surprise dusting of sleet, this crew embraced the adventure and made the most of every moment. ❄️🌲

What an unforgettable way to connect classroom learning with Arkansas’s natural treasures!

🎄📚 The CHS Spanish Honorary Society spent the day at Ellen Smith Elementary sharing bilingual holiday stories!

Our elementary Spanish-speaking students felt seen and celebrated, and non-Spanish-speaking students got to experience the beauty of a new language. 💬✨

Our CHS bilingual readers shined as they practiced their Spanish and connected with younger students who share their language and culture. ❤️

author: Conway High School
text:
✨ Our Spanish 4 and AP Spanish students visited the University of Central Arkansas for a campus tour completely in Spanish! 🇪🇸🎓
Our guides were bilingual UCA students who shared information about campus life, programs, and traditions. Students practiced real-world Spanish and explored UCA as a future college option. 🌟
It was raining 🌧️, but that didn’t stop us—we toured the campus under umbrellas ☂️ and made the most of our day!
We had an amazing time, learned so much, and loved seeing our students use their language skills outside the classroom! 💜📚

author: Conway High School
text:
Our Organic Chemistry students had an exciting day at UCA! 🔬✨
They completed a steam distillation of cinnamon to isolate cinnamaldehyde, the compound that gives cinnamon its warm, familiar aroma. Afterward, Dr. Singleton helped analyze their results using IR and NMR spectroscopy to see if they successfully produced the real thing. 👩‍🔬📊

In the afternoon, ACS brought the fun with hands-on science demos, including carbon-dioxide bubble making that filled the room with smiles and suds. 🫧😄

Science days are the best days! 🌟🧪

#FutureScientists #ChemistryInAction #WampusCatsInSTEM

author: Conway High School
text:
The Conway High School Speech & Debate Team traveled to New Orleans, LA, to compete at the 47th annual Isidore Newman Speech & Debate Tournament. Competing were: Newton Nganga (novice Lincoln-Douglas debate), Ian Lee-Kim (Original Oratory), Wren Welky (Original Oratory), Kamryn Young (Informative Speaking), and Joshua Mendoza (Informative Speaking). They all did a wonderful job writing and presenting their pieces, competing against students from across the United States. 

Newton Nganga finished in 3rd place in novice Lincoln-Douglas debate. His next competition will be in January at the Saints Classic in Ridgeland, MS, where he will once again compete in Lincoln-Douglas debate. 

Wren Welky finished in 2nd place for her Original Oratory persuasive speech. She also earned her first bid to compete at the University of Kentucky Tournament of Champions in April. Her next tournament will be at the Saints Classic in Ridgeland, MS, where she will compete in Congressional Debate. 

All students are members of the CHS Speech & Debate team and are coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith.

Before students headed off for Christmas break, the Conway High School National Honor Society partnered with Mrs. Lindsay Spicer’s kindergarten class at Carolyn Lewis Elementary to spread some holiday cheer 📚🎄

Mrs. Spicer hoped each of her students could head into the break with a cozy Book Buddy stuffie to cuddle up with and a Christmas book to enjoy, and NHS was excited to help make that wish a reality. Knowing the lasting impact reading can have, NHS members were proud to support this meaningful project and help foster a love of reading in our youngest learners.

Pictured with Mrs. Spicer and her kindergarten students are NHS seniors and Executive Board members Addison Choate, President; Katharine Welky, Projects Chair; and Ian Lee-Kim, Parliamentarian.

🎉 Conway High School Named to College Board AP School Honor Roll 🎉

Conway High School has earned a spot on the College Board’s AP School Honor Roll for the 2024–2025 school year, receiving Silver-level recognition!

The AP School Honor Roll recognizes schools that are expanding access to Advanced Placement courses while supporting strong student performance and college readiness.

At Conway High School, students have access to 27 AP courses, taught by 26 AP-trained teachers. Last year alone, CHS seniors took a total of 555 AP exams, with 58% earning scores of 3 or higher, qualifying for potential college credit.

This Silver distinction reflects CHS’s continued commitment to academic excellence, opportunity, and preparing students for success beyond high school. 🐾📚

#ConwayHighSchool #APHonorRoll #AcademicExcellence #CollegeReady #WampusCatPride

Ms. Brown’s 8th period juniors took Walt Whitman’s words literally:

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Dear Conway High School Parents & Families,

We want to share information regarding conversations that may be circulating about the possibility of students choosing to leave class during the school day.

Our role as a school district is not to promote or suppress student viewpoints. Our responsibility is to ensure student safety and to maintain an orderly learning environment for all students.

When a student leaves class during the school day, it creates safety concerns and disrupts the learning environment for other students. For that reason, if a student chooses to leave class, the situation will be addressed as a behavioral and attendance matter in accordance with our student code of conduct. 

School will operate as normal. Instruction will continue throughout the day, and administrators will supervise students appropriately to ensure safety. This is not a school or district initiated activity. We encourage families to talk with their students about school expectations, safety considerations, and how choices made during the school day can impact learning for all students. 

This information has also been emailed to all Conway High School Parents and students. 

Thank you for your partnership as we continue to focus on student safety, learning, and maintaining a respectful school environment.

Conway Public Schools

text: New procedures will apply for LR Central game on Friday!Student AdmissionLRSD high school students attending their home school’s game must present both an LRSD Student ID and a ticket for entry.Students from other K–12 schools (inside or outside LRSD, including elementary, middle, and high school) must be accompanied by an adult (21 years or older with valid ID).No refunds will be issued for minors attempting to enter without an adult.Game Entry GuidelinesNo entry will be permitted after halftime.No refunds will be issued for late arrivals.Ticket sales will close at 4:00 PM on game day. This allows security and police staffing to be properly adjusted for crowd size and safety.Clear Bag PolicyAll attendees must follow the LRSD clear bag policy. This policy is designed to increase safety and speed up the entry process.One clear plastic, vinyl, or PVC bag not exceeding 12" x 6" x 12".One clear, one-gallon plastic freezer bag (Ziploc-style).One small clutch (no larger than 4.5" x 6.5") for personal items.Medically necessary items will be permitted after proper inspection.Phones, cameras, and binoculars may be carried outside of a bag or case.Purpose of These ProceduresThese measures are designed to ensure a safe, family-friendly, and supportive environment for all LRSD games. Increased adult supervision, controlled entry, and clear safety policies will allow students, families, and fans to enjoy the game in a respectful atmosphere.

🎉🐎 2nd Annual Lunar New Year Celebration at the Faulkner County Library 🎉🐎
On Saturday, February 7th, the CJHS & CHS Asian Club, in partnership with the Faulkner County Library, local Chinese community members, and the UCA Center for Asian Languages and Cultures, proudly hosted Conway’s 2nd Lunar New Year Celebration.
With approximately 200 attendees, the event was filled with energy, learning, and fun! Families enjoyed interactive stations featuring dumpling-making, Chinese calligraphy, crafts, chopsticks games, and more. It was a wonderful opportunity for our community to come together and celebrate the Year of the Fire Horse.

A heartfelt thank-you to the Faulkner County Library for providing the space and incredible support that helped make this event possible. We are also grateful for our amazing team of 20 student volunteers from Conway High School and Conway Junior High School, along with 14 local Chinese community members, whose enthusiasm and dedication made the celebration such a success.

Special thanks to our generous supporters:
 🥟 Sakura Ocean A.Y.C.E. Sushi & Hibachi (coming soon) for the $200 donation supporting the dumpling station
 🧋 Boba Love for donating nearly 200 cups of boba tea
 🍩 Shimmery Donut for donating 50 dozen donut holes

Events like this truly highlight the cultural vibrancy of our community and the growing excitement for Chinese culture and language. Interested in learning more? Join our Chinese program or the Asian Club! 🌏❤️

#LunarNewYear #ConwayAsianClub #ChineseCulture #CommunityCelebration #YearOfTheHorse #ConwayHigh

text:
Congratulations to CHS Senior, Naomi Brooks for being named a National Speech & Debate Association’s Academic All American! 

The Academic All American award recognizes high school students who have earned the degree of Superior Distinction within the NSDA Honor Society by competing in speech and debate events at tournaments; completed at least 5 semesters of high school; demonstrated outstanding character and leadership; and earned a GPA of 3.7 or higher. Fewer than 2% of National Speech & Debate Association student members earn the Academic All American award every year. 

This honor is an indicator of Naomi’s academic achievement and competitive success. 

Naomi is a 3 year member of the CHS Speech & Debate Team. Naomi competes in Program of Oral Interpretation, Poetry & Prose Interpretation, Original Oratory, and Mock Trial.

author: Conway High School
text:
Congratulations to CHS SeniorAddison Choate for earning Premier Distinction within the National Speech & Debate Association's Honor Society. 

Premier Distinction is the highest degree in the NSDA Honor Society! This is an outstanding achievement. Fewer than 3% of NSDA members earn Premier Distinction prior to graduation! This milestone is a celebration of the hundreds of hours Addison has spent preparing, practicing, and competing to hone her communication and leadership skills. Along with earning Premier Distinction, Addison is also an NSDA Academic All-American. 

Addison is a 3-year member of the CHS Speech & Debate team and has competed across the state of Arkansas, along with Philadelphia, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana and Mississippi. Addison competes in Lincoln-Douglas debate, Informative Speaking, Student Congress and is a 3-year member of our Mock Trial team.

author: Conway High School
text:
Congratulations to the Conway High School Mock Trial team for winning the 2026 Arkansas High School Mock Trial State Tournament!!! The tournament, sponsored by the Arkansas Bar Association, was held February 27-28, 2026, in Little Rock at the Richard Sheppard Arnold United States Courthouse. Mock trial is an academic and competitive simulation of a trial-level court proceeding, where students act as attorneys and witnesses to argue a fictional criminal or civil case. Teams analyze a provided case packet, develop legal theories, and follow simplified rules of evidence to compete in courtrooms.Twenty-one teams from across Arkansas gathered to try the civil case of Justice Miller v. Jace Talent Agency. 

The team competed in four preliminary rounds against Parkview, Bentonville West, Des Arc, and then the final round against Little Rock Central High School. Conway was the only team to go undefeated, with no dropped ballots. The team also earned Star Attorney & Star Witness awards. Out of over 100 attorneys, the tournament awards the top 7 attorneys in the 4 prelim rounds. Katharine Welky and Addison Choate were named Star Attorneys. This is the 2nd year for Addison Choate to be named a Star Attorney. The tournament awards the top 5 witnesses, and Annabel Champlin and Naomi Brooks brought home 2 of the Star Witness Awards. 

The CHS team will be the team to represent Arkansas at the National High School Mock Trial Championships in May. They will travel to Des Moines, IA, to compete against the top team from each state, along with South Korea, Guam, and Northern Mariana Islands. 

All members of the CHS Mock Trial Team are members of the CHS Speech & Debate Team and are coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith. The team is also coached by volunteer attorney coach, Mr. Matt Brown.

The Conway High School Beta Club has been named a 2025–2026 recipient of the John W. Harris Leadership Award — one of the highest recognitions in National Beta.

Named after Beta’s founder, John W. Harris, this award celebrates clubs that truly live out Beta’s four pillars: achievement, character, leadership, and service. Out of clubs across the nation, only five Senior Beta clubs were selected for this prestigious honor — and Conway High School is one of them!

Our club was nominated through a competitive application process and selected by the Alumni Review Committee for the impact our students are making both in school and throughout the community.

As part of the award, our Beta Club will be able to send 10 members to a Regional Leadership Summit, where they will collaborate with students from across the country and continue growing their leadership skills.

We are incredibly proud of these students and their commitment to serving others and leading by example. 💙

author: Conway High School
text:
Ms. Dunn’s class wrapped up Black History Month with an inspiring project that combined research, creativity, and real-world problem solving! 🖤

Students first researched influential African Americans and explored the 5 W’s of their impact. They also learned about African American inventors whose ideas still shape the world today.

Inspired by these innovators, students then created their own solutions to real-world problems. Ideas included an AI hairbrush to recommend hair care products, translation glasses to help people communicate across languages, and a hotel-style housing program that would provide shelter, job training, and counseling for people experiencing homelessness.

Students also tackled issues like climate change, world hunger, water quality, school safety, traffic solutions, and even disease detection.

We’re proud of the creativity, innovation, and thoughtful problem-solving from Ms. Dunn’s class! 💡

#WampusCats #BlackHistoryMonth #StudentInnovation

From managing emergency calls to directing resources, these professionals are the calm voices and quick thinkers that help keep our community safe. Our students left with a deeper understanding of how teamwork, communication, and quick decision-making keep the EMS system running smoothly and efficiently. 👩‍⚕️🚨

Thank you to the MEMS team for welcoming our students and giving them such a valuable real-world learning experience! 🙌

#WampusCats #CTE #FutureFirstResponders 🐾

author: Conway High School
text:
🌎🍽️ Spanish IV students explored culture, cuisine, and connection!

Sabores de la Cultura | Flavors of Culture: Students learned vocabulary around food and discovered how dishes like Rosca de Reyes and panettone play an important role in cultural celebrations.

Recetas Auténticas | Authentic Recipes: From researching traditional Hispanic recipes to measuring ingredients and cooking, students prepared arepas, baked bread, and horchata, practicing language skills while experiencing authentic cultural traditions.

Conectando Culturas | Connecting Cultures: The unit culminated in a Zoom exchange with students from Montemayor School in Zipaquira, Colombia, where our students practiced Spanish and their peers practiced English, sharing perspectives on nutrition, celebrations, and the role of food in daily life.

A meaningful journey connecting language, culture, and real-world experiences! 🌟

#CHSWampusCats #CHSLanguageLearners #SaboresDeLaCultura #SpanishIV #CHSCultureConnection

author: Conway High School
text:
🎉 Huge Congratulations to Mrs. Chen’s Chinese III Students! 🎉

We are thrilled to celebrate the outstanding achievements of all 13 Chinese III students who passed the HSK Chinese Proficiency Test with exceptional results! The HSK (Hànyǔ Shuǐpíng Kǎoshì) is an internationally recognized standardized test of Chinese language proficiency, and this entire group demonstrated remarkable dedication, earning a 100% passing rate.

✨ Special Highlights:
 • Four students scored an impressive 90% or above.
 • A huge shout-out to Madison Johnson, our amazing junior, who achieved a perfect 100% score! As a non-heritage speaker, this accomplishment is truly extraordinary. 🌟

These students are now on track to apply for the Arkansas Seal of Biliteracy this spring, reflecting their hard work, perseverance, and growing global competence.

To celebrate this milestone, Mrs. Chen hosted a joyful celebration featuring boba tea, donuts, and Pocky. Special thanks to Boba Love and Shimmery Donuts for generously donating delicious treats. 🧋🍩

We are incredibly proud of our students and our Chinese program. Hard work and perseverance truly pay off! 👏🎊

#HSK #ARSealOfBiliteracy #ChineseLanguage #StudentAchievement #ConwaySchools 🎉

🌍 Expanding Horizons: Meet Our World Languages Department!

With nearly 90 years of combined teaching experience, our Foreign Language Department opens doors to the world every single day.

From Spanish, French, and Mandarin to Russian and regional Chinese dialects, this team brings true global perspective to the classroom. Several teachers have international roots — including Colombia and China — and many have lived, studied, or worked abroad. From careers in international logistics to building Chinese language programs and organizing Lunar New Year celebrations in Faulkner County, their real-world experiences enrich every lesson.

They hold multiple bachelor’s and master’s degrees, advanced certifications, international diplomas, and even National Board Certification. 🏅

When asked to describe learning a new language, they chose words like:
Rewarding. Humbling. Revelatory. A superpower.

Because language isn’t just vocabulary and grammar — it’s connection, culture, opportunity, and understanding.

text:
Congratulations to CHS Junior, Joshua Mendoza for being named a National Speech & Debate Association’s Academic All American! 

The Academic All American award recognizes high school students who have earned the degree of Superior Distinction within the NSDA Honor Society by competing in speech and debate events at tournaments; completed at least 5 semesters of high school; demonstrated outstanding character and leadership; and earned a GPA of 3.7 or higher. Fewer than 2% of National Speech & Debate Association student members earn the Academic All American award every year. This honor is an indicator of Joshua’s academic achievement and competitive success. 

Joshua is a 3-year member of the CHS Speech & Debate team and has competed across the state of Arkansas, along with tournaments in Virginia, and Mississippi. Joshua competes in Big Question Debate, Informative Speaking, and Congressional Debate.

Conway High School’s Key Club members just returned from their District Leadership Conference, where they competed against clubs from across Missouri and Arkansas—and brought home some big honors! 🎉

The club earned 1st place for their 100-page scrapbook highlighting the incredible work they’ve done this year, as well as 2nd place in Major Emphasis, which recognizes a club’s year-long service focus. This year’s emphasis was supporting Conway’s youth.

Over the past year, CHS Key Club members completed 16 service projects and contributed 948 hours of service to Conway athletic programs, middle schools, elementary schools, Kiwanis, and Community Connections.

Two members also served on the district executive board this year: Heidy Hernandez Lagos as Secretary and Nicole Reynolds as District 9 Lieutenant Governor. These students helped organize a three-day conference for more than 250 students from across two states!

If you see a Key Club member today, be sure to congratulate them for their dedication to service and leadership! 💙 #WampusCatPride

Ms. Bowden’s AP Biology students took learning beyond the classroom with an unforgettable, hands-on field trip experience! 🧬🔬

The group visited the National Center for Toxicological Research and the FDA Arkansas Human and Animal Food Laboratory, where students saw firsthand how cutting-edge biology, chemistry, and physics are used in biomedical research and to protect the safety of food for both people and pets. They even stepped into the role of scientists—participating in sensory testing of seafood and learning how experts detect insect and rodent contamination in consumer products!

After lunch, the learning continued at the Witt Stephens Jr. Central Arkansas Nature Center in Little Rock. Students explored Arkansas’s wetlands, observed live and preserved animals, and gained a deeper appreciation for conservation efforts across the state.

Experiences like this bring science to life and show our students the real-world impact of what they’re learning every day! 🌎✨

#APBiology #CHSWampusCats #STEMEducation #HandsOnLearning #ScienceInAction

author: Jamie Bratton
text: The Wampus Cat yearbook program has earned the Jostens 2026 National Yearbook Program of Excellence award at the Silver Level. This year marks the 80th edition of the school's yearbook and the 10th consecutive year that the program has received this national honor. Under the direction of adviser Jamie Bratton and editors Anna Liles, Sylvia King, and Lauren Simpson, the staff is nationally recognized as a program that creates an inclusive book which reflects the entire student body. The program stands out as one of the best in the country because of its efficient management and excellent communication during the production process. By meeting high standards for school engagement and organization, the staff repeatedly proves they can successfully handle the challenges of professional journalism and design. This award highlights the team's dedication to telling the school’s story through a high-quality, well-managed publication.

author: Conway High School
text:
🔬🎓 Exploring the Future of Science & Healthcare! 🎓🔬

Ms. Bowden’s UACCM Concurrent Microbiology students recently had an incredible opportunity to visit University of Central Arkansas for a hands-on, behind-the-scenes look at college-level science and healthcare programs.

During their visit, students met with Dr. Kari Naylor, microbiologist, who led a tour of the life sciences labs and student spaces while sharing insights into college life and how to get involved in undergraduate research. Students also participated in a two-hour lab experience where they practiced key microbiology skills—identifying bacterial cell morphology and endospores using staining techniques and microscopy with samples they had previously collected.

The day continued with a visit to the nursing simulation lab, where Dr. Susan Gatto introduced students to "high-fidelity manikins" and discussed pathways into the nursing program and career opportunities in the field. Students also connected with Dr. Chris Ryan from Occupational Therapy, along with guest speakers from Physical Therapy and Speech Pathology, who shared valuable information about their programs, acceptance criteria, and career paths.

This immersive experience gave students a meaningful glimpse into future possibilities in science, healthcare, and beyond. Thank you to everyone at UCA who made this day so impactful!

#CHS #WampusCats #FutureReady #STEM #HealthcareCareers

Congratulations to CHS Seniors Ian Lee-Kim and Addison Choate for qualifying to represent Arkansas at the National Speech & Debate’s NATIONAL TOURNAMENT this June in Richmond, Virginia. 

Ian will compete in Congressional Debate- House. Only 6 students were selected to represent Arkansas in Congressional Debate- House.  Ian is a 2-year NSDA National Tournament Qualifier. Ian was selected to represent Arkansas in Original Oratory at the 2025 tournament.  

Addison will compete in Informative Speaking. Only 2 students were selected to represent Arkansas in Informative Speaking. Addison traveled to the NSDA National Tournament in 2025 and competed in the supplemental event of Expository Speaking. 

Katharine Welky was selected as 1st Alternate in Congressional Debate- Senate. 
Annabel Champlin was selected as 2nd Alternate in Dramatic Interpretation.

Members of our delegation were: Katharine Welky and Landon Harvey in the Senate. Ian Lee-Kim, Roseli Pineda, Amelia Garrett, Milina Michel, Hugh Lamey, and Dylan Simmons in the House. 

The CHS Speech & Debate Team is coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

text:
🎶 Conway High School Band Earns Top Honors at State Contest! 🎶

The Conway High School Band’s Wind Symphony and Symphonic Band delivered outstanding performances at the Arkansas School Band and Orchestra Association’s State Concert Contest on Tuesday, April 14th in Cabot.

After winning the DD-7A (2nd bands) classification last year, the Symphonic Band returned as the Honor Ensemble this year—earning a 1st Division Rating. As the Honor Ensemble, they were not eligible for ranked competition, but their performance once again showcased their excellence.

The Wind Symphony performed in Class 7A (1st bands), earning a 1st Division Rating and being named State Runner-Up “Reserve Honor Ensemble” for the second consecutive year—an incredible achievement!

The Conway High School Band continues to stand out as one of the most decorated programs in the state, known for its superior musicianship and artistry.

📍 The attached photos highlight their recent performance at the Windgate Center for Fine and Performing Arts on the UCA campus.

👏 Congratulations to all of these talented students on their continued success! #WampusCatPride #CHSBand #ExcellenceInMusic

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Students, As the week comes to a close, Conway Public Schools wants to speak directly to you. This week brought challenges that required attention from school teachers, staff, SROs, the Conway Police Department, and the Conway Fire Department. Schools remained safe because teachers and staff stepped up, stayed focused, and handled situations the right way, while you, our students, continued to do the right things.Now it’s time to move forward.The expectations are simple and important for maintaining a safe and productive learning environment. Each day, come to school ready to learn, support one another, and make good decisions.Please remember that your actions have consequences. Choices, especially those involving threats or inappropriate behavior on social media, are taken seriously and will be addressed accordingly.More importantly, Conway Public Schools believes in its students. There is confidence in your ability to lead, look out for one another, and represent your school and community the right way.It’s time to get back to work and finish the week strong.Have a great Friday and Go Wampus Cats.Conway Administration

author: Conway High School
text:
🎉 Big News from Conway at AYAA! 🎉

For the first time since 2019, Conway returned to the Arkansas Young Artists Association (AYAA) Competition—and made a powerful impact!

This statewide event brings together 60+ schools and over 1,300 student artists from across Arkansas. Our students rose to the occasion with incredible success:

🏆 Over 70 CHS and CJHS students participated
🏆 14 total awards earned
🏆 12 awards from CHS students
🏆 2 awards from CJHS students

We are extremely proud of the creativity, dedication, and talent our students showcased throughout the competition. This marks an exciting return for Conway, and we are already looking forward to building on this momentum and bringing home even more recognition in the years ahead!

Congratulations to all of our student artists! 🎨✨

author: Conway High School
text: Good afternoon parents and guardians,CHS will be administering the ATLAS Assessments on April 20th and 21st, as well as April 28th and 29th. Testing will begin at 8am and end around 10:30am. Please make sure your students are present and refrain from checking them out until the testing period is over.As ATLAS testing approaches, we wanted to share a few important details and ways you can help support your students in doing their very best. These assessments are an opportunity for students to show what they have learned and the growth they have made throughout the year.To help encourage strong effort, we will once again offer incentives for student growth and achievement. ATLAS results may also play a role in your student’s schedule for the upcoming school year. Students who score in the bottom 25% may be placed in an Academic Intervention period. This would be a supportive class designed to provide extra help and ensure students have the skills they need to be successful.You can support your student by encouraging them to take their time, stay focused, and give their best effort on each test. Making sure they get a good night’s sleep and arrive at school on time will also help them feel prepared and confident. Please also be sure to remind them to come to school with a fully charged chromebook and charger.Thank you for your continued support. If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out.

author: Conway High School
text: Good afternoon students,As ATLAS testing approaches, we want to remind you that this is your opportunity to show what you’ve learned and the progress you’ve made this year! Your effort on these assessments truly matters, and we encourage you to take them seriously and give your best.Just like in the past, there is an incentive for showing growth! Students who demonstrate growth from summative to summative may earn an additional day toward their semester test exemptions. In addition, we want to help incentivize achievement, so for every Level 3 or 4 a student achieves, they will earn an entry for various raffle prizes. This would be a great time for you to log into your ATLAS portal and review your ATLAS scores from last year’s summative. Many of you are already on track to beat that score based on your interim results! Now is the time to really give it your best!It’s also important to know that your ATLAS scores may impact your schedule for next school year. Students who score in the bottom 25% may be placed in an Academic Intervention period. This is a support designed to help you strengthen skills and be successful moving forward.You’re capable of doing well on this assessment. Take your time, stay focused, and put in your best effort on every question. Make sure you get a good night’s sleep and come prepared on testing days with your chromebook fully charged. It’s also a good idea to bring your charger.We’re rooting for you and excited to see what you can do!

author: Conway High School
text: Good morning teachers,As ATLAS testing approaches, we wanted to share a few reminders and opportunities to help support and encourage students to put forth their very best effort. While these assessments do play a role in our school letter grade and teacher VAM scores, they are also an important opportunity for students to demonstrate their growth and progress.As in the past, we will continue to incentivize student growth by offering an additional day toward semester test exemptions for students who grow their Average Scale Score by 1 point or more from last year’s summative. In addition, we want to help incentivize achievement, so for every Level 3 or 4 a student achieves, they will earn an entry for various raffle prizes.  Please take a moment to highlight this opportunity with your students and ensure that they understand we are tracking growth now from summative to summative. It is also important to communicate to students that their ATLAS performance may impact their course schedule for the upcoming school year. Students who score in the bottom 25% may be placed in an Academic Intervention period. This is designed as a support system to provide targeted help and ensure continued growth.Thank you for the work you do each day to support and motivate our students. Your encouragement plays a critical role in helping them take ownership of their learning and perform at their highest level. Please let us know if you need additional materials or support as we prepare for testing.We appreciate all you do!

🎓🌟 Conway High School was proud to celebrate our 2026 Sheltered ESL graduates at this week’s Graduation Banquet!

This program has experienced incredible growth in just two years. In 2024, we celebrated 4 graduates. This year, we are honoring 19 graduates — a powerful testament to the hard work of these students, the support of their families, and the dedication of the CHS staff and faculty who have invested in their success.

During the banquet, Dr. Worley recognized Ms. Goodnight for the tremendous impact she has made on the CHS ESL program over the past 9 years. We are deeply grateful for her heart, commitment, and service to our students.

Please join us in congratulating our graduates and celebrating this special milestone! 🎉👏 #WampusCatPride #CHSGraduates #ESLSuccess

Conway Baseball 9th -12th Grade Tryouts

Tryout dates for Conway High School and Conway Junior High School students wanting to participate in baseball for the 2025-2026 school year will be May 26-28 at the Conway Baseball Field from 3:00-5:00. A current physical must be entered into DragonFly Max in order to participate. . Email hardinl@conwayschools.info to sign up.



GET STARTED 
WITH DRAGONFLY

PARENTS & STUDENTS

1 Download the DragonFly MAX app from the App Store or Google Play.

2 Tap ‘Get Started’ and ‘Sign Up for Free’ then follow the prompts to create your
Parent account with your own email address.
Note: please do not create an account with your child’s name or contact information — you will get 
the chance to add your child soon!

3. Verify your account with the verification ID sent to your email address.

4 Tap ‘Connect to your school’ to select ‘Parent’ as your role and search for your
child’s school.

5. After selecting your child’s school, tap ‘Join’ to request access. An administrator
at your school will approve your request.

6 Tap ‘Set up your children’ and follow the prompts to add your kid(s) and fill out forms

author: Kameron Wright
text:
With the conclusion of the decathlon competition in Springdale, AR, these two Wampus Cats battled through ten grueling events over the course of two days. The decathlon is one of the toughest challenges in track and field, featuring the 100‑meter dash, long jump, shot put, high jump, 400‑meter dash, 110‑meter hurdles, discus throw, pole vault, triple jump, and the 1500‑meter run.

Out of 66 competitors, Gavin Garrison finished 12th overall and Cardagan Hicks finished 36th overall. Huge congratulations to these athletes for showing the mental and physical toughness required to compete in such a demanding event.

author: Conway High School
text:
❤️ Conway High School is honored to be recognized as a Heart Safe School through the Arkansas Children’s Project ADAM program!

This designation means CHS has taken important steps to prepare for cardiac emergencies through CPR/AED training, emergency response planning, and campus-wide preparedness measures designed to protect students, staff, and visitors. Project ADAM’s mission is to help schools respond quickly and confidently when every second matters.

We are incredibly thankful for the dedication of our nurses, staff, administrators, and community partners who helped make this possible. Their commitment helps ensure Conway High School remains a safer place for everyone who walks through our doors. ❤️🐾

#ConwayHighSchool #WampusCats #HeartSafeSchool #ProjectADAM #CatStrong

text:
📚✨ This summer, Conway High School was proud to host Arkansas AIMS for a week of incredible professional development focused on strengthening teaching and learning across Arkansas.

More than 300 math, science, and English educators from districts across the state — alongside our own Conway educators — joined us for content-specific learning designed to deepen content knowledge, align instruction to Arkansas standards, and help prepare students for ATLAS testing.

We appreciate the opportunity to continue strengthening our partnership with Arkansas AIMS and value the important work being done to support educators through meaningful, content-specific professional learning. 🤝💙

#ConwayHighSchool #ConwayPublicSchools #ArkansasAIMS #ProfessionalLearning

author: Conway High School
text:
CHS is proud to announce Gabriella Ponce as the recipient of the Cole Jett Memorial Scholarship.

Established by Cole’s family, this scholarship honors Cole’s legacy of kindness, strength, and compassion while providing students with opportunities to further their education and pursue their dreams.

Gabriella exemplifies the values this scholarship represents, and we are honored to support her educational journey. We know she will continue to make a positive impact in her community and inspire others along the way.

Please join us in congratulating Gabriella on this well-deserved achievement. 

💙 In memory of 2026 Conway High School graduate, Cole Jett. 

May we continue to live by the words that define his legacy:

Be Kind.
Be Strong.
Be the Light.

author: Conway High School
text: Dear Parents and Guardians,As we prepare for the upcoming school year, we would like to share important information regarding student parking at Conway High School.Students who drive to school may purchase a parking permit, which authorizes them to park on campus. Parking permits will be sold on a first-come, first-served basis during schedule pickup. If permits remain available, they may also be purchased during Open House on Wednesday, August 12, from 4:00–7:00 p.m., or at any time during the school year through the main office.Beginning this school year, parking spaces will no longer be assigned. Instead, students may park in any available designated student parking space upon arrival each day. In previous years, assigned parking was necessary due to limited parking availability. Because additional parking is now available, we are transitioning to open parking. This change will better accommodate students who participate in before- and after-school activities by allowing them to park closer to the location of their activities, enhancing both convenience and safety.To purchase a parking permit, students must provide the following:$25.00 (cash or check only; credit and debit cards are not accepted)A valid driver’s licenseCurrent proof of insuranceVehicle information, including:License plate numberMake and modelColorWe appreciate your partnership and support as we prepare for another outstanding school year. We look forward to welcoming our students back to campus and wish everyone a successful start to the new school year!

text:
📣 CPSD ATHLETICS SPECTATOR GUIDELINES

Conway Public Schools is excited to welcome students, families, and community members to our athletic events! To help make every game safe, positive, and enjoyable for everyone, please review these important spectator guidelines.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 STUDENT SUPERVISION
• Conway High School events: Elementary, middle school, and junior high students must be accompanied by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.
• Conway Junior High events: Elementary and middle school students must be accompanied by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.
• Conway Middle School events: Elementary students must be accompanied by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.

🏟️ AT ALL ATHLETIC EVENTS
• Students should remain in the stands unless visiting the concession stand or restroom. No loitering in unauthorized areas, including the high school courtyard.
• Backpacks, balls, skateboards, bikes, and similar items are not permitted.
• No outside food or drinks. Concessions are available inside the event.
• School rules apply. Please cooperate with all game workers and school personnel. Failure to follow expectations may result in removal from the game.
• Students must leave campus promptly after the game. Students who are not picked up within 20 minutes of the end of the game will not be permitted to attend future games. Please make transportation arrangements before the game ends.

Thank you for helping us create a safe, respectful, and enjoyable environment for our students, families, and fans! We appreciate your cooperation and your support of Conway Public Schools Athletics! 🐾

text:
9th graders interested in participating in the CHS Fall production, The Play That Goes Wrong, should join the Schoology group using the code below. Auditions are Tuesday, August 29th. 

Get ready for a night of mishaps, mischief, and madcap mania! It’s the opening night of the Cornley Drama Society’s newest production, “The Murder at Haversham Manor,” and things have quickly gone from bad…to utterly disastrous. The troupe’s ambitious 1920s whodunit has everything you never want in a show: falling props, collapsing scenery, an unconscious leading lady, a corpse that can’t play dead, and actors who trip over everything…including their lines. How will this eager ensemble battle against all of the disastrous odds? Will they make it to the final curtain call?

An international hit that’s equal parts Monty Python and Sherlock Holmes – The Play That Goes Wrong is full of hilarious perfection.

Great things happening at CJHS! 
Coke and Candy is one of the nine incentive days that we have scheduled at CJHS.  With all of our incentive days, the purpose is to reward and celebrate kids for excelling behaviorally and academically.

For our coke and candy incentive, the only requirement is that you have not been in any verbal or physical altercations. Essentially, we want to celebrate the kids that do exactly what they’re supposed to do because they deserve it.  
 
Thank you to all of our PAWS volunteers who helped distribute at all lunches! #ContinuingTheLegacy

author: Casey Buck
text:
The Conway Public Schools Orchestra program presents its annual "La Fiesta Orquesta” event on Monday, November 13, featuring the nearly 300 students of the orchestra program in free concerts throughout the night in the James H. Clark Auditorium. In addition, a taco supper fundraiser is held in the Conway HS Cafeteria from 5-8 pm.  

Tickets to the dinner are on sale now and can be purchased from any orchestra student, and donations and ticket purchases can also be made online at conwayorch.square.site. This year we are partnering with Tacos4Life, so every meal purchased raises funds for the orchestra AND provides a meal to a person in need!
 
We hope you’ll support these amazing students and come hear us play!!

Mrs. King has some cool things going on in her classroom, check them out! 

Spanish 2 classes had the option to make paper flowers as part of their lesson on Día de los Muertos. Cempasúchil, or marigold flowers, is commonly seen for Day of the Dead. The beautiful orange and yellows represent a celebration of life. 

Her classes also receive pesos as rewards. Every 9 weeks they have an auction entirely in Spanish where they can buy authentic snacks with their class pesos.

Way to make learning fun and engaging Mrs. King! #ContinuingTheLegacy

They were divided into groups of 4-5 and they had to work collaboratively in order to come up with and sketch out their plan. They then recreated their sketch in the hallway on a larger scale using painters tape.  And they are AMAZING! Can you believe our students MADE those?! We have some great things happening at CJHS and our students are a big part of it! #ContinuingTheLegacy

text:
The Cat Nation Christmas tree is up in the Cafeteria! Cat Nation Christmas is a program we proudly sponsor at Conway Jr. High to provide our students whose families are struggling financially with gifts at Christmas time. 
Here’s how it works:
Scan the QR code on the back of the paw print ornaments on the tree in the cafeteria.
Select a gift or gifts from the list.
Buy the gift and return it unwrapped to the front office or room 2032 by Dec. 6.
If you don’t want to buy a gift, you can still support the Cat Nation Christmas program by donating money during our “Stuff the Stocking'' money drive! You will have the opportunity to donate before school on Thursday, Nov. 30 and Friday, Dec. 1st.

Congratulations to Mrs. Barnett!  She is our November Teacher of the Month sponsored by The Wells Family at Lumber1 Home Center.  Here are a few words from coworkers and students:
"She works so hard and wants the best for every student."
"She is doing such a great job organizing Student Council. The new things they’ve implemented this year have been awesome (peer tutoring, helping with backpack program, assisting during PT conferences, etc.). Been such a positive change."
"Mrs. Barnett is a great teacher, and I could not imagine having anyone else as my civics teacher. She is kind, and very compassionate about her job. She truly tries her best to teach us about our civil duties as citizens, and nurtures a very welcoming and open environment where everyone is welcome, and there are no wrong opinions."

Thanks for being such a positive part of CJHS!
#ContinuingTheLegacy

Our first Black History Month Highlight will be Pastor Maltbia!

Pastor Maltbia is Founder and Senior Pastor of True Holiness Saints Center, Inc. in Conway, Arkansas where he has faithfully served for more than two decades. Pastor Maltbia currently serves as a member of Conway Regional Health System Board of Directors, Chaplain for the Conway Police Department, Chaplain for Veasley Funeral Home and Cremations, and a member of Conway Ministerial Alliance.  Pastor Maltbia was appointed by Governor Asa Hutchinson to the University of Central Arkansas’s Board of Trustees, where he served a seven year term. Pastor Maltbia was also appointed as Chaplain of the State of Arkansas’s House of Representatives 87th General Assembly.
 
He has impacted the City of Conway by serving on the board of directors of the following organizations: United Way of Faulkner County, Salvation Army of Faulkner County, Faulkner County Leadership Institute, Conway Regional Health System Community Advisory Board, Community Foundation of Faulkner County, the University of Central Arkansas’s Inaugural Parent and Family Council, Arkansas Martin Luther King, Jr. Commission, and as a founding member of the Conway Community Race Relations Initiative, and the City of Conway’s Civil Service Commission. 

Pastor Maltbia is married to his high school sweetheart, Natasha Maltbia. God has blessed them with two beautiful children, Kennedy and Connor.

We appreciate all that Pastor Maltbia has done and continues to do for our community! 

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
CJHS Highlights: Thelma Moton

Thelma Moton, a trailblazing force, is not just the Founder and CEO of Choosing to Excel (C2E) in Central Arkansas; she's a relentless advocate for youth and families, boasting over 30 years of impactful commitment. Born amidst twelve siblings in Twin Groves, Arkansas, Thelma, a product of both segregated and integrated education, is driven by a profound mission to transform the lives of Arkansas youth one choice at a time.

Breaking the mold, Thelma's journey inspired the birth of Choosing to Excel, a dynamic program employing a multifaceted approach across schools, communities, alternative educational settings, summer programs, and mentoring initiatives. With an annual reach of over 10,000 youth spanning multiple counties, C2E is a beacon of positive change.

Beyond the numbers, C2E's Nurturing Families component is a lifeline for parents and teen parents, fostering healthy interactions, reducing teen pregnancy, and providing crucial support for preventive healthcare. Thelma's brainchild, the Youth Leadership Initiative, empowers young voices, emphasizing community involvement and decision-making. Their rallying cry, "Nothing About Us Without Us," echoes the belief that every young person deserves a voice and recognition.

Thelma, married for 50 years with eleven children and seventeen grandchildren, is more than a leader—she's a catalyst for change. With a mantra of "Keep The End In Mind," she understands that combining information with trusting relationships in various settings creates lasting bonds, fostering behavioral change and optimal health.

Thelma's journey is a testament to collaboration, weaving together community leaders, school boards, parents, and local governing bodies. She doesn't just promote the "CHOICE TO EXCEL"; she lives it, embodying the belief that everyone, regardless of circumstances, deserves a safe, nurturing haven because, in Thelma's world, "they matter."

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Highlights: Korry Garrett!

Korry Garrett is a Principal Broker at Sandstone Real Estate Group. He chose this
career path based on his relationships with people and continues to nurture and grow those relationships as he progresses in his work. Korry credits his wife, Shawnte Garrett, for inspiring him to enter the real estate business, as he knew many people and believed it would be a good fit for him. However, it was his colleague Greg Hunt who ultimately showed him the way and taught him about real estate and life. Despite their initial dislike for each other, their paths crossed again, and Greg became an important figure in Korry's life and career. In his role as Principal Broker, Korry is responsible for training, assisting, and equipping 26 licensees with the tools they need to achieve their ultimate goal of helping clients realize their dreams. Outside of work, Korry devotes his time to his wife and theirchildren, Jaxen and Jersei Grey, finding joy in watching them grow and their daily antics.

Korry's accomplishments include being named to Arkansas Business 40 Under 40,
serving as a Conway Chamber of Commerce Chairman 2024, being a member of the
Arkansas Association of Realtist, being a charter member of the graduate chapter of
Omega Psi Phi Fraternity Incorporated, and being an active member of New Hope
Baptist Church, and being the 1st and only African American to own a real estate
franchise in the State of Arkansas

Korry is passionate about inclusivity and believes in sharing his knowledge and
experiences to help others succeed. He believes that when one person wins, the entire community benefits.

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

text:
CJHS Highlights: Nadia Eslinger 

Dr. Nadia Eslinger is a native of West Memphis, AR. She came to Conway to study at the University of Central Arkansas in the Fall of 2000. Nadia graduated from UCA in 2005 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History and African American Studies and again in 2008 with a Master of Education degree in College Student Personnel Services and Administration. After completing her studies at UCA, Naida worked at the University of Georgia and Arkansas State University. Then she returned to UCA, where she has worked for almost ten years. While at UCA, Nadia worked in academic advising. Academic Recovery, and Student Success. She oversees the First-Gen @ UCA program and is the Inaugural Director of the BEAR Life program, a grant-funded program for pell-eligible students. Nadia recently concluded her studies at Maryville University, where she received her Educational Doctorate Degree (EdD) in Higher Education Leadership. Additionally, Nadia is an Adjunct Professor in the CSPA Graduate program. 

Dr. Eslinger is a member of the Conway Public School Foundation Board, where she served as Outreach Chair for many years. Nadia is a member of the Central Arkansas Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., where she serves as Recording Secretary.  She also participates with the Faulkner County Democratic Women’s Organization, NAACP, PTO, and the UCA Black Alumni Association. Nadia is a mom to two teenagers, Aidan and Ariah, who are her pride and joy and keep her very busy. Ten years ago, Nadia helped Aidan start his own Business, The Aidan Eslinger Company, where she continues to work as the COO and Executive Producer of his projects. 

 Dr. Eslinger believes by supporting and challenging at-risk students in their pursuit of higher education, she not only empowers individuals to break the cycle of poverty but also contributes to building a more inclusive and educated community. 

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Highlights: Dr. Shaneil Ealy

Dr. Shaneil Ealy, community leader and champion for women's empowerment and youth leadership, has been making waves in Conway for years. A true local, she's proud to call herself a Wampus Cat,having grown up right here in Conway.
For over 20 years, Dr. Ealy has been part of the University of Central Arkansas, where she's currently the Associate Vice President in charge of connecting the campus with the community. You might have seen Dr. Ealy around town, involved in engaging initiatives like the Conway Area Youth Leadership Institute or the Women’s Leadership Network, now a nonprofit organization. Dr. Ealy is all about making connections and supporting her community. She's passionate about education and spent many years supporting teachers by serving on the Conway Public Schools
Foundation Board. The Conway Chamber recognized Dr. Ealy’s leadership with a CALI Award in 2018, and in 2020, she was named Outstanding Women in Nonprofit by the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce. UCA honored Dr. Ealy with the Employee of the Year Award in 2017. Dr. Ealy is all about sisterhood and service, living out the principles of her beloved sorority, Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.

When she's not busy with all that, Dr. Ealy and her husband, Tafty Ealy, III, run a couple of diesel repair shops and even own some cattle farms. But the real joy in her life? That's her two boys, Jase (10)  and Henderson (15). You'll often find Dr. Ealy cheering them on at their football games! She also loves creating new dishes in the kitchen and creating memorable experiences - whether it's fun workouts, hiking and cycling or traveling with her Ealy men and friends. 

She's all about showing that success isn't just about work—it's about community, family, and being true to who you are and where you come from.

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence 
#ContinuingTheLegacy

text:
CJHS Highlights: Felix Maull

Mr. Maull was born November 24, 1970 in Dequeen, Arkansas. H was the first male child of Felix and Annie Maull.  His father had a 6th grade education, while his mother’s schooling during that time was limited to 8th grade for females.  His father entered the US military at the age of 14 and spent the better part of 26 years serving his country.  Mr. Maull says, "What my parents could not assist their five children with academically or financially, they more than made up for with love, encouragement and structure. "

His father had a belief that one should not know everything about one thing, but rather know a little about everything you encounter so that you would never be lost in any endeavor.  He says his mother instilled in him that faith in God is the core of everything. "When you have done your very best, be okay with it" is what she would say.  He states that he strives to pass that on to his students--Learn as much as you can. Do your best and be willing to accept the results.  

In 1989, Mr. Maull graduated from DeQueen High School as an honor student, ranked 7th in his class.  He attended the University of Central Arkansas  and graduated with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics education and a masters degree in curriculum instruction and administration. In the fall of 1995, Mr. Maull became the first African-American mathematics teacher to be hired in the Conway Public School District. In that same year he married the love of his life and two children- Nathan and Sarah- were added to this union.  

During his tenure, Mr. Maull has taught 8th grade math, Inclusion math,  Accelerated Algebra 1, and Accelerated Geometry.  He has also served on several educational committees both local and nationwide.

He states, "My greatest achievements do not lie in what  I have done in my life;  but rather when I see my children, students and everyone I encounter succeed." 

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Highlights: Delbra King

Mrs. King was born and raised in Hempstead County  (Southwest Arkansas), in the town of Hope. She is the third of four children, two girls and one boy,  born to her Mom and Dad. She states her grandparents were a huge part of her upbringing and helped  teach her the value of family relationships and a good work ethic.

 She is married to Milton King and they were blessed to be the proud parents of seven boys and four girls. She has a Bachelor of Arts in Science degree from Hendrix College. She believes that success is more than grades, money, and what brand of clothing we wear. Success is rooted in how a person serves and helps the people who cross their paths; some may pass by only once in life and others may pass more, but how they are affected by your investment in them whether, small or great, can be the difference between success and failure for them.

Mrs. King states,  "I became an educator because it is important to me that students understand there is no substitute for self love and respect, and as individuals, their place in this world is important. They need to know that they can win; win  is out there...... it is waiting to be found, but they have to go and get it." She states she feels she is  called to help prepare the next generation for life beyond the brick and mortar environment. It is a challenge which takes on many different faces, but if I can just do my best to answer that call, then I would not have "run my race in vain."

Mrs. King states the persons she admires the most are her parents because they were determined to raise children who could contribute to the health of their community. She explains, "They taught my brother, sisters, and me to work hard, save, and to protect our name and each other. They would say, "your name is all you have; take care of it and it will take care of you".

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Highlights: Jasper Johnson
Assistant Principal (Conway Public Schools)  & Owner of Shoe Junky Fitness

Jasper Johnson was born in Pine Bluff, AR. He is the son of Gloria Johnson and graduated from Dollarway High School in Pine Bluff. He attended the University of Central Arkansas on a football scholarship and graduated with his Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology:Criminology in 2007. Jasper was the first person in his entire family to graduate college. He would later return to school in 2009 in which he received his Master of Arts in Teaching degree (2011) before getting his Educational Specialist degree in 2016.

Jasper started his work career in college serving as a case manager with Arkansas Counseling Associates. Jasper served as a liaison between the schools and courts for at-risk kids, mainly those in the alternative learning environment and incarcerated juveniles. Upon graduating college, he went on to sign a free agent contract with the NFL Dallas Cowboys in 2007. In 2009, Jasper went to play in the Canadian Football League (CFL) for the Winnipeg Blue Bombers. After his football career, Mr. Johnson returned home and pursued his second degree to become an educator. Mr. Johnson started teaching 7th Grade English-Language Arts at Ridgeroad Elementary in North Little Rock in 2010. After only one year in NLR, he would spend his next nine years at Bob Courtway Middle School. 

Jasper is a huge fitness enthusiast and sneakerhead. In the peak of COVID, Jasper started his fitness business, Shoe Junky Fitness. He has trained over 1000 clients and currently has his own fitness app located in the Google Play Store and Apple App Store. His passion for sneakers grew when he was a young boy, but couldn't get the high end kicks his heart desired like some of his friends. He always stated, “when I grow up, I’m gonna get any shoe I want.” In his spare time, he does competitive men’s physique bodybuilding in which he was crowned “Mr. Arkansas 2022.”

Currently, Mr. Johnson is serving as an administrator in the Conway Public School District. He is an Assistant Principal at Preston & Florence Mattison Elementary. He is a member of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Inc. in which their mission is to encourage achievement in every field of human endeavor. He also travels around the Central Arkansas area speaking to at-risk youth in schools about overcoming adversity. 

Jasper is married to LaShanta Johnson, and they have two beautiful children, Kaleb and Kynlei. He loves to travel around the country with his family and visit places he couldn’t have imagined as a kid.
