text:
CJHS Highlights: Derrick Carruth

Derrick Carruth, born on December 31, 1976, in Forrest City, AR, was raised by a strong network of women including his mother, aunt, grandmother, and great-grandmother. Recognizing the importance of education as a way for taking care of his grandmother and great-grandmother, Derrick pursued excellence in academics, understanding that college would pave the way for their well-being. 

In 1995, Derrick graduated from Forrest City High School, where he distinguished himself as the only black male in the top 10% of his class. He earned a scholarship to the University of Central Arkansas in Conway, majoring in Computer Information Systems. In 1996, he became a member of the Iota Gamma Chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Inc., where he became an active member and Canemaster in the state of Arkansas.

Following his graduation in August 1999, Derrick embarked on his professional journey, joining Acxiom Corporation as a Data Analyst. He continued to pursue higher education, obtaining a Masters Degree in Computer Information Systems in 2003 from Baker College.  Derrick’s career at Acxiom flourished, as he currently serves as a Digital Solution Architect specializing in Databases and Campaign tools. Shortly after he was hired, he married his high school sweetheart, Nicole Thomas. Nicole has been an RN at Children’s Hospital for the past 21 years working in allergy research. Their union blessed them with two daughters, Kennedi and Emmersyn. 

In 2003, Derrick helped charter the Conway Alumni Chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi. For the past 20 years, the chapter has been a contributor to the community and surrounding areas. In 2019, Derrick became the Polemarch of the Alumni chapter (i.e. President). That same year, he took on the challenge of being the lead coordinator of the chapter’s 10for10 Scholarship Drive which, at the time, had been in place for
10 years raising over $12000 in scholarships. Over the last 5 years, the chapter has rewarded over $34,000 in scholarships under his guidance. Along with programs such as Wheels & Wishes, NupesGiving, Kappa League and Annual Backpack Giveaway, Conway Alumni was able to win Medium Chapter of the Year twice in the past 3 years for the Southwestern Province, which is the fraternity’s largest province.

In addition to his professional and philanthropic endeavors, Derrick shares his expertise by teaching coding at UCA’s Arkansas Coding Academy. Leveraging his skills as a Graphics Designer, Derrick designed clinics. Throughout his journey, Derrick remains committed to uplifting his community and empowering the next generation.

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence
#ContinuingTheLegacy

text:
CJHS Highlights: Kenyon McNeail 

Born on March 22, 1991, in Memphis, Tennessee, Kenyon McNeail's story is one of perseverance, passion, and transformation. His love for basketball sparked early, shortly after moving to Conway, Arkansas, in fourth grade. It was at Conway High School where Kenyon's basketball talents truly shone, leading his team to a state title in the 2009-10 season as a three-star recruit. This was not just a victory but a testament to what dedication and hard work can achieve, opening doors for Kenyon to play Division I basketball at Louisiana Tech.

At Louisiana Tech, Kenyon didn't just play basketball; he made an indelible mark, contributing to two conference championships and two NIT appearances over four successful years. His collegiate career was not just about scoring points; it was about building a foundation for his future, both on and off the court.

After graduation, Kenyon pursued a professional basketball career overseas, embracing the challenges and triumphs of playing internationally. However, in a move that speaks volumes about his character, Kenyon chose to retire from professional basketball to focus on what mattered most to him: family and community.

With more time to dedicate to his passions outside of playing, Kenyon ventured into entrepreneurship, learning the business side of basketball. From training to launching a brand of custom knee and elbow sleeves, he poured his knowledge and love for the game into creating something that could benefit others.

Today, Kenyon is the proud owner of IGN Academy, a three-court facility nestled in Conway, Arkansas. But IGN Academy is more than just a place to play basketball; it's a beacon of hope and a source of inspiration for kids from kindergarten to 12th grade, boys and girls alike. Through leagues, tournaments, and training, Kenyon is passing on his love and dedication for basketball to the next generation, helping them to learn, grow, and dream big.

Kenyon McNeail's journey from a young boy with a dream in Memphis to a community leader in Conway shows us all that with passion, dedication, and a heart for giving back, anything is possible. He reminds us that the true value of our achievements lies not just in the trophies we win, but in the lives we touch and the futures we inspire. To the kids looking up to him: dream big, work hard, and never forget the power of giving back. Your journey is just beginning.

#CJHSCelebratingBlackExcellence 
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Celebrates: Lindsey Swanigan 

Lindsey (McDaniel) Swanigan was born in Conway, AR in 1993. She is the daughter of Sam and Sharon McDaniel and graduated from Morrilton High School in 2011. She obtained a bachelor’s degree from Arkansas Tech University in 2015 in Biology. Following graduation, she pursued a career in Pathology. She began her teaching career at the Future School of Fort Smith after marrying her husband, Deondra Swanigan in 2018. She and her husband moved back to Central Arkansas in 2020, and she began teaching at Graduate Arkansas in Little Rock, AR. In 2021, they moved to Conway, AR and she began teaching math at Conway Junior High in 2022. During this time, she obtained a masters degree in teaching from the University of Central Arkansas in May of 2022.  This same year, she founded Swan Academics, a educational consulting and tutoring business. She is also a minister of music at New Generation Church here in Conway and has been playing the piano for 13 years. She and her husband currently reside in Conway, AR and they have been married for 5 years. 

Lindsey is currently in pursuit to become Dr. Lindsey Swanigan, a change leadership expert with a Ph.D. in Equity and Inclusion K-12 Education at the University of Central Arkansas. Alongside being a devoted wife, minister of music, makeup artist, and teacher, she is an educator with six years of experience and the founder of Swan Academics, driven by compassion, selflessness, and boldness. Her journey in education has made a significant impact on students' lives, fostering an environment where learning thrives. Her innovative teaching methods and dedication have empowered students to overcome challenges and achieve academic excellence. Her passion for breaking barriers in education stems from the belief that every student deserves equal opportunities. Through personalized guidance and encouragement, she challenges traditional norms, encouraging students to explore their full potential. Witnessing their transformations brings her immense joy, fueling my commitment to innovate and adapt continually. Her legacy lies in inspiring others to believe in the power of education. With compassion, selflessness, and boldness, she shapes positive, supportive learning environments, leaving a lasting impact on the lives of her students and the communities she serves.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
CJHS Celebrates: Tanya Smith

Born and raised in the small farming community of Piggott, Arkansas, Mrs. Smith learned to value hard work and determination from her parents, Larry and Donajo Simpson. Along with her younger brother Erik, she spent many hours on the family farm and enjoyed small town events such as marching in the Independence Day Parade with the high school band, cruising the Sonic Drive-In on weekends with friends, and hosting hayrides and bonfires. Moving from a hometown of around 3000 people to a college campus of about the same number seemed daunting at first, but Tanya soon found her niche and enjoyed performing with the university chorus. Thanks to the opportunity of touring and performing in several European countries (France, Germany, Czech Republic, and Poland to name a few) she began to see how language learning could open new doors of opportunity. Embracing the importance of understanding other cultures and languages, Tanya  went on to graduate Summa Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts in French from UCA. 

Tanya’s love for languages was preceded by her love for teaching.  Insisting on playing school with her younger brother in her early years and teaching Sunday school, piano, and flute as a high school student were just the beginning. Upon graduating from college, she taught Exploratory French, French I and French II at Horace Mann Arts and Science Magnet in Little Rock, but then took a twenty year break from the public school classroom while raising and homeschooling her own five children. The homeschool years were rich with opportunities for sharing an excitement for education. During that time, Mrs. Smith taught a wide range of subjects in various homeschool co-ops as well as instructing her own children. From K4 to history to English composition and creative writing, Mrs. Smith enjoyed developing interactive, hands-on lessons with the hope of inspiring a love for learning in her students. 

After twenty years of teaching in non-traditional settings, the path back to the classroom took some interesting turns: substitute teaching at all levels in Conway public schools, working as a paraprofessional in a 1:10 classroom, and teaching 8th grade PAP English during the height of Covid restrictions all turned out to be delightful and educational experiences for Mrs. Smith. She has now come full circle, returning to her first love in the field of education - teaching French. Mrs. Smith takes great joy in introducing language and culture to her students through conversation, songs and games, and she hopes that along the way they also learn to increase their understanding and compassion for people of other cultures as well as students in their very own classrooms. Mrs. Smith is proud to be a member of the Conway Junior High School team -  a high quality, high energy group of professionals who truly care about the students they serve each day. She is also thankful to be a part of the Smith team, where she is strongly supported by her husband of almost twenty-seven years, David, and by her children - Elisha, Isaac, Olivia, Samuel, and Ezra - all amazing human beings.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Celebrates: Teri McMoran

Teri McMoran was raised in Conway along with three sisters who are  all proud to be  Wampus Cat graduates. Her parents and grandparents  dedicated their lives showing the importance of hard work and determination to bring success and happiness in whatever path of life you chose as well as having a strong faith. Mrs. McMoran loves spending time with her family, especially her  three sons and their families. Her four grandchildren keep her busy with fun outings and visits to Conway. 
 
Mrs. McMoran received a BSE  English degree  from the  University of Central Arkansas but decided to pursue a career in the family business for a decade before going back into education. In 1992 she graduated with a Master of Arts in Literature and began her teaching career at the University of Central Arkansas. She also taught for several years as an adjunct professor at Central Baptist College. Her journey with the Conway Public Schools began in 1995 at Conway High School where she taught 10th and 11th grade English. Once the school split to two campuses, she settled in at Conway High East teaching 10th grade Pre-AP.  When the campus became 8-9, she chose to stay and teach 9th grade English.  She currently  teaches 8th grade English. 

In 2003 Mrs. McMoran was recognized as the National Career Academies Coalition Exemplary Teacher of the Year for her leadership shown within the Medical Academy Team. She was also recognized for developing curriculum relevance, leading the development of  the Keystone transition course to help acclimate freshmen to high school, develop school spirit, teach the importance of community service, goal setting, and career exploration. In the same year she was chosen the Conway High East teacher of the Year. Her biggest accomplishments, however, come in the classroom where she strives for student success in all areas and continues to be a positive influence for her students who struggle academically and emotionally.  Recently, Mrs. McMoran was named the 2023 Arvest Teacher of the Year. She does an amazing job of blending the traditional on-level students with Inclusion and has high expectations for all of her students. 

 Mrs. McMoran  believes  that any child is capable of learning as long as the teacher and student recognize the problem and  work together to find a solution.  She often says to her students, “Is it the skill or the will that is the problem?”    Mrs. McMoran is a veteran teacher who continues to make a difference at CJHS!

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#ContinuingTheLegacy

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
CJHS Celebrates: Marlene Hazel

Marlene Hazel has been impacting students in the classroom since 1987, after graduating magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Science in Education degree from the University of Central Arkansas. Coming from a long line of educators in her family, she knew from an early age that she was called to the profession of teaching. Her first experience in the classroom was in Morrilton, AR where she taught 7th grade mathematics and also Computer Coding classes. Her teaching journey eventually brought her back to her own alma mater, Conway High School. During these years Ms. Hazel began to hone the art of teaching, focusing on studying the various learning styles of her students so that she could individualize instruction for those in her classroom. During the ‘90s, Marlene took a break from teaching to spend time at home with her young children.  In 2003, she returned to Conway High School East, which later became Conway Junior High, and has been influencing teenage learners in her classroom since.  

During her 20+ years at Conway Junior High, she has served terms as Mathematics Department Chair and Math Focus Teacher, which allowed her to influence other math educators with her experience, knowledge, and proven successful strategies. With a passion for teaching mathematics, Ms. Hazel is known for having high standards in her classroom, helping her students strive for excellence in learning, and encouraging perseverance in their efforts. Her consistently high state test scores year after year give evidence to her proven success in the classroom. Students in her classes know that she will meet them where they are in their learning, and teach them whatever necessary background skills they lack to be successful in their current learning standards. She equips her students with creative and critical thinking skills, encouraging them to find their own way to a problem’s solution. Early in her career, she was delighted to be asked to teach the Advanced Geometry classes, which was her favorite high school math subject, and that led her to earn her Gifted and Talented certification to further enrich the learning environment for her students.  Knowing most of those advanced students would be college-bound, she regularly implemented testing skills and strategies into her curriculum to equip students to improve their ACT and SAT scores.  Those efforts have helped untold numbers of students receive hundreds of thousands of dollars in scholarship money over the years, and many of her students have received the prestigious distinction of National Merit Finalist. 

In a career that has spanned 5 decades, Ms. Hazel has taught all secondary grade levels 7th- 12th, and all academic levels from remedial courses to advanced level courses.  In a file folder labeled “My Happy File”, one of many cards Marlene has saved from former students reads “I’ve never been good at math.  I just couldn’t do it until you showed me that I AM smart enough to learn math.  You teach in a way that makes sense to me.  Thank you for not giving up on me.” Those sentiments, and many others that are similar, give special meaning to her life’s work and is the true measure of her personal success as an educator to the thousands of students whose lives have been touched by hers, and vice versa.  

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference 
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Celebrates: Toralya Davis

From the Delta region of Arkansas, in the small town of Marianna AR, Toralya “Toya” Davis was born and raised and it is there where she learned the true value of perseverance, leadership, hard work, community and family.

Toya is married to her high school sweetheart, JD Davis Jr. and has 3 beautiful daughters: DyJuana-23, Camille-20, and Jayla-15 and the caregiver for her mother, Delois Smith. For the last 12 years, Toya has been a Regional Insurance Advisor at ArCare where she supervises a team of outstanding women and covers the entire west side of AR. With this position, Toya has helped hundreds of Arkansans with navigating the waters of insurance (Medicaid, Marketplace, Medicare, Life, Vision/Dental) and provides help to her community through various programs and events. She also serves as an ambassador on the Conway City Chamber of Commerce and aids in the enhancement of our beautiful city and CAYLI (Conway Area Youth Leadership Institute). Staff, parents, and students here at CJHS may recognize her as our PAWS President as she helps bridge parental involvement onto our campus. She has been working with Conway Public Schools PTO since her first bornghters started school at Florence Mattison Elementary. Toya believes strongly that parent involvement helps students to thrive and do better in school all while also helping the teacher. She and her husband are big advocates for parents being and getting involved in the education of their children. Her husband volunteers with MENTOR, Men Taking Our Responsibility, a new program within the Conway School District, that focuses on and allows men from our community to be there for the students before school, during lunch and after school.

In her spare time, Toya attends school (University of AR @ Grantham) and is pursuing her degree in Healthcare Administration. She loves to spend time with her family and friends, cooking and baking. In 2022, she started her home bakery business, Blessed Hands. Blessed Hands is designed to bring joy through baked goods to each family’s table. She specializes in all types of cakes, cookies, pies, cinnamon rolls, but her most popular and requested item is her white chocolate banana pudding. She started making this with her daughter, Camille when she was in the 2nd grade, in her teacher’s classroom no less as a project. Over the years, she added, tweaked, took away and finally got the recipe just to her liking and it is AMAZING!

Toya and her family attend True Holiness Saints Center here in Conway under the leadership of Pastor E.C. Maltbia where she serves on the Greeter’s ministry, Hospitality ministry, and the Women’s Life Group.

Her greatest fulfillment is her family, and her relationship with Christ and showing his love to others.

CJHS Celebrates: Penny Chen (陈老师)

Penny Chen's journey began in a remote village in Pingxiang, China. Despite the lack of formal education, her parents instilled in her the profound value of learning. Their unwavering dedication to their craft in the firecracker and fireworks business set the stage for Penny's pursuit of higher education and her eventual journey to the United States in 2005.

In the face of limited resources, Penny's parents made significant sacrifices to support her education, emphasizing the importance of dedication and knowledge. In her junior year at Changsha University of Science and Technology in China, Penny seized an opportunity for a study abroad program, transferring to Harding University in the United States at age 20. This marked the beginning of her challenging journey in a foreign land, armed with limited English skills and devoid of familial connections.

Undeterred by obstacles, Penny graduated from Harding University with a Bachelor's degree in English in 2007. Her passion for teaching ignited during a transformative year as a long-term substitute at Hall High School, where she taught Chinese and English. This experience propelled her to pursue a Master's in Secondary Education at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock.

Despite a demanding academic load, Penny excelled, maintaining a perfect 4.0 GPA and becoming a three-year recipient of the Harambee Award for minority students who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement. During her graduate study, Penny simultaneously worked as a graduate assistant in the Graduate Admissions Office and the Office of International Services at UALR, contributing to recruiting international students from various countries. Her dedication and achievements culminated in her graduation in May 2011.

Post-graduation, Penny contributed significantly to the growth of the Chinese program at eStem High Public Charter School for five years, earning two nominations for Teacher of the Year. Under her guidance, Chinese student enrollment rose significantly, reaching the highest in Arkansas. Some of her students even attended summer camps in China, and others pursued Chinese majors after high school.

In 2011, Penny's life took another significant turn when she met her husband, Jacob Curran, on a blind date. They wed in 2013, and today, their children, Leila and Liam, attend Carolyn Lewis Elementary School. Penny's commitment to education and cultural understanding continued when she joined Conway Public Schools in 2016.

In 2016, the Chinese program at Conway Public Schools had 28 students enrolled in Chinese 1 and 2. Currently, Penny is teaching five different levels of Chinese, from level 1 to AP. Penny serves as the teacher sponsor for the Asian Club, showcasing her belief in the power of cross-cultural understanding and positive relationships among students from diverse backgrounds. Her daily efforts reflect her dedication to making the Conway community a more inclusive and welcoming place for individuals of different cultural backgrounds and ethnicities, ensuring that her impact extends beyond the classroom.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#ContinuingTheLegacy

Fun fact: Mrs. White earned a seminary degree in Old Testament Studies from Denver Seminary. While she would tell you now that she is very rusty, she can read a few dead languages, including Biblical Hebrew, Greek, and Akkadian.  

In addition to her academic accomplishments, she serves as Music Director at First Presbyterian of Conway, directs a women’s community choir, and sings in a rock duo with a fellow teacher. Jaylin Ealy was born and raised in Conway, AR. She attended Conway Public Schools from kindergarten through 12th grade where she graduated from Conway High School in 2012. She obtained her bachelor’s degree in Biology, a masters degree in Advanced Studies in Teacher Leadership and a second masters degree in Library Media and Information Technology all from the University of Central Arkansas. She is currently working toward her Education Specialist degree in reading and will graduate from Arkansas State University in May.

Jaylin has enjoyed 6 years in education. After graduating college she got her first teaching opportunity, teaching 9th grade physical science, at Wynne High School in Wynne, AR. She then taught 8th grade science at Horace Mann Magnet Middle School in Little Rock, AR. She now teaches 8th grade science at Conway Junior High School where she has been teaching since 2020.

She got into education because she believes that educators get the opportunity to make an impact in their students’ lives and that impact can be lifelong. She continually strives to make a positive impact in the lives of her students. She sets high expectations for her students in the classroom and supports them in meeting those expectations. Her goal is to see her students be successful. Her students would describe her as no nonsense but also funny and caring. She is a resource to her coworkers, always lending a helping hand when needed and ready to take on any task that is assigned to her.

Jaylin has been actively involved in many different aspects within her school and community. She volunteers her time tutoring young readers and she currently helps with the children’s choir ministry at her church. CJHS Highlights: Marcia Pierce

Marcia Pierce was born and raised in Conway, AR. Throughout her childhood, she received her education in the Conway Public School system and graduated in 1985.  Marcia proudest moments in life have been becoming the mother of two amazing children and being a grandmother to five granddaughters who affectionately call her Mimi. Marcia attended Petit Jean College where she received a Certificate in Childcare. She then attended the University of Central Arkansas majoring in Family Consumer Science. Marcia later moved to San Antonio, TX where she obtained a Child Development Associate Certificate. After living in San Antonio for a few years, she moved back Conway and secured a position in the Conway Public School district, her alma mater.

Marcia has affectionately worked with children for more than twenty-three years. During this time, she has had the opportunity and pleasure to work with children of all ages, infants to junior high. Marcia spent eight years working in early childcare and has spent fifteen years working in the Conway Public School District. One of her favorite jobs over the years was working with teen mothers. She enjoyed helping teach them parenting skills and preparing them with life-skills and resources for college and first-time jobs. Marcia spends her days committed to student success by assisting certified staff in devising special education strategies to reinforce learning materials and skills development. Her favorite thing about teaching is knowing that she has helped students develop skills that they will use for the rest of their lives.

Marcia loves reading, being with her family and friends. She enjoys spending her free time traveling and experiencing new, exciting places. Her favorite places to travel so far have been New York City, New York and Washington, DC. Her most memorable traveling experience was being able to visit the 911 memorial and the African American History Museum. Marcia’s favorite thing about Conway Public Schools is working with her students. It’s very rewarding for her to educate students with intellectual abilities and to watch their daily progress from the beginning to the end of the school year.

CJHS Celebrates: Lisa Worlow

Lisa Worlow is a dedicated educator and coach with over two decades of experience in various roles at Conway Public Schools. Graduating from the University of Central Arkansas with a Bachelor of Science in Education in Health Education and Kinesiology, Lisa's journey in education has been marked by a passion for teaching and guiding students towards healthier lifestyles. She furthered her education by earning a Master of Science in Education Curriculum from Arkansas State University, enhancing her expertise in educational leadership and curriculum development.

Throughout her 22 years at Conway Public Schools, Lisa has held multiple teaching and coaching positions. She has taught a range of subjects, including 7th-grade social studies, 7th-9th grade Health and Physical Education, and Credit Recovery. Notably, during her tenure at Conway Junior High School, Lisa piloted the first digital health class in the state, showcasing her innovative approach to education.

Lisa's dedication to enhancing health education is evident through her involvement in curriculum development and program improvement. She has witnessed significant changes in the curriculum over the years and takes pride in educating students about the impact of their daily choices on their well-being.

In recognition of her outstanding contributions, Lisa was named "Teacher of the Year" for Conway Junior High in the 2019/2020 academic year. Additionally, she has served as the Department Chair for health and physical education at the junior high for the past eleven years, demonstrating her leadership and commitment to academic excellence.

Beyond the classroom, Lisa has coached various sports, including volleyball, basketball, track, and cross country, enriching the lives of students through athletic participation.

Lisa's dedication to her field extends beyond the confines of her school. She was selected to be part of the committee responsible for evaluating and rewriting the standards for health education in the state of Arkansas in 2019, reflecting her expertise and influence in the educational community.

Outside of her professional endeavors, Lisa finds joy in spending time with her family. She is the wife of Dustin Worlow and the proud mother of Sydney, a 7th-grade teacher in Greenbrier, and Jackson, a junior at Conway High School. Lisa's hobbies include watching sports, fishing, hunting, hiking, and enjoying the outdoors, reflecting her active and adventurous spirit.

Lisa Worlow embodies the qualities of an exemplary educator and coach, enriching the lives of students and contributing to the advancement of health education in Arkansas.

text:
CJHS Celebrates: Leona Walton

Ms. Walton was born March 31, 1956 in Conway, AR – into the Pine Street Community. She attended Pine Street Schools through the 6th grade and then went on to join her classmates at Conway Jr High in the 7th grade.

She graduated from Conway High school in 1974 as an A,B student. 
While attending Conway High School, she was part of the American Black Culture Club serving as Treasurer in the first year the club was established. This club was established at Conway High School the first semester of ’72-’73. The purposes of the club was to establish and maintain an understanding relationship between black and white students through the study and revelation of black culture and to foster black pride through the study of blacks and their contributions to society.  As a sophmore, she was part of the Home Making class.

 In 1973, she served on the Black - White Human relations Council and continued to participate in the American Black Culture Club. She was also a part of the Pepper’s Club and helped to promote school spirit. 

In 1974  Ms. Walton also served on Student Congress. While on Student Congress, she also served on The Program Committee. She served as President of the American Black Culture Club. In addition, she represented (along with 5 other students from Conway High) Conway’s Jr. Miss held on the campus of the University of Central Arkansas - winning the Citizenship Award.  She had no plans of attending college after graduating high school. At the age of 59 in 2015, she graduated from Central Baptist College Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology. She states, "If you want to get your degree, it is never too late!!"

Ms. Walton states, "I was always civic minded, from the play ground as a kid to the passion I have for treating people fairly in whatever state they are in."  Before the Congress passed  the Affordable Care Act National Health Insurance in 2010 (Obama Care), she served as part of the team that started the Pine Street Free Clinic (2004). That Clinic served persons with no insurance and provided any medication prescribed by the Clinic Physician free of charge. Thank you Mrs. Mary Beard!

A few of her accomplishments from the past few years include:
-Assisted the City of Conway with the Martin Luther King Park – completed 2022
-Current Board President for Pine Street CommUnity Museum
-Current Board Member for  Robinson Cemetery
-Inducted into the Conway Public Schools Foundation Hall of Honor Distinguished Alumna 2023
-Co-founder of the Pine Street Back Pack Program – operating for 17 years

She says she enjoys substitute teaching in the Conway School District, spending time with her Church Family (Greater Pleasant Branch Baptist Church in Conway) where she serves as Church Secretary and helping out where she can.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#ContinuingTheLegacy

CJHS Celebrates: Teresa Lever

Mrs. Lever grew up in Russellville and graduated from Russellville High School. She attended the University of Arkansas, but her father’s cancer diagnosis and untimely passing caused her to return home to Russellville to be with her family. She went on to graduate from Arkansas Tech University in Russellville with a degree in Economics and Finance.

After graduating, Mrs. Lever pursued a career in Banking as a Credit Analyst in Commercial Lending. She met and married her husband, David, and they have been married for 31 years. She has 2 sons; Jake, who lives and works in Rogers, AR and Seth, who is a Senior at Conway High School. She believes being a mom is her highest calling in life and felt it was important to take time off from her career to support her family from home. Mrs. Lever worked in childcare settings and taught preschool while her kids were young. During this time, her family relocated several times, eventually moving to Fort Smith, which was home for 17 years.

Mrs. Lever worked as a substitute teacher in the Fort Smith Public Schools for 5 years. She then sought to combine her background in business with her love for working with students and teachers. She was given the opportunity to work in the office at Chaffin Junior High in Fort Smith, where she filled many roles including Media Clerk, Attendance, Bookkeeper and Registrar. Mrs. Lever relocated to Conway
almost 3 years ago following a career opportunity for her husband. She joined the CJHS staff in 2021 and has become an integral part of our office team.

Mrs. Lever’s favorite things involve spending time with her family…traveling, attending sporting events, concerts and being at home, grilling and hanging out by the pool.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference

CJHS Celebrates: Marquis Rogers

Marquis Rogers was born and raised in the vibrant community of Conway, Arkansas. He embarked on his educational journey at Conway High School, where he graduated with honors in 2012, laying the foundation for his future endeavors.

Driven by both academic and athletic pursuits, Marquis continued his education at the University of Arkansas at Monticello (UAM), where he showcased his talents on the football field as a student-athlete. Over the course of four years, he not only excelled in sports but also dedicated himself to his studies, earning a Bachelor's degree from UAM in 2015.

Undeterred by challenges, Marquis pursued further academic excellence, obtaining a Master's degree from UAM in 2017. His thirst for knowledge and commitment to education led him to delve deeper into his field, culminating in the completion of an Education Specialist (Ed.S.) program at Arkansas State University.

Marquis's passion for education extended beyond his own learning as he embarked on a fulfilling career as an English Language Arts (ELA) teacher. For five years, he imparted knowledge and inspired young minds at Lakeside High in Lake Village, Jacksonville High School, and back to his alma mater, Conway High School. Not one to shy away from new experiences, Marquis spent a year teaching Physical Education at Ruth Doyle Middle School, broadening his expertise and impact.

Eager to assume greater responsibilities in shaping educational environments, Marquis transitioned into a leadership role. Over the last three years, he has served as an Assistant Principal at Conway Junior High School, where he continues to make significant contributions to the educational landscape of his community.

Outside of his professional pursuits, Marquis finds joy in the simple pleasures of life. He resides in Conway, Arkansas, with his beloved wife of eight years, April, and their two children, Daniel and Aria Kaye. Together, they relish the adventures of travel, the excitement of live concerts, and the cherished moments spent creating lasting memories as a family. Ben Broyles was born in Pine Bluff, Arkansas to the late Lula Pearl and Bennie Broyles Sr. Despite facing the challenges of being the oldest son of six children and growing up in one of the toughest cities in Arkansas, Ben was successful in graduating from Watson Chapel High School in 1990.

Ben would later attend the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff, which he considers his beloved Alma Mater because of his extraordinary experiences of meeting Paris, his beautiful wife of twenty-six years, and becoming a member of the Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated in 1995. Even though Ben earned his Bachelor’s degree in Biology, his love for education was forged during his time as a long-term sub at the Accelerated Learning Center. After earning his certification to teach Science and Math, he would teach at the ACC for seven years, receiving the honor of Teacher of the Year in 2004.

Wishing to continue his education, Ben attended the University of Arkansas at Little Rock and obtained his Master of Education in Educational Administration in 2003. Ben would later move with his lovely wife and three wonderful children, Deja, Charity, and Benjamin, to Conway, Arkansas after landing the job as the Assistant Principal of Conway Jr High School in 2007. However, his incessant thirst for knowledge would guide him to the University of Central Arkansas to earn his Educational Specialist in Educational Leadership in 2018.

When he is not at work, Ben enjoys reading and studying the bible, playing the drums, and listening to all types of music. He enjoys watching and attending various sporting events.

Through his seventeen years in the Conway Public School System, Ben has always done his best to enforce the importance of fairness and consistency in the lives of the students he guides. Understanding the experiences of his hometown has only made him more determined to be an inspiring role model for children, teaching them the value of an education and their responsibility for their life’s successes. 

#ContinuingTheLegacy

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
CJHS Celebrates: Damitra Crow- Assistant Principal 

Mrs. Crow's journey is one of dedication, growth, and community involvement. Born and raised in Heber Springs School District, she developed a strong foundation for her educational pursuits from Kindergarten through graduation. Her passion for education led her to Arkansas Tech University, where she earned a Bachelor's degree in Elementary Education.

During her summers, Mrs. Crow embraced opportunities beyond traditional education by serving as a camp counselor at a Christian Sports Adventure camp, enriching the lives of young campers with experiences outside the classroom.

Following graduation, Mrs. Crow and her husband embarked on a unique adventure as Assistant Directors at Camp Bear Track. However, their journey eventually led them to settle in Conway, Arkansas, where her husband pursued ministry, and she dedicated herself to nurturing their growing family. Not only did she prioritize her own family, but she also opened her home to the children of teachers, firefighters, and police officers, showcasing her commitment to supporting her community.

Driven by her strong calling to the classroom, Mrs. Crow eagerly seized an opportunity to teach Kindergarten at Anne Watson Elementary. Over the years, she transitioned roles, teaching various grade levels from Kindergarten to fourth-grade literacy, before eventually transitioning into the role of a school counselor. Alongside her teaching career, she pursued higher education, earning a Master's in School Counseling from UALR.

Seeking new challenges and opportunities for personal and professional growth, Mrs. Crow transitioned to Bigelow High School, where she served as a school counselor while also coaching cross country and track. Her journey continued at Conway Junior High School, where she embraced the role of a school counselor and pursued an Educational Leadership Degree in Administration from ASU.

Mrs. Crow's dedication and leadership did not go unnoticed, as she eventually took on the role of Assistant Principal at Conway Junior High School. Throughout her career, she has cherished the moments shared with both staff and students, finding fulfillment in the impact she has made within the educational community.

Outside of work, Mrs. Crow finds joy in spending quality time with her family, engaging in sports, exploring the outdoors, and fostering meaningful connections within her church community. Her commitment to both her personal interests and her community exemplifies her well-rounded nature and dedication to making a positive impact wherever she goes. As she looks forward to new adventures in the upcoming school year, Mrs. Crow reflects with gratitude on the friendships made and the growth experienced along her remarkable journey.

#ContinuingTheLegacy

author: Conway Junior High School
text: We are thrilled to introduce Ms. Rebekah Dixon as a new Assistant Principal at Conway Junior High School. Born and raised in White Hall, Arkansas, Ms. Dixon brings a decade of educational experience to our school, having spent the last two years with us as a secondary instructional facilitator. Outside of her professional life, she enjoys quality time with her family, her three fur babies, and is even learning how to fly a plane. Ms. Dixon is enthusiastic about her new role at CJHS and looks forward to contributing to our school community with passion and dedication. #LevelingUp #UnlockingOurFullPotential

author: Conway Junior High School
text: We are excited to announce Mrs. Dozler's transition to the role of Assistant Principal at Conway Junior High School. Mrs. Dozler, who holds a Master's  degree in Education Leadership, has been a vital part of our school community since 2018, serving as a Dean of students for the past 2 years. With 13 years of experience as a 7-12 Science teacher, she brings a wealth of knowledge and dedication to her new position. Growing up in a military family, Mrs. Dozler has called many placed home and continues to cherish creating new memories with her husband, four children, and loved ones. We look forward to her continued contributions and leadership at CJHS. #LevelingUp #UnlockingOurFullPotential

author: Conway Junior High School
text: We are excited to announce that Mrs. Holly Schroeder will be joining the admin team as a Dean of Students at Conway Junior High School. With 11 years of experience teaching Family and Consumer Sciences at CJHS, Mrs. Schroeder has been a cornerstone of our school community. Her dedication was recognized when she was named Teacher of the Year for the 2024-2025 school year. A Conway native, Mrs. Schroeder deeply values her role in shaping the lives of local students and is thrilled to embrace this new position, where she will continue to support and inspire our students in a new capacity. With three children of her own, Mrs. Schroeder understands the importance of a nurturing school environment and is committed to making Conway Junior High School a supportive and enriching place for all. #LevelingUp #UnlockingOurFullPotential

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
We are thrilled to announce that Mr. Jasper Johnson will be joining us as a new Assistant Principal! With a decade of experience as a teacher at Courtway Middle School, and previous roles as Dean at Conway Junior High and Assistant Principal at Florence Mattson, Mr. Johnson brings a wealth of knowledge and a passion for education to our school community. 

His dedication to student success and his extensive background in educational leadership make him a perfect fit for our team. We look forward to the positive impact he will undoubtedly make at Conway Junior High!  #LevelingUp #UnlockingOurFullPotential

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
Over the past couple of days, our admin team has been busy making sure we're all set for a safe and successful school year! 

We participated in a district-wide drill to ensure our safety protocols are in place. Safety is our top priority, and this drill helps us stay prepared and vigilant.

In addition, we had the pleasure of helping out with the Pine Street Backpack Program! We spent time stuffing backpacks with essential supplies to support our community and ensure that every student has the tools they need to succeed.

A huge thank you to everyone who contributed and supported these initiatives. Together, we're making a difference for our students and our community! #LevelingUp #UnlockingOurFullPotential

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
In Mrs. Chen's Chinese classes at CJHS, students had the opportunity to celebrate the Moon Festival 🌕, the second most important festival in China and several other Asian countries. As part of the celebration, students learned about the history and customs of the festival 📜 and enjoyed a hands-on experience making snow skin mooncakes 🍰. They also got to sample traditional baked mooncakes 🥮, immersing themselves in the tastes and mythologies behind this special occasion. The activity brought Chinese culture to life in a fun and interactive way! 🎉

Huge thanks to Velda Lueders Realtor Coldwell Banker RPM Group - Conway AR for sponsoring the enrichment activities of the Chinese program at CJHS!!!

#StudentsFirst #DiversityAndInclusion #CJHSStudents #GetInvolved

author: Casey Buck
text:
The Conway Public Schools Orchestra program presents its annual "La Fiesta Orquesta" Taco Supper on Thursday, November 21 on the campus of Conway High School from 5:00-9:00 pm. This southwestern-themed event features the nearly 300 students of the orchestra program in free concerts throughout the night. All performances take place in the James H. Clark Auditorium, with city-wide Intermediate Orchestra performing first at 5:30, the Conway High School Orchestra performing at 6:15, city-wide beginning orchestra students at 7:30, and the Conway Junior High School 8th and 9th grade orchestras at 8:15. 

The event also serves as the orchestra program's primary fundraiser, with money raised through dinner ticket sales, donations, and a silent auction. Dinner service is held from 5-8 pm in the Conway High School cafeteria, and the meals include drinks and dessert as well. Meal tickets for the taco salad dinner (or soft taco child's plate) are on sale online at conwayorch.square.site or at the door the night of the event for $15/adults and $10/children. Dinner is available for dine-in or for carryout. The silent auction, with many items donated by local businesses, will take place from 5:30-8:15 p.m. in the lobby of the James H. Clark Auditorium. 

We hope you’ll support these amazing students and come hear us play!!

author: Casey Buck
text: We were so thrilled to host cellist Andrei Ionițsă at Conway Junior High and Conway High School on Thursday. He’s the guest soloist with the Arkansas Symphony Orchestra this weekend, and we were able to have him come visit with our orchestra students here in Conway. He performed some great music for us and spoke to our classes on what it’s like to play music and travel the world, consistency in practice, and managing performance anxiety. Our orchestra program is fulfilling our district’s core values of cultivating community relationships and providing innovative educational opportunities!

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
CJHS will be celebrating Black History Month by highlighting local community members. We will start off with Mr. Tim Ester!

Tim Ester was born and raised in Menifee, Arkansas. He is a graduate of Morrilton High
School. He attended the University of Central Arkansas in Conway, but while in college
Tim worked a full time job that eventually became a high priority in his life. From that
point forward Tim found his profession in the restaurant business and he is best known
as the General Manager of Stoby’s Restaurant where he served for 26 years before
retiring at the early age of 49.

Tim is also well known for his service to the community that all began with his work on
the United Way Board of Directors. Through Stoby’s Restaurant, Tim was also
instrumental in supporting many, many causes throughout the city of Conway in the
pancake breakfast fundraiser. In 2008 Tim co-founded the Pine Street Backpack
Program, a non-profit that supports education by providing school supplies to students
in need in grades K-12 that live in Faulkner County. Over the past 16 years the Pine
Street Backpack Program has raised nearly $370,000 and served more than 14,000
students.

In 2019 Tim had a vision to open a food truck. After considerable thought and a great
deal of research, he started the process by first special ordering his dream kitchen that
would be manufactured in the state of Georgia.

When COVID hit and businesses were shut down, plans to open this small business
was stalled. What appeared to be the worst time to open a business, while others were
closing as a result of the pandemic, was actually the opportune time. As people could
no longer dine inside of restaurants, they looked for environments that accommodated
outdoor seating and curbside pickup.

In June of 2020 Uncle Tim’s Food Truck was established; and today it is a staple in the
community. Located at the corner of Highway 286 East and Skunk Hollow Road, on a
historic site owned by his wife’s family, and formerly Highway 286 East Grocery and
Gas.

Tim and his wife, Gena Ester, have been married 36 years. The two work hand in hand
in their family’s business operations of running a food truck and catering company as
well as managing a number of rental properties. They have two children, Kiera Oluokun
(Seyi) and Jordan Ester (Kirstan). The Esters are also proud grandparents of two
handsome boys, Ezekiel (7) and Isaac (3).

#CJHSCelebratesBlackExcellence

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
Conway Junior High Celebrates: Torrie Achan

Torrie C. Achan was born in Little Rock, Arkansas. She is the oldest child of Agnes Stewart-Hill and the late Elihu Stewart Jr. She has three siblings. She graduated from J.A. Fair High School in 1996. She attended Henderson State University and received a Bachelor of Science in Education with an Emphasis in Early Childhood in 2000. While at Henderson, she was initiated into the Theta Eta Chapter of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated in Fall 1998. Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated is the oldest Greek-letter organization founded by African- American college-educated women. Also, while at Henderson, she met and married her college sweetheart, Joey Achan. In December 2002, she received a Master of Science in Education from the University of Central Arkansas.

Torrie started her teaching career in Conway Public Schools in 2000. She taught at Theodore Jones Elementary from 2000-2010. While at Theodore Jones Elementary, she taught fourth and first grades. In 2010, she received a position at Woodrow Cummins Elementary School where she is currently serving as a teacher. From 2010-2023, she served as a third grade teacher. Currently, she is teaching fourth grade math and science. In May 2025, she will complete her 25th year as a classroom teacher. Torrie feels blessed beyond measure because she has worked with so many wonderful administrators, teachers, support staff, parents, and students during her career. Each day when she enters her classroom, her goal is to be the teacher that I would want for my personal children to encounter each day..

Conway Junior High School Highlights: Aaron Glass

Aaron Glass grew up in the small rural town of Elaine, Arkansas where he also graduated from Elaine High School. Upon graduation, he moved on to attend the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff where he majored in Biology, played a little bit of football, and pledged the greatest fraternity known to man in Omega Psi Phi. 

He then returned to UAPB to complete his Masters of Education in Life Sciences Education which began his foray into the world of education. He states he is the son of an educator and administrator so it was only a matter of time before he got into the field for himself. 

After obtaining his masters, Mr. Glass was hired here at Conway High High School as a biology teacher where he remained for 10 years. During that time as a teacher, he became interested in moving into administration which led him to return to school to obtain his Educational Specialist and Building Level Administration certification from Arkansas State University.  Mr. Glass was then able to transition into administration as an Assistant Principal at Carl Stuart Middle School where he is currently employed. 

He explains, "Life as an administrator or an educator at all for that matter is challenging, but oh so rewarding! I get to wake up every day and do what I love, which is work with kids and try to help them be the absolute best versions of themselves daily!"

text:
Conway Junior High Highlights: Ben Broyles

Ben Broyles was born in Pine Bluff, Arkansas to the late Lula Pearl and Bennie Broyles Sr. Despite facing the challenges of being the oldest son of six children and growing up in one of the toughest cities in Arkansas, Ben was successful in graduating from Watson Chapel High School in 1990.

Ben would later attend the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff, which he considers his beloved Alma Mater because of his extraordinary experiences of meeting Paris, his beautiful wife of twenty-six years, and becoming a member of the Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated in 1995. Even though Ben earned his Bachelor’s degree in Biology, his love for education was forged during his time as a long-term sub at the Accelerated Learning Center. After earning his certification to teach Science and Math, he would teach at the ACC for seven years, receiving the honor of Teacher of the Year in 2004.

Wishing to continue his education, Ben attended the University of Arkansas at Little Rock and obtained his Master of Education in Educational Administration in 2003. Ben would later move with his lovely wife and three wonderful children, Deja, Charity, and Benjamin, to Conway, Arkansas after landing the job as the Assistant Principal of Conway Jr High School in 2007. However, his incessant thirst for knowledge would guide him to the University of Central Arkansas to earn his Educational Specialist in Educational Leadership in 2018.

When he is not at work, Ben enjoys reading and studying the bible, playing the drums, and listening to all types of music. He enjoys watching and attending various sporting events.

Through his eighteen years in the Conway Public School System, Ben has always done his best to enforce the importance of fairness and consistency in the lives of the students he guides. Understanding the experiences of his hometown has only made him more determined to be an inspiring role model for children, teaching them the value of an education and their responsibility for their life’s successes.

author: Conway Junior High School
text:
🎉 Lunar New Year Celebration at the Faulkner County Library 🎉

Recently, four Conway Junior High School Asian Club members — August Cardin, Sophia Lin, Lyla Moore, and Addison Nelson— volunteered at the first-ever Lunar New Year Celebration at the Faulkner County Library. This event was made possible through the collaboration of the Conway High School Asian Club, the Faulkner County Library, local Chinese community members, and the UCA Center for Chinese Language and Culture.

Approximately 400 attendees participated in the event, enjoying various interactive stations such as dumpling-making, calligraphy, crafts, games, wishing trees, traditional dress-ups, and more. It was a wonderful opportunity for the community to come together, learn about Chinese culture, and celebrate the Year of the Snake.

Events like this reflect the vibrant cultural diversity in our community and the growing interest in Chinese culture and language. If you’re interested in learning more, consider joining our Chinese program or the Asian Club! 🌏❤️

#LunarNewYear #ChineseCulture #CommunityCelebration #YearOfTheSnake #Diversity

text:
Conway Junior High School Highlights : Sonya Strickland

Sonya Strickland was born and raised in Arkansas and is a graduate of both Conway High School and the University of Central Arkansas. Early in life Sonya was gifted with a spirit of care for others and this was most humbly the spirit that she gained from her parents by far and her late Papason (daddy) specifically. Sonya was raised to be strong yet approachable, firm yet fair, hard worker with the desire to achieve yet able to slow down and help those in need. 

Sonya began working as a Special Education teacher in 1996 for Pulaski County Special School district and soon returned home to Conway in 1997 as a Special Education teacher for the district. She taught at Bob and Betty Courtway Middle School and enjoyed watching the progress that her students made. She worked with many teachers over the years and gained as much as she gave away. Over the decades of teaching, Sonya has shown herself as an educator, supporter, role model and encourager.  

Sonya was encouraged by many to seek administration and as she did, she found her next passion which was guiding parents and students in a more global way toward success in middle school. She became the Assistant Principal at Ruth Doyle Middle School in 2004. At Ruth Doyle, Sonya worked with parents and students on homework plans, behavioral incentives and community resources needed to help them achieve. In 2015 Sonya was hired as the Assistant Transportation Supervisor. In this role, Sonya has the privilege of working with employees, administrators, parents and students at all levels. 

In her work away from work, Sonya has been involved with various agencies and groups that keep the communities of Arkansas. Over her lifetime, Sonya has been a member of the Habitat for Humanity Organization as well as the United Way. She most loves volunteering for a cause dear to her heart which is The CALL, a Christian Based Adoption Entity. As she gives back to her community, she feels as if she is giving back some of what was given to her like love, compassion, vision and support for her endeavors. Sonya is a proud member of the illustrious Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. and is committed to the work of the sisterhood which is community service.   

Sonya is mother to one son, Darian. But she has gained many other children and family along the way in her educational career. Sonya believes the greatest gift is seeing her students all grown up and especially when they specifically bring their spouses/and or children to her job to meet her. 

#CJHSCelebratesBlackExcellence

Verdell Bunting, Jr. was born in Little Rock, AR. He is the only child of Verdell Bunting, Sr. and Debra Nichols Bunting. He graduated from Catholic High in 1991. He attended Hendrix College and received a Bachelor of Arts in History in 1995. He attended UALR and received both a Bachelor of Science in Education in 1998 and a Master of Education in Educational Administration and Supervision in 2003. He recently received an Educational Specialist degree in Reading from ASU in 2024. He recently was honored with a Compass Award for
being a positive mentor in a teen’s life. He was also included in the 100 Faces of Conway Project.

Verdell began his teaching career in 1998 in the NLRSD at Indian Hills Elementary. There he taught fifth grade (mainly math and science) for twenty years. He received teacher of the year for the 2003-2004 school year. He was also recognized with the “Who’s Who Among America’s Teachers” in 2005. In 2018, Verdell joined the Conway School District as a fourth grade math teacher at Theodore Jones Elementary (TJE). He is currently teaching fourth grade math and phonics at TJE. Verdell loves the students and staff at TJE. He feels very fortunate to work alongside a very supportive group of educators and support staff daily. He states the motto in his classroom is simple – be fair, firm, and consistent. He loves to host student interns in his classroom too always willing to support our future educators.

In his spare time, Verdell enjoys hanging out with family and friends, reading, and watching television from the comfort of his living room recliner. He is also very active in his church, St. Bartholomew. He has a goddaughter Hannah who will graduate from pharmacy school from the University of Tennessee in May, 2025.

text:
Conway Junior High Highlights: Audrey Cooper

Audrey Cooper is a dedicated educator and passionate advocate for families and children, whose career and personal life reflect a deep commitment to service, education, and community. With a strong academic foundation and an unwavering desire to make a positive impact, Audrey has built a career that spans multiple educational fields, earning a variety of honors and accolades along the way.

Audrey graduated from Conway High School in 1997, where she excelled both academically and in extracurricular activities. She attended the University of Central Arkansas where became a member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., in the Spring of 1999. She obtained a Bachelor’s degree in Family and Consumer Science, graduating in 2004. Her studies in family dynamics, consumer issues, and human development fueled her desire to make a difference in the lives of individuals and families.

In 2007, Audrey earned a Master’s degree in Family and Consumer Science from UCA, further enhancing her ability to advocate for and support families. Her journey of learning and growth continued with the completion of a Master’s in Art in Teaching from UCA in 2013. Audrey’s belief in the transformative power of education led her to this path, where she could put theory into practice, especially within the classroom.

Audrey’s dedication to education deepened further when she earned her K-6 Special Education Endorsement in 2023 from the University of Arkansas at Monticello, broadening her capacity to meet the diverse needs of students. She continues to serve as a teacher, ensuring all children, regardless of their challenges, have the opportunity to thrive in the educational environment.

Audrey’s career is marked by numerous achievements and recognitions. In 2014, she was named Teacher of the Year at Sallie Cone Preschool, an honor that reflected her dedication to her students and the impact she had on their lives. She was also named Ellen Smith Teacher of the Month in October 2022 and September 2023, further highlighting her commitment to excellence in the classroom and her positive influence on both students and colleagues. In January 2025, Audrey was recognized as a Conway Public Schools Core Value Champion, an award that reflects her dedication to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment for all students.

Audrey’s commitment to professional growth and development was recognized when she was accepted into the CEAL (Conway Educational Aspiring Leadership) Hub program through Conway Public Schools for the 2024-2025 school year. This prestigious program has allowed her to further refine her leadership skills, empowering her to make an even greater impact in the educational community.

Beyond her work in education, Audrey is deeply committed to her faith and community. She
attends Mt. Gale Baptist Church, where she is actively involved in various ministries. Audrey serves with the choir, the praise team, and in the Youth and Young Adult programs, where she nurtures and mentors the next generation of leaders. Her contributions to the church reflect her desire to serve others and make a positive impact in all areas of her life.

On a personal level, Audrey is married to Marcus Cooper, with whom she has built a loving and supportive family. Together, they have raised three children: Martel, Deisha, and Alexandria, each of whom continues to inspire them with their individual paths. In 2023, Audrey’s joy multiplied with the arrival of her granddaughter, A'Miley. 

As a dedicated educator, community leader, and loving family member, Audrey Cooper’s life is a testament to the power of service, education, and lifelong learning. She continues to inspire those around her, always striving to make a difference in the lives of others.

Conway Junior High Highlights: Boris Scott

Boris Scott, a 1991 graduate from Stuttgart, Arkansas (affectionately known as Sugartown), moved to Conway to pursue higher education. He earned a BFA in Graphic Design from the University of Central Arkansas, where he was also a key player on the UCA Bears football team that claimed the 1991 NAIA National Championship title. The team was later inducted into the UCA Hall of Fame. After college, Boris played semi-professional basketball for two years before settling in Conway.

In 2009, Boris married into a blended family, becoming a father to six children—five daughters and one son, ranging in ages from 24 to 7 years old. In 2015, he took a position with Arch Ford and transitioned into his current role as a behavior interventionist, driven by his passion for helping children.

A lifelong lover of sports, Boris has dedicated much of his energy to youth athletics. He led the Conway Optimist Football team to a Super Bowl victory for four consecutive years, alongside fellow former UCA Bear greats. He later shifted his focus to basketball, coaching boys at the Boys and Girls Club of Conway. In 2012, Boris became certified as a trainer by Nike and Impact Basketball in Las Vegas. His work quickly gained recognition, and he founded the successful Conway Vipers AAU basketball program. He also played a key role in launching Peak Performance Academy in 2017, where he coached teams within the Arkansas Wings and The Woodz organizations.

Over the years, Boris expanded his focus to include girls' basketball, leading girls' teams and emphasizing their participation in the sport. He is currently coaching with the Iso Joe EYBL/EYCL girls' program, continuing his commitment to fostering athletic growth in young players. Conway remains his home, where he has made a lasting impact on both his family and the local sports community.

text:
Conway Junior High Highlights: Rita Pirtle 

Rita Pirtle is a passionate childcare professional and entrepreneur who was raised in Menifee, Arkansas. Rita’s journey began at UCA, where she took general classes but struggled to choose a major. It was her stepfather, Milton Rice, who suggested she pursue childcare, leading her to transfer to UACCM to earn an associate’s degree and management degree specifically in childcare.

Through her classes and hands-on experience with children, Rita quickly discovered her true calling and fell in love with the field. She started her own childcare business in Menifee, supported by her cousin's dad, David Hood, who provided her with a space to rent and helped her navigate the early stages of her journey.

Though Rita faced the heartbreaking loss of her husband, the late Earl Pirtle III, and her son, the late Earl Pirtle IV, her faith and resilience have kept her moving forward. After relocating to Conway, her business flourished, and she was on the brink of turning her in-home childcare into a center when tragedy struck again. However, Rita’s unwavering faith in God has been her strength. She believes that with God guiding her, she has been able to overcome life's obstacles and continues to live by the belief to “Cast all my cares on Him.”

Rita’s story is one of perseverance, love, and faith. Her dedication to children and her community is truly inspiring.

text:
Conway Junior High Highlights: Dr. Corey Oliver

Dr. Corey Oliver’s teaching career began at Bob Courtway (now Bob and Betty Courtway)
Middle School in 1997, the year the school opened. He is now in his 28 th year of teaching there. Dr. Oliver graduated from the University of Central Arkansas with a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in English in 1996. In 2000, he completed his Master of Science in Education (MSE) degree in Secondary School Leadership, also at UCA. In 2021, he earned a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree from UCA’s Department of Leadership Studies. His dissertation is titled “The Role of School Leaders in Addressing Discipline and Developing an Equitable Organizational Culture”.

Dr. Oliver approaches each teaching opportunity with a singular focus: to engage every
member of the class in a productive learning experience, accommodating the students’ diverse interests and learning styles through effective teaching strategies while fulfilling the lesson’s accompanying goals and objectives. Whether it be through the involvement of students in decision making or through individualized learning, he enthusiastically engages students to maximize each student’s learning potential. Someone once said, “Tell me and I forget, teach me and I may remember, involve me and I learn.” Involving students in their learning and believing in each student’s ability to set and achieve goals through rigor, relevance, and relationship, Dr. Oliver has encouraged his students to “Strive for Excellence!”, his class motto since 1997. Throughout his 28 years as a classroom teacher, Dr. Oliver has not only strived to involve his students in the learning process, but he has also engaged in routine reflection to grow from previous practice and strived to fulfill his obligation to make a positive, lasting impact on each student in this rewarding work of heart—teaching!

Dr. Oliver is a Certified Candidate Support Provider for the National Board for Professional
Teaching Standards (NBPTS), a consultant for the Arkansas Department of Education’s Arkansas Professional Pathway to Educator Licensure (APPEL) program, and a former adjunct instructor in UCA’s College of Education.

Passionate about international travel, Dr. Oliver has participated in international training
programs for educators in Russia, China, Japan, and South Africa. In all, he has traveled to 45 countries in his quest to experience other cultures and to increase others’ cultural appreciation.

Dr. Oliver’s greatest inspirations are his parents, Johnnie and Evon Oliver, who passed away 33 days apart in 2022. Their support was constant, and their love was unconditional. 

Dr. Oliver’s career highlights include:
- Conway Public Schools Foundation Teacher of the Week (2024)
- Arvest Bank “We Love Teachers” Award (2022)
- National Board Certified Teacher (2006 & 2015)
- Teacher of the Year, Courtway Middle School (2000 & 2014)
- Wal-Mart and Sam’s Club Teacher of the Year Award (2007)
- Milken Family Foundation National Educator Award (2007)

Conway Junior High Highlights: Denesha Taylor

Born in Southaven, Mississippi, and raised in Earle, Arkansas, Denesha Taylor relocated to Conway, Arkansas, in June 2007 when her father secured a job opportunity in the area. Her educational journey in Conway began at Bob Courtway Middle School for 8th grade, followed by Conway Junior High, which was formerly known as Conway High School East Campus. Denesha graduated with highest honors from Conway High School in 2012 and was actively involved in numerous extracurricular activities, including the band and the National Beta Club.

After high school, Denesha pursued a Bachelor of Business Administration degree, graduating summa cum laude in 2016 and receiving the President's Medallion for academic achievements. During her time at the university, Denesha was the founding president of the College of Business' Beta Gamma Sigma Chapter and was honored as the Outstanding College of Business Student of the Year. Additionally, she tutored and participated in various campus organizations.

Continuing her academic pursuits, Denesha earned a Master of Business Administration degree from the same institution in 2018 and further engaged in campus life by joining the Black Graduate Student Association and the National Society of Leadership and Success.

Currently, Denesha holds the position of Data Analyst Team Lead at Insight Enterprises, Inc., where she oversees the training of over 130 global teammates and implements projects within her department.

In addition to her professional responsibilities, Denesha is committed to community service and volunteer work, participating in initiatives such as back-to-school events, food drives, and charity walks. Notably, she serves as a co-leader for the Hospitality Ministry at New Hope Baptist Church, contributing to community engagement and social responsibility projects.

In her leisure time, Denesha enjoys traveling, attending concerts, spending quality time with friends and family, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle through regular exercise and healthier eating habits. One of her personal goals is to continue checking items off her travel bucket list.

Marlow also serves as an Assistant Pastor at Fellowship of Champions Church, teaching others to walk in love, live by faith, and experience God’s prosperity.

Marlow values family. Married to his childhood sweetheart, April, and a proud father to Aiden, Major, and Ava, he believes that strong families build strong communities and strives daily to lead, teach, and empower others.

text:
For the Month of March we will be celebrating Women who make a difference here at Conway Junior High School or within our school community 

Conway Junior High Celebrates: Sadeidre Lawrence

As a ninth grader from the tiny, no-stoplight town of Danville, Sadeidre Lawrence knew on an FBLA field trip to UCA that she wanted to make Conway her home one day. Since her parents had already instilled her with a formidable work ethic thanks to countless hours spent cleaning carpets, waxing floors, and rebuilding flood and fire damaged homes because of the family’s restoration business, Sadeidre knew she would have to apply that same set of principles to her education in order to turn her dream into a reality. 

In 2010, Sadeidre graduated from Danville High School with honors, her freshman year of college already completed, and a full-ride to UCA as an English major. A short time after beginning classes, Sadeidre realized that she wanted to double-major in Sociology and began that coursework as well. While attending college, Sadeidre held several jobs: a paid internship at the Faulkner County Juvenile Court, a seasonal position at Old Navy, and a part-time job at Lowe’s Home Improvement. 

In 2013, after being named the Katherine Hinson Outstanding Sociology Student, Sadeidre graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in English and Sociology. After graduation, she applied for a full-time job at Lowe’s and, over the course of the next two years, worked her way up to a managerial position in 2015. 

Sadeidre knew after working retail for several years that she was ready for a change, and in 2017, she decided to return  to college and temporarily relocate to Mount Ida. Around that time, she became engaged, and while Sadeidre was attending Henderson State University for her Master of Arts in Teaching, she became an English instructor at Mena High School. In 2018, she and her fiancé returned to Conway to purchase their home, and she began teaching 9th grade at Benton Junior High. In November of 2018, Sadeidre married her husband, Matthew, in Conway, and in early 2019, she was hired by the Conway Junior High to teach 8th grade English. 

In 2020, Sadeidre knew she was not done with her educational career yet. She returned to her aluma mater of UCA to earn her Educational Specialist Degree in building-level administration. While driving a bus full-time, attending graduate classes, and teaching every day, Sadeidre gave birth to her son, Matthew, in March of 2022 then graduated from UCA for a second time in August of 2022. 

Since earning her Ed.S., Sadeidre  continues to help transport students as a substitute bus driver, assist in her school’s leadership team, and serve on the school’s Personnel Policy Committee. She is also a member of the Conway Educational Aspring Leaders (CEAL) cohort, was voted August’s Teacher of the Month, and has been selected as a presenter at the upcoming PD Palooza event this summer. 

Sadeidre treasures her family time, and when she is not at work, you can find her spending quality time with her son and husband, going camping, hunting, fishing, or simply just hanging around the house and reading a good book.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference 
#LevelingUp
#UnlockingOurFullPotential

Conway Junior High Celebrates: Megan West

Señora (Mrs.) Megan West teaches Spanish 1 and 2 and coaches the 8th Grade Dance team at the Junior High. Originally from Conway, she works hard as a dedicated educator with a deep passion for language and leadership. A lifelong Wampus Cat, Mrs. West graduated from Conway High School, where her interest in languages, dance and education first flourished. To pursue her passions further, she attended the University of Central Arkansas, earning a degree in Spanish and ESL Education, along with a Master's in Advanced Studies in Teacher Leadership.

Señora West loves being with her husband, two sons and black lab, Maisy. In addition to her classroom work, Mrs. West actively participates in her church community, engaging in various activities, including singing in the praise band since high school. 

Her appreciation for languages and diverse cultures grew through summer studies abroad in Mexico and Spain—experiences that enhanced her linguistic abilities and deepened her understanding of cultural diversity. For the past 17 years, Coach West has committed herself to teaching, spending four years in North Little Rock before spending the last 13 years at CJHS. She believes that language skills are essential for success in life and shares this philosophy with her students. Inspired by Nelson Mandela’s quote, "If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his own language, that goes to his heart," she applies this sentiment in her teaching approach.

Outside of her professional commitments, Señora West enjoys reading, working out, traveling, and spending quality time with her family and friends. Her teaching methods feature engaging, enjoyable, and innovative activities designed to help each student realize their full potential. Mrs. West strives to instill a love for learning in every child, believing that education, specifically learning world languages, paves the way to greatness.
