Conway Junior High Celebrates: Sarah Holt

Sarah was born in Conway, but her family moved away after she finished kindergarten. Growing up, she lived in 3 states (AR, MS, CA) and attended 7 different schools while her dad worked  jobs in construction. Returning to AR in 5th grade, she is a graduate of Lake Hamilton HS, where she fell in love with music.  

She would go on to study Trumpet Performance at UCA and then get her Master's in Performance at The University of Arizona.  Retuning to AR in 2006, she married her husband James and initially worked as a freelance musician and private lessons instructor in NE Arkansas, teaching at Dixie Band Camp and performing with the Pine Bluff and Delta Symphonies and Delta Brass Quintet.

During this time, Sarah began substitute teaching in several area schools and soon discovered a new passion of working with students in the classroom.  She started the AR Non-Traditional Teacher Liscensure Program and was hired to teach science at Blytheville HS.  After 3 years, Sarah relocated to head the Physics department at Arkadelphia HS for 2 years before coming home to Conway, where she is now in her 9th year, teaching Accelerated Physical Science.

Last year, Sarah received her certification in ESOL and began teaching 8th and 9th grade Science for English Second Language students.

Her passion is in empowering students to discover and understand the world around them.  She loves to challenge her students while supporting them to achieve their best.  There is no greater joy than witnessing students gain confidence and pride in their education!

When not teaching, Sarah can be found kickboxing, hiking, reading, gardening, or riding across the country with her husband on their Can-Am Spyder.

text:
Conway Junior High Celebrates: Jenny Bassett 

Jenny Bassett is a proud Graduate of University of Central Arkansas with Bachelor Degree in Special Education with Honors and a few years later received her Master's Degree as a Reading Specialist with Honors. Jenny first made an impact as an Elementary Special Education teacher for years, where she loved working with younger students and watching them develop as readers and writers. Jenny worked at the Heber Springs School district for three years as an Elementary Special Education Teacher and Guy-Perkins School District for twelve years as an Elementary and High School Special Education Teacher and the Special Education Designee for K-12. Now, as a Junior High School Special Education Teacher in the area of English for the last 8 years, she continues to inspire and support students in their academic journeys. She is grateful to be a part of our CJHS family! 

Jenny is passionate about fostering the ability to read and write in her students. Jenny knew she wanted to be a teacher,since the 3rd Grade, even though she had dyslexia and struggled to read and write in school. By the 3rd grade with the support of a loving teacher, Mrs. Ward, Jenny no longer checked out books to look at the pictures, but to read the words written on each page. The ability to read and write is not a privilege , but a necessity for life! The ability to read is the path that leads to all other learning possibilities. 

Originally from Blue Springs, Missouri , Jenny now calls Vilonia home with her husband , Bob, and their 2 rescue dogs and 8 rescue cats . Each of their furry babies have their own individual story. Beyond just helping an animal in need, Jenny and Bob give a rescue an opportunity to find their voice; to be themselves and get a second chance to become a dog/ cat beyond the walls of shelter or rescue.

Jenny and Bob truly give them the keys to start a new life where second chances can often be hard to come by. Jenny is passionate about all kinds of animals , which led her to being a Zoo Docent (educated volunteer) for several years in the early 90’s at the Little Rock Zoo. Jenny also owned a small farm during her college years, which now her family runs in Greenbrier. Jenny is a proud Aunt of three nephews and two nieces and four great nephews. She is a faithful member of the Liberty Church of the Nazarene and enjoys painting, traveling, and kayaking in her free time. 

“Be of good cheer. Do not think of today's failures, but of the success that may come tomorrow. You have set yourselves a difficult task, but you will succeed if you persevere; and you will find a joy in overcoming obstacles. Remember, no effort that we make to attain something beautiful is ever lost.”  ― Helen Keller

Conway Junior High Celebrates: Sherry Washington

Ms. Sherry Washington is a strong advocate for the opportunity to learn, and she has consistently demonstrated this throughout her career. She started her educational journey as an undergraduate at the University of Central Arkansas, where she earned her bachelor's degree in Family & Consumer Sciences and a licensure in Middle School Science (grades 4-8). Ms. Washington's commitment to Education did not stop there; she furthered her expertise with a Master's in Education from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock while teaching Science at Lisa Academy West Campus. 

Although Ms. Washington is new to Conway, she brings her 12 years of experience in various educational roles. Recognizing her passion for supporting English-language learners, she pursued and obtained a K-12 ESOL endorsement. She takes pride in helping students discover their preferred learning styles while encouraging them to face challenges head-on. Her dedication to personal growth led her to complete the Arkansas Teacher Leadership Academy in 2023. 

In 2017, Ms. Washington confidently embraced the Science Fair Coordinator and Science Olympiad Coach roles, leading her teams to an impressive total of 4 State Championships. In 2018, Ms. Washington led the Science department for Project Lead the Way (PLTW) Gateway Courses, a position she held for five years. This initiative allowed her to enhance student learning through a project-based curriculum that fosters engagement and critical thinking. Over the years, she has served as a department head and enjoyed collaborating with students and colleagues in her educational journey. As she completed her tenure in Little Rock, she successfully served as the ELL Coordinator at the Lisa North Campus, where she gained a broader perspective on Education. 

Ms. Washington's hard work and dedication culminated in becoming Arkansas 2023 Charter School Teacher of the Year. This prestigious award has inspired her to positively impact student learning further. She firmly believes that with collaborative efforts, all students can succeed!

Mrs. Barnett moved to Arkansas in 2007 from San Jose, California where she taught middle school language arts and social studies. She joined CJHS team in 2016 and has taught 9th grade advanced civics and on-level civics ever since. Beyond her teaching duties, she is also the Social Studies Department Chair, Student Leadership Council advisor, and a co-sponsor for Cat Nation Christmas. She has run an after school peer tutoring program for CJHS students for the last two years, and created the Period Product Platoon with female students from the Student Leadership Council who stock all girls restrooms with period products twice a week. This year she also worked with the CJHS basketball program, coordinating and supervising student volunteers working the concession stand.

Mrs. Barnett was named the CJHS Teacher of the Year in 2018, received the Harry Readnour Exemplary History Day Teacher Award for the state of Arkansas in 2019, and was awarded the Conway Public Schools Foundation Teacher of the Week on October 6, 2023.

Mrs. Barnett’s classroom immediately puts students at ease with the soft lighting and flexible seating options. She empowers her students to be the best version of themselves, encouraging them to discuss classroom topics with their peers and families, ask questions, and seek out facts to support their stance on issues.

In her free time she enjoys reading, taking road trips with her family, and hanging out with her two cats, Milo and Winston.

Her favorite quote is, “we do not have the agree on anything to be kind to one another,” reminding everyone that their opinions are valid and kindness matters.

Conway Junior High Celebrates: Coach Cheyenne Kuhn

Coach Kuhn was born and raised in the Mississippi Delta. In the summer of 2008, she and her family moved to Conway, Arkansas because of her dad becoming the new head softball coach at the University of Central Arkansas (UCA). She attended Conway Public Schools from 7th grade through 12th grade, and she was a part of the Conway Softball team during her high school career. 

She went on to play college softball at UCA for 5 years (redshirted her freshman year), where she would play under her dad and older sister. At UCA she majored in Family and Consumer Science in Education. In her 5th year playing softball at UCA, she went on to graduate school and majored in Sports Management. After finishing her softball career and her final year of graduate school, she went on to be a graduate assistant for the softball program at UCA.

In May 2020, one of Coach Kuhn’s career goals came into fruition, and she was able to become a teacher/coach at her former alma mater. She joined Conway Junior High School as a Career Development Teacher/ Jr. High Volleyball Assistant Coach/ Conway High School Assistant Softball Coach. 

Coach Kuhn has been blessed with so many great mentors that have helped her grow to become the teacher/coach she is today. She is not only proud to call herself a 3rd generation teacher in her family, but is also proud to be a softball coach just like her dad and older sister. Her favorite part about teaching/coaching is being able to create relationships with her students, players, and coworkers. Coach Kuhn’s overall goal as an educator is to be a light to her students.  

One of her favorite quotes is one that she learned from her dad that she heard many times while playing softball at UCA.
 “Gentlemen (Ladies), we will chase perfection, and we will chase it relentlessly, knowing all the while we can never attain it. But along the way, we shall catch excellence.”

author: Holly Schroeder
text:
Conway Junior High Celebrates: Nakeia Guiden

Born and raised in the small town of Twin Groves, just outside Damascus, Nakeia Guiden's journey has been shaped by her passion for sports, education, and community. After graduating from Guy-Perkins High School in 2008, where she was recognized as an Honor Graduate. Nakeia went on to further her education at the University of Central Arkansas. There, she earned both her Bachelors and Masters degrees, solidifying her commitment to academic excellence and personal growth.

A standout athlete, Nakeia made history at UCA as the 21st Sugar Bear to score over 1,000 points during her four years with the team (2008-2012). Her dedication on and off the court helped her leave a lasting legacy, inspiring future generations of athletes.

In 2021, Nakeia embraced motherhood, welcoming her daughter, Annalaya, into the world. Her role as a mother has further fueled her passion for coaching and mentoring, as she strives to pass on the lessons she's learned through sports and life.

When she's not busy with family or work, Nakeia enjoys playing and coaching basketball, traveling when the opportunity arises, and attending live sports events. These hobbies reflect her deep love for both the game and the joy of connecting with others through shared experiences.

Looking toward the future, one of Nakeia's primary goals is to own her own business, continuing her path of growth and achievement while making a positive impact on her community and beyond.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#UnlockingOurFullPotential
#LevelingUp

author: Holly Schroeder
text:
Conway Junior High Celebrates: Lori Williams

Lori Williams launched her career in 2001 as a freelance fashion stylist for Dillard’s Corporate, where her sharp eye for detail and deep passion for fashion flourished and evolved.  After years of thriving in her work in the fashion industry, Mrs. Williams felt a deep calling for more personal fulfillment and decided to follow her passion into the field of education.

She earned a Bachelor’s degree in Mid-Level Education from Arkansas State University and later pursued a Master of Science in Special Education Instructional Specialist. Mrs. Williams  also earned her ESL education certification, further expanding her expertise of diverse learners. With a heart for making a difference, Mrs. Williams has now spent 16 years as a public school educator, teaching a diverse range of students in subjects such as mid-level English—ranging from special education to Pre-AP—as well as general and advanced science. Mrs. Williams is looking forward to beginning her next educational journey to earn her Education Specialist in Educational Leadership.

In addition to her teaching career, Mrs. Williams’ passion lies in Special Education Law and due process. For the past two years, She has served as the Special Education Designee at Conway Junior High School, under a supportive and collaborative administration. In this role, Mrs. Williams facilitates the special education process, working closely with teachers, parents, and administrators to ensure due process and the best outcomes for students. Her dedication to serving the needs of diverse learners is reflected in her unwavering commitment to supporting the school community.

Born in Tampa, Florida, and raised in Central Arkansas from a teenager, Mrs. Williams’ personal life is deeply rooted in family and community. Having married into a rodeo family 27 years ago, she and her husband raised two daughters who grew up competing in rodeo. When not working, Mrs. Williams enjoys antiquing, fishing, and cherishing time spent with their two grandchildren.

Through all of her endeavors, both in the fashion industry and education, Mrs. Williams has shown a remarkable dedication to growth, service, and making a positive impact wherever she goes.

#CJHSCelebratingWomenMakingADifference
#UnlockingOurFullPotential
#LevelingUp

text: Dear Parents and Guardians, We are excited to announce that permission slips for our upcoming Urban Air Incentive Field Trip on Tuesday, May 13th have been sent home today with eligible students. To qualify for this trip, students must have earned all A’s or all A’s and B’s during the 3rd Nine Weeks and 4th Nine Weeks Interim, and must not have received any disciplinary action resulting in ISS, OSS, or Saturday School. To participate, students must return the signed permission slip along with $10 by this Friday, May 9th. Once the permission slip and payment are received, students will be given a waiver form from Urban Air that must be signed by a parent or guardian and brought on the day of the field trip. Please note: Students without a signed waiver will not be allowed to board the bus or attend the trip. We’re proud of our students’ hard work and positive behavior, and we’re looking forward to celebrating their efforts with this fun event! If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out to Mrs. Schroeder. Thanks!

text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

author: Conway Junior High
text:
🏝️✨ Government in Action!

Students in Mrs. Barnett’s Advanced Civics class faced an exciting challenge: they were “stranded” on a deserted island with all 1,600 CJHS students! 🌊

Working in teams, they designed their own governments from the ground up—deciding how to organize, lead, and build a thriving society. The next step? Attracting new citizens and visitors!

Each group created a persuasive, creative, and informative travel commercial to convince others why their island nation was the place to be. 🎥🌟

This hands-on project brought civics to life, blending teamwork, critical thinking, and creativity in a fun and memorable way!

author: Marquis Rogers
text:
It is with deep sadness that we share the news of the passing of one of our students, Jadelyn Vega. Our hearts are with her family, friends, classmates, and teachers during this difficult time.

Jadelyn will be remembered for her creativity and love of the arts, especially her talent for drawing and her dedication as a member of the Conway orchestra program. She was also a hardworking student who challenged herself through advanced classes and inspired those around her with her determination and kindness.

Please join us in keeping Jadelyn and her loved ones in your thoughts as we remember and honor her life.

author: Conway Junior High
text:
🎶 Conway Choir All-Region Workshop 🎶

On Tuesday, September 23rd, Conway Choir hosted an All-Region Workshop at the Conway High School James H. Clark Performing Arts Center for all Conway students in grades 7–9 preparing to audition for the Region 4 All-Region Choir.

It was a night full of focused rehearsals, lots of singing, and of course—pizza 🍕! Our students worked hard while having fun, and we are so proud of their dedication.

Now, we’re excited to welcome over 1,000 students from across Region 4 to Conway Junior High this Saturday, October 4th, as they audition for the All-Region Choir.

Good luck to all of our Conway singers—you’ve got this! 💙🎶 #ConwayChoir #AllRegion

text:
🎨 Although Hispanic Heritage Month has wrapped up, we're still celebrating the lasting influence of Latin American artists — and we couldn’t wait to share this!

This stunning piece was created by Layla, who recreated Frida Kahlo’s "Still Life with Parrot and Fruit" (1951) using oil pastels. Her vibrant take is a beautiful nod to Frida’s iconic style and cultural legacy. 🦜🍊🌿

Art like this reminds us that appreciation doesn’t end with a calendar month — Frida's impact lives on year-round. 💛

In Ms.Jordans 9th grade Personal Finance Class, students have been diving into the exciting world of the stock market! They’re able to compete against each other and other participants across the state! 🏆

Over the past few weeks, we’ve learned about:
💡 Ticker symbols
🐂 Bull vs. 🐻 Bear markets
📊 Diversification
…and so much more!

It’s been incredible watching students apply what they’ve learned, make investment decisions, and see firsthand how markets move.

A HUGE thank you to Economics Arkansas for providing this amazing opportunity for our school and helping our students gain real financial literacy skills that will last a lifetime! 🙌

author: Conway Junior High
text: Students in Advanced Economics simulated the Circular Flow Model for a Market Economy by playing "Econoland." Students were split into two groups, businesses and consumers. Businesses were given an investment of $10 and consumers were given three physical items to represent the three factors of production: bolts (capital), rocks (natural resources), and googly eyes (human labor). Resources were bought by the businesses, then taken to the local "factory" to produce finished goods. Those goods were then sold back to the consumers so that they businesses could make a profit. Students with the most products or money at the end of the game, won!

📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.

text:
Exciting Choir News!

We are thrilled to announce that two Conway Junior High Choir students have been selected for the Southwestern American Choral Directors Association (SWACDA) Honor Choirs! Congratulations to:

Aiden (AJ) Johnson – 7th–9th Grade Tenor-Bass Honor Choir

Ella Tavener – 7th–9th Grade Treble Honor Choir

Both AJ and Ella recently earned high chairs at the All-Region Choirs held in Russellville last weekend, and now they continue to see the rewards of their hard work with this prestigious recognition. These outstanding students were chosen through a highly competitive process involving singers from seven states across the Southwest region.

The SWACDA Conference and Honor Choirs are held every two years, and the next event will take place in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in March 2026. This is a tremendous honor and an incredible opportunity for AJ and Ella to represent Arkansas, the Conway School District, and Conway Junior High School on a regional stage.

text: NAEP 2026 PARENT-GUARDIAN NOTIFICATION LETTER Grades 4, 8, and 12 Civics, Mathematics, Reading, or U.S. History Thursday, January 8, 2026 Dear Parent or Guardian: Conway Junior High School will participate in the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) on Wednesday, March 4, 2026. NAEP is the largest nationally representative and continuing assessment of what students know and can do in various subjects. NAEP is administered by the National Center for Education Statistics, within the U.S. Department of Education. NAEP is different from our state assessments because it is a common measure of achievement across the country. Your child will/may take a mathematics or reading assessment. In addition to subject-area questions, students voluntarily complete NAEP survey questions. These questions provide valuable information about participating students’ educational experiences and opportunities to learn both in and outside of the classroom. More information about NAEP survey questions is available at https://nces.ed.gov/nationsreportcard/parents under the section “Survey Questionnaires & Your Student: What You Need to Know.” The assessment takes about 120 minutes for most students, which includes transition time, directions, and completion of survey questions. The information collected is used for statistical purposes only. Your child’s grades will not be affected. Students may be excused for any reason, are not required to complete the assessment, and may skip any question. While the assessment is voluntary, NAEP depends on student participation to help policymakers improve education. If you do not want your child to participate, please notify me in writing by Tuesday, February 17, 2026. There is no need to study in preparation for NAEP, but please encourage your child to do their best. Contact Bennie Broyles at 501-450-4860 or at broylesb@conwayschools.info if you have any questions. We are excited that our school is participating in NAEP. We know that Conway Junior High School’s students will show what our nation’s students know and can do. Sincerely, Marquis Rogers The National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) conducts the National Assessment of Educational Progress to evaluate federally supported education programs. All of the information you provide may only be used for the purposes of research, statistics, and evaluation under the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002 (ESRA; 20 U.S.C. § 9543) and may not be disclosed, our used, in identifiable form for any other purpose except as required by law. Every NCES employee as well as every NCES agent, such as contractors and NAEP coordinators, has taken an oath and is subject to a jail term of up to 5 years, a fine of $250,000, or both if he or she willfully discloses ANY identifiable information about you. Electronic submission of your information will be monitored for viruses, malware, and other threats by Federal employees and contractors in accordance with the Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015.

text:
It is once again ATLAS Interim Testing Time!  
We are excited to see how much you all have grown in your learning from the last interim!  Interim Testing will be January 29th and 30th.

Just like last interim, there will be a food truck incentive on February 6th for all those that:
Electronic Device (1pt) - Turned off and put in backpack; this includes phones and watches
Behavior (1pt)- Not a disruption during testing
Attendance (1pt) - Be present and on time
Effort (1pt) - Must try your best
Charged Chromebook (2pts only on Morning Tests)- Must be charged to 80% at beginning of each day

!!GROWTH INCENTIVE!!
Any student that has shown growth from Interim 1 to Interim 2 will receive an excused absence on February 9th.  This is the only day of that week students are required to be at school.  This will give students an extra long break.

If a student did not show growth, they will not have an excused absence on this day and there will be intervention lessons taking place on Monday, February 9th. 

We want you to try hard and do your best to show what amazing students we have here at Conway Junior High!

author: Conway Junior High
text:
CJHS Asian Club students had a special opportunity to learn from a guest speaker from UCA at their most recent meeting 🍙. Dr. Reed, who was born and raised in Japan and now teaches Japanese at UCA, guided students through making onigiri while sharing the culture and history behind this traditional food.

Students enjoyed hands-on learning as they made their own onigiri. This easy, affordable, and healthy Japanese snack, often seen in popular anime and YouTube videos 📺, was especially exciting for students to experience in real life. The onigiri-making activity was a big hit, with many students sharing that they plan to make it again at home!

Asian Club gives students the chance to explore Asian culture, food, and history through fun, interactive experiences, making it one of the most fun and unique clubs at Conway Junior High School 🎉.

🎉🐎 2nd Annual Lunar New Year Celebration at the Faulkner County Library 🎉🐎

On Saturday, February 7th, the CJHS & CHS Asian Club, in partnership with the Faulkner County Library, local Chinese community members, and the UCA Center for Asian Languages and Cultures, proudly hosted Conway’s 2nd Lunar New Year Celebration.

With approximately 200 attendees, the event was filled with energy, learning, and fun! Families enjoyed interactive stations featuring dumpling-making, Chinese calligraphy, crafts, chopsticks games, and more. It was a wonderful opportunity for our community to come together and celebrate the Year of the Fire Horse.

A heartfelt thank-you to the Faulkner County Library for providing the space and incredible support that helped make this event possible. We are also grateful for our amazing team of 20 student volunteers from Conway High School and Conway Junior High School, along with 14 local Chinese community members, whose enthusiasm and dedication made the celebration such a success.

Special thanks to our generous supporters:
 🥟 Sakura Ocean A.Y.C.E. Sushi & Hibachi (coming soon) for the $200 donation supporting the dumpling station
 🥤Boba Love for donating nearly 200 cups of boba tea
 🍩 Shimmery Donut for donating 50 dozen donut holes

Events like this truly highlight the cultural vibrancy of our community and the growing excitement for Chinese culture and language. Interested in learning more? Join our Chinese program or the Asian Club! 🌏❤️🐎

text:
Dear Conway Junior High School Parents & Students,

We want to share information regarding conversations that may be circulating about the possibility of students choosing to leave class during the school day.

Our role as a school district is not to promote or suppress student viewpoints. Our responsibility is to ensure student safety and to maintain an orderly learning environment for all students. When a student leaves class during the school day, it creates safety concerns and disrupts the learning environment for other students. For that reason, if a student chooses to leave class, the situation will be addressed as a behavioral and attendance matter in accordance with our student code of conduct. 

School will operate as normal. Instruction will continue throughout the day, and administrators will supervise students appropriately to ensure safety. This is not a school or district initiated activity. We encourage families to talk with their students about school expectations, safety considerations, and how choices made during the school day can impact learning for all students. 

This information has also been emailed to all Conway Junior High School Parents.

Thank you for your partnership as we continue to focus on student safety, learning, and maintaining a respectful school environment.
Conway Public Schools

author: Conway Junior High
text:
✨ Black History Month Spotlight: Celebrating Excellence in Our CJHS Community ✨
Harvell Howard is a mission-driven leader with more than two decades of experience advancing youth development, education, and community impact across Arkansas and beyond. Known as a collaborative strategist and program innovator, he is deeply committed to the transformative power of mentorship.
Prior to joining Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Arkansas (BBBSCA), Dr. Howard held leadership roles shaping statewide youth, education, and workforce initiatives. He convened higher education, government, and community partners through Arkansas Summits, Inc. to strengthen college and career pathways, supported youth workforce curriculum development with the City of Little Rock, and advanced youth leadership and civic engagement through the Urban League of Arkansas.
Dr. Howard also brings extensive experience in higher education and nonprofit capacity building. At the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, he was a part of a team that led student success initiatives serving more than 500 students and directed award-winning programs that improved retention and completion. Through his consulting firm, Essential Solutions, Inc., he has helped organizations design sustainable strategies for growth, collaboration, and community wellness.
A strong advocate for data-informed leadership, Dr. Howard’s research centers on cross-sector collaboration and integrative leadership to drive measurable outcomes. He holds a Ph.D. in Interdisciplinary Leadership Studies, a Master of Public Service, a bachelor's degree in economics and business, and is a proud 1999 graduate of Conway High School. His work has been recognized nationally and internationally for leadership and community engagement.
As Executive Director of BBBSCA, Dr. Howard leads with a passion for mentorship and youth empowerment, focused on expanding access to mentoring, strengthening partnerships, and ensuring every young person has the support they need to thrive. He and his wife, Dr. Rosa Howard, have three sons, Harvell II (Harvie - 11), Harrison Levi (9), and Harland Lance (6) and reside in Central Arkansas.

Today we’re proud to celebrate School Social Worker Day by highlighting one of our incredible team members, Laney Doan! 💙

Laney has been a school social worker for the past seven years and is currently in her second year with Conway Public Schools. She earned both her bachelor’s and master’s degrees in social work from University of Arkansas at Little Rock and is originally from Searcy, Arkansas, where she graduated from Searcy High School.

Social work has always been part of Laney’s story. She grew up in an open foster home and has four siblings through adoption. With a mother who is also a social worker, Laney witnessed from an early age the importance of serving others and saw firsthand the hardships many families face. Those experiences shaped her heart for service and led her to pursue a career in social work.

Laney loves working with students each day and helping remove barriers to their learning and success. Whether she’s providing food, offering encouragement, or connecting families with vital resources, she is grateful for the opportunity to support students and families as they overcome challenges and thrive—both at school and at home.

Thank you, Laney, for the compassion, dedication, and care you bring to our schools every single day!

Ms. King grew up near Benton, Arkansas and graduated from Harmony Grove High School in 2010. She went on to attend the University of Central Arkansas, graduating Summa Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts in Spanish Education and minors in Teaching and Learning, Visual Art, and English as a Second Language.

Since 2014, Ms. King has been teaching Spanish at Conway Junior High, inspiring students and sharing her passion for language and culture. She credits her love of teaching Spanish to Ms. Katrina Cox, Ms. Jamie Bird, and Dr. Jennifer Parrack, whose influence continues to shape her classroom today.

Outside of school, Ms. King enjoys reading, cooking, hiking, and camping around Arkansas with her family. She is also a blue belt in jiu-jitsu at Arte BJJ, where she trains multiple times each week.

One of her favorite quotes comes from Maya Angelou:
“If you don’t like something, change it. If you can’t change it, change your attitude.”

Thank you, Ms. King, for the passion, dedication, and positivity you bring to our students every day. We are proud to celebrate you this Women’s History Month!

As we celebrate Women’s History Month, we are proud to highlight the incredible women who make a difference in our school community. This week, we’re featuring Ms. Marcia Pierce, our 2025–2026 Conway Junior High Employee of the Year! 

Marcia Pierce was born and raised in Conway, Arkansas, where she attended the Conway Public System and graduated in 1985. Some of her proudest moments have been becoming a mother of two wonderful children and a grandmother to four granddaughters who lovingly call her "Mimi".

Marcia earned a certificate in childcare from UACCM and went on to study Family and Consumer Science at the University of Central Arkansas. Afterward, she moved to San Antonio, Texas, where she obtained a Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. After a few years, she returned to Conway and began working in the very school district that  shaped her, Conway Public Schools.

Marcia has dedicated 25 years to childcare and education, working with children from infancy through junior high.  She spent 8 years in childcare and 17 years in the Conway Public School District.  One of her most rewarding roles was working with teen mothers, guiding them in parenting, college preparation, and first jobs.

Today, Marcia is dedicated to student success, assisting certified staff in developing strategies to reinforce learning and support new students. She finds joy in knowing she helps students build lifelong skills. In her free time, Marcia enjoys reading, spending time with family and friends, and traveling. Some of her favorite destinations include New York City and Washington D.C., and her most memorable trip was visiting the 9/11 Memorial.

Thank you for all you do for our CJHS community Ms. Pierce!!

Happy National Assistant Principals and Dean of Students Week! 🎉

All week long, we’ll be highlighting the incredible leaders who help make our school a success. Today, we’re proud to recognize Mr. Broyles!

Originally from Pine Bluff, Arkansas, Mr. Broyles has served as an assistant principal at Conway Junior High School since 2007. He graduated from Watson Chapel High School in 1990 and went on to earn his bachelor’s degree from the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff in 1996. He later received his master’s degree from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock in 2003 and most recently earned his Educational Specialist degree from the University of Central Arkansas in May 2018.

Mr. Broyles’ dedication, experience, and commitment to students and staff make a lasting impact on our school each and every day. We are grateful for his leadership!

Stay tuned as we continue celebrating our outstanding assistant principals and deans all week long! 👏

author: Conway Junior High
text:
Happy National Dean of Students  and Assistant Principals Week! 🎉

All week long, we’ve been highlighting the incredible leaders who help make our school a success. Today, we’re proud to recognize our final spotlight, Ms. Breanna Taylor!

Ms. Taylor is in her first year serving as the Dean of Students at Conway Junior High School. Prior to this role, she spent ten years as a Special Education educator at the high school level, including the last six years working with students enrolled in the Center for Academic, Social, and Career Development program.

Although not originally from Conway, Ms. Taylor was born in Tennessee and moved to Arkansas at the age of two. She grew up in the Little Rock/North Little Rock area and was a proud North Little Rock Charging Wildcat until her senior year, when she relocated to Batesville, Arkansas.

Ms. Taylor is eager to be part of the Conway community and has enjoyed all it has to offer. Outside of school, she enjoys reading and thrifting—most of her wardrobe and home décor has come from thrift stores!

Ms. Taylor’s passion for supporting students and her dedication to building meaningful connections make a positive impact on our school community. We are grateful for her leadership!

Thank you for celebrating our outstanding leaders with us this week! 👏

text:
Team,

There has been a threat reported by a student.  We are currently working with police and fire to resolve the situation.  Please do not alarm students.  We are currently working on messaging to parents.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Conway Junior High families,
We want to inform you that a bomb threat was reported at Conway Junior High. As a precaution, all students and staff have been safely evacuated to a secure location.
Local law enforcement and emergency personnel are on site and are actively checking the building. For the safety of everyone involved we ask that parents do not come to the campus unless directed to do so, as this may interfere with emergency operations.
We will provide updates as more information becomes available. Please monitor your email and phone for continued official communication. 
The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority, and we appreciate your patience and cooperation during this time.
Conway Public Schools

author: Marquis Rogers
text: Transporting students to the arena.  Please sit in the seating assignments that you sat for the pep rally.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Dear Conway Junior High Families,

We are writing to follow up on the earlier report of a bomb threat. 

The investigation is ongoing and students and staff have been safely moved to Buzz Bolding Arena at the Conway High School.

All students are in a safe location and are welcome to stay. If any parents/guardians wish to check their student out, you may proceed to Buzz Bolding Arena at 10 a.m. to do so. This will be an excused absence. 

All students who remain, will return to their campus when it is safe to do so.

To check out a student, please enter the Conway High School Campus from Prince Street and make your way towards Buzz Bolding Arena. A map is attached. Please have your identification ready as no student will be released without verification of identification. 

This process will take time, so we ask for your patience as we navigate this situation together.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Thank you to all parents and guardians for your patience and cooperation during today's situation.

Our staff is working as quickly and safely as possible to assist with student check-out. Please continue to follow the instructions outlined in our previous message regarding pick-up procedures to help keep the process moving efficiently.

Student safety and accountability remain our top priority. We appreciate your understanding and support.

Further updates will be provided as needed.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Dear Conway Junior High Families,
We are following up on the earlier bomb threat reported at the Junior High. Law enforcement and emergency personnel responded immediately and the bomb squad determined there is no credible threat. The campus has been cleared and is safe.
All students and staff remained safe. 
Students who have not been checked out will return to campus at 1:00 p.m.
Parents/Guardians may retrieve student belongings after 1:30 p.m. today or any time tomorrow.
We appreciate the quick response of law enforcement and emergency personnel and the cooperation of our students and staff. Counselors are available for any student who may need support.
We also want to thank our parents/guardians for your patience and support during the reunification process.

author: Marquis Rogers
text:
Conway Junior High School Families,

After 1:30 PM, you may bring your child back to campus to retrieve their belongings, or you may choose to wait until tomorrow morning. For safety and efficiency, only students will be permitted to enter the building, and all students must enter and exit through the front office.

Thank you again for your patience and support throughout this process.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:

Conway Public Schools

author: Marquis Rogers
text:
Team,

I want to take a moment to sincerely thank each of you for how you handled today's situation. What we experienced was not easy - evacuating the building, relocating to the arena, serving lunch in an unusual setting, returning to campus, and managing the backpack retrieval process - but throughout it all, you were incredible.

You remained calm, steady, and focused when our students needed you most. Because of you, our kids stayed safe, supported, and reassured during a stressful and uncertain time. That doesn't happen by accident - that happens because of who you are and the way you show up for our students every single day.

I'm especially grateful for the way you kept students calm and under control, while also being flexible and willing to do whatever was needed in the moment. Today required teamwork at the highest level, and you delivered.

Please know this - this could not have been done without you.  I'm proud to serve alongside you, and our school is better because of each of you.

Thank you again for everything you did today.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”

author: Marquis Rogers
text:
CPSD ATHLETICS SPECTATOR GUIDELINES
The Conway School District is proud to welcome all our students, as well as parents and members of the community, to the exciting athletic events that we offer.  Conway students (band, cheerleaders, dance squad, and athletes) practice numerous hours so they are prepared for our extracurricular events. These guidelines are designed to make our games safe and enjoyable for all spectators.

CONWAY HIGH SCHOOL ATHLETIC EVENTS

Elementary, Middle School and Junior High students must be accompanied to the game by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.

CONWAY JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL ATHLETIC EVENTS

Elementary and Middle School students must be accompanied to the game by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.

CONWAY MIDDLE SCHOOLS ATHLETIC EVENTS

Elementary school students must be accompanied to the game by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.


Regardless of grade level, all students are expected to follow standard rules for proper sporting attendance.

1. NO LOITERING around unauthorized areas of the stadium, arena, fields, and campus.  This includes the High School Courtyard. Students should be seated in the stands, unless at the concession stand or the restroom.

2. Fans may not bring items such as backpacks, balls, skateboards, or bikes into the game.

3. No outside food or drink is allowed. Concessions are available inside the game.

4. School rules apply and cooperation is expected with all game workers and school personnel. Failure to follow rules or lack of cooperation will result in removal from the game.

5. It is expected that all students will leave school grounds in a timely manner after completion of the game.  Students that are not picked up in a timely manner (20 minutes from the end of the game) will not be allowed to return for future games.  Students can call parents before the end of the game to allow transportation to get there in a timely manner.   

Thank you for your cooperation and your support of Conway Public Schools Athletics!

author: Marquis Rogers
text:
PLEASE READ - First Day of School Reminders

CJHS Staff,

The first day is almost here! I want to share a few reminders as we get ready to welcome our students back:

Staff Shirts: Please wear your blue staff shirt that you wore for Open House.
Morning Coffee: Coffee will be available in Room 118 in the morning.
Lunch: Lunch will be provided in Room 118 during all four lunches. Coach Prince is providing pulled pork for everyone—thank you, Coach Prince!
Mentors: Please make sure you share this information with your mentee(s). Some of our new staff members may not have been added to the staff listserv yet, and we want to make sure everyone receives these reminders.

I also want to thank everyone who took the time to complete our Leadership Support Feedback Survey. We appreciate your honesty. We were encouraged by the results, but we also heard your suggestions for how we can improve. Your leadership team is motivated to take that feedback and continue getting better at how we support you.

As we begin the first week, I ask that we all demonstrate grace and patience with one another. The first few days never go as smoothly as we would like. There will be schedule issues, questions, unexpected situations, and a few wrinkles that we have to iron out. We will get better each day.

For this first day, let's keep the main goal simple: Get our students in the building, take care of them while they are here, and get them home safely in the afternoon. Everything else, we can work through together.

Thank you for all of the work you have put in to get us to this point. Let's have a great first day and a great start to the school year!

Purposeful Impact starts Day 1!

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
Hello CLE Families!

It was so good to see so many of our families at our Open House last week!  We are SO excited for our kiddos to start with us on Monday morning!

We always get so excited about school starting back that we often forget how crazy car rider lines and bus routes are the first several days of school.  CLE is a bus hub which means more than just CLE students come to our campus for transportation.  Additionally, we have many new families to our campus that haven't practiced our drop off and pick up procedures.  All of these factors make these lines a little longer and a little slower.  We promise it will get easier and shorter.  We ask that you give us grace as work to make sure our procedures are SAFE and efficient.  Sometimes this requires us to make changes.  We appreciate your patience.  To keep the line moving most efficiently your student should be unbuckled, back pack on, and ready to exit the vehicle on the drivers side when the line stops at the door.  Getting out on the passenger side requires your child to walk between vehicles.  This is unsafe and takes longer.  

I understand that some of our procedures do not make sense to you or may not be convenient for you.  We are responsible for making sure over 600 students (CLE and secondary students) arrive to their classrooms and other campuses safely and on time.  All of our procedures are designed around that goal...SAFETY and EFFICIENCY! Again, we ask for grace and patience!

A few new procedures this year are:
DROP OFF (CLE students without older siblings catching a shuttle bus):  No longer will car riders be allowed to enter the front of the building.  Previously, students were allowed to be walked to the front door by parents and enter the building there.  Due to some changes we are making, this will now be an unsafe practice.  All students who do not ride a bus must be dropped off in the car rider drop off line which goes around our building.  (blue arrows on map)
SHUTTLE STUDENTS DROP OFF (with and without CLE siblings): The front loop (around the parking lot) will be open for you to pull up and park to wait for bus loading.   You will NOT use the parking lot.  The parking lot will be for teachers and anyone with business to take care of in the building.  THIS IS FOR MORNINGS ONLY!   (red arrows on map)
PICK UP (CLE students with older siblings on shuttle buses):  If you have a CLE student and a secondary student riding a shuttle bus, you will need to drive through the pick up line to get your CLE student.  You will then need to pull around and park in the parking lot to wait for your secondary student to be released from the shuttle bus.  Shuttle bus riders do not get dismissed from the buses until ALL buses have arrived on campus.
On the first day of school, parents may park and walk their child to their classroom.  This is for the first day only!  The above procedures start on DAY 2! Reminder, K students can wait until 9:00 to start on the first day!  We hope you had a great weekend, resting up for the start of school!  We will be ready to see you first thing in the morning!

author: Lindsey Jones
text:
August Garden Update! We are so thankful and fortunate to have an amazing garden with some wonderful people helping weekly.

Last Saturday morning was a big success. A total of 25 people came out to harvest some vegetables and then cut buckets of flowers for the bouquet making team to make something special that all the teachers received for their first day of school. Those that go through the pickup line saw the welcome back signs that the kids decorated.  A big thanks to all that were able to join us. We hope everyone had a successful first week of school.

This week will hopefully be the last of the heat.  Let's hope. The plan is to pull up the field pea bed along with the pole bean bed. The heat has limited what those plants could do. Then the wire grates will be put up for a planting of sugar snap peas for the students to enjoy later in the fall. The peppers, okra and blackberries are still producing, and the strawberries are making baby plants that need to be tucked into new homes. A newer soaker hose will also be used to replace the brittle one currently in the herb bed. 

Once we get into September a fall garden will be planted. So, it's still not too late to join us at the garden. Hope you can join us this Saturday, 8/26, starting at 9:00 am for about an hour. 

Happy Gardening,
Richard, Jill & Sara

Hope you can join us Saturday at 9:00 at the CLE garden!

author: Lindsey Jones
text:
Hello School Gardeners,

While the weather is cooler it still does not feel like fall. And we sure could use some of the rain they are calling for.  Last Saturday, we thinned out one of the strawberry beds since the plants are overcrowded. We moved them to other empty beds and had the wonderful idea of selling some of the extra strawberry plants at the plant sale. Most of the fall seeds we planted have emerged and growing nicely.  The picture below is the collection of gourds harvested last week. Of course, still harvesting green peppers and okra.

This Saturday, starting at 9:00 am, we will be thinning out some the baby plants that are too crowded together to grow properly. Also flower seeds need to be harvested with some showing up at plant sales in the future. Hope you can join us.

Happy Gardening,

Richard, Jill & Sara

text:
Quick garden update 💙

-Last week Krista Quinn with the FCES conducted a lesson on greens with all our 3rd grade classes.  Each class had a short lesson, tasted 3 different varieties, and also picked a pumpkin for their classroom.

-Last Friday, 1st, 2nd, and 4th graders were invited into the garden to pick a pumpkin for their classrooms.  Kids enjoyed observing all the garden has to offer.

-Last Saturday, we celebrated our final Learning Garden Day.  We are beginning to plan for spring 2024 as we hope to engage even more people! Come be part of our garden community! 

-We WILL be meeting in the garden TOMORROW, Saturday at 9am, for some final clean up after our first freeze.  Join us if you can!

-November 10th we will be conducting the same lesson on greens with our 4th grade students.  If you would like to volunteer, please let Jill Steed know. 

Thanks to everyone who works so hard to make our garden a success!

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
Good Rainy Thursday to everyone!

Hope this day finds you doing well.  I want to share a quick update about all things garden.  I did give an update via GroupMe last Friday, so if you’re not in our group please email me with your phone number and I will get you added.

-Tomorrow!!!  4th grade lessons on greens will take place with our great friend Krista Quinn from the Faulkner County Extension office.  Lessons begin at 9am.  Fingers are crossed that the rain will be over and we will be able to learn in our beautiful garden. 

-December 18th-Deck the Shed 9-10:30-This will be a fun time of decorating our garden for Christmas and the CLE Drive Thru Parade.  We will be making live wreaths, bird feeder ornaments, decorating a living Christmas tree, and trimming the shed.  There may also be some light garden chores to accomplish. 

-Garden Update-We still have some of our fall crops growing in the garden.  The very warm temperatures followed by the low temps resulted in some damage.  We will continue to care for these crops and harvest greens until it gets very cold.  Our summer crops are over and most have been pulled from the garden.  The flower seed heads are remaining to provide winter food for the birds.  We will be using cover crops to add nutrients back into the soil over the winter. 

This fall has been the best fall our school garden has ever seen!  We’ve been able to raise over $1,400 for our garden program.  It has produced hundreds of pounds of produce over the growing season.  The garden has allowed students so many learning opportunities.   And it has brought our CLE families together as a garden community.  I’m so grateful for each of you and your unique role in this process.  It would not have been possible without you!!  I’m incredibly grateful to Mr. Richard Klerk and Ms. Sara Tyler for their work and leadership.  Our committee is the largest and most diverse it’s ever been with so many wonderful teachers and community members involved.  The future looks bright for the CLE Garden!

Grateful for you all,
Jill Steed

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

text:
Good Afternoon Garden Committee,
We have our first workday of the year this Saturday at 10am. We plan to remove and install a new garden border.  The back border will be taller so that we can also save our precious mulch from washing out. We will also be reworking one of our garden beds where we have our perennial asparagus growing. There is also some inside work setting up a new rack and getting other supplies ready for our plant sale. 
We will begin planting seeds for the plant sale in the coming weeks! This is going to be a BIG SPRING for our garden! 

We appreciate the support and perspective each of you bring to the table.  It could NOT happen without you! The garden hopes to see you Saturday!

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
Happy Wednesday, Gardners! 
Here is a quick update on all the things happening in our garden right now!

Be looking for a couple of VERY important Sign-Up Genius forms to come out.  If you’ve wanted to volunteer but haven’t been able to I hope you find an opportunity here.  As always, please reach out with any questions!

-Seed planting starts today!  Cue the confetti!  This is the biggest fundraiser of the year and it’s also going to be a great way for the CLE Garden to support other school gardens in Conway.  *We have plenty of volunteers for this!

-Following close behind the seed starting is the Watering Schedule.  Without consistent water these tiny seeds will simply just sit.  Consistent watering is extremely important!  There are 14 days to choose from on the schedule.  This is during school hours.  It will be important to operate in the most professional manner so we don’t disturb learning and testing.  There is an explanation of how to water in the sign up and I will also send out a guide in another email.

-Our First and Second Grade lessons with Krista Quinn are happening March 8th and March 12th!!  Fingers crossed we will be able to hold the lesson in the garden and plant peas and potatoes with students.  If it rains, we will continue with lessons only in the tornado shelter.  Sign up is going out for these as well.

One other thing, if you see any of our wonderful CLE PTO Board Members PLEASE thank them for their generous contribution to our Volunteer Appreciate Picnic (Planned for later this spring).  They are so supportive of our school and garden. 
I hope you’re as excited as I am about watching our plants grow this spring.  An undertaking like this simply would not be possible without you, our wonderful, strong, and reliable volunteers.  You are the best!

Jill
jillsteed2015@gmail.com

On your mark, get set, go! 👟💨Registration for the 16th annual Kids Run Arkansas® is now open 👏🏼

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟 Today, as the Solar Eclipse graces our skies, we're thrilled to share the excitement that's been building up in our town! Last week, in collaboration with UCA, Carolyn Lewis Elementary had the pleasure of hosting Morton Brown, a former UCA student and Arkansas native, who also happens to be the Artistic Director for the city of Philadelphia. Morton brought to life LUNA, a magnificent 25’ Solar Eclipse superhero sculpture, right here in our beloved town, in anticipation of today's COSMIC event! You may know of some of Mr. Brown's work as he has done murals in downtown Conway!

🌞 Huge thanks to Mr. Morton and UCA for their incredible efforts and the captivating presentation they shared with us! Not only did Mr. Morton gift Carolyn Lewis Elementary with a special drawing, but a group of our students also had the amazing opportunity to create Birthday Capes! Each student received a personalized chart depicting the sky on their exact birthdate. They meticulously plotted stars from the chart onto graph paper, then sewed them onto capes, forming unique constellations representing their birthdays.

✨ Today, LUNA takes center stage at the UCA Solar Eclipse event, marking this momentous occasion in the most spectacular way possible.  🌒 
#solareclipse2024 #ChampionsForKids

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text: Tired of the slow long car rider line? Here are some things that will help! AM: Your child should be unbuckled, ready to get out of the car as soon as you stop. Cars should pull all the way up and not leave big gaps between vehicles. We can unload more children the closer the cars are together. Please drive off as soon as your child is safely out of the way; waiting until they get into the building slows our car line down tremendously. Do not get out of your vehicle. Students should exit their cars independently. Duty teachers/volunteers will not always be there to open each door; your child should be able to open the car door and exit without assistance. Remember, the gate closes at 7:50 a.m. If you arrive and the gate is still open, you should utilize the car line. Only park and walk your child in if the gate is closed. PM: Have your Driveline tag. Cars should pull all the way up and not leave big gaps between vehicles. We can load more children the closer the cars are together. If you must buckle your child, please proceed through the line and then pull over to do that. Do not get out of your vehicle. Students should load their cars independently. author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text: Just a few reminders about our car line procedures. These procedures are put into place to ensure a smooth and efficient student drop off and pick up. Adults should not get out of their vehicle ever in the car line. Students should be ready to get out of the car in the morning before arriving at the drop off spot (backpack on, coat on, lunchbox in hand). The morning car line gate closes at 7:50 due to the tardy bell ringing at 8:00 a.m. You must walk your child in and sign them in if it is after 8:00 a.m. The afternoon car line gate closes when there is no longer a line. If you do not want to have to park and come in the office to get your child, you should be in the line no later than 3:35. Duty ends at 3:45 for staff. Please be considerate of their time and arrive no later than 3:35 to pick up your car rider. Thank you.

CPSD Bell to Bell No Cell
At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. To help keep our classrooms focused and follow state guidelines, students should not use personal electronic devices during the school day. This includes cell phones, AirPods, wireless headphones, and smartwatches. We ask that all devices be turned off and kept in backpacks during school hours.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

text:
Dear Parents,
We are excited to kick off the new school year! We will be using Rooms, our school's communication platform, to share important updates and connect you with your child's teacher.

Teacher Introductions
Your child's teacher will be sending an introductory message to you through the platform.

Action Required: Check Your Notification Preferences
To ensure you receive these important updates, please make sure your notification preferences for Rooms are turned on. You can choose to be notified by push notifications from the school app, email notifications, or SMS text messages.
To update your notification preferences, you can either use the school app or a web browser.

If you use the school app:
Open the school app.
Tap "More" and then the Settings icon.
Select "Notification preferences".
Customize your preferences for messages and announcements.
If you do not use the school app:
Log in using your mobile phone number on your phone's web browser.
Tap your name in the top-right corner.
Scroll to "Notifications" and adjust the settings for Messages and Announcements.

You can choose to receive real-time alerts, hourly updates, or a once-a-day digest.
We have attached a flyer with more detailed instructions on how to set up your notifications.

Thank you,
Carolyn Lewis Elementary School

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌱 We are thrilled to announce that Carolyn Lewis Elementary has been awarded the 2025 Harvest Community Partnership Garden of the Year! 🌱

This recognition means so much to our school, and we are incredibly proud of the hard work, care, and dedication that made our garden flourish this year.

We are especially thankful for our amazing partnership with Krista Quinn and the Faulkner County Extension Office, the wonderful Mr. Richard Clerk and the Master Gardeners, as well as Kelli Burke who continually support, guide, and encourage our students. Their expertise and willingness to invest in our school garden have helped create meaningful, hands-on learning opportunities for our kids.

A huge heartfelt thank-you goes to Mrs. Tyler and Mrs. Parham—your passion, time, and sacrifice are the heartbeat of this project. Because of your leadership and commitment, our students not only learn about gardening, but also about teamwork, responsibility, and the joy of watching something grow.

Thank you to everyone who has supported our garden. This award is a celebration of community, collaboration, and the belief that great things can grow when we work together. Thank you to Leslee Tell from the Arkansas Department of Agriculture coming to present this award to us!🌿💚

#CarolynLewisElementary #GardenOfTheYear #ArkansasGrown #SchoolGarden #FaulknerCountyExtension #MasterGardeners #ProudToBeCLE

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Gifted & Talented Referrals Now Open – Spring Testing Cycle 📣

The district is now accepting parent referrals for Gifted & Talented services for the spring testing cycle.
GT services are designed to support students who demonstrate advanced learning needs in areas such as
reasoning, problem-solving, and creativity. Identification is based on multiple measures and is not something
students need to study or prepare for.

🗓 Parent Referral Deadline: March 9
📄 Parent Referral Form:  https://forms.gle/h7Lz51cMTfAjUres7

Please note: Teachers have been sent a separate referral link via email. Teacher Referral deadline is March
6th.

If you have questions about the GT referral or identification process, feel free to contact your campus or the GT
coordinator: reynoldsa@conwayschools.info. You may also visit the website for more information. 

Thank you for helping us ensure all students receive the services they need to grow and thrive!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

⏰ Today's Topic: Student Check-Out

Why can't students be checked out at 3:15 p.m.? By that time, our dismissal process is already underway. Our staff is focused on safely and efficiently getting more than 500 students to the correct buses, cars, and after-school destinations.

If you need to check out your child, please plan to do so before 3:15 p.m. Thank you for helping us keep dismissal safe, organized, and efficient for every student! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

🚪 Today's Topic: The 7:50 Gate Closure

The gate closes at 7:50 a.m. so our staff can transition from arrival duties to preparing students for a successful school day. This helps classes begin on time while keeping our campus organized and safe.

After 7:50 a.m., families should park and walk their students into the building. Thank you for helping us start each day safely and smoothly for all of our Little Wampus Cats! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

🍽️ Lunch Visitors

Why don't lunch visitors begin at the start of the school year? The first few weeks of school are dedicated to helping students learn routines, build independence, and settle into their new classrooms.

Waiting to welcome lunch visitors allows our cafeteria and classrooms to establish smooth procedures first, creating a calmer, more successful start for everyone. We appreciate your patience as we help our Little Wampus Cats get off to a great start! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

🚗 Today's Topic: Parking Lot Drop-Offs

For the safety of all our students, we do not allow parking lot drop-offs. Students walking through moving traffic without staff supervision creates a significant safety concern during our busy arrival time.

Our car rider line is designed to provide a safe, supervised location where students can exit their vehicles and begin their day. Thank you for helping us keep every Little Wampus Cat safe by using the designated car rider line each morning! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

⏳ Patience During the First Two Weeks

The first two weeks of school are a time of learning—not just in the classroom, but for our routines as well! Students, families, and staff are all adjusting to new procedures, so arrival and dismissal lines may take a little longer as everyone learns the process.

With a little patience and consistency, things quickly become smoother. Thank you for your understanding, flexibility, and partnership as we help our Little Wampus Cats have a successful start to the school year! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

👨‍🏫 Staff Children

You may occasionally see a CLE staff member bringing their own child into the building as they report to work. Since our staff members are already on campus and beginning their workday, their children enter with them.

For all other students who are not bus riders, arrival should take place through the designated car rider line. This helps us maintain safe, consistent arrival procedures for everyone.

Thank you for partnering with us to keep arrival safe, organized, and efficient for all of our Little Wampus Cats! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE
