author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

💬 Teacher Conferences

Arrival and dismissal are some of the busiest times of the day. During these times, teachers are focused on supervising students and making sure everyone arrives and leaves safely.

If you'd like to discuss your child's progress or have questions, please reach out through the communication app, email, or contact the office to schedule a time to talk. This allows teachers to give your concerns the time and attention they deserve while keeping all students safe. Thank you for your understanding and partnership! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

author: Carolyn Lewis Elementary
text:
🐾 Behind the Procedure – The Why Behind the Way 🐾

🪪 Visitor IDs

Keeping our students safe is our top priority. That's why all visitors who have not yet been entered into our visitor system are required to present a valid photo ID when entering the building during school hours.

Our visitor check-in process helps us know who is in the building at all times and is an important part of maintaining a safe and secure learning environment. Thank you for helping us keep our Little Wampus Cats safe! 💙🐾 #WeAreCLE

text:
🌟Mr. Mark Dibrell is our Core Values Champion for the Month of September.🌟
"Mr. Dibrell drives a bus to and from Julia Lee Moore daily. Mr. Dibrell is a true champion for kids! When school started, the temperature was 100 degrees, so he brought a cooler of water bottles on his bus and had them ready as students loaded the bus to keep them cool. He did this with his own money. Today a student left their lunch behind on the bus, so after he was finished with his morning route, he made a special trip back to JLM to drop off the student's lunch to him so he wouldn't be upset. Every single day Mr. Dibrell goes above and beyond to serve our students!" Mr. Dibrell, you are a true #ChampionForKids! #StaffCommittedtoExcellence
Video surprising Mr. Dibrell is on our Youtube Channel -https://youtu.be/yftV68zJAR0

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟Shiloh Harder - Middle School Math Instructional Facilitator - is a Core Values Champion for the Month of September.🌟

"Ever since Mr. Harder took his current role, he has worked tirelessly with teachers on curriculum and instruction in the math classroom at the middle school level. Go to any middle school and you will meet teachers with nothing but positive things to say about Mr. Harder. His professionalism and preparedness leading middle school math teachers is phenomenal. We started the year with two long term math substitutes. Mr. Harder worked with those individuals until he knew students were being taken care of every single day. In one class three different long-term substitutes attended and Mr. Harder modeled every day until the teacher was comfortable with the content. 

On top of the amount of work he does for this district in curriculum, he planned for and prepped other adults to teach mathematics to our students. It was truly inspiring to watch him back in the classroom solely focused on giving our students the best possible education with their regular teacher on leave. He’s more than deserving of this recognition."

Mr. Harder, you are a true #ChampionForKids! #StaffCommittedtoExcellence
Video surprising Mr. Harder at his home campus Ruth Doyle Middle School is on our Youtube Channel - https://youtu.be/K-P-CilSZF4

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟Sam Dobson - Custodian at Woodrow Cummins Elementary - is a Core Values Champion for the Month of October!🌟

"Mr. Sam inspires our students and staff on a daily basis! When he notices a student's shoe is untied, he immediately bends down and offers to tie it for him/her. When he sees our cafeteria is short-handed, he just jumps right in and assists with whatever is needed. He walks around and engages in conversations with students during breakfast and lunch. When our teachers call on the walkie-talkie about a custodial need, Mr. Sam responds regardless of whether the need is in his area of responsibility or not. He is a true CHAMPION FOR KIDS!"

CPSD is honored to have Mr. Sam on our team! Thank you for all that you do! #ChampionsForKids #StaffCommittedtoExcellence

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
The Conway Public Schools Orchestra program presents its annual "La Fiesta Orquesta” event on Monday, November 13, featuring the nearly 300 students of the orchestra program in free concerts throughout the night in the James H. Clark Auditorium. In addition, a taco supper fundraiser is held in the Conway HS Cafeteria from 5-8 pm.  

Tickets to the dinner are on sale now and can be purchased from any orchestra student, and donations and ticket purchases can also be made online at conwayorch.square.site. This year we are partnering with Tacos4Life, so every meal purchased raises funds for the orchestra AND provides a meal to a person in need!

We hope you’ll support these amazing students and come hear them play!!

text:

You won't believe the talent we have here in our school on and backstage!

Thursday: 7:30 PM
Friday: 7:30 PM

Students & Staff: $7

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟Amy Hubbard - Special Education Classroom Teacher - Ellen Smith Elementary - is a Core Values Champion for the Month of October!🌟

Mrs. Hubbard is AMAZING with her students and their families. She is constantly going above and beyond to make sure her students have what they need to be successful every day at school. She is patient with each student and knows exactly what will motivate them or bring a smile to their face. She has been great with helping staff and students at Ellen Smith learn how to be comfortable and interact intentionally with her class. She is great at making sure they are included in all activities at Ellen Smith. She has great relationships with the paraprofessionals in her classroom and treats them like family. I am so happy we have Mrs. Hubbard on staff and that I get to work and learn from her. She makes inclusion a top priority for her classroom and our school. She is a champion for her students every single day, and does it so well!"

Mrs. Hubbard, you are a true #ChampionForKids! #StaffCommittedtoExcellence 
Thank you for all that you do!!!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🚙Stop #5 for the Conway School Board "CPSD Road Trip" was recently at Woodrow Cummins Elementary with the theme of “Champions For Kids!” School Board Members and District leaders were welcomed by fun music and cheers by the “Kindness Squad” led by Counselor Ms. Ashley Patchell. Principal Dr. Lewis, Assistant Principal Ms. Ross, and Instructional Facilitator Ms. Martin led a great presentation of walking through a Champion day at WCE! 

Ms. Sorrells Elementary choir put their spin on “We’re all in this Together” that featured the Wampus Cats and rocked it!! 

Mr. Nail’s Math Fact Fluency Champion students had a friendly Math Fact Fluency competition with the Board Members and District Leaders. Who won you ask?? The Champion Students of course!!  

To end the visit, Ms. Moyer’s students demonstrated their working model of the human eye where they used a magnifying lens as a model of the cornea to explore how the structure of the lens was related to the function of their eyes. The students paired up with Board members and District leaders to show them how it all worked. They were fantastic teachers! 

It was a wonderful experience at Woodrow Cummins Elementary and we are excited about all of the exciting things taking place for our students! 
Stay tuned for the next stop of the CPSD Road Trip! 11 More schools to Go!! 
#ChampionsForKids

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🚙 The 6th stop on the Conway School Board's "CPSD Road Trip" recently took place at Bob Courtway Middle School, where School Board Members and District leaders were warmly welcomed by exceptional students! Amidst the festivities, Board Member Jason Sandefer and Director of Safety Eric King joined students in some recess fun, showcasing their jump roping skills. Adding to the joy, Choir Teacher Ms. Shaw presented the incredible 7th-grade choir, whose enchanting performance immersed everyone in the holiday spirit. Notably, 7th Grade student Kemper shared her positive experience with the Courtway Choir, highlighting her outstanding leadership!

During the presentation, Ms. Smith delved into Courtway’s WIN (What I Need) Time, featuring a video showcasing students expressing how this personalized approach benefits them. Students shared sentiments like, "Every week looks different, but every week I get exactly what I need. When I receive what I need… I win! And I like to Win! When I Win, We all Win! We are Champions!"

Principal David Yates concluded the event by highlighting the positive happenings at Courtway Middle School, offering words of encouragement, and praising the exceptional efforts of the staff. Special mention was made of their culinary skills that contributed to a delightful Thanksgiving feast! It was truly a fantastic day at Courtway, and CPSD takes pride in the ongoing determination and hard work evident each day! #ChampionsForKids

School Board Members and District leaders were warmly greeted by the 4th-grade Jaguar Leaders. These exceptional students led the entire presentation, highlighting all the wonderful things happening at TJE. The TJE Choir, under the guidance of Ms. Johnson, did a remarkable job of immersing us in the holiday spirit.

The Pinnacle Program, led by Ms. Story, showcased their highly impressive Macy’s Day Parade Robots, with floats zooming around on their own. Additionally, they presented their cardboard Putt Putt courses and demonstrated the level of difficulty they had incorporated into them. The hard work of these students was truly showcased during this part of the presentation.

Ms. Lakey, TJE Instructional Facilitator, hosted a session of FUN & LEARNING, where students engaged in learning games with the School Board members and District Leaders. The excitement in the room was contagious, and the students were both having fun and learning.

A noteworthy highlight was the Staff Spotlight, where Principal Carise Echols recognized Ms. Massery for her thoughtfulness and going above and beyond to provide a care cart for students, offering access to everyday care items if needed.

Our District Leaders experienced a delightful surprise with the special guest appearance of THE TJE JAGUAR! School Board Members were honored with STUDENT-MADE Trophies, symbolizing their role as #ChampionsForKids. Special thanks to Principal Carise Echols and Assistant Principal Heath Dow for delivering an exceptional presentation of your campus!

text: CPSD In-District Transfers (waivers) for 2024-2025 School Year

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
In-District Transfers (waivers) for 2024-2025 School Year

-If your student (upcoming 1st-7th graders) is on a waiver this year, they are grandfathered in and you will not need to reapply unless you want them to attend a middle school not in your zone or you wish to change elementary school for next year

-Once your child is granted a transfer, you only need to reapply before they go to middle school or you wish to change schools

-Applications will be accepted through March 15 and will be processed after that date, we want to give our principals time to verify enrollment numbers to ensure we do not exceed capacity

-Applications will be granted in the order in which they are received and must be complete to be considered

-For all transfers, parents must be able to transport their student(s) 

-Transfers for incoming kindergarten students will be accepted once Kindergarten Registration is open

-Please use the following link to access the transfer application - https://www.conwayschools.org/page/registration

New Language:
Transfers-moving forward this term will be used rather than waiver, transfer refers to any student who would attend a school they are not zoned to attend

Capacity-each classroom and school must remain within the state-mandated enrollment count, for example: each kindergarten class can only have 20 students enrolled to one teacher or each 4th grade class can only have 28 students enrolled to one teacher

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟 Today, as the Solar Eclipse graces our skies, we're thrilled to share the excitement that's been building up in our town! Last week, in collaboration with UCA, Carolyn Lewis Elementary had the pleasure of hosting Morton Brown, a former UCA student and Arkansas native, who also happens to be the Artistic Director for the city of Philadelphia. Morton brought to life LUNA, a magnificent 25’ Solar Eclipse superhero sculpture, right here in our beloved town, in anticipation of today's COSMIC event! You may know of some of Mr. Brown's work as he has done murals in downtown Conway!

🌞 Huge thanks to Mr. Morton and UCA for their incredible efforts and the captivating presentation they shared with us! Not only did Mr. Morton gift Carolyn Lewis Elementary with a special drawing, but a group of our students also had the amazing opportunity to create Birthday Capes! Each student received a personalized chart depicting the sky on their exact birthdate. They meticulously plotted stars from the chart onto graph paper, then sewed them onto capes, forming unique constellations representing their birthdays.

✨ Today, LUNA takes center stage at the UCA Solar Eclipse event, marking this momentous occasion in the most spectacular way possible.  🌒 
#solareclipse2024 #ChampionsForKids

🚒Our Conway Area Career Center's EMT students successfully completed auto extrication with the help of Conway Fire Department and Steve's Auto!

During extrication, students learn techniques and tool usage on how to quickly and safely remove patients from vehicles involved in collisions, rollovers, and various types of impact. 

Extrication is the final component of the EMT class for National and State certification. Other components of the class are clinical hours on board an ambulance and inside an ER, as well as a grade in course work of at least an 80%.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Honoring Conway Public Schools School Board Member Mr. Bill Milburn

It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our school board member, Mr. Bill Milburn. Mr. Milburn has been a valued member of the Conway School Board since March 2024, and he also served during a previous term from October 2022 to May 2023. Our hearts and thoughts are with his family, friends, and the entire CPSD community during this time of grief. Mr. Milburn’s dedication and contributions will be remembered with deep appreciation.  

"We truly appreciate Mr. Milburn's service on the board.  His willingness to run for the board and be fully engaged and supportive was an incredible testament to his character and love for the district.  We will truly miss his presence and contribution as a board member.  We hope to carry on his legacy of leadership and service with our team.  He will be truly missed." - School Board President Dr. David Naylor Jr.

“It was a privilege and honor to serve with Bill Millburn on the board for Conway Public Schools. I enjoyed the time we spent together professionally and personally. He truly has a servant’s heart which is demonstrated by his years of public service, his dedication to his local church, love for his family, and his commitment to our community. He will be greatly missed and I extend my deepest condolences to his family and loved ones.” - School Board Vice President Trip Leach

“Bill Milburn was a man of great character!  He was solid in his faith, and there was no gray area for Bill when it came to what was right or wrong. We have lost an incredible board member and friend. Heaven has gained an angel! Rest in peace, my friend. You will be missed by all of us!” 
- School Board Secretary Linda Hargis

“I first became acquainted with Mr.  Bill Milburn when he was appointed to the School Board in 2022. Mr. Bill was always a very kind and gentle person. He brought value to our board because of his extensive background and experience in law enforcement along with his knowledge about safety and most importantly “School Safety.” He will be missed!” - School Board Member Andre Acklin

“Mr. Milburn was my neighbor at our board meetings. He shared stories and pictures with me of his grandchildren and especially his great grand. He was definitely a family man and loved them dearly. Thank you for your kinds words to me, thank you for your service to our community and to CPS. You will be missed! RIL” - School Board Member Sheila Franklin

“Within the short time that I had the privilege of serving on the board with Mr. Milburn, I quickly learned that he had such a huge heart and an absolute desire to keep our kids and staff safe. I learned of his common sense approach and his depth of knowledge from his years of public service. It was an honor serving with him.  An outstanding man who will be dearly missed.”
 - Former School Board Member Jason Sandefer

"Our hearts are very heavy and saddened by the loss of Mr. Bill Milburn, one of our recently elected Conway Public School District Board Members.  During the short time I served with him I was always impressed with his huge heart for all students, his thoughtfulness, and sincere dedication to "getting things done the right way."  He will be sincerely missed and our thoughts and prayers are with Mrs. Pam, his wife and the entire family during this time.” - Superintendent Dr. Jeff Collum.

text:
🌟 Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now? 🌟

We're kicking off our series with someone close to home—Katie Vinson! A proud CPSD  Class of 2007 alumna, Katie is now an 11th Grade English teacher at Conway High School, fulfilling her lifelong dream of teaching in the district she grew up in.

After graduating from CPSD, Katie attended the University of Arkansas at Fayetteville, majoring in English with an emphasis in Creative Writing. She then earned her Master of Arts in Teaching from UCA. Katie is married to fellow Wampus Cat alum, Thomas Vinson, and they have two children, Charlotte (7) and Payne (5). Katie’s excitement for her 12th year of teaching is evident as she steps into what she calls her "dream job."

Katie’s journey with CPSD began in Kindergarten at Jim Stone Elementary, where her passion for teaching started early. She would imitate her first-grade teacher by drawing stars on papers, just like her teacher did. In high school, she participated in band, played clarinet, and was a varsity dance team member, serving as captain her senior year. A highlight for Katie was taking a class called Education as a Profession, where she observed one of her former English teachers, Mrs. Paglianite, confirming her path to becoming an English teacher.

Her favorite teacher? Debbie Hibbs, who made AP Lang an unforgettable experience and inspired Katie with her incredible teaching methods.

Katie’s advice for current CPSD students? "Your teachers are there to help you. One teacher can make all the difference in your school journey. Take risks, put yourself out there, and get involved! If you find a job you truly love, you'll never work a day in your life."

Join us in celebrating Katie’s journey and the remarkable educators shaping our future Wampus Cats! 💙🤍

text:
🌟 Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now? 🌟

This week, we’re proud to feature Doneshia Boyd (Moore), CPSD Class of 2009!

Doneshia followed in her parents' footsteps, Dennis and LuVeta Moore, by attending the University of Central Arkansas, where she earned a Bachelor’s in Business Administration. Her career started at UCA, eventually transitioning into HR. Today, she’s the Manager of Talent Acquisition at Acxiom, leading the Early Career and University Relations team, helping students launch careers in STEM. Doneshia’s dedication shines through—she's a 2023 Conway Area Leadership Institute graduate and serves on the boards of the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and the Boys and Girls Club of Faulkner County.

She married the love of her life, Derrick Boyd, in 2020, and together they have two beautiful daughters, Demi and Skylen. But that’s not all—Doneshia is also the Founder and Owner of Soirée Rentals, an event rental business offering unique pieces for any occasion. Her commitment to her family, church, and community is unwavering, and she credits God for guiding her every step of the way.

Reflecting on CPSD, Doneshia cherishes her time at JLME, CSMS, CJHS, and CHS. She was a key player in basketball, helping her team win the 1st 7A Girls Basketball title her sophomore year. She also received the Dandra Thomas True Blue Award her senior year. Field days, honor rolls, and being an honor graduate are treasured memories. 

When it comes to teachers, Doneshia has several favorites: Mrs. Bray, Ms. Sowers, and Coach Irons all played a significant role in her education and development.

Her advice for students? "Your teachers and staff are there to help you. Listen, learn, and grow. Be sure to handle the things you can and ask for help when needed."

Join us in celebrating Doneshia's achievements and her ongoing impact on Conway! 💙🤍

#WeAreWampusCats #Ascend #AscendToExcellence #CPSDascends #WampusCatWednesday #WhereAreTheyNow

Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now? 🕰️✨

This week’s spotlight is on Anthony Nail, Class of 2010! 🎓⚾

Anthony is marking his 11th year as a teacher and coach, currently in his 2nd year as the head baseball coach at Gentry High School. His coaching career has also included 6 years as the head baseball/head golf coach at Ouachita High School, a year as assistant baseball/head tennis coach at Sheridan High School, and 2 years as assistant baseball and 1 year as head golf coach at Marion High School.

Reflecting on his CPSD days:
Anthony looks back with gratitude for the incredible educators who taught him to think critically rather than just follow instructions. CHS Baseball coaches Noel Boucher, Barry Lueders, and Ryan Reed left a lasting impact, shaping his love for the game and life itself. He recalls the excitement of cheering on his classmates at football games and supporting every volleyball and basketball game during his high school years.

One of his fondest memories? Throwing baby powder in the air during the 2009 starting lineup introductions to create a dramatic effect. 🚀

Favorite Teacher Highlight:
Anthony’s favorite teacher was Jim Owen, whose dynamic approach to teaching history made it feel alive and engaging. Jim’s memorable “Owenisms” and his lesson on using our “B.S. detectors” are still relevant today, especially in an age of misinformation.

Advice for Current Students:
“Enjoy your time as a Wampus Cat—the years go by faster than you think. The friendships you make from kindergarten through 12th grade are some of the best you’ll ever have, so make an effort to stay in touch after graduation.”

Thank you, Anthony, for sharing your journey and inspiring us all! 🌟👏

text: Important Safety Update 09-20-24

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Update Message: Sent 09-20-24

Conway Public School Community, 

Please read both of these important messages regarding School Safety information related to Conway Public Schools. Please know that we continue to make the safety of our students and staff the number one priority. 

We understand there has been some confusion surrounding recent articles about threats involving Carl Stuart Middle School. Please know that the information being circulated relates to an incident that occurred three years ago. It is unrelated to the recent situation affecting our district.

The email sent to parents and staff by Conway Public Schools referred to an anonymous, statewide threat that has been circulating for the past week, which has reached some students in our district. The message did not target any specific school or district, and we want to assure you that there have been no direct threats made against Carl Stuart Middle School or any other school in Conway Public Schools at this time.

While there is no specific threat to our schools at this time, we are taking all necessary precautions and working closely with the Conway Police Department to monitor the situation. Below is the message that was sent to parents and staff on 09-19-24:

Email Message sent 09-19-24
Dear Conway Public Schools,

We want to make you aware of a situation impacting several school districts across Arkansas. Over the past few weeks, an anonymous threatening message has been circulating, unfortunately reaching students in our district. As always, Conway Public Schools takes any and all threats seriously, and we are handling this matter with the utmost care and attention.

Our district remains highly vigilant, and will continue working closely with local law enforcement to ensure the safety of our students and staff. We want to remind everyone that threats made against schools are treated with the highest level of seriousness. Any students found responsible for such threats and/or sharing these types of messages will face school-based disciplinary action and legal consequences.

We encourage you to take a moment to discuss with your student the serious consequences of making or sharing harmful threats. These actions cause alarm and disrupt the learning environment. Please remind your student to immediately inform school personnel if they come across any concerning messages or situations.

Thank you for your cooperation and commitment to keeping our schools safe. As always, please feel free to contact CPSD with any questions, concerns, or information.

Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

After a remarkable 30-year career teaching high school history and economics at Conway High, Cindy transitioned into a new role as a ghostwriter, crafting memoirs for multimillionaires. She also serves on the Faulkner County Museum Board and the Faulkner County Historical Society board. An accomplished author, Cindy has published several books and edits the FCHS journal.

Her favorite teacher? Sherry Henderson. Cindy's advice to current CPSD students? "Soak up all the education you can."

Let’s celebrate Cindy's incredible journey from CPSD to a fulfilling career and her continued contributions to our community! 💙🤍

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣Mr. Bart Dooley, Music Teacher at Marguerite Vann Elementary is a CPSD CORE VALUE CHAMPION! 🏆🚾

"Of the many Vann teachers working diligently to uphold our shared values in the work that they do, Mr. Bart Dooley is certainly one to note.  He demonstrates his commitment to excellence in everything he does.  He is organized in his planning, thorough in his communication, and a creative genius.  Mr. Dooley provides innovative educational opportunities inside and outside of his classroom.  His lessons provide all students with the opportunity to learn about music, listen to music, and most importantly, make music.  His classroom is rarely silent as students are encouraged to make a joyful noise with instruments and their voices.  Outside of the classroom Mr. Dooley’s students have the opportunity to participate in grade level musical productions (complete with impressive costumes & set designs), join the Vann Voices choir, sing the national anthem at sporting events, perform at Toad Suck Daze and other city festivals, visit nursing homes, entertain peers at Vann’s annual student talent showcase, join friends and family in holiday caroling, and entertain at the state Capitol.  Students in Mr. Dooley’s class are embraced by a safe and caring environment in which they are challenged to try new things, discover their talents, and learn the value of practice in order to master new skills. Mr. Dooley’s positive attitude is infectious, brightening the days of his students and his colleagues.  His gifts of hospitality and encouragement help make Vann a wonderful place to teach and learn.  Above all, Mr. Dooley’s “students first” mindset guides his actions and makes him a tremendously important part of the Vann team and a Core Values Champion indeed." - Vann Employees 

Mr. Dooley! Thank you for your work and dedication to being a #ChampionForKids and continuing to help our district #AscendtoExcellence!

This week, we’re excited to spotlight Koni Garrett Wade, Class of 1980!

Koni moved to Phoenix after 10 years in welding at Virco and transitioned into law enforcement, earning a degree while working with the Phoenix PD and at the men’s prison. After five years, she started a successful 26-year career in sales, specializing in mobile veterinary clinics and police command trucks, achieving #1 sales for 24 of those years. Koni is married to Jim Wade, a retired special education teacher, and they have one daughter, Amra, and a grandson, Lucas. After 30 years away, Koni recently moved back to Conway and is thrilled to be home!

School Memories:
Koni loved Conway schools, starting with Mrs. Wilson in 1st grade. She made many lasting friendships.

Personal Highlights:
Koni received awards in business classes and was recognized in the school newsletter for being the only female in Mr. Brice’s refrigeration and repair classes.

Favorite Teacher:
Mr. Bill Brice.

Advice for Students:
“ENJOY IT! Once you’re an adult, you don’t get those summers off!”

Additional Thoughts:
“I love my Conway, my Wampus Cats, and live life like tomorrow won’t happen!”

Join us in celebrating Koni’s inspiring journey from CPSD to a successful career in sales and her return to Conway! 💙🤍

text:
🌟 Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now? 🌟
This week, we’re excited to spotlight Lavonne Riggins, Class of 2015!

Lavonne is currently pursuing her Master’s in Wind Conducting at UCA under the guidance of Dr. Michael Hancock. She previously taught at Little Rock Central High School as an assistant band director, teaching sectional classes, jazz band, and more. After graduating in May 2025, Lavonne plans to return to teaching high school band.

School Memories:
Heavily involved in band, color guard, Caring Cats, and Student Council, Lavonne found her place in music. Band was the one place she felt she truly belonged and could be herself. Because of that, she worked to become a music teacher, believing she could create opportunities for students just like the ones she was given. A standout memory is the 2013 Fall band show, “365,” where her band won every single award at every contest!

Personal Highlights:
Lavonne performed at Pearl Harbor and marched in the Macy’s Parade with the National Band Directors Band, representing Arkansas as 1 of only 2 chosen directors.

Favorite Teachers:
Mrs. Martha Reynolds and Mrs. Shelia Brooks were both major influences. Mrs. Reynolds made learning fun, even meeting Lavonne after graduation for life chats, while Mrs. Brooks helped guide her toward becoming a music teacher.

Advice for Students:
“Spend your time wisely and do something you LOVE. You’ll miss high school!”

Join us in celebrating Lavonne’s musical journey and her bright future in education! 💙🤍

#WeAreWampusCats #Ascend #AscendToExcellence #CPSDascends #WampusCatWednesday #WhereAreTheyNow

She was part of the ASBOA All-State Symphonic Band, performed in the Spring Musicals, and visited Disney World with the CHS Band, sparking her love for travel. She’s now visited 13 countries with her husband.

All of her band and choir directors, including Tim & Jan Cunningham, Todd Johnson, Dewayne Wilson, and others, had a profound impact.

Advice for Students:
“Find an elective, sports team, or student organization/club to join! These activities elevate your educational experience!”

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📢🎶 The Conway High & Junior High School Choirs are proud to announce that several of their talented students have earned coveted spots in the prestigious American Choral Directors Association (ACDA) National Honor Choir 🎤✨, which took place this past week in Dallas, Texas 🇺🇸. These exceptional students joined other outstanding young singers from across the country to perform in one of the most esteemed choral events in the nation.

🎼 The ACDA National Honor Choir provides a unique opportunity for top-tier student vocalists to work with renowned conductors 👨‍🎤🎵, rehearse challenging music 🎶, and perform at a national level 🌟. The event is a testament to the hard work, dedication, and musical excellence 🎼👏 displayed by these students throughout the year.

💙 We congratulate the following students who earned a spot in the choir:

🏅 Caroline Chrysler – 11th grade
🏅 Hadassah Smith – 11th grade
🏅 Emerie Thurow – 10th grade
🏅 Addison Roth – 10th grade
🏅 Jacob Barnes – 9th grade
🏅 Ainsley Barnett – 9th grade
🏅 Aryana Tyler-Hashemi – 9th grade

🗣️🎶 “We are incredibly proud of these students and their remarkable achievement,” said Sam Huskey and Kayla White, Choral Directors at Conway High and Junior High School. “This opportunity to perform at the national level is a testament to their talent, passion for music, and commitment to excellence. They represented our school with pride in Dallas.” 🎵💫

🌍🎤 The ACDA National Honor Choir offers a once-in-a-lifetime experience for young musicians, providing a platform for them to further develop their vocal skills 🎶 while connecting with peers and mentors from across the nation. This honor not only highlights their individual abilities but also showcases the outstanding choral program 🎼🏫 at Conway Public Schools.

👏🎉 Congratulations to these incredible students! 🎶🏅🎤

#CPSChoirs #WampusCatPride #ConwayPublicSchools #GoWampusCats #ACDAHonorChoir #MusicExcellence 🎶💙
#ChampionForKids #CPSDascends #Ascend #AscendtoExcellence #WampusCats #6legs

🎉 CPSD Receives $2,500 Grant for Backpack Food Program! 🎒🍎

Conway Public Schools has been awarded a $2,500 grant from the Arkansas Community Foundation to support our backpack food program! This initiative helps fight food insecurity by providing nutritious, easy-to-prepare meals for students to take home.

A huge thank you to Ms. Lani Jennings-Hall, board member of the Arkansas Community Foundation, for visiting and presenting this generous donation to our district and building leaders. 🙌 These funds will go toward purchasing food items and backpacks, ensuring that more students have consistent access to healthy meals outside of school hours.

We are grateful for this support in helping remove barriers to learning and care for the whole child! 💙🐾 #ChampionForKids #CPSDascends #Ascend #AscendtoExcellence #WampusCats #6legs

text:
🏆Dr. Randi House, 4th Grade Teacher at Theodore Jones Elementary School, is a CPSD CORE VALUE CHAMPION! 🏆 

Dr. House exemplifies what it means to be a dedicated, passionate, and innovative educator. After many successful years of teaching kindergarten, she bravely stepped out of her comfort zone and embraced a new challenge by teaching 4th grade for the first time this year. And she is absolutely rocking it.

Dr. House has transformed the 4th grade classroom into a vibrant and engaging learning environment. She brings creativity and excitement to the curriculum, ensuring that every lesson is not only rigorous but also meaningful and fun. Her students are thriving under her instruction, and the data speaks for itself. Significant growth in writing and academic performance clearly reflects the effectiveness of her teaching.

What makes Dr. House truly special is her unwavering commitment to student success, her willingness to grow professionally, and her courage to take on new challenges with grace and excellence. Her transition from kindergarten to 4th grade is a testament to her adaptability, leadership, and dedication to our district’s core values.

Dr. Randi House is more than deserving of this recognition. She is a true champion in every sense of the word.

We appreciate you Dr. House! Thank you for all you do for students and staff!! #ChampionForKids #CPSDascends #AscendtoExcellence #CoreValueChampion

Her relentless pursuit of excellence is evident in everything she does, and she truly embodies the core values of our school. 🌟  Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now? 🌟
Meet Straisley Dubois, Conway High Class of 2015!

After graduation, Straisley stayed true to her Wampus Cat roots and is still living in Conway, working as an Occupational Therapy Assistant at Pediatrics Plus. 💙

During her time at CPSD, she made lifelong friendships and was guided by incredible teachers—especially her favorite, Mr. Terrell—who helped shape her path forward. 🙌

A few highlights from her journey? Graduating with honors, attending three colleges, earning two degrees debt-free, and persevering through two brain surgeries while still showing up every day to serve kids with heart and purpose. 🧠💪

Her advice for current students?
“You don’t have to know right now what you want to be as an adult… If one path doesn’t feel right, don’t be scared to take another.”

Straisley proves that success isn’t always about leaving your hometown—sometimes it’s about building a life right where your roots run deep. 🏡💫

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🌟Wampus Cat Wednesday: Where Are They Now 🌟

Meet Joey Slayton, proud member of the Conway High Class of 1989!

Joey is still rooted right here in Conway, serving and protecting the next generation of Wampus Cats as a School Resource Officer at Marguerite Vann and Carl Stuart Middle School. He's been with the Conway Police Department since 2012 and began his work as an SRO in 2014—giving back to the same district that helped shape him.

His favorite CPSD memories?
⚾ Winning the State Baseball Championship in 1989
🧰 Auto mechanics class 
🚪 Wooden lockers and getting lost in the old building!

Some personal highlights include being named All-State, earning his brick at the field, and passing Mr. Owens’ history class! He also made lifelong friendships that still matter today.

Joey gives a shoutout to some unforgettable teachers—Coach Boucher, Coach Leuders, and Mr. Owens—who each played a role in his journey.

His advice to today’s students is simple but powerful:
“Treat others with respect. The Golden Rule is still one that works. Embrace silence to get away from the noise. Get outside and off the screen. Live every day to the fullest.”

And one last reflection?
“I didn’t care much about school back then—my dad had to make a deal with me just to go to college. But looking back, high school was one of the highlights of my life. I’m honored to now serve my alma mater.”

💙Thank you, Officer Slayton, for your dedication to Conway and for continuing to lead with heart and hometown pride. 

#WampusCatWednesday #WeAreWampusCats #Ascend #AscendToExcellence #CPSDascends

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🏆 We are thrilled to share that two incredible teachers from Carl Stuart Middle School have been selected as 2025 Mental Health Champion Award recipients by Arisa Health! 💙

Congratulations to Jonathan Gunsolus and Charles “Chuck” German, who were chosen out of more than 110 educators nominated across dozens of Arkansas counties for their unwavering dedication to student well-being.

Mr. Gunsolus, "Mr. G", was recognized for his deep connections with students, his leadership in the D3 (Discipline, Determination, Dreams) program, and the way he encourages and supports students daily—whether it’s mentoring, playing soccer, gardening, or simply being a listening ear.

Mr. German was honored for his years of mentorship work, founding both the D3 and G3 programs that now impact nearly 200 students with the help of 10 staff mentors. His focus on character development, community service, and leadership has made a powerful and lasting difference on campus.

We are incredibly proud of these two Wampus Cat educators for being Champions for Kids in every sense of the word! 👏

🌟 A National Honor for One of Our Own! 🌟

In January, it was announced that Ms. Blake Tinsley, Conway High School teacher, was selected to receive the Presidential Award for Excellence in Mathematics and Science Teaching (PAEMST)—the highest honor bestowed by the U.S. government specifically for K–12 STEM educators. 🏅

We celebrated Ms. Tinsley at our February Conway School Board Meeting, and just last week, she was formally recognized by the Arkansas Department of Education at the State Board Meeting in Little Rock. 📍

This prestigious award reflects Ms. Tinsley's outstanding teaching, innovation, and dedication to student success in science and mathematics. We are beyond proud to have her represent Conway Public Schools at the national level! 💙👏

Help us celebrate Ms. Tinsley and this incredible achievement!

text: Dear CPS Staff,Recently the Board and Mr. Black asked the C&I team to work toward making additional resources available to our teachers in order to better support instruction. Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear CPSD Employee,Thank you so everyone who has filled out our survey so far. Our Employee Engagement survey is still open and will be until tomorrow, Friday, August 8th at 10:00am. At Conway Public Schools, we are committed to creating a district where staff feel heard, supported, and empowered to grow. As part of our information gathering, we’re asking every CPSD employee to take a few minutes to complete an important survey.This survey is designed to give us a clear picture of how you felt about your work environment, communication, leadership, collaboration, and professional growth during the 2024–2025 school year. Please answer the questions with last school year in mind, even if your leadership has changed since then.Your responses are completely confidential and will not be linked to any individual in any way. Your honest feedback will help us identify areas of strength and opportunities for growth as we work together to build a stronger future for our district.The results will be used to recognize successes and guide improvements where needed, both at the district and campus levels. author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Parents & Guardians,Thank you to everyone who has filled out our survey so far.  Our Parent/Guardian Satisfaction  survey is still open and will be until tomorrow, Friday, August 8th at 10:00am. At Conway Public Schools, we believe strong schools are built through partnership—and that begins with listening to the voices of our families.As part of our information gathering, we are inviting parents and guardians to complete a short, completely confidential survey to help us better understand your experience with our schools and our district.Please answer the survey based on your experiences during the 2024–2025 school year. This will help us establish a clear baseline as we evaluate areas such as communication, leadership, and the overall effectiveness of your child’s school environment.Once the survey results are collected, we will share a summary of key findings with the community and use your input to guide meaningful improvements across the district.<span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-size: 11pt; box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; appearance: none; border: 0px; background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre

text: 🇺🇸 An Honor to Begin the Year 🇺🇸At our Back-to-School Convocation, we were deeply honored to be led in the Pledge of Allegiance by Retired United States Air Force Captain Floyd Brantley.Born in 1925, Captain Brantley’s life is a remarkable story of service, sacrifice, and perseverance—from serving as a Navy corpsman in World War II, to flying in Korea with the Air Force, to devoting decades to education and publishing. With 23 years of military service and a lifetime of impact, he continues to inspire us all.We are grateful to have Captain Brantley as part of our Conway community and thankful for the example he sets for our students and staff. ❤️💙#WeAreCPSD #WeAreConway #BackToSchool #WampusCatNation #ChampionsForKids #LittleCats #CPSD #WampusCats

author: Conway Public Schools
text: The Hispanic Heritage Festival was held at Laurel Park on September 6th. This event is a community-wide celebration of Hispanic heritage. Conway Public Schools was thrilled to be invited to host a booth there. Several members of our Conway Public Schools ESOL team were present along with Assistant Superintendent Bryce Bennett, Interim Superintendent Jason Black, ESOL Instructional Facilitator Melinda Fraser, and CHS TOY and District TOY Kait Smith. CPS hosted a table where we gave out Conway Wampus cat shirts and items that were donated by local schools. We also created an art display where we showcased art from several Conway Public Schools campuses. Art teachers created projects with students to celebrate Hispanic heritage and the top five pieces of art were chosen to be on put display. Community members were able to scan a QR code and vote for their favorite student artwork. Those winners will be celebrated in the coming weeks. Conway Public Schools was honored to have representation at the festival and we look forward to our continued partnership with the Hispanic community.

Today is a very special day! It's Conway Public School's Organization Day!
On October 3, 1878, our district officially began its journey of educating generations. That means Conway Public Schools is celebrating its 147th birthday! 🎈📚

We are so proud of our incredible students, staff, and community, both past and present, for building this incredible legacy. Here's to many more years of excellence!

In the picture, you can see a rendering of Conway's Little Green Building, the first public school in Conway, AR.
(Source: "Faulkner County Its Land and People" by the Faulkner County Historical Society)

text:
🚌 School Bus Safety Starts with YOU!Whether you’re a Wampus Cat riding the bus or a driver sharing the road, everyone plays a part in keeping our students safe. 💛💙For Students:
🐾 Arrive at your stop 10 minutes early
🐾 Stay back at least 10 feet from the curb
🐾 Wait for your driver’s signal before crossing
🐾 Use the handrail when boarding
🐾 Stay seated and face forward
🐾 Keep noise down — no distracting behaviorFor Drivers:
🚗 Stop for flashing red lights
🚗 Slow down in school zones
🚗 Watch for crossing students
🚗 Never pass a stopped bus
🚗 Be patient — safety comes first!Thank you for helping protect our Wampus Cats every day. Together, we make the ride to school a safe one! 🐾#BusSafetyWeek #WampusCatPride #SchoolBusSafetyStartsWithYou

text: 💙 Principal Carise Echols – Theodore Jones ElementaryToday, we’re highlighting Mrs. Carise Echols, Principal of Theodore Jones Elementary“What I enjoy most about being a Principal is the kids, hands down. text: 💙 Principal Marquis Rogers – Conway Junior High SchoolAs we continue celebrating National Principals Month, today we’re proud to highlight Mr. Marquis Rogers, Principal of Conway Junior High School!For Mr. Rogers, the best part of being a principal is the unpredictability of each day—and the opportunity it brings to make a meaningful impact on students and staff. Every morning is a new chance to connect, inspire, and help others grow.A proud graduate of Conway Schools, Mr. Rogers says returning as principal is deeply personal: “Conway Junior High is a special place with a tradition of excellence, and I’m honored to continue building on that strong foundation alongside our students, staff, and families.”He and his wife, April, who owns April Rogers Law PLLC, are raising their two children—Daniel, a first grader, and Aria Kaye, a kindergartener—right here in Conway Schools. His love for this community runs deep, and his leadership reflects that same commitment to every student’s success.A former college football player at the University of Arkansas at Monticello (and a twin!), Mr. Rogers brings energy, teamwork, and focus to everything he does. His guiding belief: “Students thrive when they are challenged in a safe and supportive environment where their individual strengths are recognized and celebrated.”Beyond the classroom, Conway Junior High’s strong sense of community shines through programs like the Cat Nation Christmas Program, which provides gifts for students in need, and the Backpack Program, which ensures families have meals and snacks over the weekend.💙 Join us in celebrating Mr. Marquis Rogers for his leadership, his heart for students, and his dedication to making Conway Junior High a place where every student feels valued, supported, and inspired. Celebrate Mr. Rogers in the comments or send him a note of appreciation here:conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/staff-celebrations

text: 💙 Principal Dr. Kate Worley – Conway High SchoolAs we end National Principal’s Month, we’re proud to highlight Dr. Kate Worley, Principal of Conway High School!For Dr. Worley, being a principal is all about serving others. She finds the greatest joy in creating opportunities for students they might not have otherwise and supporting teachers and staff so they can thrive in their work. “It’s rewarding to see the positive impact these efforts have on both individuals and our school community as a whole,” she says.Her favorite quote, from Theodore Roosevelt, reminds her to stay dedicated and courageous in the work: “It is not the critic who counts... The credit belongs to the man who is actually in the arena.”A former college softball player at UCA, Dr. Worley brings the same determination, teamwork, and passion to leading Conway High. She’s also a proud wife and mom to a precious 2-year-old, and she loves the balance of family life and leadership.Under her leadership, Conway High School continues to thrive through innovative programs like the Conway Area Career Center, which offers outstanding career and technical education opportunities for students across multiple districts. CHS also takes great pride in its Special Olympics program, which unites special education and general education students to experience teamwork, friendship, and sportsmanship together.💙 Join us in celebrating Dr. Kate Worley for her servant leadership, her heart for students, and her dedication to helping every Wampus Cat succeed—both in school and in life! Show your appreciation for Dr. Worley in the comments or send her a note here:conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/staff-celebrations

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

text: Dear Simon Families,I wanted to personally share an update as I begin a transition over the next two weeks. I will be moving into the role of Head Boys Basketball Coach at Conway High School. Before coming to Simon, I spent seven years coaching at Conway Junior High, and my passion for this program and our student-athletes has always remained strong. I am grateful for the opportunity to return to this work and continue serving students and our community in a different capacity.This new chapter is exciting, but it also comes with mixed emotions. My time at Simon has meant so much to me. Serving this incredible school community has been one of the greatest honors of my career, and I will always be thankful for the students, families, and staff who make Simon such a special place.I am thrilled that Mrs. Branch will be stepping into the role of Principal. She is an outstanding leader who cares deeply about students and staff, and she brings both the skill and the heart needed to guide Simon forward. I have complete confidence in her ability to continue the strong traditions and values that define this school.Over the next two weeks, I will be working closely with Mrs. Branch to ensure a smooth and steady transition so that the school continues moving forward without interruption.Thank you for your trust, support, and partnership. I deeply value the relationships built during my time at Simon, and I will always believe in the great things happening here.With appreciation and pride,Joey Moon

text: CPSD Team!We are excited to announce that our district has earned a “B” rating from the Arkansas Department of Education in the latest state accountability report!This achievement is a direct reflection of the dedication, hard work, and heart of our incredible teachers, staff, students, and families. Every classroom, every grade level, and every campus contributed to this success — and we are proud to celebrate this accomplishment together as one Conway Schools team!Our ‘B’ rating shows that great things are happening every day in Conway Public Schools.  It represents the passion our educators bring to their classrooms, the effort our students put into learning, and the support our families provide. I am so proud of what we’ve accomplished together — and even more excited about where we’re headed next.The Arkansas Department of Education assigns district ratings based on factors like student achievement, academic growth, and graduation rates. Our strong results across these areas highlight the district’s ongoing focus on student success and continuous improvement.This rating is something to celebrate. It takes all of us — teachers, staff, parents, and community members — working together to make our district the special place it is. We are grateful for every person who helps make learning come alive for our students each day.While we’re proud of our “B” rating, we know this is just one step in our ongoing journey toward excellence. Together, we’ll keep striving, growing, and aiming for that “A” — because our students deserve the best!Enjoy your weekend! Only 5 more days until a break. text:
🌱 We are thrilled to announce that Carolyn Lewis Elementary has been awarded the 2025 Harvest Community Partnership Garden of the Year! 🌱

This recognition means so much to our school, and we are incredibly proud of the hard work, care, and dedication that made our garden flourish this year.

We are especially thankful for our amazing partnership with Krista Quinn and the Faulkner County Extension Office, the wonderful Mr. Richard Clerk and the Master Gardeners, as well as Kelli Burke who continually support, guide, and encourage our students. Their expertise and willingness to invest in our school garden have helped create meaningful, hands-on learning opportunities for our kids.

A huge heartfelt thank-you goes to Mrs. Tyler and Mrs. Parham—your passion, time, and sacrifice are the heartbeat of this project. Because of your leadership and commitment, our students not only learn about gardening, but also about teamwork, responsibility, and the joy of watching something grow.

Thank you to everyone who has supported our garden. This award is a celebration of community, collaboration, and the belief that great things can grow when we work together. Thank you to Leslee Tell from the Arkansas Department of Agriculture coming to present this award to us!🌿💚

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Coach Buck James
Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame Inductee CPSD recognized Coach Buck James at our December School Board Meeting for being inducted into the Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame! It is stated that Coach James boasts one of the state's most successful high school coaching careers. With head coaching jobs at Star City, Camden Fairview, Bryant and now Conway, James has led teams to seven state championships -- one in Class 5A at Camden Fairview (2012) and a record five consecutive in Class 7A at Bryant (2018-22). In six seasons with the Hornets, he compiled a 68-9 record. He has earned 14 conference coach of the year awards and guided his teams to 13 conference titles.  Conway is known for having the best of the best. Here is a list of Wampus Cats who are in the Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame: Peyton Hillis, Tim Horton, Marvin Delph, Lawson Pilgrim, Henry Hawk, Raymond Bright, Ken Stephens, Bryce Molder, Ray Rogers, Willis Watkins, and now Buck James. Please help us congratulate Coach James!

text:
🎙️ On the Radio This Morning — Two Special Guests! 🎙️This morning, we were excited to welcome Conway High School teacher Ms. Casey Griffith and Senior Wren Welky to the radio to talk about all things CHS Debate/Forensics, including the incredible success of their Mock Trial State Champion team and their busy competition schedule across Arkansas and beyond.They also have major highlights to share from the 57th Arkansas Student Congress on Human Relations State Tournament, where CHS students earned outstanding recognition at the state level. Arkansas Student Congress, the oldest model legislative event in the state, gives students a powerful opportunity to experience the democratic process through caucuses, committees, and floor debates at the State Capitol.🏆 2025 Arkansas Student Congress Honors for Conway High School include:
 • Multiple Superior and Excellence awards across caucus, committee, floor debate, and parliamentary procedure
 • CHS Best Delegate: Ian Lee-Kim
 • Highest Scoring Delegate (House I): Ian Lee-Kim
 • Melinda Valdez-Milloway Award: Ian Lee-Kim
 • Tournament Overall Delegation: 2nd Place — Conway High School
 • Numerous Best Delegation, Best Bill, and Bill Passed recognitions across House I, II, and III
Check out more information here: https://www.conwayschools.org/article/2648554All CHS Student Congress participants are members of the CHS Speech & Debate Team, coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith, and their achievements reflect months of preparation, collaboration, and leadership.👏 We are incredibly proud of these students and their dedication to excellence, civic engagement, and academic competition.📻 Be sure to tune in every Wednesday morning at 7:30 AM to hear more amazing stories and updates from Conway Public Schools on the radio!#WampusCatPride #WeAreCPSD #CHSDebate #SpeechAndDebate #StudentLeadership #MockTrial #ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCatsOnAir

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Theodore Jones Elementary Principal, Carise Echols, recently traveled to Washington, D.C., to advocate for public education on Capitol Hill. Mrs. Echols met with U.S. Senators, Representatives, and congressional staff to ensure the voices of elementary and middle-level principals and the students they serve are represented in national conversations.

In her capacity as the upcoming NAESP State Representative for Arkansas, she joined education leaders from across the country to advocate for policies that directly support students, educators, and schools nationwide.

During her visit, she engaged in discussions with members of Congress regarding:
• Increased special education funding
• School-based health supports
• Expanded access to early childhood education
• Educator retention efforts
• Mental health resources for educators and students“Every decision made at the federal level eventually impacts our state and our classrooms. I wanted to ensure the voices of our students, educators, and community were represented in those conversations. My role is to make sure our students and staff have the support they need to thrive each day, and that responsibility does not stop at the doors of our school. Any opportunity to speak on behalf of our schools whether locally or nationally is simply an extension of that commitment to the children and families we serve.” - Mrs. Echols

We are proud of Mrs. Echols for representing our district, our state, and most importantly our students at the federal level!!

text: Staff Committed to Excellence: three of our music teachers presented professional development sessions for fellow music educators across the state this past weekend at the Arkansas All-State Music Conference in Hot Springs.Casey Buck (orchestra teacher at Conway High School and Carl Stuart Middle) led a session titled "The Science of (Sight-) Reading" for the Arkansas chapter of the American String Teachers Association. The session included strategies for developing more fluent music readers, based on the latest research and the statewide Science of Reading initiative. Mr. Buck also represented instrumental music students across the state at several board meetings of the Arkansas School Band and Orchestra Association, and was reelected Arkansas State Orchestra chair, a position he has held since 2019.Elementary music teachers Bart Dooley (Marguerite Vann) and Felix Guzman (Ellen Smith) co-presented a session entitled "Unlocking the Recorder: More than B-A-G." They shared their expertise to a room full of fellow general music teachers on behalf of the Arkansas Music Educators Association, the state chapter of the National Association for Music Education.Incredible educators at CPSD!! text:
The CHS Mock Trial team is the 2026 Arkansas High School Mock Trial STATE CHAMPIONS!!! Help us Congratulate them!!

Congratulations to the Conway High School Mock Trial team for winning the 2026 Arkansas High School Mock Trial State Tournament!!! The tournament, sponsored by the Arkansas Bar Association, was held February 27-28, 2026, in Little Rock at the Richard Sheppard Arnold United States Courthouse. Mock trial is an academic and competitive simulation of a trial-level court proceeding, where students act as attorneys and witnesses to argue a fictional criminal or civil case. Teams analyze a provided case packet, develop legal theories, and follow simplified rules of evidence to compete in courtrooms.Twenty-one teams from across Arkansas gathered to try the civil case of Justice Miller v. Jace Talent Agency. 

The team competed in four preliminary rounds against Parkview, Bentonville West, Des Arc, and then the final round against Little Rock Central High School. Conway was the only team to go undefeated, with no dropped ballots. The team also earned Star Attorney & Star Witness awards. Out of over 100 attorneys, the tournament awards the top 7 attorneys in the 4 prelim rounds. Katharine Welky and Addison Choate were named Star Attorneys. This is the 2nd year for Addison Choate to be named a Star Attorney. The tournament awards the top 5 witnesses, and Annabel Champlin and Naomi Brooks brought home 2 of the Star Witness Awards. 

The CHS team will be the team to represent Arkansas at the National High School Mock Trial Championships in May. They will travel to Des Moines, IA, to compete against the top team from each state, along with South Korea, Guam, and Northern Mariana Islands. 

All members of the CHS Mock Trial Team are members of the CHS Speech & Debate Team and are coached by Mrs. Casey Griffith. The team is also coached by volunteer attorney coach, Mr. Matt Brown.

text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We’re sharing the final video in our series about third grade promotion under the Arkansas LEARNS Act, and we want to thank you for taking the time to stay informed and engaged in your child’s education.In this video, Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, addresses an important question many families have asked:What happens if a student does not meet the 3rd grade reading standard?In this video, you’ll learn:What the state requires for 3rd grade promotionWhat “good-cause exemptions” are and when they applyWhat happens if a student is not promoted to 4th gradeThe additional supports provided for all students who need themBeginning with the 2025–2026 school year, students must meet the state’s reading standard (Level 2 or higher on the ATLAS ELA assessment) or qualify for a good-cause exemption to be promoted. If a student does not meet these requirements, they may be retained in 3rd grade.We understand this can feel concerning, but please know: retention is not the first option. Our district provides continuous, targeted support throughout the year, and our goal is always promotion with proficiency.Students who are promoted through a good-cause exemption or retained will receive additional support, including:Intensive, targeted reading instructionPlacement with highly qualified teachersAn at-home reading planOngoing literacy interventionsImportant Reminder: ATLAS Literacy Testing is scheduled for April 14–15. Families can expect results very soon after testing, along with communication about next steps. Students who score at Level 1 may have an opportunity for additional tutoring and retesting.We are committed to keeping you informed every step of the way. You can continue to monitor your child’s progress through the ATLAS Family Portal, atlasportal.org/families.html and your child’s teacher or principal is always available to answer questions and provide support.Watch the final video here: CPSD 3rd Grade Promotion Information Video 3To watch Videos 1 & 2:CPSD 3rd Grade Promotion Information Video 1CPSD 3rd Grade Promotion Information Video 2If you have additional questions or would like more information about curriculum, instruction, or reading supports, please click CPSD Curriculum & Instruction for information on our website.Thank you for your continued partnership and support. Together, we are helping every student build the reading skills they need for a successful future.Sincerely,Conway Public Schools

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Conway Public School District Issues Statement Following Reported Bomb ThreatThe Conway Public School District is providing an update following a reported bomb threat at Conway Junior High School earlier today.Upon receiving the report, district officials immediately activated established safety protocols and coordinated with local law enforcement and emergency personnel. The parents/guardians of the junior high students were notified immediately of the reported threat and they were updated in real-time regarding their students. Students and staff were kept safe while authorities conducted a thorough on-site investigation, including a sweep of the building by the bomb squad.The bomb squad determined that no credible threat existed and the bomb squad cleared the building. The campus has been deemed safe for normal operations. Parents/Guardians were given the option to pick up their students and students were able to return to the building today.  Counseling support will be available for any students who may need assistance processing today’s events.The matter remains under review by local law enforcement.“All of our emergency procedures were implemented immediately, and the safety of our students and staff was never compromised,” said Jason Black, Superintendent of Conway Public School District. “We are grateful for the swift response of local law enforcement and emergency personnel and the cooperation of our students, staff, parents, and community.”District officials followed established safety protocols throughout the incident. The District extends its appreciation to local law enforcement and emergency personnel for their quick and professional response. The District also wants to thank its students, staff, parents/guardians, and community for their patience, trust, and support as we navigated this situation together.

text:
Good evening Conway families and staff,

As the week comes to a close, I want to thank you for your support, patience, and partnership. This week presented challenges that required quick action and strong coordination, and I’m proud of how our teachers, staff, SROs, Conway Police Department and Conway Fire Department worked together to keep our campuses safe. Our teachers and staff handled this week with professionalism, care, and a strong focus on students, and I’m grateful for their work.

As we move forward, our focus is simple, getting back to the important work of teaching and learning. Our schools will operate as normal and I look forward to welcoming our students back ready to learn and finish the week strong.

I recorded a short video with Chief Harris that will be shared tomorrow. In it, we reinforce the seriousness and consequences of making threats, while also encouraging parents to stay engaged, have conversations with their children, and communicate with schools if concerns arise.

I appreciate your trust and support. It takes all of us working together to ensure a safe and positive environment for our students.

Have a great evening, and Go Wampus Cats.

Jason Black 
Superintendent 
Conway Public School

Arkansas had an average score of 2.66Mrs. Nohora Tedford- AP Spanish Language → 12 students took the exam and scored an average of 4.13. Arkansas had an average score of 3.31. We have 37 students taking this exam this year. Mr. William Richardson- AP US History → 171 tests given with an average of 3.48 and Arkansas had an average of 2.58.  Additionally, we highlighted Conway High’s School’s AP Honor Roll Recognition. In 2024, CHS was a Bronze school and we are pleased to announce that for the 2025 school year we have moved to the SILVER tier of recognition! In the state of Arkansas 251 qualified to be considered for AP Honor Roll. Only 49 schools in Arkansas earned a place on the AP School Honor Roll. Help us cheer on these amazing educators, the success of our students, and Conway High School as a whole for their tremendous overall accomplishments!

author: Conway Public Schools
text: We are proud to highlight an incredible partnership with Lisa’s Closet, founded in honor of the late Miss Lisa Barber—an exceptional educator in the Vilonia School District who lived a life centered on service and giving back. Today, her legacy continues through the work of her husband, Shawn Barber, along with dedicated board members who share her passion for supporting students.Lisa’s Closet is making a meaningful impact across our elementary campuses by helping provide one of the most essential—and often first noticed—items a student wears: shoes. Currently serving four of our elementary schools, the organization will expand this fall to all nine elementary campuses, ensuring even more students have access to quality footwear.Through strong collaboration with school counselors, Lisa’s Closet has already been meeting student needs by providing funds for shoe purchases. Now, they are going a step further—working to streamline the process by directly purchasing and delivering shoes to campuses, easing the workload on school staff while continuing to meet student needs quickly and compassionately.This partnership reflects the very best of our Conway community. We are deeply grateful for Lisa’s Closet and their unwavering commitment to serving our students and families.

text: A message from CPSD School Board President Sheila Franklin:May 11, 2026To the Conway School Board, Superintendent Jason Black and his leadership team, and Dr. Jeff Standridge:I extend my sincere gratitude to each of you, as well as to our outstanding students, parents, administrators, educators, and staff. author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Important Message from School Board Member Trip Leach:

Below is the resignation letter from Trip Leach. His resignation is effective May 12, 2026.

Wesley ‘Trip’ Leach, III
School Board Zone 4May 11, 2026To: Conway Public School Board
Subject: ResignationDear Conway Public School Board,I am writing in my capacity as the Zone 4 Representative and a duly elected member of the Conway Public School Board to formally submit my resignation from the Board.Serving the students, families, staff, and community of Conway over the past 12 years has been a tremendous honor and privilege. I have sincerely valued the opportunity to work alongside fellow board members, administrators, teachers, and staff who are deeply committed to the success of Conway Public Schools.At this time, I believe this important role deserves someone who can give it their full attention and energy. Due to the need to focus more fully on my family and personal health, I have made the difficult decision to step away from my position on the Board.I remain confident that Conway Public Schools is in excellent hands under the leadership of the current administration and Board. I look forward to watching the district continue its important work and ongoing success in the years ahead.Thank you again for the opportunity to serve this incredible community.Sincerely,Wesley 'Trip' Leach, III
Zone 4 Representative
Conway Public School Board

text:
Conway Families:

As we continue to monitor the weather, the safety of our students and staff remains our top priority. If a tornado warning is issued during dismissal hours (3:00-3:35 PM), dismissal operations will immediately stop, and students and staff will move to designated safe areas until the warning has been lifted. Once conditions are safe, normal dismissal procedures will resume.

Please remember that school Safe Rooms are open to the public only when a tornado warning is issued after school hours.

Thank you for your patience, understanding, and cooperation as we work to keep everyone safe. We will continue to provide updates as needed.

Conway Public Schools

Conway Families,

Conway Public Schools has paid spots still available for our Sallie Cone Preschool's Pre-K program! This is a wonderful opportunity for families looking to enroll their children in a high-quality early education setting. This program is designed to provide a nurturing and educational environment for our youngest learners. We encourage all interested to take advantage of this opportunity.
Information:Date of Birth: Child must be 3 yrs old by February 28, 2026 or 4 yrs old by August, 1, 2026 in order to be eligible for the program.

text:
The Arkansas State Board of Health Rules and Regulations Pertaining to Immunization Requirements states that every child attending a public school in the state shall receive a series of immunizations in order to enter school. Religious, Medical, and Philosophical exemptions can be obtained through the Arkansas Department of Health. However, proof of exemption letters must be obtained each year and provided to the school for their records. (AR Code Annotated 20-7-109, 6-18-702, 6-60-504, 20-78-206).

If your child is already 11 years old or will turn 11 yrs. before September 1, 2023, he/she will need the Tdap and the MCV4 vaccines before returning to school this year. If your child is entering 7th grade and has not received the MCV4 vaccine, he/she must have this before returning to school this year. 

The deadline for receiving these immunizations is September 1, 2023. If your child does not have the required immunizations by this date, he/she will be sent home until immunizations are updated. There will be NO exceptions! 

All updated records must be turned in to Nurse Siegel. 
Any questions or concerns should be sent to Nurse Siegel at siegelh@conwayschools.info. Or, please call 501-329-2782 with any questions. Thank you!
