Mr. Noland's 6th grade students will study star constellations and their origins in order to create a work of art. Each student will design their own constellation! For stars, students will create circuits on the back of their art using copper tape, batteries, and LED lights. This project will connect art across multiple disciplines. 

Fifth-grade science teachers, Mrs. Harness, Mrs. Sanders, and Mr. Gunsolus, cannot wait to get their students involved in designing and creating compost piles!

Mr. Smith's The Books with a Backpack program is to provide new, free books to students that are a part of the school food backpack program. Every time a student receives a food backpack, they can take home a book of their choice. Studies have shown that having an in-home library is crucial for students' academic success. More importantly, we want to foster a love of learning and reading, to positively affect students throughout their lives. We were given a $750 grant which has purchased over 300 new books!

text:
What is eWallet?
No more bills stuffed in backpacks! At the Scholastic Book Fair, kids shop without cash thanks to eWallet, a digital payment account for purchases at the Fair. Family and friends contribute funds. Then kids choose their own books. It’s convenient, simple, and secure.

How does it work? 
It starts on your school’s Book Fair homepage. A child’s family follows a link to create a free eWallet account. There are three ways to fund an account: Add money with a credit card, use funds from a previous eWallet, or invite friends and extended family to contribute. 

Because funds are available immediately, a child can shop the Fair with eWallet right away. Families can use a leftover balance to fund an eWallet for a future Fair.  #ChampionsForKids #celebratecsms

https://www.scholastic.com/bf/carlstuartmiddleschool1

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
Mrs. Pillow's students have been learning about the Paleolithic and Neolithic Stone Ages. They researched Otzi the Iceman who lived around 3300 B.C. His frozen body was found by two hikers more than 5,000 years later in the Alps in Europe, in September 1991. His clothing, tools, and even the contents of his stomach have helped scientists understand how prehistoric people lived. They still research Otzi today.

text:
Good evening CSMS Families,Arrival/Dismissal News:
We would like to remind you of our car rider arrival times. Doors to the school open at 7:25 AM. Car riders may be dropped off preferably between 7:25 and 8:00. The bell to go to class rings at 8 o'clock. The tardy bell rings at 8:05. Students who are dropped off after 8:05 will need to be signed in at the front office. School is dismissed at 3:15 PM. Car riders must be picked up by 3:45. We would like to thank all of our families for doing a fantastic job getting into our car line and getting your students picked up on time. Should your student have an alternate method of getting home for the day, you may call our front office and our secretary will let them know.Counselor News: If your family is in need of assistance for the holidays, please contact our counseling center. Deadline for assistance applications is November 10th. If your family is not being served by another school, please contact our counselors as soon as possible. We would like to thank you for supporting your student this year. We have had a great behavior from our students, which had led to more learning opportunities. If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to our front office. Have a great weekend and Go Cats!

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
The Veterans Day Assembly took place on Friday, November 10, and it was a special event honoring our Veterans. The school's band, orchestra, and choir all performed during the assembly, adding a meaningful touch to the event.

The assembly also highlighted the importance of family and pride in service. Students had the opportunity to introduce their family members who had served in the military and share which branch they belonged to. This created a personal connection and allowed the student body to better understand the sacrifices made by these individuals.

The Student Council played a significant role in hosting a reception for both the veterans and their family members in the media center. This gathering provided a chance for everyone to connect and appreciate each other's company. Additionally, the Student Council shared valuable information about each branch of service, educating the attendees about the different roles within the military.

Guest speakers were Veterans Paul Tull, Jason  Tooke, Angela Campagna, and Dr. Phillip Fletcher.  They spoke about the importance of Veterans Day and the significance of joining the military. The Veterans emphasized how being part of the military helps individuals find their sense of belonging and purpose. They also touched upon the sacrifices that service members make, but highlighted how the military gives back in numerous ways.  

During the assembly, the veterans had the privilege of sitting beside their students.  This served as a reminder of the importance of supporting and acknowledging the sacrifices made by these servicemen and servicewomen.

text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

We would like to extend a huge THANK YOU to everyone who supported our first-ever Read-a-Thon!  We're incredibly proud of our readers and grateful for your support, which made our fundraiser a success. In 15 days our students read 78,846 minutes.  We raised $6,780 and of this amount, CSMS was able to keep $5,085.  The top three readers were Ella M. 3,181 minutes, Aayan K. 3,077 minutes, and Eamon R. 2.413 minutes.  They each received a Kindle.  The three students who raised the most money were Devin E. $425, Claire B. $370, and William K. $350. They each received a $35 Visa gift card.  Mrs. Powers’ students had the highest class average of minutes read per person, 864 minutes. and Mrs. Masters’ classes received the most donations, $3,570. Those who participated will get a pizza and ice cream party.

The Beautiful Tomorrow Assembly was created by motivational speaker, music artist, and college enthusiast, Jason Lewis aka Humble  TIP. He has traveled all around the country speaking to youth and performing at venues aimed at promoting peace, hope, and empowerment. His goal is to challenge the minds of the youth in attendance and spark an excited desire to pursue their future and its endless potential. 

Mrs. Buddenberg said, "In 25 years of teaching, I've never attended an assembly that got the students more involved than the Beautiful Tomorrow assembly. They were engaged in fun activities while hearing about goal setting and peer pressure. Very uplifting and positive way to encourage our students to have a Beautiful Tomorrow."

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
CSMS welcomes our new principal, Mr. Ty Hendricks. He has been an assistant principal at Conway High School for the past several years. During his time at CHS he taught various social studies courses.  Before CHS he was at Ahlf Junior High School in Searcy. 

Mr. Hendricks received his Bachelor of Science in Education Degree in Social Studies in 2012. In addition, he has a Masters Degree in History, a Masters Degree in Education, and an Education Specialist Degree. 

He is excited and looking forward to working with the wonderful students, faculty, and staff of CSMS. 

Mrs. Campbell accepted the position of Director of Human Resources for Conway Public Schools

text:
Book Fair October 8-17
Give your child a safe, cashless way to shop at the Book Fair.  What is eWallet? No more bills stuffed in backpacks! At the Scholastic Book Fair, kids shop without cash thanks to eWallet, a digital payment account for purchases at the Fair. Family and friends contribute funds. Then kids choose their books. It’s convenient, simple, and secure. How does it work? It starts on your school’s Book Fair homepage. A child’s family follows a link to create a free eWallet account. There are three ways to fund an account: Add money with a credit card, use funds from a previous eWallet, or invite friends and extended family to contribute. Because funds are available immediately, a child can shop the Fair with eWallet right away. Families can use a leftover balance to fund an eWallet for a future Fair. #AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms https://www.scholastic.com/bf/carlstuartmiddleschool1

text: Mrs. Bri Irvin’s DoodleBirds club had loads of fun with today’s craft! They each designed papel picado pieces to create banners to decorate the hallways for Hispanic Heritage Month. Papel picado is a traditional Mexican craft that involves cutting intricate designs into colorful tissue paper. This art form dates back to the 16th century and symbolizes the beauty and fragility of life. Each design often reflects themes of nature, celebrations, and cultural heritage, making it a perfect way to honor this special month. A huge thank you to our DoodleBirds for their creativity and hard work in bringing this vibrant tradition to our school! #AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms

text:
The Conway Public Schools Orchestra program presents its annual "La Fiesta Orquesta" Taco Supper on Thursday, November 21 on the campus of Conway High School from 5:00-9:00 pm. This southwestern-themed event features the nearly 300 students of the orchestra program in free concerts throughout the night. All performances take place in the James H. Clark Auditorium, with city-wide Intermediate Orchestra performing first at 5:30, the Conway High School Orchestra performing at 6:15, city-wide beginning orchestra students at 7:30, and the Conway Junior High School 8th and 9th grade orchestras at 8:15. 

The event also serves as the orchestra program's primary fundraiser, with money raised through dinner ticket sales, donations, and a silent auction. Dinner service is held from 5-8 pm in the Conway High School cafeteria, and the meals include drinks and dessert as well. Meal tickets for the taco salad dinner (or soft taco child's plate) are on sale online at conwayorch.square.site or at the door the night of the event for $15/adults and $10/children. Dinner is available for dine-in or for carryout. The silent auction, with many items donated by local businesses, will take place from 5:30-8:15 p.m. in the lobby of the James H. Clark Auditorium. 

We hope you’ll support these amazing students and come hear us play!!

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
Exciting News for Our Middle Schools! We will begin implementing Yondr pouches on November 4, 2024. Students will receive their own Yondr pouch to take home on that morning.

What does this mean for students? To create a focused and distraction-free environment, all cell phones, smart watches, and AirPods will be secured in these special bags during school hours. Students are required to bring their Yondr pouches every morning and place their devices inside before entering the school. The bags will remain with them, but all devices must be turned off during school hours. At the end of the day, students will unlock their Yondr pouches as they exit the school and will keep their pouches with them. This initiative will help foster learning, connection, and engagement—without the screens!

Important Reminder: Violating district policy regarding the possession of cell phones can lead to disciplinary action. Students who tamper with the Yondr pouch, repeatedly forget to bring their pouch, damage or take another student's Yondr pouch, or use their phone without authorization during the school day may face consequences ranging from warnings and phone confiscation to detentions, Saturday school, or in-school suspension. Additionally, restitution may be required to replace a Yondr pouch.

We will also be participating in a survey of students as part of a program supported by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders and the Office of Education Policy. This survey aims to gather valuable insights into the effectiveness of our new policies and the overall school experience. Consent forms will be sent home soon, so please return them to your student's third period teacher by November 8, 2024.

Let’s work together to enhance our students’ educational experience!

#AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms

Mrs. Pillow's cooking club had the exciting opportunity to prepare the food for the school board luncheon on Friday. The menu featured poppyseed chicken, green beans, corn, salad, rolls, a "Death by Chocolate" trifle, and a festive holiday punch with an ice ring.

Reflecting on the semester, Mrs. Pillow shared how much her students have grown. They learned valuable skills like converting recipes for large quantities, planning menus, slicing, chopping, mixing, whipping, baking, and, just as importantly, cleaning up afterward.

Through her career awareness class, Mrs. Pillow has also strengthened partnerships within the community. Her students visited the Conway Career Center at the high school, where they connected with Ms. Tell, the culinary arts teacher. In a collaborative effort, Mrs. Tell sent her senior pro serve students to help supervise the cooking club last week, providing mentorship and hands-on guidance.

This collaborative experience not only enhanced the students' cooking skills, but also provided valuable insights into culinary career paths.

#AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
At the school board luncheon held last Friday, the student council shared many of the exciting initiatives underway. They discussed their goals for the year, their ongoing book study of The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens, and their leadership roles in organizing key events such as Red Ribbon Week, the Winter Dance, the Veterans Day Assembly, Pep Rallies, and helping with the Fall Festival.

Additionally, the D3 and G3 clubs highlighted their mission to bring joy to others. They shared examples of their efforts, such as helping with the Fall Festival and selling peppermints to raise money for Christmas gifts for families in need.

Mr. Hendricks praised the outstanding work of Mrs. Sellers and Ms. Calhoun with the new coding class, which has generated incredible excitement among the students. Beyond the classroom, they’ve also launched a Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA) chapter that has already made a significant impact. The group has organized donations to create Craft Kits for Arkansas Children’s Hospital and initiated the sale of “Believer Bells”—necklaces engraved with the word “Believe.” These necklaces serve as powerful symbols, encouraging belief in ourselves, our dreams, and the strength of our community. These initiatives showcase the transformative impact of these programs on our school, fostering creativity, leadership, and a positive mindset.

#AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms

text:
Carl Stuart FBLA Spreads Holiday Cheer with Craft Kits for Arkansas Children’s Hospital
This year, the Carl Stuart Mid-Level FBLA celebrated the season of giving in a truly meaningful way! To kick off our winter break, we combined a festive holiday party with a community service project: packing craft kits for the children at Arkansas Children’s Hospital (ACH).
Thanks to the generosity and support of our amazing community, we were able to assemble 803 craft kits for children receiving services at ACH. These kits will bring joy and creativity to kids facing medical challenges, giving them a much-needed distraction and an opportunity to create something special.
We want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who contributed supplies, donated their time, or supported our efforts in any way. This event was a success because of YOU, and it was a wonderful reminder of how much good we can accomplish when we work together.
Thank you for helping us make a difference. From all of us at Carl Stuart FBLA, we wish you a joyful holiday season and a happy New Year!
#FBLA #CommunityService #ACH #CraftingSmiles #AscendtoExcellence #celebratecsms

Each year during school counselor week, Arisa Health asks schools to nominate the school counselor they believe goes above and beyond for students both academically and in meeting their mental health needs. Each school in the central region covers six counties (from Little Rock-Clarksville) and has the opportunity to nominate their school counselor. Arisa Health then has the task of choosing one counselor from the elementary level and one from the secondary level across this region. Carl Stuart submitted a lot of nominations for Mrs. Franklin. Nominations were received from admin, teachers, and secretaries—all commenting on the great work she exhibits each day. 
Mrs. Franklin was chosen as  Arisa's Mental Health Champion for this school year.  Congratulation!!!

text:
🏆 We are thrilled to share that two incredible teachers from Carl Stuart Middle School have been selected as 2025 Mental Health Champion Award recipients by Arisa Health! 💙

Congratulations to Jonathan Gunsolus and Charles “Chuck” German, who were chosen out of more than 110 educators nominated across dozens of Arkansas counties for their unwavering dedication to student well-being.

Mr. Gunsolus, "Mr. G", was recognized for his deep connections with students, his leadership in the D3 (Discipline, Determination, Dreams) program, and the way he encourages and supports students daily—whether it’s mentoring, playing soccer, gardening, or simply being a listening ear.

Mr. German was honored for his years of mentorship work, founding both the D3 and G3 programs that now impact nearly 200 students with the help of 10 staff mentors. His focus on character development, community service, and leadership has made a powerful and lasting difference on campus.

We are incredibly proud of these two Wampus Cat educators for being Champions for Kids in every sense of the word! 👏
#WampusCatsASCEND #ConwayPublicSchools #CPSDascends #ChampionsForKids #WeAreConway #6legs #MentalHealthMatters #TeacherAppreciation

text:
🏆 We are thrilled to share that two incredible teachers from Carl Stuart Middle School have been selected as 2025 Mental Health Champion Award recipients by Arisa Health! 💙

Congratulations to Jonathan Gunsolus and Charles “Chuck” German, who were chosen out of more than 110 educators nominated across dozens of Arkansas counties for their unwavering dedication to student well-being.

Mr. Gunsolus, "Mr. G", was recognized for his deep connections with students, his leadership in the D3 (Discipline, Determination, Dreams) program, and the way he encourages and supports students daily—whether it’s mentoring, playing soccer, gardening, or simply being a listening ear.

Mr. German was honored for his years of mentorship work, founding both the D3 and G3 programs that now impact nearly 200 students with the help of 10 staff mentors. His focus on character development, community service, and leadership has made a powerful and lasting difference on campus.

We are incredibly proud of these two Wampus Cat educators for being Champions for Kids in every sense of the word! 👏
#WampusCatsASCEND #ConwayPublicSchools #CPSDascends #ChampionsForKids #WeAreConway #6legs #MentalHealthMatters #TeacherAppreciation

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text: Immunization Reminder:The Arkansas State Board of Health Rules and Regulations Pertaining to Immunization Requirements states that every child attending a public school in the state shall receive a series of immunizations in order to enter school. Religious, Medical, and Philosophical exemptions can be obtained through the Arkansas Department of Health. However, proof of exemption letters must be obtained each year and provided to the school for their records. (AR Code Annotated 20-7-109, 6-18-702, 6-60-504, 20-78-206).If your child is already 11 years old or will turn 11 yrs. before September 1, 2025, he/she will need the Tdap and the MCV4 vaccines before returning to school this year. If your child is entering 7th grade and has not received the MCV4 vaccine, he/she must have this before returning to school this year. The deadline for receiving these immunizations is October 1, 2025. If your child does not have the required immunizations by this date, he/she will be sent home until immunizations are updated. There will be NO exceptions! All updated records must be turned in to Nurse Siegel. Any questions or concerns should be sent to Nurse Siegel at siegelh@conwayschools.info. Or, please call 501-329-2782 with any questions. Thank you!

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
Immunization Deadline: OCTOBER 1, 2025

The Arkansas State Board of Health Rules and Regulations Pertaining to Immunization Requirements states that every child attending a public school in the state shall receive a series of immunizations in order to enter school. Religious, Medical, and Philosophical exemptions can be obtained through the Arkansas Department of Health. However, proof of exemption letters must be obtained each year and provided to the school for their records. (AR Code Annotated 20-7-109, 6-18-702, 6-60-504, 20-78-206).

If your child is already 11 years old or will turn 11 yrs. before September 1, 2025, he/she will need the Tdap and the MCV4 vaccines before returning to school this year. If your child is entering 7th grade and has not received the MCV4 vaccine, he/she must have this before returning to school this year. 

The deadline for receiving these immunizations is October 1, 2025. If your child does not have the required immunizations by this date, he/she will be sent home until immunizations are updated. There will be NO exceptions! 

All updated records must be turned in to Nurse Siegel. 

Any questions or concerns should be sent to Nurse Siegel at siegelh@conwayschools.info. Or, please call 501-329-2782 with any questions. Thank you!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

On Tuesday,  some of our 7th Grade G3 girls had the privilege of hearing from Lindsey Rolfe, the amazing founder of LURE by ELLE and LURE by ELLE Cosmetics!

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
🏀 Basketball Game Tonight!
Benton is coming to Carl Stuart at 4:30PM —come cheer on our students and pack the stands! 💙🤍

As a reminder, please review our Conway Middle Schools Athletic Event Guidelines for game days:
Elementary school students must be accompanied to the game by a parent/guardian or responsible adult.
Regardless of grade level, all students are expected to follow standard rules for proper sporting attendance.

1. NO LOITERING around unauthorized areas of the stadium, arena, fields, and campus.  This includes the High School Courtyard. Students should be seated in the stands, unless at the concession stand or the restroom.

2. Fans may not bring items such as backpacks, balls, skateboards, or bikes into the game.

3. No outside food or drink is allowed. Concessions are available inside the game.

4. School rules apply and cooperation is expected with all game workers and school personnel. Failure to follow rules or lack of cooperation will result in removal from the game.

5. It is expected that all students will leave school grounds in a timely manner after completion of the game.  Students that are not picked up in a timely manner (20 minutes from the end of the game) will not be allowed to return for future games.  Students can call parents before the end of the game to allow transportation to get there in a timely manner.   


Thank you for your cooperation and your support of Conway Public Schools Athletics! 

#WeAreCarlStuart #WeAreConway #ChampionsforKids

⭐ TEACHER FEATURE #1 ⭐

Mrs. Powers | 5th Grade Reading | Jigsaw Reading w/ Case Studies 

Jigsaw is a cooperative learning strategy that supports high levels of engagement in that it segments a broader text into smaller sections for students to analyze and share out with the larger group.

We divided, read, and annotated the text “Exploring the Wild West” by subheading. Student teams had fun making the case as to why their section was most relevant to the topic. 

Super Student question: Which challenge that the pioneers faced did your team argue was the most relevant?

text:
TEACHER FEATURE #2

Ms. Crawford  | 5th Grade Social Studies | Cooperative Learning 

 I enjoy fostering different strategies for collaboration groups in my classroom! The pictures on display show some of my students engaging in the strategy, "cooperative learning". They collected data on the population of different countries.  This strategy was student centered where small, diverse teams were assigned to work together to maximize their own and each other's learning, relying on positive interdependence, individual accountability, and structured interaction. My students created a population pyramid of age groups from birth to the oldest life expectancy. They also used math skills to analyze the population density of different countries. They were AMAZED at how each country collects data on EVERYONE to determine the needs of each country economically and more!

text:
🎂 Happy Birthday to the legend himself — Carl Stuart! 🎂

Today we’re celebrating the man behind our name!

Carl W. Stuart (1923–1993) was a leader in Conway schools, serving as a Conway High principal and later as Superintendent of Conway Public Schools. His dedication to students and education left such a lasting impact that in 1988, our middle school was named in his honor!

Today, he would have turned 103 years old — and we’re proud to continue the school community he helped build. 💙

Happy Birthday, Carl Stuart!

text:
👏TEACHER FEATURE #3👏

Ms. Frazier | 5th Grade Reading | Overheard Quotes

This strategy engages students in listening to various ideas and drawing meaningful conclusions about the information. They are listening to their peers. They collect clues to figure out the topic. Each student was given an index card with a Christmas quote that had similar grammar mistakes. They read their card out loud to the class, they determined the mistakes and shared the conclusions with the class to decide the similar characteristics of each card.  This activity went well and they enjoyed listening to their peers and figuring out the mistakes.

text:
💙 TEACHER FEATURE #4 💙

Mrs. Masters |  5th Grade Reading |  Questioning Protocols

During a recent read-aloud of Crash, students engaged in purposeful questioning to deepen their understanding of the text. As we read, students paid close attention to the questions that naturally arose, helping them remain focused and actively engaged in the story.

We also examined question stems and discussed how different types of questions lead to different levels of thinking. Students learned that while some questions clarify basic understanding, others encourage deeper analysis, inference, and reflection. By intentionally using higher-level question stems, students were able to think more critically about characters, motivations, and events in the novel.

This strategy reinforced that asking thoughtful questions is an essential reading skill—one that builds curiosity, strengthens comprehension, and supports deeper cognitive engagement with complex texts.

We discussed as tables and as a whole class as we worked together to complete the first row of the chart .Students were SO excited to tell me other ideas and really loved the creative thinking involved in this activity!

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
⭐Black History Month Spotlight⭐

Odie Phillips is the Pastor/Teacher of the Greater Fellowship Christian Church of Conway, Arkansas.  He has an extensive background and training in counseling and public relations.  He is involved in every aspect of the Greater Fellowship Ministries and the social aspects of the community.  Pastor Odie Phillips has pastored in the City of Conway for 37 years.

Odie Phillips is a staff member of the Conway Public Schools where he counsels, instructs, and disciplines At-Risk-Youth. He has a longstanding history of Civic and Grass Roots involvement where he served as an active participant in the NAACP, Operation Push, the Minority Independence Block Association, the Faulkner County Leadership Institute, the Minority Mentors of the University of Central Arkansas, the Faulkner County Chapter for Drug Free Youth; and Vice President of the Community Task Force.  He had the privilege to serve on the Advisory Board to Family Development under former Governor Bill Clinton and he was a weekly journalist for the “Insights” column that appeared each Friday in the “Our Style” section of the Log Cabin Democrat.

In 1986, Mr. Phillips, at the age of 26, tossed his hat in the ring in bid for the vacated Little Rock Mayor’s seat.  At the time he was serving as the Vice President of the Community Task Force.  The Task Force was formed to improve the plight of blacks in the city.  He has also served as the former President of the Central Arkansas Ministerial Alliance and currently serves as President of the Fellowship of Christian Pastors and Ministers Alliance.

After 17 years of service, on May 26, 2009, Pastor Phillips retired from the Boys and Girls Club of America in Conway where he served as Unit Director, Mentor, Activity Coordinator, and Counselor.  He received a congratulatory certificate and recognition from the Arkansas Senate and a proclamation from the City of Conway’s Mayor, Tab Townsell, who declared May 26, 2009 as “Odie Phillips Day.”

Odie Phillips is a Man of God with a vision for the 21st Century; he teaches the Word of God with authority that enables and empowers God’s people to mature to higher spiritual levels; and he has evangelized under the power and the anointing of the Holy Spirit from Coast to Coast.  He is a Pastor that labors in the Word, in the Church, and in the Community.

text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE #8 ⭐

Mr. German | Health/PE | Adding Movement to Learning

Mrs. Wanamaker and I collaborated on this lesson to combine movement with learning by creating a review game focused on text structures in reading. Students used scooters to move around the room and find their assigned color card, which contained a short passage of text. They then had to evaluate the passage, determine which of the five text structures it represented, and explain their reasoning to either Mrs. Wanamaker or me. If their answer and explanation were correct, they placed their passage on the gallery wall under the matching text structure category.

This process continued until all passages were correctly identified. We played two rounds of the game. Although we ran out of time, the planned closure was for the groups to participate in a gallery walk, reading each passage and discussing why it fit its assigned text structure category.

text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE #11  ⭐

Ms. Kronberg | 5th Grade Math |  Math Vocabulary to Build Understanding

When starting our module on fractions, we decided it was important to focus on vocabulary to help students build strong background knowledge. Students first worked with a definition sheet that introduced key fraction terms. They then used those definitions to complete an activity page where they had to identify the type of fraction being described. Once they determined the correct type of fraction, they colored each one using the corresponding color. This activity helped reinforce the vocabulary while also allowing students to visually group and recognize the different types of fractions.

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE # 10  ⭐

Mrs. Spears | 5th Grade Math | Understanding Vocabulary 

We use math-specific vocabulary daily to help students become more familiar and confident with key terms. To support understanding, we connect new vocabulary to students’ background knowledge, such as relating the word plus to addition and minus to subtraction. As we introduce new concepts, we begin with vocabulary study so students understand the language of the concept before applying it. We also provide explicit instruction for each term and include clear examples so students can see how the vocabulary is used in context.

text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE #12 ⭐

Mrs. Mosley | 5th Grade ELA | Adding Movement to Learning

This strategy encourages students to physically move as they learn new concepts, which helps keep them engaged and focused. I used this approach to get my students up and active while introducing the structure of an informational essay. To make the parts more memorable, I taught them a chant paired with purposeful hand motions that represented each part of the essay—such as the introduction, the thesis statement, body, and the conclusion. Students practiced the chant with partners, allowing them to rehearse the sequence, offer each other feedback, and build confidence with the movements. This interactive routine not only strengthened their understanding of the essay’s parts and their functions, but also provided a multisensory tool they can rely on to recall the structure during the writing process.

#WeAreCarlStuart #WeAreConway #ChampionsforKids

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE # 13 ⭐

Mrs. Callaway | 5th Grade ELA | Peer Critiquing 

“Peer critiquing refers to the process of students sharing their work with students for constructive feedback, which they can subsequently use to revise and perfect their work.” 

This strategy is something that I have used in my teaching process for many years, but I have  been hesitant to let students say anything except positive comments about another students writing. This process led me to see that I could lead students to share with each other both the positive things about their writing and the things they could improve on in their writing.

text:
⭐ TEACHER FEATURE #16 ⭐

Stradling | 6th Grade Math | Analyze Level Thinking

Students analyzed a chart of numbers 1-100. We discussed our observations (prime numbers have a solid ring around them, even numbers all have an orange piece, multiples of five have blue pieces, etc) and our questions (why aren’t 2, 3, 5, and 7 red like the other prime numbers?). Each period’s discussion was different because students found so many different patterns and connections about the rings around the numbers. 

This was an ideal lesson for all levels of students because the observations made could be simple or complex.

text:
TEACHER FEATURE #18:

Mrs. Hunter | 7th Grade Science | Vocabulary-Building Movement

As simple and foundational as it often is, vocabulary plays a huge role in our science curriculum. There are many terms students MUST know in order to be successful in our new curriculum. Although I know most of the terms and definitions have been taught, I have found many students have a difficult time retaining the prior knowledge they have learned in regards to vocabulary. In our new curriculum, they have a section of their binders that is titled the Word Wall. This is the spot to record “new” words with the definitions and “art” to accompany. This has been a great resource for students and the feedback and recalling skills I have witnessed is showing improvement in vocabulary retention. In addition to their in binder word walls, I created a larger version in the classroom for the ones who just need that little bit of reassurance. It is a growing resource that we will continue to add to and watch grow throughout the year.

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
TEACHER FEATURE #20

Mrs. Irvin | 7th Grade ELA |  Implementing Strategies for Create-Level Thinking

Students read two accounts of the myth of Icarus: a retelling of the myth “The Flight of Icarus” by Sally Benson and a poem “Icarus’s Flight” by Stephen Dobyns. They were then tasked with writing 3 paragraphs comparing and contrasting the two versions of the story. Before they began writing, I had them brainstorm the similarities and differences by using this Hits and Spots Strategy. I gave student groups (ranging from 3-6 students) a set of sticky notes and a sheet of “dots” (stars). The students started by writing any similarities and differences they could think of on the sticky notes. Then, they analyzed each other’s ideas and put dots on the ideas (sticky notes) they felt were most effective and most relevant. Next, they grouped the sticky notes into similarities and differences. Finally, we had a class discussion about their findings and completed a brainstorming page together.

#WeAreCarlStuart #WeAreConway #ChampionsforKids

author: Carl Stuart Middle School
text:
TEACHER FEATURE #21

Mrs. Charton | 7th Grade ELA | Think Pair Square Share

The goal of this activity was to support students in developing strong research questions for an expository research essay through collaboration and consensus building. To begin the process, students independently created research questions based on specific characteristics that were provided and recorded them in individual boxes. They then shared their questions with an elbow partner at their table, allowing for initial feedback and discussion. Next, pairs joined with another pair across from them to form small groups, where they continued sharing and evaluating their questions. Within these groups, students discussed and agreed upon the strongest research question, which they recorded in the center box. Finally, each group shared their selected question with the class, and I collected them on a Google Slide in real time so that students could reflect on the examples and revise or replace weaker questions as needed.

#WeAreCarlStuart #WeAreConway #ChampionsforKids

text:
Immunization Reminder:
The Arkansas State Board of Health Rules and Regulations Pertaining to Immunization Requirements states that every child attending a public school in the state shall receive a series of immunizations in order to enter school. Religious, Medical, and Philosophical exemptions can be obtained through the Arkansas Department of Health. However, proof of exemption letters must be obtained each year and provided to the school for their records. (AR Code Annotated 20-7-109, 6-18-702, 6-60-504, 20-78-206).

If your child is already 11 years old or will turn 11 yrs. before September 1, 2025, he/she will need the Tdap and the MCV4 vaccines before returning to school this year. If your child is entering 7th grade and has not received the MCV4 vaccine, he/she must have this before returning to school this year. 

The deadline for receiving these immunizations is October 1, 2025. If your child does not have the required immunizations by this date, he/she will be sent home until immunizations are updated. There will be NO exceptions! 

All updated records must be turned in to Nurse Siegel. 

Any questions or concerns should be sent to Nurse Siegel at siegelh@conwayschools.info. Or, please call 501-329-2782 with any questions. Thank you!

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

author: Susan Henderson
text:
Dear CPSD families, 

CPSD is currently monitoring the weather, roads, and bus routes for today.

Decisions to alter the school schedule will be made based on the ability of CPSD to safely transport students to and from school.  Any decisions made will be based on the most accurate information and forecasts available.  As always, our top priority is the safety of our students, staff and parents.

As we approach inclement weather season, we would like to inform each of you of the process and methods Conway Public School District will disseminate information regarding possible school closings. Please review the following.

Mornings of possible inclement weather, CPSD will begin evaluating road conditions within Faulkner County by 4:00 a.m. while monitoring weather projections for the remainder of the day. Possible actions could include closures, delayed start times, or in certain scenarios an early release. School closings or late start determinations will occur by 6:00 a.m. before morning bus routes begin. 

CPSD will utilize an automated calling and texting system to notify students, parents and staff of possible closings or delays.  A pre-recorded message will be sent to all phone numbers in the student and staff directory within 10 minutes.  Please make sure the numbers that you listed on the student information sheet are current.

If school is to continue as normal, CPSD will not make an announcement. 

Our social media outlets will be continuously updated to keep parents and community members informed of school closing status. To ensure everyone is informed, television stations will also be contacted.

Please review the CPSD Bus Routes - Snow/Inclement Weather Routes.

Visit our website at conwayschools.org for more information. CPSD Inclement Weather

Thank you for your support and cooperation!

Conway Public Schools

text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

author: Ellen Smith Elementary
text:
According to the American Academy of Sleep Medicine, school-age children need the following amount of sleep for optimal health and development:
ages 3–5 years old: 10–13 hours (including naps)
Ages 6-12: 9-12 hours of sleep per night 
Ages 13-18: 8-10 hours of sleep per night 
Research suggests that a bedtime between 7:00 p.m. and 8:30 p.m. is ideal for elementary age children, depending on their morning wake-up time.
Establishing a bedtime routine that includes calming activities, such as reading or quiet conversation, can help children wind down and prepare for a restful night's sleep. Consistent bedtimes also help reinforce their internal body clock, making it easier for them to fall asleep and wake up naturally.

author: Ellen Smith Elementary
text:
Important Reminder: Car Line Procedure

Please note that car line officially ends at 8:00 AM. At that time, staff members will go inside, the doors will be locked, and instruction will begin. Any students arriving after 8:00 AM must be walked in by a parent and signed in at the front office. These students will be marked tardy, even if they were waiting in the car line.

To ensure a smooth and efficient drop-off, we ask that 4-6 cars unload students at a time, rather than just the three cars directly in front of the school. Please help your child have their coat and backpack ready, so they can exit the car quickly and safely.

Thank you for your cooperation in making car line smoother for everyone!

text:
Support Our Spring Carnival!We are excited to announce our upcoming Spring Carnival, a fun-filled event that brings together our students, families, and community! To make this year’s event a success, we’re reaching out to ask for your support.Your sponsorship will directly contribute to creating an unforgettable experience for our children, helping fund activities, games, prizes, and more. Sponsoring our event is also a wonderful opportunity to show your support for education and connect with local families.How You Can Help:
We are seeking donations of:Monetary contributionsGoods or services for our carnival activitiesPrizes or gift cards for our games and rafflesAs a sponsor, your generosity will be recognized during the event and in our promotional materials, showcasing your commitment to our school and community.If you’d like to contribute, please complete the attached form and return it by Tuesday, April 1, 2025. For questions or more information, feel free to contact Audrey Cooper at 501-450-4815 or by email at coopera@conwayschools.info.Thank you for considering this opportunity to support our school and make our Spring Carnival an incredible success!

text:
CPSD District Wide STEAM Night - Mark your Calendar!!
🚀 You’re Invited to an Unforgettable STEAM Night!
📅 Date: April 03, 2025
🕕 Time: 5:30 - 7:30 
📍 Location: Buzz Bolding Arena and James H. Clark Auditorium 
Join us for an action-packed K-12 CPSD STEAM Night—a night of hands-on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics fun for the whole family!
🚁 See a Helicopter Up Close!
🎈 Marvel at a Hot Air Balloon!
🔬 Engage with the Museum of Discovery’s Awesome Science Shows!
🎨 Watch Live Art Demonstrations!
🦁 Meet Special Animal Ambassadors From the Little Rock Zoo!
🏗️ Explore BIG Machines from Conway Corporation!
🎣 Learn from Arkansas Game & Fish Experts!
🚔 Meet First Responders, Law Enforcement Officers, & Their Equipment!
🔥 Say Hello to Smokey Bear and His Heavy Equipment!
🎓 Engage with Demonstrations from Local Colleges & Universities!
🛠️ Meet Real Engineers & Industry Experts!
👩‍🏫 Visit and Learn from CPSD Teachers!
🌟 Discover Pathways to Exciting Careers in STEAM Fields!
…and so much more! 
This is a free event open to all CPSD K-12 students and their families. Centennial Bank will be cooking free hotdogs for the whole family while supplies last. Kona Ice and Food Trucks will also be available for purchase. Don’t miss this incredible opportunity to explore, discover, and experience STEAM in action while learning how these fields can shape your future!

We can’t wait to see you there! 

Thank you, Centennial Bank and Conway Area Chamber of Commerce, for your financial support and your investment in our students!

text: I’m excited to share something new that’s coming for your child as they move into 3rd grade: departmentalization. That’s just a fancy way of saying that instead of staying with one teacher all day, students will rotate between a few teachers—each one focusing on just one or two subjects. Let me tell you why this is a great thing! 1. Teachers Teach What They Love Each teacher gets to focus on the subject they’re most passionate about—like reading, math, or science. That means your child gets deeper, more exciting instruction from someone who truly loves the subject.2. It Prepares Kids for the Future This small shift helps kids build responsibility, learn to work with different teachers, and get used to transitions—just like they’ll do in upper grades and in the real world.3. It Keeps Their Day Fresh Sometimes a change of scenery or teacher is all it takes to keep a student focused and excited. With new faces and different teaching styles throughout the day, students stay more engaged. 4. Better Support for Every Child When a teacher focuses on just one or two subjects, they can really zero in on how to help each student grow in that area—whether they need extra support or a bit more challenge. 5. Teachers Work Together as a Team Behind the scenes, these teachers are constantly communicating to make sure every child is thriving. Your child may have two or three teachers—but they’re all part of one unified team. We’re excited to see your child grow through this model, and we’re here to support them (and you!) every step of the way. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out @ riners@conwayschools.info. I will not check every day, but I will check it periodically!! Have a great summer! Mrs. Riner

text:
Hi Ellen Smith Families!

We want to make sure drop-off and pick-up go as smoothly as possible for everyone! Please follow these simple steps:

Morning Drop-off:
1. Pull all the way forward when you get to the car line. Look for staff members to help direct you.
2. Please don’t park on the crosswalk—we want to make sure everyone can walk safely to and from the building.
3. Be ready to go! Give your hugs and kisses ahead of time and make sure your student has their backpack on.
4. Once you enter the parking lot, students can exit the car and walk straight to the sidewalk.
5. Students need to be able to open their own door on the passenger side. Parents/guardians must stay in the car.

If you need to help your student in a different way, please pull forward to a parking spot and walk them into the building.

Please note: Students can’t be dropped off before 7:35 AM since there are no staff members available to supervise the front porch before that time.

Afternoon Pick-up:
You’ll need a car tag to pick up your student. If you don’t have one, please come to the office with a photo ID to sign them out.
If you child requires additional help, you may want to change their way home to be a walker, where you can retrieve them from the cafeteria doors and walk them to your vehicle. 
Need more tags? You can get extra ones for $3 at the front office.

Thanks so much for helping us keep things running smoothly! Let’s work together to make drop-off and pick-up as easy as possible for everyone.

author: Ellen Smith Elementary
text:
🚗 Help Us Keep Car Line Running Smoothly! 🚗
We want to make sure our car line is safe and efficient for everyone! Please remember the following tips when dropping off or picking up your child:
✔️ Prepare your child ahead of time: Ensure they have everything ready to exit the vehicle—backpacks, lunchboxes, etc.—before reaching the drop-off zone.
✔️ Say your goodbyes in advance: If you want to hug or chat with your child, do so before getting to the drop-off area so we can keep things moving smoothly!
✔️ Student loading/unloading: Students should load and unload only on the passenger side of the car for safety.
✔️ Pull all the way up: Always pull up as far as you can to help with traffic flow and ensure there’s enough room for everyone.
Align your back door with the cones that are set out.
✔️ Stay focused: For everyone's safety, please avoid using your phone while in the car line.
❌ Avoid stopping too early: Stopping too far from the drop-off zone can block traffic and create unnecessary delays.
Thank you for helping us keep our car line efficient and safe! Your cooperation is much appreciated. 💙

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

text: Congratulations to Our CPSD District Employee of the Year, Mr. Tony McCoy!!! We are proud to announce that Mr. Tony McCoy, Special Education Paraprofessional at Ellen Smith Elementary, has been named the Conway Public Schools District Employee of the Year! Mr. McCoy is known for his incredible work ethic, positive attitude, and genuine care for students and staff. He consistently goes above and beyond to support students, encourage those around him, and create meaningful relationships throughout the school community.His coworkers describe him as dependable, uplifting, compassionate, and always willing to help wherever needed. The impact he makes each day is felt far beyond the classroom, and his dedication to students is truly inspiring.Mr. McCoy’s commitment to excellence, teamwork, and student success makes this recognition so well deserved. Please join us in congratulating him on this incredible honor!

author: Matthew Coatney
text:
As we begin a new school year Monday, our commitment is simple: Every student will be known, loved, and challenged.

This is not a phrase that will just be said, but lived out each day inside Ellen Smith. Our goal as a staff is to know them deeply, love them intentionally, and challenge them relentlessly to grow and give their best while attending ESE. 
There will be days that are challenging, but our commitment to your children will never change. We will celebrate progress, learn from mistakes, and continue moving forward together.
Monday is the beginning of something special at Ellen Smith. Let’s make it an incredible year together!-Mr. Coatney

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

author: Amy Howell
text: Happy Friday Parents and Students!We have had such a great week at Ida Burns! Your students have done so well learning new procedures, meeting new friends, and getting started learning new skills. We are looking forward to a great year of growth. I wanted to send a few reminders as we go into the weekend to work on for next week. Remember that our front doors do not open until 7:30, you may drop your students off before that, but there will not be an adult on duty until the doors open. You may not sit in the car line to wait until the doors open. If you would like to wait with your student, you will need to park in a parking spot until the doors open so that the other parents in the line can get to work. If your student needs to change their mode of transportation, please make sure that you send that in writing to the teacher, send a message through Rooms, or come into the office to do so before 2:00. Please remember that when you exit our parking lot we only make a right turn during drop off and pick up so as to make our car flow quick. We also only allow turning right on Donaghey Street during these times as well so that traffic can keep moving on Lee Street. If you have any questions, please free to contact me! Also, if you have not had a chance to get signed up for Rooms, please get connected. This will be the primary way to get in touch with your child's teacher this school year!Thank you for partnering with us this year!Mrs. Howell

author: Anna Schichtl
text:
Part 1 From Beckie- Just a quick note of praise for today. 
I have received results from the scan I had today and there had been no spread of disease. The only cancer cells that were found are in the thyroid bed, as expected.  Those cells will be taken care of by the ablation that I had on Dec. 6.

author: Anna Schichtl
text: Part 2 from Beckie:No more treatment is needed at this time.We will continue to monitor through my 3 month bloodwork which is already routine.Thank you to all who have prayed for &hugged on me.Please keep off social media as my parents are dealing with health concerns of their own and don’t need to be worried about me.

text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

text:
Good afternoon, 
Please mark your calendars for our school musicals taking place on November 7th! In preparation for our Veteran’s Day-themed musicals, Mrs. Parker is collecting photos of our students’ veteran family members to include in a special musical tribute. If you have a family member (whether past or present) who has served in the military, we would love to honor them in our programs.  Please have all photos turned in by October 17th. Please email their military photo to parkerk@conwayschools.info with the following information:

1.  Veteran Name & Military Branch (include military title if possible)
2.  Relationship to Student (father of _____ , aunt of ____, etc.)
3.  Service Information (can include details such as time served, honors received, wars served in, etc.)

author: Ida Burns Elementary
text:
🌟 Welcome, Mrs. Ferrebee! 🌟

We are thrilled to welcome Mrs. Ferrebee as the new Assistant Principal of Ida Burns Elementary! 🐾💙

Mrs. Ferrebee brings 15 years of experience in education across Arkansas and Texas. She has taught kindergarten through second grade, served as an instructional facilitator for K–5, and supported students through roles including 504 coordinator and RTI committee member. She also holds an Ed.S. in Building Level Leadership and is passionate about helping students and teachers thrive.

But what truly makes this homecoming special is Mrs. Ferrebee’s connection to Ida Burns. In her own words:

"In 2009, I had the privilege of being placed at Ida Burns for my senior internship. That year, I fell in love with not only teaching, but also the students and families of this community. When I saw there was an opening, I wanted to return to where it all began! As I am stepping into this new role, I still feel the same welcoming spirit that was there 16 years ago. I am excited to work alongside Mrs. Howell, the teachers, and staff in serving the Ida Burns community!"

🎉 Fun Fact: She has a mini horse named Pumpkin! 🐴🧡

Please help us give Mrs. Ferrebee a warm Wampus Cat welcome — we’re so lucky to have her back where it all began!

#IdaBurnsElementary #WelcomeMrsFerrebee #WampusCatPride #FullCircleMoments

author: Ida Burns Elementary
text:
🎉 Welcome, Coach Huett! 🎉

We’re thrilled to welcome Coach Katy Huett to Ida Burns Elementary as our new P.E. Coach! 🐾💙

Coach Huett joins us from the classroom at Theodore Jones Elementary, bringing 11 years of teaching experience across first through fourth grades. A proud Conway native and lifelong Wampus Cat, she’s excited to bring her passion for movement and learning to our gym!

Coach Huett describes herself as funny, outgoing, and full of energy — and she’s all about helping students stay active while supporting their academic growth. Her belief in the power of learning through movement is sure to make P.E. a highlight of every Wampus Cat’s day!

"I’m thrilled to join the Ida Burns team and can’t wait to meet our amazing students and families in August!"

🎤 Fun Fact: A childhood video of Coach Huett forgetting her lines during an elementary school musical once aired on America’s Funniest Home Videos! (She says her eyes got as big as bowling balls — we believe it!)

Help us give Coach Huett a warm Wampus Cat welcome — we’re so lucky to have her join the IB family!

#IdaBurnsElementary #WampusCatPride #WelcomeCoachHuett #MoveLearnGro

text:
CPSD Bell to Bell No Cell
At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. To help keep our classrooms focused and follow state guidelines, students should not use personal electronic devices during the school day. This includes cell phones, AirPods, wireless headphones, and smartwatches. We ask that all devices be turned off and kept in backpacks during school hours.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color

We love having families involved, and we always welcome parents who choose to eat lunch with their child throughout the year.

text:
Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

author: Ida Burns Elementary
text: 📚 Read Across America Week is Coming! 🇺🇸We are excited to celebrate Read Across America Week next week, March 2–6! This nationwide initiative, led by the National Education Association, encourages children to read and develop a lifelong love of books.Throughout the week, students may participate in special reading activities, themed dress-up days, guest readers, and classroom celebrations — all designed to make reading fun and engaging!Read Across America is traditionally celebrated around March 2 in honor of Dr. Seuss’s birthday, while also highlighting diverse books and helping every child discover stories they enjoy.We encourage families to join the celebration by setting aside extra reading time at home. Even 15–20 minutes a day can make a big difference!We can’t wait to celebrate a wonderful week of reading together! 📖✨

text: CPSD Families,We want to provide a follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media that contains a threatening message.At this time, there is no new information regarding the credibility or origin of the message. The matter remains under active investigation by local law enforcement, and we are continuing to work closely with them.School will be in session tomorrow, and we will continue to be vigilant with all our safety measures across all campuses. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.We understand that families may have concerns, and we respect each parent/guardian's decision regarding attendance. As always, please make the decision that is best for your student and your family.We will continue to monitor the situation closely and share updates as appropriate.Thank you for your continued trust and partnership.Conway Public Schools

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

CATS IN COMMUNITY FOOD DRIVE 

Our Wampus Cat family is coming together to support Conway Public Schools students and families this summer!

We're collecting non-perishable food items now through July 21 that will be distributed during our Cats in Community Food Giveaway on July 23 in the Conway High School roundabout between 10:00am till 1:00pm or until supplies last. Every donation helps provide food and resources to families in need during the summer months.

 Donation Drop-Off Dates: Now till July 21

 Drop-Off Locations:
• Conway High School
• Kroger (Prince Street)
• Walmart (Highway 65)
• United Way

 Most Needed Items:
• Peanut butter, canned tuna, canned chicken, soups, chili, canned beans, protein snacks
• Mac & cheese, pasta, rice, pasta sauce, instant potatoes, ramen noodles, boxed meal kits
• Canned vegetables, canned fruit, applesauce, crackers, granola bars, cereal, oatmeal packets, pancake mix, breakfast bars

Please ensure all food items are unopened, sealed, and within their expiration date.

Together, we can make a difference for our school families. Thank you for helping us show what it means to be a Wampus Cat community! #CatsInCommunity #WampusCatsCare #ConwayPublic Schools #TeamConway See less
