author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

Parents, we know dismissal can be a busy time, and we truly appreciate your patience and cooperation as we work to keep all of our students safe and dismissal running smoothly! ❤️

🚨 PLEASE READ THESE IMPORTANT DISMISSAL REMINDERS:

❌ Parents may NOT walk up to pick up a student. All student pickups must follow the designated car-line procedures.

🚫 Jr. High and High School students may NOT walk up to the car line to pick up siblings. If an older sibling is picking up a younger sibling, they must meet them outside the cafeteria and will be picked up from the shuttle parking lot.

➡️ Jr. High and High School students are not permitted to walk up to the car line to pick up students.

We need EVERYONE'S help to keep our dismissal process safe, organized, and efficient. Thank you for following these procedures and helping us make dismissal as smooth as possible for everyone! 💙

Thank you, Ida Burns families, for your patience, understanding, and support! 🙏

author: Julia Lee Moore Elementary
text:
We are excited to welcome you to school tomorrow morning for our first day of the 2023-24 school year. Students in grades 1-4 may go to their classrooms beginning at 7:45 am. Kindergarten will start at 9 am for the first day only. Parents may walk their children to class on the first day of school. We will have all of our staff and teachers available to help get our students to their rooms.

If you are dropping your children off in the car line please adhere to the following guidelines: 
•Pull all the way forward and do not stop in front of the door
•Children must exit the vehicle from the passenger side to avoid a potentially dangerous situation 
•Please move younger siblings car seats to the driver's side
•Parents should pull into a side parking spot if they need to help their child get out of the vehicle.
•Park in the side parking spots if walking up and avoid walking across the lanes of moving traffic. This is very dangerous.
•Please put down your cellphone. Only hands free cell phone use is allowed by law in school zones. 

Thank you for helping us with these important procedures. Working together we can all help ensure a smooth and safe transition back to school.

Check out our website for information about JLM!
https://www.conwayschools.org/o/jlmes

text:
The JLM Fall Book Fair is open October 23rd to October 27th. The  Online Fair open till October 27th  as well!@ https://efairs.literati.com/ The online fair is perfect for loved ones who do not live locally and would like to purchase books or gift cards for your child.
* Remember* All Literati book fair items have taxes included. When considering how much money to send, please remember to send extra for tax purposes.
Payment options: Literati gift cards, Cash, Check, Credit Cards, Debit Cards, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay, Google Pay, Contactless Cards like Cash App. Purchase gift cards: https://efairs.literati.com/ Many parents LOVED the gift card option. Mrs. Epps able to look up gift card information throughout the day AND SO PARENTS DO NOT HAVE TO PRINT ANYTHING. 

The book fair will be open during both conference nights for parents to drop in and shop! Email Mrs. Epps if you need to ask anything about anything ...eppsj@conwayschools.info

text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

text:
The JLM Read-A-Thon begins on Monday February 12th  and is sure to be a fun and exciting event. That's why we are encouraging JLM parents to activate their student's Read-A-Thon account as soon as possible.

Your child's account will serve as a hub for recording and monitoring your child's progress as a Reader in the event, and for you to share their Read-A-Thon message with friends and family. Use the link below to activate your student's Reader account:
https://www.read-a-thon.com/readers/r/3538373131/1

Our kids will be reading to earn prizes for themselves and earn money for our school that will go directly back into the students and their reading. One example is we will hope to create a JLM Lunch Room Library full of new and fun books.

We are so very excited to be participating in our first Read-A-Thon event but we need your help so this will be a successful event for our readers!

If you have any questions, please email our Instructional Facilitator, Porscha Albert, albertp@conwayschools.info or our Library Media Specialist, Jennifer Epps, eppsj@conwayschools.info. Thank you for supporting JLM!

text:
Would you like to win an all-expense paid trip to Walt Disney Theme Park for your family? We'd love to make that dream come true!

Our school is holding a Read-A-Thon Fundraiser, and it's a fantastic opportunity for your child to raise money while enjoying their favorite books.

As a special bonus, any child who sends 10 text messages through their dashboard to promote our fundraiser will automatically be entered into a nationwide drawing for a magical trip for four to Walt Disney Theme Park.

We'll select one lucky winner each season from all the Read-A-Thons held during that season.

To create your student account, click on the link below (less than 5 minutes):

https://www.read-a-thon.com/readers/r/3538373131/2

Thank you for your support,

Warm regards,

Julia Lee Moore Elementary

Grandparents are a huge part of our children's lives, and they can be a great support in reaching those reading goals. During our Read-A-Thon, they can help encourage your child by donating to your child's reading goal.

Together let's encourage a lifelong passion for reading! Thank you!

📚🍎 Exciting news! Kindergarten Registration for the upcoming school year will officially open on April 2nd, 2024! 🎉 Are you ready to embark on this incredible journey with us? 🌟

For more information and to begin the registration process, please visit our website at conwayschools.org/preregistration. Here, you'll find all the necessary details and resources to ensure a smooth enrollment experience for your little one. 🏫✏️

Remember, to enroll in kindergarten, your child must be 5 years old on or before August 1st, 2024. We can't wait to welcome your child into our school family and witness the amazing growth and learning that lies ahead! #ChampionsForKids #WeAreWampusCats #KindergartenRegistration

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🎉📚 Parents and guardians! Kindergarten Registration is NOW OPEN! 🎉📚

If your student will be 5 years old on August 01, 2024 here are the steps to register them for Kindergarten: 
1️⃣ Find your zoned elementary school.
2️⃣ Register your student online.
3️⃣ The Registrar at your student's school will be in contact.

For full information and registration links, please visit conwayschools.org/preregistration. 🏫✏️

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

text:
Mary Jane Naylor (Janie), of Conway, Arkansas, recently passed away at the age 81.  Mrs. Naylor was a dedicated educator in Pulaski County and Conway Public Schools for over 42 years.  Mrs. Naylor requested donations be made to the Julia Lee Moore Elementary School Backpack Program in lieu of flowers.  The staff of Julia Lee Moore appreciates your generosity.  If you wish to donate, you may send a check made out to the JLM Backpack program in honor of Mrs. Naylor.
Thank you!

Julia Lee Moore Backpack Program
1301 Country Club Road
Conway, Arkansas 72034.

author: Julia Lee Moore Elementary
text:
Julia Lee Moore Elementary will hold a Read-A-Thon again this year! Read-A-Thons actually get your reader excited about reading and it gives friends and family the opportunity to encourage your child to read even more.  Our Read-A-Thon starts Monday March 10, 2025.  Next week we will send home instructions on how to activate your reader's personal page. This is where you will be able to view and record their progress. We encourage you to activate your reader’s account today by scanning the QR code or visiting https://www.read-a-thon.com/readers/r/FLzxTx/1 and following the simple instructions.
We've chosen Read-A-Thon because it will not take much of your time, gives your child a great reason to read while developing stronger reading skills.

We hope EVERYONE signs up their child whether they raise funds or not.

Thanks so much,
Julia Lee Moore Elementary

CPSD District Wide STEAM Night - Mark your Calendar!!
🚀 You’re Invited to an Unforgettable STEAM Night!
📅 Date: April 03, 2025
🕕 Time: 5:30 - 7:30 
📍 Location: Buzz Bolding Arena and James H. Clark Auditorium 
Join us for an action-packed K-12 CPSD STEAM Night—a night of hands-on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics fun for the whole family!
🚁 See a Helicopter Up Close!
🎈 Marvel at a Hot Air Balloon!
🔬 Engage with the Museum of Discovery’s Awesome Science Shows!
🎨 Watch Live Art Demonstrations!
🦁 Meet Special Animal Ambassadors From the Little Rock Zoo!
🏗️ Explore BIG Machines from Conway Corporation!
🎣 Learn from Arkansas Game & Fish Experts!
🚔 Meet First Responders, Law Enforcement Officers, & Their Equipment!
🔥 Say Hello to Smokey Bear and His Heavy Equipment!
🎓 Engage with Demonstrations from Local Colleges & Universities!
🛠️ Meet Real Engineers & Industry Experts!
👩‍🏫 Visit and Learn from CPSD Teachers!
🌟 Discover Pathways to Exciting Careers in STEAM Fields!
…and so much more! 
This is a free event open to all CPSD K-12 students and their families. Centennial Bank will be cooking free hotdogs for the whole family while supplies last. Kona Ice and Food Trucks will also be available for purchase. Don’t miss this incredible opportunity to explore, discover, and experience STEAM in action while learning how these fields can shape your future!

We can’t wait to see you there! 

Thank you, Centennial Bank and Conway Area Chamber of Commerce, for your financial support and your investment in our students!

text:
We are excited to announce that online registration is now OPEN for Kids Run Arkansas®! 🎉

On Friday, April 25, at 6:00 pm for an exciting, family-friendly event, sponsored by Groovy Smiles Pediatric Dentistry. This event is all about fun, fitness, and spending quality time with your loved ones!

Whether you're walking, jogging, or running, this event is open to kids of all ages and their parents. There’s no chip timing – just a focus on having fun, staying active, and making lasting memories together!

This year, there are two amazing events:

👟 The classic 3-mile run/walk
👟 Reggie’s Rush: A new ½-mile race designed for younger kids to move in a fun and safe way. The scenic, easy out-and-back route will take participants along the beautiful Tucker Creek Trail. Reggie, the friendly face of Conway Regional Health System, will be there to inspire smiles, energy, and healthy living!
📝 Register Now!

For more information, feel free to contact Mallory Lefler at 501-450-9292 ext. 309 or via email at mlefler@conwayregional.org.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

text:
Why Should I Fill Out the Free & Reduced Lunch Form? Filling out this form helps your family and your school! 
🍎If you qualify, your child can get free or reduced-price meals at school.
🍎Families may also get discounts on testing fees, internet service, and activities.
🍎Schools receive extra funding based on how many families fill out the form—this means more teachers, programs, and resources for all students.

🔐All information is confidential—no one will know if your child qualifies.

Even if you don’t think you qualify or your child doesn’t eat school meals, turning in the form helps our whole school community!

To apply: https://secure.ezmealapp.com/ApplicationScreen.aspx

📣 Attention Military Families!
The Arkansas Council for Military Children wants to hear from YOU! 
Each year, the Council holds a public forum to gather feedback from families of active-duty service members about how well Arkansas laws and resources are supporting military children.
🗓 The first forum for the 2025-26 school year will be held virtually on Thursday, October 2, 2025, from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
The event will start with a short presentation about helpful resources for military families, followed by an opportunity for families to share their experiences and speak directly with Council members.
💻 This is a great chance to have your voice heard and help shape support for military-connected students across the state!

text:
Dear Parent: 10-15-25
Hello! The third and fourth grade students will be presenting “Music Potpourri” on Tuesday, November 18 at 6:00 P.M. The students are working to get their songs memorized and the parts are beginning to come into place. I wanted to send some specific information about general costuming and for two specific parts. Please reach out if you have any questions or need help with a particular costume.
*GENERAL DRESS: Students should wear nice, bright, comfortable clothing and comfortable shoes. Please avoid t-shirts with logos or writing on the front. Also, avoid shoes that come off easily (flip-flops, strapless sandals, etc.)
*Unless otherwise specified, general dress will cover all other parts

Props for the railway workers, cue cards, flag bearers and the Yankee will be provided
1950' DANCERS: These students should dress 1950's style.
BOYS: White t-shirts, jeans, sunglasses, leather jackets, letterman jackets, khaki pants, tennis shoes or loafers.

GIRLS: Poodle skirts, saddle oxford shoes, Keds , or tennis shoes, jeans, button down shirts, colored scarves to tie on a pony tail or around your neck.
SQUARE DANCERS: Cowboy, cowgirl style. Jeans, button down shirts, cowboy hats, bandanas, boots or dark shoes that do not come off easily.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

Painting Fundraiser Week!
Sunday, November 9th - Saturday, November 15th
During all regular business hours
We are teaming up with our friends at Good Day Pottery & Art Studio for a holiday ornament painting fundraiser!
This fun opportunity is walk-in only - no appointments or reservations needed!
The Good Day staff will guide you through the pottery painting process to start a fon new family tradition this year - just tell a staff member you are there for JLM's fundraiser!
All supplies will be provided including washable ceramic glaze paints. Their pre-lined ornaments make it easy for even the youngest of artists to paint masterpieces.
These ceramic ornaments are a treasure for your own tree, are wonderful for gift-giving, and are loads of fun to paint however you like! Plus, each ornament painted raises funds for Julia Lee Moore Elementary's PTO.
The finished ornaments will be returned to school for distribution before your Winter Break.

Dear Families,

Over the next few weeks, your second grader will participate in a districtwide assessment. Each spring, Conway School District screens all second grade students using a nationally normed measure that evaluates students’ reasoning abilities in verbal, quantitative, and nonverbal areas.

This assessment helps us better understand each student’s learning strengths and academic potential. The results are one of several data points we use to determine whether a student may benefit from further evaluation for gifted and talented services. There is nothing you need to do to prepare, and testing will take place during the regular school day.

If you have any questions, please contact the Gifted and Talented teacher at your child’s school. There is also more information about GT services on the district website.

Thank you for your continued support.

Sincerely,
Conway School District

Thanks!
Mr. Cole

It's time for the Julia Lee Moore Elementary Read-A-Thon!

Our school Read-A-Thon begins on Monday 
March 9, 2026 and is sure to be a fun and exciting event.

We understand that your time is valuable. We also know that providing the best education for your child is important. That's why we are encouraging everyone to activate their student's Read-A-Thon account as soon as possible. The instructions are straightforward, making it quick and hassle-free, and it should take less than 5 minutes of your time.

Watch a short video to see how to signup your reader:
https://youtu.be/12tmuXH8zCg

This account will serve as a hub for recording and monitoring your child's progress as a Reader in the event, and for you to share their Read-A-Thon message with friends and family. Use the link below to activate your student's Reader account:
https://www.read-a-thon.com/readers/r/sdyxkr/1?utm=email

Thank you so much for your participation and support. Together, we can make this Read-A-Thon an amazing experience for our young readers! Thank you,

Julia Lee Moore Elementary

Our students aren't just reading about technology—they are putting their thoughts onto paper (and whiteboards!) to process their experiences. 

✍️ Seeing our learners write about the school 3D printers shows the powerful link between hands-on exploration and literacy development. When students are excited about what they are doing, their desire to share those ideas through writing naturally follows! 

🚀📚 From big ideas to the fine details, we love seeing their voices come to life.

Third Grade Parents--Please mark your calendars for the following dates:

Tuesday, April 14th: 3rd Grade ATLAS Writing

Wednesday, April 15th: 3rd Grade ATLAS Reading

Why Attendance and Punctuality Matter:

To ensure your child feels confident and prepared, it is vital that they arrive at school on time and are present for both testing days. Testing begins promptly in the morning; arriving late can be stressful for students and may require them to stay for make-up sessions later in the week, causing them to miss regular classroom activities.

How You Can Help:

Rest: Ensure your child gets a good night's sleep before each testing day.

Breakfast: A healthy, protein-filled breakfast will help them stay focused.

Encouragement: A few words of "You've got this!" go a long way in easing testing jitters.

We are so proud of the hard work our third graders have put in this year. Thank you for your continued support in helping them succeed!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

text:
📝 Get Ready for ATLAS Testing!
Attention JLM families! Our 3rd and 4th graders are gearing up for the ATLAS assessments next week. We are so proud of the hard work they’ve put in all year, and now it's time for them to show off what they know! 🌟

Here is the testing schedule for the week of April 27th:

Monday, April 27th: 4th Grade Writing ✍️

Tuesday, April 28th: 4th Grade Reading 📚

Wednesday, April 29th: 3rd & 4th Grade Math 🔢

Thursday, April 30th: 3rd & 4th Grade Science 🔬
____________________________________________________________________
💡 Tips for a Successful Testing Week:
Early to Bed: A well-rested brain is a sharp brain! 😴

Fuel Up: A healthy, protein-rich breakfast helps maintain focus throughout the morning. 🍳

Be on Time: Arriving early helps students settle in and feel calm before testing starts. 🏫

Positive Vibes: Encourage your child to simply do their best. A little "you've got this!" goes a long way. ❤️

Let’s make it a great week, JLM! ✨

#JuliaLeeMoore #ATLASTesting #StudentSuccess #TestingTips #JLMmustangs

text:
🍎 Let's take a moment to shine a bright spotlight on the heart and soul of Julia Lee Moore Elementary—our incredible principal, Mr. Kenny Clark! 🌟

Being a principal is so much more than managing a building; it’s about shaping the future, one student at a time. Whether he’s greeting students with a high-five in the morning, supporting our hardworking teachers, or ensuring JLM is a place where every child feels safe, seen, and inspired, Mr. Clark does it all with a smile and true dedication.

Why we’re grateful for Mr. Clark:

His Heart for Students: He knows that every child has a story and works tirelessly to help them write a great one.

His Leadership: He leads by example, showing our JLM family what kindness, integrity, and hard work look like.

His Spirit: He makes our school more than just a place of learning—he makes it a community.

Mr. Clark, thank you for your vision, your patience, and your unwavering commitment to our kids. You make Julia Lee Moore a better place every single day!

Help us celebrate! 👇 Drop a comment below with a "Thank You" or your favorite memory of Mr. Clark to show him some JLM love!

#JuliaLeeMoore #JLMmustangs #PrincipalAppreciationDay #JLMElementary #MustangPride #ThankYouMrClark #LeadingWithHeart

text:
Our third grade scholars have been working hard in the library, and this week they finally took the stage to share their incredible animal research findings! 🎤📚
From the icy habitats of penguins to the depths of the rainforest with anacondas, these young researchers used their library time to dive deep into the animal kingdom. Using their hand-drawn posters and reports, they practiced their public speaking skills by presenting to their peers.
It was so inspiring to see their confidence grow with every "Fun Fact" shared! We are so proud of their hard work, curiosity, and the way they supported one another during their presentations. 🌟
Way to go, JLM 3rd Grade! 🦁🐧🐍

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

⏰ Important: If you haven't received your child's snapcode by August 1st, please make sure to contact your child's school. We want to ensure a smooth registration process for everyone, and our team will be more than happy to assist you with any questions or concerns you may have.

Thank you for being a part of our school community! We can't wait to welcome all the students back for another fantastic year of learning and growth. 🌟 If you have friends or neighbors who are part of our school family, don't forget to share this update with them too!

#ChampionsForKids #WeAreWampusCats

author: Mark Lewis
text:
Thank you to everyone for an amazing first day.  Everything went as smoothly as it possibly could have.  Traffic will be heavy as it always is for the first two weeks of school.  Until we get our afternoon pick-up routines operating more smoothly, we are going to dismiss all modes of transportation except for busses at 3:00.  This is so we can have traffic mostly cleared for our busses to arrive.  

Please look over the parent guide that we shared on Friday.  It has lots of helpful information such as arrival and drop-off procedures.  Also, if an older sibling comes from a secondary campus please park across the street in the designated area or in the front parking lot so that we can keep traffic flowing.  

It was great seeing our families back and walking kids to classes today.  Please remember that tomorrow begins "Independence Day" and normal drop-off procedures begin.  We will begin welcoming lunch guests on Tuesday, September 5th.  This is so we can get our lunch procedures in place prior to Labor Day.  

Thank you and I know this year is going to be amazing!

*Put First Day of School Treat in memo and your child's name*
*Put the word “EXTRA” in the memo if you are providing for other students. (We will make sure no child is left out)
*Also available for purchase with  EXACT cash or check. Just send the money to school in a labeled envelope.
Money collected from this will go towards back to special treats and activities for the students, and fundraising start-up fees for the fall fundraiser.

author: Laurel Breashears
text: This year at Jim Stone Elementary School, all students take part in a daily 40 minute block of time that is called WIN time. WIN is an acronym that stands for "What I Need," and this time is built into their daily master schedule. It is a time set aside for teachers and staff to deliver specific instruction targeting the individual needs of each student. All students in each grade level go to an assigned classroom during their WIN time sessions to receive direct, skill-based instruction based on their individual needs. This classroom may/may not be their classroom teacher and may/may not be in their grade level. We have worked extremely hard to get WIN going at Jim Stone and that causes for celebration. Student’s hard work during WIN the 1st nine weeks is celebrated with Popsicles on the Playground. Each student received a popsicle, a scratch and sniff bookmark, and little extra time on the playground. We are so excited to see the academic results from our implementation of WIN this spring.

text:
Good afternoon!

Next week is our book fair!  This week, students have received notes and flyers about the book fair with lots of information.  This book fair company is different from the one we have used in the past, but mostly everything is the same with the exception of eWallet.  This company uses gift cards instead of eWallet. 

Gift cards are an easy student payment method that won’t get lost in a backpack. They also make great gifts for teachers and librarians! You can buy book fair gift cards from our online fair, and they can be used for both online orders and in-person purchases. If you’re sending a gift card to another recipient, they’ll know who it came from. Gift card codes are delivered via email. To redeem a gift card, simply present or enter your code at checkout.

Go to efairs.literati.com. Select the “GIFT CARDS” tab at the top of the page.
 Choose a gift card amount. (For a custom amount, select “Choose Your Own Gift Card.”) 

If it’s a gift to a teacher or another student, check “Send as Gift?” and enter your recipient’s email, your name, and an optional message. Click Add to Cart, then continue to checkout.

If you don't want to print out the gift card, just forward it to bentleyk@conwayschools.info, and  Mrs. Bentley will take care of it for you.

We will also have stickers for sale for 50 cents each and pointers to help raise money so that each student can get a book at the book fair.  Some pointers are $5.00 and some are $2.00.  Tax will not be added to these purchases. These will NOT be available during Grandfriends Day.

Parents are always welcome to come and shop!

❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Abby Roberts
text:
Please join us in welcoming Mr. Josh Smith, 4th grade teacher, to our Stallion family! 

"My name is Josh Smith. I'm starting my 12th year in education, fifth year as a Wampus Cat!  I have taught every subject in 6th and 7th grade. I am pumped to be moving to 4th grade and the “land of the littles”. 

My wife and I have two boys, our oldest son, Graham, is 4 and our youngest son, Porter, is 2. They are a handful but we wouldn’t want it any other way. 

I enjoy being active with my family and laughing as much as possible. You can usually find me doing anything outside or in a CrossFit gym. I’m a big fan of the razorbacks and good food, not necessarily in that order. 

I hope those JSE 4th graders are ready for the reading and writing adventure they are about to go on!"

author: Abby Roberts
text:
Please join us in welcoming Ms. Catie Overton, K-2 1-15 classroom teacher, to our Stallion family! 

"As a Jim Stone alumni, I'm excited to be teaching at a school I have such fond memories of and with a district I attended my whole life!! I graduated from UCA in the fall of 2023 with a degree in Special Education. Currently, I am working on my masters in literacy. I had an opportunity to leave my internship early to start a teaching position in November! I am excited to take what I have learned thus far and keep growing my knowledge from the staff and students! I have always been around students with different abilities, from visiting my mom who is a special education teacher at Conway High School, to participating in Caring Cats, volunteering with Special Olympics, and teaching at and helping direct a summer camp! Inclusion and maximizing opportunities has become a passion of mine over the years and I am over the moon to make it my career!"

I live in Center Ridge with my husband Scott and youngest son (16) Tucker. My oldest daughter (26) Kaylee lives in Conway with her husband and sweet baby girl (6 months) Cozy. author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

We are off to a great start on fundraising for Winterfest!  As of right now, 1st and 4th grade are in the lead for the battle of the grades incentive we have going on. The grade that raises the most will win a field trip to IGN Academy for a celebration party! We would like to make reaching friends and family easier by using a QR code, so please save this and share it with anyone you know who would want to sponsor your student! Remember, a sponsor of $25 and your child will receive 30 tickets for the Winterfest event, a sponsor of $50 and you will receive one unlimited wristband, $100 sponsor and you will receive 5 unlimited wristbands for your family to enjoy! Also, for every $100 raised, your child will be entered into a drawing for principal for the day and two lucky students will be selected for that! If you have a business that would like to be a sponsor and receive recognition, we have options for that as well! author: Jim Stone Elementary
text:
Grandparents and other “grand” adults are very important people in children’s lives. Children feel a sense of pride and accomplishment when they know that people in their extended family and community are vested in their education.  So, we are having a special celebration!

We’re inviting the grandparents of our students to an event on Friday, November 22nd.  This event is intended for students and their grandparents or a special “grandfriend.”  We understand that all children don’t have grandparents and that some grandparents will be unable to attend.  We encourage these children to invite another special friend - - like a relative, an aunt/uncle or any “grand” friend.  Woodland Heights will also have volunteer “grandfriends” here.  Some children are also happy to share their grandparents with a classmate.  Sorry but our space is limited, so parents and siblings cannot attend this event with their student’s guests.  A parent can however attend if they are the student’s “grandfriend” for the day.

Kindergarten through Fourth Grade students will spend time with their guests in the classroom.  Refreshments will be served.  After classroom time, children are welcome to visit our annual book fair with their special guest.  

We welcome all of our guests to spend some time with your children this day!  If you plan on allowing your child to check out, please email your child’s teacher.  Also, due to space and parking we will not be able to host lunch guests this day.

The schedule for each grade is listed below:

K - 9:15-10:00
1st - 10:05-10:50

2-hour Delayed Start Announcement
All Conway Schools will have a 2-hour delayed start on Friday, February 21, 2025. School will start at 10:00am. The buses will run 2 hours later than their normal time in the morning. Snow Bus Routes will be in effect for the morning and afternoon routes.

Please visit our district website for detailed information about snow bus routes: https://www.conwayschools.org/page/inclement-weather-information.

Thank you for your understanding and we will see you tomorrow!

text:
We are excited to announce that online registration is now OPEN for Kids Run Arkansas®! 🎉

Join us on Friday, April 25, at 6:00 pm for an exciting, family-friendly event, sponsored by Groovy Smiles Pediatric Dentistry. This event is all about fun, fitness, and spending quality time with your loved ones!

Whether you're walking, jogging, or running, this event is open to kids of all ages and their parents. There’s no chip timing – just a focus on having fun, staying active, and making lasting memories together!

This year, we’re offering two amazing events:

👟 The classic 3-mile run/walk
👟 Reggie’s Rush: A new ½-mile race designed for younger kids to move in a fun and safe way. The scenic, easy out-and-back route will take participants along the beautiful Tucker Creek Trail. Reggie, the friendly face of Conway Regional Health System, will be there to inspire smiles, energy, and healthy living!
📝 Register Now HERE: https://runsignup.com/Race/AR/Conway/KidsRunArkansas

For more information, feel free to contact Mallory Lefler at 501-450-9292 ext. 309 or via email at mlefler@conwayregional.org.

🎓💙 Honoring a Legacy of Service 💙🎓
Conway Public Schools celebrated our 2025 retirees yesterday with a special luncheon recognizing 25 incredible individuals who have dedicated their lives to education—some with over 36 years of service to CPSD!

SPECIAL RECORDS TO BE DESTROYED
On July 7, 2025, the Conway Public School District will destroy Special Education records of students who graduated, moved or were dismissed from Special Education services in the district between January 1, 2019 and June 30, 2019. Students, parents and/or guardians may obtain any data from folders prior to July 7, 2024, by calling the Special Education office at (501) 450-6634, extension 0303 or emailing at records@conwayschools.info.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Bell to Bell No Cell
At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. To help keep our classrooms focused and follow state guidelines, students should not use personal electronic devices during the school day. This includes cell phones, AirPods, wireless headphones, and smartwatches. We ask that all devices be turned off and kept in backpacks during school hours.

text:
📢 UPDATED DROP OFF & DISMISSAL PROCEDURES

🚗 MORNING ARRIVAL
All vehicles traveling east toward Hogan must utilize the Blue Ribbon Loop at the south end of the building. These students will exit vehicles four at a time.
Only vehicles traveling west on College will be allowed access to the front drop off area. No vehicles will be permitted to access the front entrance by turning right. To expedite this process, please pull all the way forward, and have your child exit your vehicle at any point that there is sidewalk.

🏫 AFTERNOON DISMISSAL
Car Rider Dismissal (3:15 p.m.)
• Students in grades K, 3, and 4 will be picked up in the front of the building.
• Students in grades 1 and 2 will be picked up in the south (Blue Ribbon) loop.
• Siblings report to the younger sibling’s spot.

🚶‍♂️ Walkers and Cyclists (3:15 p.m.)
Walkers and Cyclists should use the crosswalk that crosses College.

🚌 Bus and Daycare Riders
Students who ride buses or daycare vans will be loaded between 3:15 and 4:00 when their bus or van arrives.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

text:
Dear Families, 
Over the next few weeks, your second grader will participate in a districtwide assessment. Each spring, Conway School District screens all second grade students using a nationally normed measure that evaluates students’ reasoning abilities in verbal, quantitative, and nonverbal areas. 
This assessment helps us better understand each student’s learning strengths and academic potential. The results are one of several data points we use to determine whether a student may benefit from further evaluation for gifted and talented services. There is nothing you need to do to prepare, and testing will take place during the regular school day. 
If you have any questions, please contact the Gifted and Talented teacher at your child’s school. There is also more information about GT services on the district website.

Thank you for your continued support. 
Sincerely, Conway School District

author: Jim Stone Elementary
text: We are excited to be hosting a talent show this year for our 1st through 4th grade students! If your child is interested in participating in this year’s talent show, please fill out the form below and submit it by Friday, April 24th at 4:00pm. No entries will be accepted after this date and time. The talent show will take place during school on:Wednesday, May 20th, 2026 3rd and 4th grade will be from 9:00-10:00 a.m.1st and 2nd grade will be from 1:00-2:00 p.m.**"Parents are welcome to check in through the office and come watch their child perform at the talent show.CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP "Previews" will be held in the music room and during music class the week of April 27th - May 1st. This is required in order for students to participate. If a participant is absent on their preview day, their act MUST be made up on May 4th or 5th during activity time. ** This is to ensure all acts and performances are school appropriate and reflect a talent. Students MUST bring all items required for their performance to school on their preview day (including any dance uniform or costume if applicable). All items needed for an act MUST be provided by the participant. This includes any sound files needed for music.Music for songs and dances should be provided in one of the following ways: on a CD, flash drive, or emailed to Mrs. Carroll as an MP3 file attachment.  This must be turned into Mrs. Carroll on the day of the preview. ****Mrs. Carroll will not provide music tracks.*****Please keep in mind that talents will be performed in the school's gym/safe room - so acts must be appropriate to be performed indoors and in a small area.  A piano will be available for use. Students may do a group performance with students of the other age group (ex: 1st grader with 4th grader, etc.) - they may perform for both talent shows in order for their classes to be able to see their group. Talents examples (not limited to): Singing, dancing (clog, tap, hip hop, ballet, group routine), playing an instrument, basketball dribbling, fancy soccer ball footwork, juggling, comedy routine, cheer routine, gymnastics, skit, hand clapping or body percussion routine, jump rope, hula hooping, karate. Please remember the following guidelines:* Students may only participate in one individual act.* Performances must not run over 2 minutes 30 seconds. - Please let Mrs. Carroll know if you need help trimming a music file. * Students will not be allowed to sing over a tape with a voice already on it.  They must sing with an instrument or have an accompaniment/karaoke track that is instrumental only.  * Any students doing a singing act must provide song lyrics on a piece of paper to Mrs. Carroll on the day of the preview.* Students and parents MUST provide any music file required for the act to Mrs. Carroll by preview day. You may send with your child on a CD, flash drive (MP3 file), OR email to Mrs. Carroll as an MP3 file. No online videos will be allowed. This MUST be turned in by the preview day.* Words to songs and dance moves must be appropriate (if in doubt . . . don’t do it.)* Any student who misbehaves during previews will not be allowed to participate.* A separate form must be submitted for each student in a group performance act. Please direct any questions to Mrs. Carroll at carrolle@conwayschools.info.Thank you!Mrs. CarrollElementary Music TeacherPlease fill out and submit by Friday, April 24th at 4:00pm.No entries will be accepted after this date.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

Thank you for helping us get ready for a fun day!

author: Barbara Clardy
text:
🎉BACK TO SCHOOL IS TOMORROW!🎉 

We can’t wait to welcome our little cats back for an AMAZING first day! 🐾💙 

📅 Monday, August 17 

🚗 Student Drop-Off: 
• Drop-off begins at 7:30 AM at the front of the building or in the South Loop. 
• Please do not drop students off before 7:30 — there will not be adult supervision available yet. 
• Want your student to enjoy FREE breakfast? Please arrive by 7:45 AM. 🍎🥛 
• Families are welcome to walk your little cat to class on the first day! 🥰 

Teachers will be ready to welcome students beginning at 7:45 AM. 

🚦 A little reminder for this first week: Please be patient with traffic as everyone gets back into our arrival and dismissal routines. Our MOST important job is getting every single one of our little cats home safely! 💙 Safety will always come first, and we appreciate your patience and understanding as we work through those first few days together. 

We are SO excited to see those smiling faces and kick off a wonderful school year together! 🐾💙 Let’s make it a GREAT first day! 🎉

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Out of an abundance of caution, Jim Stone Elementary was placed on a “hold” following a statement made by a student.

Conway Public School District administrators and School Resource Officers conducted a thorough investigation, and the statement was determined to be unfounded.

Students and staff have been given the all-clear, and everyone is safe. Normal activities have resumed at Jim Stone Elementary.

Thank you to our students, staff, and families for their cooperation and understanding as we worked to ensure the safety of our school community.

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text:
Vann students visit the Makerspace every other week as part of their library activity.  This space allows students to engage in hands-on learning that fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration.  To keep the creativity flowing, Ms. Etter is in need of donated items.  If you have any of the following items at home, we would greatly appreciate your contribution: 
paper towel rolls
egg cartons
fabric scraps 
packing materials (clean and flat card board, bubble wrap, Styrofoam, packing peanuts, etc.)
small or medium plastic containers (yogurt, margarine, water bottles, etc.)
small or medium cardboard containers (Pringles cans, drink carriers, etc.)
You may send items with students to drop off in the Makerspace or place them in the bin located in the front lobby.  If you have any questions, please contact Ms. Etter at etterr@conwayschools.info.

❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text: Today we kicked off our “Fast Facts” math fact fluency initiative by distributing a set of flashcards to all Vann students.  These cards may be kept at home.  Attached to these cards is a schedule we’d love for you to follow as you help your student learn their math facts at home over the next five weeks.  Our goal is students who are fluent—both quick and accurate—in their basic facts so that they can better solve more complex math problems.  If your student has already mastered the facts scheduled for one week, feel free to move on to the next week or let your child’s teacher know he/she is ready for the next set of cards.  We’ll be using our math facts to play Fast Facts Bingo at our Vann family night on April 2.  Mark your calendars and we will see you there!

text:
Marguerite Vann will celebrate National Schwa Day on Tuesday, April 9!  Wear your pajamas and be  unstressed all day! We will also enjoy some activities in class to celebrate the day!
Schwa (ə) is a sound that can take the place of any  vowel. It makes two kinds of relaxed sounds (/ŭ/ or /ĭ/) and is in the unstressed syllable of a word. Schwa makes our speech sound more natural and is the most common vowel sound in English.

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text:
DID YOU KNOW? 
Marguerite Irby Vann (1909-1996) was a music teacher for the Conway district. She and her husband, Ben Vann, owned a portion of the former Lollie Plantation from 1952 until they sold it to the Schaefers in 1973. She also led the music in the children’s department at First Baptist Church. After teaching for 15 years, she became the district supervisor of choral music in 1965. Marguerite Vann Elementary was built in 1986 and named in her honor.
(Thank you to the Faulkner County Historical Society for this information.  Find out more at https://www.faulknerhistory.org/2016/08/first-ladies-of-education-looking-back/.)

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

🌟 Kindness Challenge Begins Next Week! 🌟

Next week kicks off our Kindness Challenge here at Marguerite Vann Elementary, and we are so excited to spread kindness in our community! ❤️

As part of the challenge, we will be collecting items to support the Conway Emergency Shelter. A letter will be sent home in backpacks today with details about the items they need. Some of the items include:
🪥 Travel-size toothbrushes
🧴 Toothpaste
🛁  Shampoo/conditioner

Items can be sent with your student or dropped off at the school next week.

Thank you for helping us make a difference and showing kindness to those in need. Together, we can make a big impact! 💕

#KindnessChallenge #VannElementary #CommunityCare #ConwayEmergencyShelter

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text:
🥳🎉EXCITING news for VANN! 🎉🥳

We are so proud to announce that the Office for Education Policy at the University of Arkansas has recognized Marguerite Vann Elementary with two awards based on our 2024 content growth scores as calculated by the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education.  

Vann has been named a BEATING THE ODDS Award recipient in two categories:  High English-Language Arts Growth (Central Region) and High English-Language Arts Growth (Statewide)!

🥳🎉Congratulations to our incredible students and staff for earning this recognition!  Your hard work and dedication to learning and teaching at high levels are paying off!  We are so proud of you! 🎉🥳  #beincredible

text:
CPSD District Wide STEAM Night - Mark your Calendar!!
🚀 You’re Invited to an Unforgettable STEAM Night!
📅 Date: April 03, 2025
🕕 Time: 5:30 - 7:30 
📍 Location: Buzz Bolding Arena and James H. Clark Auditorium 
Join us for an action-packed K-12 CPSD STEAM Night—a night of hands-on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics fun for the whole family!
🚁 See a Helicopter Up Close!
🎈 Marvel at a Hot Air Balloon!
🔬 Engage with the Museum of Discovery’s Awesome Science Shows!
🎨 Watch Live Art Demonstrations!
🦁 Meet Special Animal Ambassadors From the Little Rock Zoo!
🏗️ Explore BIG Machines from Conway Corporation!
🎣 Learn from Arkansas Game & Fish Experts!
🚔 Meet First Responders, Law Enforcement Officers, & Their Equipment!
🔥 Say Hello to Smokey Bear and His Heavy Equipment!
🎓 Engage with Demonstrations from Local Colleges & Universities!
🛠️ Meet Real Engineers & Industry Experts!
👩‍🏫 Visit and Learn from CPSD Teachers!
🌟 Discover Pathways to Exciting Careers in STEAM Fields!
…and so much more! 
This is a free event open to all CPSD K-12 students and their families. Centennial Bank will be cooking free hotdogs for the whole family while supplies last. Kona Ice and Food Trucks will also be available for purchase. Don’t miss this incredible opportunity to explore, discover, and experience STEAM in action while learning how these fields can shape your future!

We can’t wait to see you there! 

Thank you, Centennial Bank and Conway Area Chamber of Commerce, for your financial support and your investment in our students!

We’ve raised $4,300 so far, and with just a little more push, we can cross that finish line together! 🚨 Here’s how YOU can help:     •    If you haven’t signed up yet, it’s not too late! 📲 Sign up here!     https://www.read-a-thon.com/readers/r/SmQtbj•    Share our Read-A-Thon on Facebook and text or email your family and friends to spread the word.     •    Encourage others to join in and support our school’s library and makerspace! Thank you to everyone who has already participated! Your support is making a HUGE difference, and we are so grateful to be part of such a wonderful school community. Let’s make this last day count — keep reading, keep sharing, and let’s hit those goals!

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text: Happy First Day of Summer!  The season officially begins with the summer solstice, which takes place this year at precisely 9:41 p.m. today (June 20, 2025).    Seasons are primarily caused by the Earth's tilt on its axis, and summer occurs when our part of the Earth is tilted toward the Sun resulting in more intense solar radiation (rays of heat from the Sun).  The summer solstice marks the day with the longest daylight hours of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, where Arkansas is located.  Enjoy every minute, Vann families! 🌎☀️

At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

Dear Parents,
We are excited to kick off the new school year! We will be using Rooms, our school's communication platform, to share important updates and connect you with your child's teacher.

Teacher Introductions
Your child's teacher will be sending an introductory message to you through the platform over the next few days. 

Action Required: Check Your Notification Preferences
To ensure you receive these important updates, please make sure your notification preferences for Rooms are turned on. You can choose to be notified by push notifications from the school app, email notifications, or SMS text messages.
To update your notification preferences, you can either use the school app or a web browser.

If you use the school app:
Open the school app.


Tap "More" and then the Settings icon.


Select "Notification preferences".


Customize your preferences for messages and announcements.


If you do not use the school app:
Log in using your mobile phone number on your phone's web browser.


Tap your name in the top-right corner.


Scroll to "Notifications" and adjust the settings for Messages and Announcements.



You can choose to receive real-time alerts, hourly updates, or a once-a-day digest.

Thank you,
Marguerite Vann Elementary

author: Matthew Coatney
text:
Good afternoon, Vann Families,

Tomorrow, August 18th, begins the first day of school for the 2025-2026 school year. We are so excited to have all of the students start tomorrow. Below are just some reminders and tips that will help the 1st day go smoothly for all. If you are on campus and have any questions or need help, you can ask anyone in a green Marguerite Vann T shirt. All of our staff members will be wearing a green shirt and will be ready to help. 

Morning Drop OffFront doors will open at 7:30am. All students will report to the cafeteria. Breakfast is from 7:30-7:55am. (students will still get a breakfast if they come in late)Students who are not eating/done eating will be dismissed to their classrooms at 7:45amThe tardy bell will ring at 8am and instruction will begin.Kindergarten students only have until 9am on the first day to report to class. For morning drop, be sure to pull all the way forward so that we can fit as many cars in as possible to unload.If you need to walk your student to the front door or they are not ready to get out of the car and walk in, please park in a parking spot. That way the line can continue to move efficiently. 

You can walk your student to class on the first day of school only. (Kindergarten students ONLY will get to be walked to class again on August 25th). Please do not park your vehicle by the sidewalk in the school parking lot. That is where cars will be moving and dropping students off. 

Students and parents will stay in the cafeteria, tomorrow morning, until it is time to dismiss students to class at 7:45am. 

We will have a morning breakfast/meet and greet for our Kindergarten families from 8-9:15am during the 1st day of school. After you drop your student off to class you can come to the library for some breakfast and meet other Kindergarten families. 

If you did not get a car pick up tag at Open House, be sure to stop by the office and get one. You will need the car rider tag to pick your student up in the carline. 

DismissalWe will begin dismissing students at 3:15pmIf your student is a walker, then you will pick them up on the side of the building inside the gated playground area. If you are picking your student up in a car, then you will need to pick them up from the front of the building. You will need to enter Carl Stuart Rd from Hubbard rd. You can get to Hubbard Rd from Timberpeg Ct, College Ave, or Bruce St. Carl Stuart is a one way street from 7am-9am & 2pm-4pm. You will not be able to get onto Carl Stuart Rd from Salem Rd during those times. When you get onto Carl Stuart Rd, you can go on either side of the road as we will have two lanes. A staff member will be outside to call for your student. Make sure you have your car rider tag. Those two lanes will merge into ONE LANE as you pull into the school parking lot. Be sure to pull all the way forward until the car in front of you stops. Even if you see your student, be sure to pull all the way forward. That way we can fit as many cars in as possible. 

With it being the first week of school, please be patient with us during car dismissal, as it takes longer than normal that first week with dismissal. 

Thank you,
Marguerite Vann Elementary

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

text:
Hello Vann families,

Vann PTO has been working hard to support our teachers, staff, and students this year. We would love to have more families join in to help us reach our goals. This email outlines a few opportunities for you to participate this month.

PTO will host pictures with the Grinch and Santa during Vann Family Night on December 16. This will be a fundraiser for PTO, which directly supports our students and staff. We are asking for a donation of at least $1 to take a picture with Santa or the Grinch. We will accept cash and Cash App. Families will be asked to use their own cameras if possible, but we will have a camera available if needed. Families may also purchase a 4x6 picture of their pose for an additional donation of at least $1. Printed pictures will be sent home with students on December 19. Please note this new fundraiser is the only activity for Family Night that will ask for a donation. All other events continue to be free. We need help to make this fundraiser successful. Please consider stopping by to take photos. We also need volunteers to operate the Photo Booth. This is a great opportunity for older siblings and other family members to assist. Here is the link to sign up to volunteer: https://www.signupgenius.com/go/60B094CA8AE22A0F58-61012956-vann

Next, December is full of holiday activities to help staff power through the end of year! PTO will sponsor Candy Apple Bar and Hot Chocolate Cart for staff. Items will need to be sent to school with your student or dropped off in the front office by Tuesday, December 10. Here is the sign-up: https://www.signupgenius.com/go/60B094CA8AE22A0F58-61009819-vann

Finally, you are always welcome to join PTO. It’s free and you can participate as actively as your schedule allows. Here is the link to sign up for PTO: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfQ-daHASWh0rateou0Mm2h8bKpK8zSvEK2Kz9UWBmwVG08SQ/viewform

Thank you in advance for your support!
Kesha Baoua and the PTO Leadership Team
