Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

author: Matthew Coatney
text:
Dear Families,

Over the next few weeks, your second grader will participate in a districtwide assessment. Each spring, Conway School District screens all second grade students using a nationally normed measure that evaluates students’ reasoning abilities in verbal, quantitative, and nonverbal areas.

This assessment helps us better understand each student’s learning strengths and academic potential. The results are one of several data points we use to determine whether a student may benefit from further evaluation for gifted and talented services. There is nothing you need to do to prepare, and testing will take place during the regular school day.

If you have any questions, please contact the Gifted and Talented teacher at your child’s school. There is also more information about GT services on the district website.

Thank you for your continued support.

Sincerely,
Conway School District

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

author: Matthew Coatney
text:
Hello Vann parents and guardians,
The Vann PTO is excited to head into the busy, but fun, month of May. We're asking for your assistance to make this an amazing month for our teachers, staff, and students. This email includes info about
Teacher Appreciation Week
May Madness
Yearbooks

Next week (May 4-8) is Teacher Appreciation Week. We celebrate all teachers and staff during this week (around 45 people!) . I have attached the flyer outlining events for each day, as well as some ideas on how to show your appreciation as a family. We're asking for help with the following:

REQUEST:
The following volunteer opportunities are available all week
Meal set-up: Assist with setting up lunch and breakfast as scheduled. If you are available to assist then please sign-up.

Copier assistance: Volunteer to make copies for teachers in the front office. If you are available any time during the week sign up and indicate your time availability.

Gifts to celebrate your students' teachers: You will receive a handout listing items teachers like. There are opportunities for your students to make items to show appreciation to their teachers (don't forget activity teachers and other staff!) and to provide other gifts.

May Madness 
May Madness Coin Challenge information went home with students last week. This is a fun activity for students to participate in, but also a necessary fundraiser for May Madness. For those new to Vann, May Madness is a fun-filled day that features stations for students to have snacks, play games, and get wet! It's one of the biggest expenses for PTO each year and it's all about the students! As the Coin Challenge flyer stated, it costs around $10 per student to host May Madness. STUDENTS DO NOT PAY TO ATTEND MAY MADNESS. Instead, we rely on donations to fund the event. Please encourage your students to participate in the Coin Challenge if at all possible, and if each student is able to collect around $10 then we will meet our budget for May Madness without a problem. 

In addition to raising funds for May Madness, we'll also need volunteers to run May Madness stations. You will receive that request at a later day. Please consider volunteering if you are available. It's a great time!

Yearbooks
If you have not already turned in yearbook orders please do so as soon as possible. They are $10. I recall last year when yearbooks were passed out to students who ordered them, there were several students who wanted to order one at that time. Unfortunately we don't order yearbooks to sell after they arrive, so please get your orders in now.

Finally, it's been a pleasure to lead the Vann PTO this year. We were able to revitalize the organization because of the hard work and dedication of all who volunteered and participated in events, and because of our wonderful staff leaders, Ms. Etter and Ms. Moore. It's not too late to join PTO. We still have work to do this year and the work for next year begins this summer.  My son is a fourth grader, so we will transition to Carl Stuart next year. Thank you for your support this year and I look forward to watching the Vann PTO continue to grow.

With appreciation,
Kesha Baoua

🚗 Car Riders — Important Reminders:
• Please remain in your vehicle during morning drop off and afternoon pick up. This helps ensure that arrival is safe, smooth, and efficient for everyone.  
• Parents/guardians should not enter the building before the designated arrival time.

We would LOVE to see all of our students on time, ready to learn, and ready to LEVEL UP!** 🎮📚

text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

Parent/Teacher Conferences are scheduled for Tuesday, October 24th and Wednesday, October 25th from 3:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

K-2 Parents: Please click on the link below to sign up for a conference time.
https://www.ptcfast.com/schools/Mattison

3rd-4th Grade Parents/Guardians:
Parent/Teacher Conferences are scheduled for Tuesday, October 24th and Wednesday, October 25th from 3:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.
To allow you the opportunity to speak with each of your child’s teachers, we will not be scheduling conference times.  Parents/guardians will go to the third and fourth grade hallway to rotate between classrooms.
Interpreters will be available on Tuesday, October 24th only.  If you need interpreter services, please be sure to come on this date.
If you have any questions, please reach out to your child’s homeroom teacher.  We look forward to talking with you about your child’s progress.

https://www.ptcfast.com/schools/Mattison

Para brindarle la oportunidad de hablar con cada uno de los maestros de su hijo, no programaremos horarios de conferencias. Los padres/tutores irán al pasillo de tres y cuarto grado para rotar entre salones de clase.
Los intérpretes estarán disponibles únicamente el martes 24 de octubre. Si necesita servicios de intérprete, asegúrese de venir en esta fecha.

Esperamos hablar con usted sobre el progreso de su hijo.

Ms. Minter, our wonderful counselor, is the newest recipient of the "I See You" award. She was presented this award by Mrs. Haynes, first grade teacher.

The kind words Mrs. Haynes said about Ms. Minter are as follows: “Having the title of counselor means that Minter goes beyond the academic needs of students. She ensures that all students have something to eat over the weekend, provides clothes/shoes, and advocates for students and families. Her giving heart has led to making sure that families in need can enjoy the joyous season without being burden. Thank you for all you do for our students, families, and staff.”

Congratulations, Ms. Minter! We are so thankful for all you do for Mattison Elementary! 💙

text: 🎉📚 Exciting News! 📚🎉Dear Parents and Guardians,We're thrilled to announce that this Friday, February 2, 2024, our Kindergarten & 1st grade students will be celebrating a special milestone – the 100th day of school! 🎉🍎✨ It's been an incredible journey of growth, learning, and fun-filled experiences, and we can't wait to mark this memorable occasion together.Our little scholars have been eagerly counting down the days and are bubbling with excitement to showcase their creativity and accomplishments. From colorful counting projects to imaginative activities centered around the number 100, our classrooms will be buzzing with joy and enthusiasm.We encourage all students to come dressed in outfits inspired by the number 100 – think colorful shirts adorned with 100 stickers, funky hats embellished with 100 sequins, or perhaps even sporting 100 beads around their necks! Let's make this day extra special by celebrating the creativity and spirit of our amazing Kindergarten learners.Please join us in spreading the word and sharing in the festivities as we commemorate this wonderful milestone in our educational journey. Thank you for your continued support, and let's make the 100th day of school a day to remember!Warm regards,PFMES Kindergarten and First Grade Teachers

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

🌟 Let's give a round of applause to our amazing media specialist, Krystal Henderson! 🌟 I'm thrilled to present her with the "I See You" award for her dedication and fantastic work at our school. Mrs. Henderson consistently stays in touch with current educational trends, using student data to help our students grow. From organizing captivating book fairs to orchestrating exciting book blasts, she continuously elevates the learning experience for our students. Currently, under her guidance, students are writing stories to publish their own books, fostering creativity and a love for literacy. Thank you, Mrs. Henderson, for your unwavering commitment to making learning not only educational but also exhilarating! 📚🎉 #MediaSpecialist #StudentGrowth #LiteracyLeadership

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

To celebrate the grand opening of Burlington's new store in Conway, AR, Burlington and AdoptAClassroom.org have generously donated $5,000 to our very own Preston and Florence Mattison Elementary School.

Superintendent Dr. Jeff Collum and Principal Shannon Black were honored to attend the ribbon-cutting ceremony, where they received the donation on behalf of the school. This support will go a long way in providing valuable resources for our students and teachers.

On behalf of the Conway School District and the staff at Preston and Florence Mattison Elementary, we extend our heartfelt thanks to Burlington and AdoptAClassroom.org for their commitment to education and our community. We look forward to seeing the positive impact this partnership will bring!

author: Preston and Florence Mattison Elementary
text:
PFMES Teacher of the Month is Mrs. Ferrell! 

We are thrilled to announce that our incredible Mrs. Ferrell has been named Teacher of the Month! 

Mrs. Ferrell exemplifies what it means to be an outstanding educator. She holds high expectations for all her students, encouraging them to reach their full potential. Her caring and nurturing nature creates a warm and supportive classroom environment where every student feels valued and motivated to learn. 

Not only does she teach with passion, but she also goes above and beyond to ensure her students succeed. Whether staying after school for extra help or finding creative ways to engage her class, Mrs. Ferrell's dedication does not go unnoticed. 

Thank you, Mrs. Ferrell, for all that you do! You truly make a difference in the lives of your students. Let's celebrate her amazing contributions to our school! #TeacherOfTheMonth #ThankYouMrsFerrell

text:
Our awesome 4th graders had an incredible educational experience when Laura Duran from Conway Regional Health Systems visited Mrs. Woods' class today! Mrs. Duran shared fascinating insights about X-rays, breaking down the science behind this important medical technology.

Students weren't just passive listeners - they actively engaged with the material and tested their new knowledge with a fun Kahoot! quiz. Mrs. Duran even took time to talk with a small group of future medical professionals who are interested in becoming radiologists. 

Huge thank you to Mrs. Duran for inspiring our young learners and showing them the cool world of medical imaging! 📚🩺 #STEM #HealthcareEducation #LearningIsFun

text:
Arkansas Children's Hospital's Dental Van will visit PFME on January 22nd to provide free dental care for eligible students with ARKids, Medicaid, or no insurance who haven't seen a dentist in the past year. Patient packets sent home in December must be returned by January 16th for scheduling, but packets will be accepted through January 30th. 

Initial cleanings and necessary follow-up treatments will be provided at no cost, all done on-site at the school without requiring parent presence. A report with findings and recommendations will be sent home afterward. 

Parents can contact the nurse at 501-450-4820 or hogank@conwayschools.info for questions or to get another packet.

text:
We are thrilled to announce that our incredible Art teacher, Mrs. Cicely Collins, has been awarded a $200 grant from the men of Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc. Out of seven nominations, she stood out as a shining example of dedication and creativity. 

But Mrs. Collins is more than just an amazing artist – she is a true champion for our school community. This year, she has gone above and beyond by offering her "Dabbles in Art Therapy" program, providing invaluable art therapy sessions for teachers before and after school. 

In a time where mental health matters more than ever, Mrs. Collins is helping our teachers practice self-care, enabling them to be at their best for their students. Her hard work and passion make our school a better place, and we are so grateful to have her on our team. 

Congratulations, Mrs. Collins! You truly deserve this recognition! #ThankYouMrsCollins #ArtTherapy #MentalHealthMatters #PhiBetaSigma

We have our first week under our belt, and it was a huge success—thanks in large part to you! Your support, encouragement, and teamwork have helped us start the year off strong, and we are so grateful.

The Mattison Team

Here are a few important reminders regarding arrival, transportation, and dismissal times:

- Morning arrival: Doors do not open until 7:35 a.m. There is no supervision outside before this time. Students must remain in vehicles with their guardians, or if they are walkers, a guardian must remain with them until the doors open. Students cannot be let out of vehicles before 7:35 a.m.

- Transportation changes must be submitted in writing before 2:30 p.m. each day.

- Student checkouts must be completed before 2:45 p.m. Parents cannot check out students after this time due to safety and traffic logistics.

- Carline dismissal runs from 3:15–3:35 p.m. If you arrive later than 3:35, you will need to walk in to check out your child, and their checkout time will be documented. Please keep in mind that our staff have other responsibilities and tasks beginning at 3:35.

We appreciate your cooperation in helping us keep arrival and dismissal smooth, safe, and efficient for all students.

With gratitude,
The Mattison Team

Although she has been a valued member of our school community for over a decade, she’s now shining in her new role as our bookkeeper. Thank you, Mrs. Freestone, for your dedication, reliability, and the many ways you support our school every day!

author: Preston and Florence Mattison Elementary
text:
Fire Prevention Day at Mattison!

Last week our students learned all about fire safety during Fire Prevention Day! Kindergarten and 1st-grade students enjoyed a fun and educational puppet show, while our local firefighters brought their popular Smoke House — giving students a hands-on experience practicing how to safely exit a house in case of a fire.

A big thank you to our amazing firefighters for teaching our students important safety skills and making learning so much fun! 

Pictures of the day can be found here:  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qqosu6Jx1DQiGCiKn1v0k54LS-1pYimO

#FirePreventionDay #MattisonStrong

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

text:
Dear PFME Families,

Thank you so much for joining us last night for PFME Lattes & Literacy! We loved seeing our Little Cats and their families reading together, creating, and engaging in so many meaningful literacy activities throughout the building. Your presence truly made the evening special.

We are excited to share that raffle drawings will be held today for students who earned six stickers on their Literacy Passport. Winners will be notified following the drawings.

We hope that the tools, activities, and resources shared during the event will help foster joyful and meaningful literacy practices at home. Whether it’s reading together, talking about books, or using one of the take-home activities, every small moment makes a big difference.

We would also like to extend a heartfelt thank you to our generous partners and sponsors who helped make this event possible:

Faulkner County Library
PBS Arkansas
Asa Biggs, local author
Shadrachs Coffee
Conway Corporation
Central Arkansas Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.

Thank you again for your continued support and partnership. We are grateful to be part of such an amazing school community and look forward to many more opportunities to learn and grow together.

Warmly,
Preston & Florence Mattison Elementary

text:
Dear Families,

Over the next few weeks, your second grader will participate in a districtwide assessment. Each spring, Conway School District screens all second-grade students using a nationally normed measure that evaluates students’ reasoning abilities in verbal, quantitative, and nonverbal areas.

This assessment helps us better understand each student’s learning strengths and academic potential. The results are one of several data points we use to determine whether a student may benefit from further evaluation for gifted and talented services. There is nothing you need to do to prepare, and testing will take place during the regular school day.

If you have any questions, please contact Mr. Duran, the Gifted and Talented teacher at Mattison. There is also more information about GT services on the district website.

Thank you for your continued support.

Sincerely,
Conway School District

Dear Mattison Families,

Paper copies of the Math Madness Jersey Design Challenge were sent home with students, but we wanted to share the information electronically as well, in case your family needs another copy. I have attached the jersey template to this email.

As part of our upcoming Math Madness Night, students are invited to complete a fun activity at home!

🏀 Jersey Design Challenge

Students will:
-Design and decorate a basketball jersey
-Pick a number to be their “player number”
-Write 3 math equations that equal their chosen number

Example (Number: 24):
12 + 12
6 × 4
48 ÷ 2

When finished, please:
Write your child’s name on the back of the jersey
Cut out the jersey

Please have your child bring their completed jersey back to school by Friday, March 13. Jerseys will be displayed at school and during Math Madness Night.

We can’t wait to see our students’ creativity and math thinking. Thank you for supporting learning at home!

text:
🏀 Join Us for Mattison Math Madness Night! 🏀

Mattison families are invited to join us for Math Madness Night this Thursday from 5:30–6:30 PM! This fun, basketball-themed event is designed for our Kindergarten–4th grade students and their families.

Families will rotate through interactive math stations where students can practice skills through games and activities like Fact Free Throws, Addition All-Stars, Bracket of Numbers, Slam Dunk Counting, and more! 🧮🏀

Students will receive a Math Madness Scorecard and can earn stickers as they complete stations. Students who complete 5 Slam Dunk Stations can enter their scorecard into a prize drawing sponsored by Academy Sports + Outdoors! 🎉

We will also have a Math Madness Hydration Station, math games, and fun activities for the whole family.

We hope you’ll join us for a night of math, movement, and family fun. We can’t wait to see our Little Cats there! 🐾

📍 Mattison Elementary

author: Preston and Florence Mattison Elementary
text:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

This Tuesday and Wednesday are critical days for our 3rd graders! We will be administering the ATLAS assessments, and I am writing to ask for your support to ensure your child is prepared and ready to do their very best.

I want to emphasize just how important these specific assessments are for your child's academic journey. **According to state law, a student's combined scores from Tuesday’s Writing test and Wednesday’s Reading test will directly determine whether they are promoted to the 4th grade.**

Because of this statewide requirement, it is absolutely essential that your child is present at school and arrives on time both days.

Our students have been working incredibly hard all year, and we want to give them every opportunity to show what they know. To help them succeed and feel confident, we highly recommend following these testing tips at home:

*   **Prioritize a good night's sleep:** Please make sure your child goes to bed early on Monday and Tuesday night. A well-rested brain focuses much better!
*   **Eat a healthy breakfast:** Whether they eat at home or here at school, a nutritious breakfast will give them the energy they need to power through the morning.
*   **Arrive on time:** Rushing into the classroom late can cause unnecessary anxiety. Arriving a few minutes early helps them settle in and relax before the test begins.
*   **Offer words of encouragement:** Remind them that they are prepared. Tell them to take a deep breath, take their time, and simply do their best!

We believe in our students and know they are ready to shine. Thank you so much for your continued partnership and for making sure your child is set up for success these next two days.

If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out.

Estimados padres y tutores:

¡Este martes y miércoles son días cruciales para nuestros estudiantes de 3.º grado! Estaremos administrando las evaluaciones ATLAS y les escribo para pedir su apoyo para asegurarnos de que su hijo/a esté preparado/a y listo/a para dar lo mejor de sí.

Quiero enfatizar lo importantes que son estas evaluaciones específicas para la trayectoria académica de su hijo/a. **Según la ley estatal, los puntajes combinados del examen de Escritura del martes y el examen de Lectura del miércoles determinarán directamente si el estudiante es promovido al 4.º grado.**

Debido a este requisito a nivel estatal, es absolutamente esencial que su hijo/a asista a la escuela y llegue a tiempo ambos días.

Nuestros estudiantes han trabajado increíblemente duro todo el año y queremos darles todas las oportunidades para que demuestren lo que saben. Para ayudarlos a tener éxito y sentirse seguros, recomendamos ampliamente seguir estos consejos en casa:

*   **Priorizar un buen descanso:** Por favor, asegúrese de que su hijo/a se vaya a dormir temprano el lunes y el martes por la noche. ¡Un cerebro bien descansado se concentra mucho mejor!
*   **Tomar un desayuno saludable:** Ya sea que coman en casa o aquí en la escuela, un desayuno nutritivo les dará la energía que necesitan para rendir toda la mañana.
*   **Llegar a tiempo:** Entrar apurado y tarde al salón de clases puede causar ansiedad innecesaria. Llegar unos minutos temprano los ayuda a acomodarse y relajarse antes de que comience la prueba.
*   **Ofrecer palabras de aliento:** Recuérdeles que están preparados. ¡Dígales que respiren profundo, que se tomen su tiempo y que simplemente den lo mejor de sí mismos!

Creemos en nuestros estudiantes y sabemos que están listos para brillar. Muchas gracias por su colaboración continua y por asegurarse de que su hijo/a esté preparado/a para el éxito durante estos próximos dos días.

text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. Parents of Ida Burns Shuttle Bus Riders, please read a message from Mrs. Howell-

We are consistently having an issue with students being let out of their cars in the middle of the street. This is a huge safety concern for us. Students should be let out in the designated area of the Ida Burns parking lot or you may park in the high school parking lot and have students walk up the sidewalk. Your student's safety is our top priority and it is unsafe to let students out in the middle of the street. Parking in the cafeteria parking lot is not a drop-off area. This is reserved for our delivery trucks and those who work in our cafeteria.  Students have been asked to waive the person on duty if they are worried about missing the bus.  As a reminder, buses are dismissed at 7:30 to ensure that students have enough time to get to Ruth Doyle and have the opportunity to eat breakfast.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Marguerite Vann Elementary
text:
Hello,

We had a great meeting Tuesday night about our trip June 2025 to New York City! If you were not able to make it, please visit our trip website which includes itinerary highlights, how to register, and other important information: https://worldstrides.com/custom/2025-ruth-doyle-ms-ny-215872/. Be sure to watch the video to see just how much fun your student will have on the trip!

Here’s some additional information about our trip:

•               Our Trip ID is 215872. Use this to sign up at worldstrides.com/signup or by phone at 800-468-5899.

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text:
Exciting News for Our Middle Schools! We will begin implementing Yondr pouches on November 4, 2024. Students will receive their own Yondr pouch to take home on that morning.

What does this mean for students? To create a focused and distraction-free environment, all cell phones, smart watches, and other wearable tech will be secured in these special bags during school hours. Students are required to bring their Yondr pouches every morning and place their devices inside before entering the school. The bags will remain with them, but all devices must be turned off during school hours. At the end of the day, students will unlock their Yondr pouches as they exit the school and will keep their pouches with them. This initiative will help foster learning, connection, and engagement—without the screens! Students will be able to access their devices at the conclusion of the school day. 

Important Reminder: Violating district policy regarding the possession of cell phones can lead to disciplinary action. Students who tamper with the Yondr pouch, repeatedly forget to bring their pouch, damage or take another student's Yondr pouch, or use their phone without authorization during the school day may face consequences ranging from warnings and phone confiscation to detentions, Saturday school, or in-school suspension. Additionally, restitution may be required to replace a Yondr pouch.

We will also be participating in a survey of students as part of a program supported by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders and the Office of Education Policy. This survey aims to gather valuable insights into the effectiveness of our new policies and the overall school experience. Consent forms will be sent home soon, so please return them to your student's third period teacher by November 8, 2024.

Let’s work together to enhance our students’ educational experience!

text:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

In our ongoing commitment to ensuring the safety and well-being of our students, we conduct regular safety drills throughout the school year. These exercises are crucial in preparing both our students and staff to respond effectively in the event of an emergency.

We want to inform you about an important reunification drill scheduled for November 22nd at Ruth Doyle. This drill will help us practice efficient procedures for transporting our students to the reunification site, where students will be reunited with their family members during an emergency situation. This drill is dedicated to transporting ONLY! Students will be released at the normal time and place on this date. We believe that thorough preparation is essential for safeguarding our children.
Students will be getting permission slips that need to be signed and returned including the option to opt out of this drill. 

Key Details:
Date: November 22nd
Time: 8:30 AM - 10:30 AM

If you have any questions or concerns about this drill, please feel free to reach out. We appreciate your support and cooperation in helping us maintain a safe school community.

Thank you!

Best regards,
Eric King

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text:
RDMS is honoring Black History Month by engaging students in a daily reflection on the remarkable contributions of African Americans who have shaped the world through perseverance, creativity, curiosity, hard work, and groundbreaking achievements. Every day, we spotlight inspiring individuals whose legacies paved the way for others across various fields—whether in science, the arts, politics, technology, or civil rights.

Some of those individuals so far are:

·         George Washing Carver

·         Thurgood Marshall

·         Dr. Mae Jemison

·         Lonnie Johnson

Each day, our school will listen to powerful stories and quotes from African American leaders, thinkers, and innovators who overcame obstacles to make lasting impacts. These daily inspirations serve as a reminder of the power of resilience and the importance of continuing to push boundaries in our own lives.

We encourage everyone to take a moment to reflect on how these historical figures' courage and determination continue to inspire positive change in today’s world. Whether it’s through the arts, technology, education, or activism, their stories remind us that anyone, regardless of their background, can contribute to transforming society.

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text: In February, 6th graders Melanie, Henry, and Greer swept the Junior Historical Paper category at History Day Regionals, earning spots at the State competition. This weekend, all three students—along with their families—braved flash flooding to successfully present their papers to judges at UCA. Greer’s paper on The Lost Year in Little Rock earned the Special Arkansas History Prize, awarded by the Butler Center for Arkansas Studies and the Central Arkansas Library System. Henry placed second in the STATE for his paper on the Newsboys Strike of 1899, qualifying him for the National History Day contest in Washington, D.C. this June! Congratulations to all three students on their outstanding achievements!

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text:
Ruth Doyle Families,
We hope you're having a great summer! In compliance with new state law and district policy, here is information regarding your student's access to personal devices for the upcoming year.  
Middle school is a time to focus on learning, growing, and building strong connections. To support this—and in line with state law—students are not allowed to use personal electronic devices (cell phones, AirPods, smartwatches) during the school day. Devices must be turned off and kept in lockers or backpacks.

✅ Student Expectations:
Students must keep devices off and stored—no use during the school day. Devices may be accessed after the final bell.

For more information, please visit: https://docs.google.com/document/d/11-mjNBe068OQCmvbw4gSmCTcCgdwEBAgpDOyljcM24A/edit?usp=sharing

Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

text:
Dear RDMS Families,

We are excited to kick off the new school year! We will be using Rooms, our school's communication platform, to share important updates and connect you with your child's teacher.

Teacher Introductions:
Your child's teacher will be sending an introductory message to you through the platform.

Action Required: 
Check Your Notification Preferences
To ensure you receive these important updates, please make sure your notification preferences for Rooms are turned on. You can choose to be notified by push notifications from the school app, email notifications, or SMS text messages.
To update your notification preferences, you can either use the CPSD app or a web browser.

If you use the school app:
Open the school app (Conway Public Schools).
Tap "More" and then the Settings icon.
Select "Notification preferences".
Customize your preferences for messages and announcements.

If you do not use the school app:
Log in using your mobile phone number on your phone's web browser. rooms.thrillshare.com
Tap your name in the top-right corner.
Scroll to "Notifications" and adjust the settings for Messages and Announcements.

You can choose to receive real-time alerts, hourly updates, or a once-a-day digest.
Please use the following link for more information.  
https://info.apptegy.com/for-parents-and-guardians

Thank you!

text:
In Mr. DeStefano’s 6th grade world history,  RDMS students stepped back in time into an Ancient Egyptian marketplace! Each student took on the role of a farmer, fisherman, trader, or artisan and bartered with their classmates to collect the goods they needed. The room was buzzing with negotiations as students learned about bartering, supply and demand, scarcity, and trade routes along the Nile River. 

It was amazing to see how creative they were in making deals and how excited they were to complete their secret missions. History truly came alive today in our classroom!

text:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

We are excited to remind you about our upcoming 2027 Washington, DC Trip during Spring Break – March 23–26. This will be a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for our students (5th,6th,&7th) to explore our nation’s capital and experience history in a meaningful and memorable way.

Trip Highlights include:

Touring several memorials on the National Mall


Visiting the Holocaust Museum, White House, and U.S. Capitol


Exploring Mount Vernon, Ford’s Theater and a Smithsonian Museum


Traveling to Williamsburg, VA for a historic tour


Enjoying a fun-filled day at Busch Gardens and more

This is an all-inclusive trip covering travel, lodging, meals, entrance fees, and activities.

We encourage families to secure their student’s spot (Deposit $49) soon so they don’t miss out on this incredible experience. Enroll by 11/15 and receive at least a $100 discount. You can register at www.worldstrides.com/register or call 1-800-468-5899. Use trip ID #224733. Scholarship money is also available and usually runs out by mid-November.  Visit www.worldstridesfundraising.com for more details.  If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out. We look forward to sharing this unforgettable journey with our students!

Please don’t let money be the primary reason for not enrolling your child.  There are many ways to fund this trip with fundraisers, etc.  

Sincerely,
Angela Rogers

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.

RDMS Fall Food Drive (Nov 10–21)
RD Student Leadership Team + Soul Food Café = feeding families before Thanksgiving!

How to help:
• Send ready-to-heat, non-perishable items (no fridge/freezer/glass).
• Students drop donations in their WIN/Homeroom collection box daily.

Great items: canned soups/stews/chili/pasta, canned meats (tuna/chicken), instant/microwave meals or rice cups, canned veggies/beans, fruit cups/applesauce (sealed plastic), granola bars/crackers/snacks.

🎈 Balloons Over Broadway in WIN! 🎈

Mrs. Daniel, Mrs. Willcutt, and our Caring Cats had a wonderful time reading Balloons Over Broadway! We explored the fascinating story behind the creation of the Macy’s Day Parade and the incredible artistry that brings those giant balloons to life.

After learning about the history and engineering behind the parade, students got to design and create their very own parade balloons during WIN this week.

It was amazing to see creativity, design skills, and collaboration shine in every group. What an inspiring and fun way to kick off the holiday season! 🎉🎨🥳

text:
Things got wild in Mr. Carroll's 6th Grade Science!
Mr. Carroll’s class cracked open dragon eggs to explore how parents pass genetic traits to their offspring. After “hatching” their dragons, students teamed up to uncover each parent’s traits and used Punnett Squares (plus a little luck!) to predict what their baby dragons would look like. Science + imagination = an awesome day of learning!
#RDMStrong

text: Mrs. Willcutt and Mrs. Daniel’s classes read stories this week about New Year Celebrations around the world. We learned about many different traditions. One we explored today was  making New Years Ramen. We read that eating long noodles for the New Year symbolizes good luck, longevity, and prosperity in many Asian cultures, especially Chinese and Japanese traditions, where longer noodles represent a longer life. Here’s to a long and healthy 2026!

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text:
Dear Parents,

We are excited to share an amazing summer opportunity for your child — Camp Invention 2026! This nationally recognized, hands-on summer enrichment program is designed to spark creativity, boost confidence, and ignite a lifelong love of learning through exciting STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) challenges.

🌟 What Is Camp Invention?
Camp Invention is a week-long, fun-filled day camp for children entering first through 6th grade. Led by caring, qualified local educators, campers dive into collaborative, hands-on activities that encourage curiosity, problem solving, ingenuity, and teamwork; all while having a blast! 
🚀 What Will Your Child Experience?
This year's 2026 “Spark” curriculum is packed with inspiring challenges that bring big ideas to life:

Space Morphers™: Build and launch a DIY rocket, conduct a rover mission, and explore scientific discoveries that stretch imaginations.

Make Waves™: Dive into entrepreneurship and physics as campers experiment with buoyancy and design their own billboard boat prototype.

Fur-ensics™: Sharpen detective skills by investigating clues with robotic capybaras and exploring forensic science fundamentals.

The Infringers™: Kids unlock their innovation superpowers — inventing, protecting ideas, and learning about real-world intellectual property concepts.

🌱 What Your Child Will Gain:
Camp Invention is more than summer fun — it cultivates real skills that support academic growth and confidence. Parents consistently report that campers return with:

Increased curiosity and confidence

Enhanced creative problem-solving and collaboration skills

A deeper interest in STEM and learning

New friends and unforgettable memories

📅 Program Details & Registration
Location: Ida Burns Elementary School 1201 Donaghey Ave, Conway, AR 72034

Date & Time: June 1 - 5, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 3:30 PM

Director: Anita Reynolds | reynoldsa@conwayschools.info

👉 Register soon Register by 3/31 and use Promo Code: SUM25 for $25 off. Visit Camp Invention Registration to start this amazing experience!

Let's make this summer one your child will never forget — full of discovery, invention, and joyful learning!

author: Ruth Doyle Middle School
text:
Ladies and gentlemen, students and staff — it is time to celebrate excellence at Ruth Doyle Middle School! 

The 2026–2027 Teacher of the Year is someone who doesn’t just teach… she builds leaders, strengthens character, and invests deeply in every athlete who walks into her gym.

Please join me in congratulating…

🥇 Coach Rhonda Holloway! 🥇

Coach Holloway is the definition of what it means to lead from the front. She invests in her athletes — not just in wins and scoreboards — but in confidence, discipline, grit, and heart.

She teaches:

	•	Accountability when it’s hard
	•	Teamwork when it matters
	•	Perseverance when things don’t go as planned
	•	Respect on and off the court


Her athletes know she believes in them — and because she believes in them, they believe in themselves.

She shows up early.
She stays late.
She pushes her students to be their best — and then celebrates them when they get there.

At RDMS, we talk about pride, ownership, and culture. Coach Holloway lives it daily. Whether in the classroom, the locker room, or the hallway, she represents what it means to be a champion for kids.

And today’s celebration is even more special — her parents and sister were able to join her for the photo that will be shared with this announcement. It’s a beautiful reminder that behind every great educator is a family who helped shape the character, work ethic, and heart we see poured into our students every day.

Coach Holloway, thank you for investing in our students, modeling excellence, and raising the standard for all of us.

RDMS, let’s give it up for your 2026–2027 Teacher of the Year — Coach Rhonda Holloway! 👏🔥💙

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Casey Buck
text:
The Conway Public Schools Orchestra program presents its annual "La Fiesta Orquesta" Taco Supper on Thursday, November 21 on the campus of Conway High School from 5:00-9:00 pm. This southwestern-themed event features the nearly 300 students of the orchestra program in free concerts throughout the night. All performances take place in the James H. Clark Auditorium, with city-wide Intermediate Orchestra performing first at 5:30, the Conway High School Orchestra performing at 6:15, city-wide beginning orchestra students at 7:30, and the Conway Junior High School 8th and 9th grade orchestras at 8:15. 

The event also serves as the orchestra program's primary fundraiser, with money raised through dinner ticket sales, donations, and a silent auction. Dinner service is held from 5-8 pm in the Conway High School cafeteria, and the meals include drinks and dessert as well. Meal tickets for the taco salad dinner (or soft taco child's plate) are on sale online at conwayorch.square.site or at the door the night of the event for $15/adults and $10/children. Dinner is available for dine-in or for carryout. The silent auction, with many items donated by local businesses, will take place from 5:30-8:15 p.m. in the lobby of the James H. Clark Auditorium. 

We hope you’ll support these amazing students and come hear us play!!

text:
In the Summer of 2026, students from Simon Middle School have the opportunity to enjoy an 8-day tour of Costa Rica! Students will fly into Costa Rica and enjoy a zipline experience through the rainforest, whitewater rafting, snorkeling, hiking , learn about the cocoa tree along with a chocolate tasting, and much more! 
All arrangements are made through EF tours. Mr. Rogers from Simon Middle will be traveling with this group.
If you are interested, please attend the informational meeting on January 22 at 6:00 PM in the cafeteria, which you can register for at the link below. author: Simon Middle School
text: Dear Simon Middle School Families, We want to make you aware of our upcoming ATLAS Summative Testing, which will begin on Thursday, April 24th. These assessments are an important part of how we measure academic growth and identify ways to best support our students moving forward. Below is the schedule for testing: Thursday, April 24th – Writing Tuesday, April 29th – Reading Wednesday, April 30th – Science Thursday, May 1st – Math Testing will take place each morning. Please help your child be successful by ensuring the following: Arrive on time to school. Get a good night’s sleep before each test. Eat a healthy breakfast at home or take advantage of breakfast served at school. Bring a fully charged Chromebook each day. Make-up testing will be available each afternoon for students who are absent. We will communicate with teachers about students needing to make up tests. We are proud of the effort our students have shown all year long, and we’re confident they’ll do great on these assessments. Thank you for your continued support in helping our students succeed! If you have any questions or need additional information, please don’t hesitate to contact the school office. Asunto: Información Importante: Pruebas Sumativas ATLAS Próximamente Estimadas familias de Simon Middle School: Queremos informarles sobre las Pruebas Sumativas ATLAS que comenzarán el jueves 24 de abril. Estas evaluaciones son una parte importante de cómo medimos el crecimiento académico y cómo identificamos las mejores maneras de apoyar a nuestros estudiantes. A continuación se muestra el calendario de pruebas: Jueves 24 de abril – Escritura Martes 29 de abril – Lectura Miércoles 30 de abril – Ciencias Jueves 1 de mayo – Matemáticas Las pruebas se realizarán cada mañana. Por favor, ayude a su hijo/a a tener éxito asegurándose de lo siguiente: Que llegue puntual a la escuela. Que duerma bien la noche anterior a cada prueba. Que desayune de forma saludable en casa o aproveche el desayuno que se ofrece en la escuela. Que traiga su Chromebook completamente cargado cada día.Las pruebas de recuperación estarán disponibles cada tarde para los estudiantes que estén ausentes. Nos comunicaremos con los maestros sobre los estudiantes que necesiten recuperar exámenes. Estamos orgullosos del esfuerzo que nuestros estudiantes han demostrado durante todo el año y estamos seguros de que les irá muy bien en estas evaluaciones. ¡Gracias por su continuo apoyo para ayudar al éxito de nuestros estudiantes! Si tiene alguna pregunta o necesita más información, no dude en comunicarse con la oficina de la escuela.

SPECIAL RECORDS TO BE DESTROYED
On July 7, 2025, the Conway Public School District will destroy Special Education records of students who graduated, moved or were dismissed from Special Education services in the district between January 1, 2019 and June 30, 2019. author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

On Friday, 10/10/25, Simon Middle School is having a little fun with "Anything But A Backpack" day.  
 Here are a few guidelines to follow to ensure we have a good time while staying safe:
You must be able to transport your item without assistance.
No sharp or breakable items.
No items that are unsafe or violate school rules.
It must fit through a classroom door & store easily beside your seat.
Your item should be silent, non-distracting, and must not require special accommodations from teachers.
No motorized scooters, bikes, or other ride-ons may be used as your item.
Students who bring items that do not follow these guidelines or are otherwise found to be inappropriate will be asked to store them in the office for the day and retrieve them at dismissal.  
Be safe and be creative!

text:
Please join us in congratulating and celebrating this DYNAMIC DUO! Ms. Jackson is our Simon Standard Teacher of the Month and Mrs. Holloway is our Simon Standard Employee of the Month for October! Ms. Jackson brings heart, dedication, and a genuine love for learning to everything she does. Ms. Jackson is in her very first year as a classroom teacher, and already she’s making a big impact. After working as a paraprofessional, she’s taken on the challenges of leading her own class with grace, determination, and a constant drive to grow.Students and staff alike have noticed her kindness, her eagerness to learn, and her unwavering support for both students and families. 
Ms. Holloway is a paraprofessional who supports Ms. Jackson and her classroom with patience, kindness, and incredible consistency. She doesn’t wait to be asked — she steps up, offers help, and always puts students first. One nomination said, “She offers without being asked,” and that really captures her spirit.She’s known for working well with others, being a calming presence for her students, and showing up each day with a strong commitment to our school community. As one colleague shared, “We can count on her.” And we do — every day.Thank you both for all that you do behind the scenes and in the classroom. Your reliability, compassion, and teamwork are what make Simon stronger.Thank you Sonic for showing your appreciation to our Employee of the month.#SimonStandard #EmployeeOfTheMonth #OctoberShoutout #StaffSpotlight#TeacherOfTheMonth

We’re excited to kick off our Thanksgiving Canned Food Drive, with a grade-level challenge! 
This is a great way to foster community spirit, give back, and bring a little friendly competition into the season of giving.

Drive Dates: Monday, October 27 to Friday, November 4

Prize: The grade that collects the most cans will earn points towards Action Jacks and the Snackapalooza & a movie incentive in December!

Collection Guidelines:
Students should bring in non-perishable canned goods. No expired, glass, or damaged items, please.

Each grade will have a designated spot to collect and store their cans.        
           
Totals will be counted on November 4.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Simon Middle School
text:
Simon proudly celebrated our 2nd Annual Black History Month Program ❤️💛💚 — a powerful assembly full of culture, history, and student excellence!
We were honored to welcome guest speaker Brandy R. Mimms, also known as Unique the Deaf Dancer. As a Deafblind dancer, choreographer, educator, and scholar, she shared her inspiring journey and powerful message about accessibility, sensory diversity, and the importance of embodied knowledge in the arts. Her story encouraged our students to embrace resilience, creativity, and inclusion.

The program also highlighted:

text:
Flip it. Predict it. Prove it. 
Our students are mastering probability! 
Students explored making predictions and identifying possible outcomes through real-world scenarios. In this activity, they flipped a penny and a dime simultaneously to determine all possible outcome combinations.
Over the past two weeks, students have consistently practiced these skills using charts and graphs to organize and analyze data. This instruction has been intentional in preparing them for probability-based questions that may appear on both Math and Science ATLAS assessments.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

He consistently goes beyond his duties by building meaningful relationships with students—taking time to talk with them, encourage them, and serve as a trusted adult in the building. His positive interactions leave a lasting impact and help create a supportive school environment where students feel seen and valued.
Officer Henderson’s dedication to our school community does not go unnoticed. We are incredibly grateful for the role he plays in supporting both the safety and well-being of our campus.
Congratulations, Officer Henderson, and thank you for all that you do!

text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

Car Rider & Dismissal Safety Reminder 🚗

To help keep our students safe during dismissal, please remember:

• In the car rider lane, students may only enter vehicles in front of the crosswalk.
• If you are picking up your child in the staff parking lot, please back into a designated parking space to increase visibility and allow you to see students more clearly when leaving.
• Vehicles will not be allowed to stop in the driving lane to pick up students. You must be parked in a designated parking space.
• Students will frequently cross through the parking lot, so please proceed slowly and use extra caution when leaving your parking space.

Thank you for following these procedures and helping us keep our students safe!

text:
❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

📚🍎 Exciting news! Kindergarten Registration for the upcoming school year will officially open on April 2nd, 2024! 🎉 Are you ready to embark on this incredible journey with us? 🌟

For more information and to begin the registration process, please visit our website at conwayschools.org/preregistration. Here, you'll find all the necessary details and resources to ensure a smooth enrollment experience for your little one. 🏫✏️

Remember, to enroll in kindergarten, your child must be 5 years old on or before August 1st, 2024. We can't wait to welcome your child into our school family and witness the amazing growth and learning that lies ahead! #ChampionsForKids #WeAreWampusCats #KindergartenRegistration

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🎉📚 Parents and guardians! Kindergarten Registration is NOW OPEN! 🎉📚

If your student will be 5 years old on August 01, 2024 here are the steps to register them for Kindergarten: 
1️⃣ Find your zoned elementary school.
2️⃣ Register your student online.
3️⃣ The Registrar at your student's school will be in contact.

For full information and registration links, please visit conwayschools.org/preregistration. 🏫✏️

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
We want to congratulate our Employee of the Year, Mrs. Wilkins! 
It’s hard to know all that Mrs. Wilkins does to keep Sallie Cone going! She is the Queen of the Office! When she helps new families register, she makes sure that they understand how our school works, and she even walks them around the building so that they understand what to do on their student’s first day of school. On top of that, Mrs. Wilkins keeps a close eye on the money and manages it well - which is a hard task on its own. She makes sure that money is spent properly, correct documentation is kept, and all paperwork is turned in to the Central Office on time. We can go on and on about all that she does to keep us in line - from managing timesheets to helping staff with EAC and greeting substitutes each morning. In addition to her responsibilities, Mrs. Wilkins is quick to help with any situation that arises - whether it be cleaning up from staff events, manning the cafeteria door for pick up and drop off, and so much more.


Mrs. Wilkins' work is incredibly valuable to us at Sallie Cone. However, the most impressive part is that everything Mrs. Wilkins' does is done with a smile. She is gracious to parents, encouraging to staff, and helpful to students. Thank you, Mrs. Wilkins, for being a Champion for Kids and doing all you do with a smile and a good attitude. We are blessed to have you here at Sallie Cone.

text:
CPSD District Wide STEAM Night - Mark your Calendar!!
🚀 You’re Invited to an Unforgettable STEAM Night!
📅 Date: April 03, 2025
🕕 Time: 5:30 - 7:30 
📍 Location: Buzz Bolding Arena and James H. Clark Auditorium 
Join us for an action-packed K-12 CPSD STEAM Night—a night of hands-on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics fun for the whole family!
🚁 See a Helicopter Up Close!
🎈 Marvel at a Hot Air Balloon!
🔬 Engage with the Museum of Discovery’s Awesome Science Shows!
🎨 Watch Live Art Demonstrations!
🦁 Meet Special Animal Ambassadors From the Little Rock Zoo!
🏗️ Explore BIG Machines from Conway Corporation!
🎣 Learn from Arkansas Game & Fish Experts!
🚔 Meet First Responders, Law Enforcement Officers, & Their Equipment!
🔥 Say Hello to Smokey Bear and His Heavy Equipment!
🎓 Engage with Demonstrations from Local Colleges & Universities!
🛠️ Meet Real Engineers & Industry Experts!
👩‍🏫 Visit and Learn from CPSD Teachers!
🌟 Discover Pathways to Exciting Careers in STEAM Fields!
…and so much more! 
This is a free event open to all CPSD K-12 students and their families. Centennial Bank will be cooking free hotdogs for the whole family while supplies last. Kona Ice and Food Trucks will also be available for purchase. Don’t miss this incredible opportunity to explore, discover, and experience STEAM in action while learning how these fields can shape your future!

We can’t wait to see you there! 

Thank you, Centennial Bank and Conway Area Chamber of Commerce, for your financial support and your investment in our students!

author: Kerri Wofford
text:
Today, we are wearing purple on MPS Awareness Day to show support for families impacted by child neurodegenerative disorders, Mucopolysaccharidosis or MPS. 

MPS diseases are rare genetic disorders that are present at birth, although symptoms may not manifest until early childhood before worsening progressively. Such symptoms can affect different parts of the body including airway passages, ears, facial features, the skeleton and joints, eyes, the liver, the heart, and in many cases, the brain.

An example of an MPS disease is Sanfilippo Syndrome - also known as Mucopolysaccharidosis type Ill or MPS III - is a terminal, neurodegenerative, rare disease. It causes children to lose all the skills they've gained, suffer seizures and movement disorders, experience pain and suffering, and then die, often before the second decade of life.

Because of its neurodegenerative nature and multi-system impact, Sanfilippo Syndrome is often called "childhood Aizheimer's." It is classified as a form of childhood dementia.

There is not currently an FDA treatment or cure for Sanfillipo Syndrome.

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text: 💛 A Journey of Courage, Love, and Healing 💛Today, we’re sharing a very special story from one of our own. One of our sweet students has shown incredible strength while bravely walking through a cancer journey.Nova was diagnosed with stage 4 neuroblastoma cancer at the tender age of 9 months old in 2022. She underwent 6 cycles of chemotherapy, 2 major surgeries, 21 cycles of radiation, and 5 rounds of immunotherapy. We are beyond grateful that she is now cancer free, going on 3 years in remission, and continuing her journey on a clinical trial.In honor of this incredible journey — and in recognition of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month — we invite all our students, staff, and families to wear yellow or gold on Friday, September 12th as a show of support and solidarity for all children and families affected by childhood cancer. 🎗️

author: Sallie Cone Preschool

author: Sallie Cone Preschool

Our right brain classroom has been *buzzing* with creativity, curiosity, and construction this week! 🧱🖍📚

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
🍎 Happy Me, Healthy Me! 🍎
Our Left Brain Classroom has been busy exploring and discovering all kinds of new ideas! We’ve been learning about measurement by comparing things that are long and short — even making our own lines with playdough to see the difference. We’ve also talked about nutritious foods that help our bodies grow strong, like sweet potatoes and pumpkins, and then used our art tools to draw and color them beautifully. Along the way, we’ve been learning more about our amazing bodies, matching and naming parts like the intestines, lungs, and kidneys.

Every day in the Happy Me Healthy Me room is full of curiosity, creativity, and healthy learning! 💪🎨📏

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:

From colorful leaves and pinecones to tiny rocks and twigs, each item told a story of exploration, creativity, and connection with nature. 🌿✨ The children loved showing and telling about their adventures and listening to their friends’ discoveries too!

We love seeing learning come to life through family experiences and creative expression. 💛

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
