The classroom was filled with creativity, problem-solving, and plenty of excitement as students learned how air, gravity, and design all work together to help things glide safely to the ground. 🌬️💡

We love watching our Right Brain learners think like engineers, create like artists, and have fun while doing it!

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Our little learners jumped into two super-focused activities! 🧠✨
One group created an adorable giraffe collage 🦒🎨, paying attention to visual details, while the other group practiced putting pieces in order from largest to smallest 📏🔽.

Both activities helped build visual differentiation, size comparison, and early sequencing skills! 🌟🧩

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
🫗✨ Pouring Practice in Our Left Brain Classroom! ✨🫗
Our students have been busy learning how to pour! Through hands-on practice, they’re strengthening fine motor skills, coordination, and independence—one careful pour at a time 💪🧠. We love watching their confidence grow as they focus, try, and succeed. Great job, little learners! 💙

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
🎅🥕 Learning About Healthy Choices! 🥦🍎
We talked about making healthy food choices! Using a template from our book, each group worked together to plan a healthy dinner for Santa—before he eats all those cookies 🍪😉. The kids had so much fun collaborating and thinking about foods that help keep Santa strong and energized!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Exploring cause & effect and building spatial awareness through PLAY! 💕✨

Our Right Brain students have been busy designing and measuring ramps, stacking towers of cups to find the perfect balance, and creating fun shape windows to peek through. Curious minds, busy hands, and lots of learning happening along the way! 🧠🎨🧱

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Sorting, counting, and learning through hands-on fun! 🐶🦁🔢
Our students have been busy sorting animals and counting objects, building early math skills while exploring.

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text: Our students are using kitchen tools like teaspoons and tablespoons to measure and compare, turning everyday items into fun learning moments. Hands-on measuring, lots of curiosity, and big smiles all around! 🥄✨

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Big ideas in the Think It Build It Room! 🧱✨

We constructed cube machines and built sentences, combining creativity, problem-solving, and early literacy all in one fun-filled space. Hands-on learning and proud smiles everywhere! 💕📚

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Little builders hard at work! 🧱✨

Planning, building, creating, and exploring concepts like structure, letters, and patterns—our students are learning through hands-on discovery. With trial and error, they carefully place each block to see what makes their towers topple or stand strong. So much thinking, creativity, and fun! 💕

author: Heather Leavell

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
So much sensory fun! ✨
We played in oobleck, explored some very “smelly” bottles 🤭, and used all five senses to investigate an orange 🍊
Messy hands, curious minds, and lots of learning! 💛

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Learning through play at its best! 🚗🧱
Using a Play-Doh mat to create construction safety hats, students strengthened their fine motor skills while having fun. They counted and sorted cars to build early math skills like number recognition and one-to-one correspondence, and explored letter shapes while continuing to develop those little hand muscles.
So much learning packed into playful moments! 💛✨

text:
Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text: Students in the Right Brain Classroom had a happy and healthy learning experience as they studied the life and work of Alma Thomas, a renowned African American artist and educator. After exploring her unique artistic style, students created their own original artworks inspired by her work. We are proud of their creativity and enthusiasm for learning!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Happy Me, Healthy Me 💛🧠🎨
Our classroom was buzzing with creativity and self-reflection! Students gathered in a Right Brain classroom, used mirrors to take a close look at themselves, and thoughtfully sketched self-portraits. Using soft pastels, they added color, emotion, and personality to their artwork—celebrating what makes each of them unique.
This activity wasn’t just about art; it was about confidence, self-awareness, and learning to appreciate who we are inside and out. Beautiful faces, bright colors, and even brighter minds! 🌈✨

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
In our Zoom and Vroom Room, we learned about Garrett Morgan, the brilliant inventor who created the three-light traffic signal 🚦

Garrett Morgan’s invention helped make our roads safer by adding the caution (yellow) light between stop and go — something we still use every single day! We love learning about inventors who made a big difference in our world.

Way to go, Zoom and Vroom Room learners! 💛

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
In the Happy Healthy Me Room, our little learners stepped into the world of architecture and community helpers! 🏗️✨
We’ve been learning about Robert Robinson Taylor, a groundbreaking architect and the first African American graduate of MIT. His creativity and determination inspired us to design and build structures of our own!
Using blocks and loose parts, students worked together to create dentist offices, doctor’s offices, and hospitals — exploring how buildings help keep our communities healthy and strong. 🏥🦷🩺
Their imaginations (and teamwork!) were hard at work. We love seeing our future architects in action! 💛

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Our little engineers have been hard at work in Bigger Than Big! 🏗️🎢

The students have been busy designing and building their very own roller coasters and towering skyscrapers. From twisting tracks to sky-high structures, their creativity and teamwork have been absolutely amazing to watch!

We love seeing their imaginations grow bigger and bigger as they explore, build, and problem-solve together. The future architects and engineers of the world are definitely in the making! 💙✨

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text: Talking with your child does more than pass the time, it builds trust, strengthens your bond, and helps them feel seen and valued. Meaningful conversations support their confidence and emotional growth, while creating a safe space for them to share their thoughts and feelings. When we truly listen, we’re building connection that lasts. 💬✨

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
We are proud to announce our Teacher of the Year, Mrs. Carter, and our Employee of the Year, Mr. Rose!

🍎 Mrs. Carter goes above and beyond every single day in her classroom. She creates engaging, meaningful lessons and activities that inspire her students to learn and grow. Her classroom is a warm, safe, and inviting space where students feel supported and encouraged. It’s no surprise her students adore her! We are so grateful to have Mrs. Carter as part of the Sallie Cone family.

🌟 Mr. Rose truly exemplifies what it means to be a team player. He is always willing to help wherever he is needed and brings incredible energy to our school. He creates exciting and engaging activities for his class, and his enthusiasm makes a lasting impact on his students. They love him, and so do we! We are so thankful to have Mr. Rose as part of our team.

Please join us in congratulating these two outstanding educators for the difference they make every day at Sallie Cone! 👏💙

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Think It, Build It
Our students are putting their creativity and imagination to the test, designing, building, problem-solving, and bringing their ideas to life. It’s amazing to watch their confidence grow as they turn simple materials into incredible creations!

Hands-on learning at its best, where big ideas start small and innovation takes shape every day. 💡🚀

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Happy Me, Healthy Me! 💚

We are learning all about keeping our bodies healthy! From caring for our teeth to understanding how our bodies work, students explored simple ways to stay strong and feel their best.

Healthy habits help build happy hearts, bright smiles, and growing minds! 😊

author: Sallie Cone Preschool

Our students have been exploring the beauty of nature through creativity and hands-on learning! From making pictures inspired by the natural world to designing beautiful flower arrangements, they are discovering the colors, textures, and patterns all around us. 🌿

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
In our classroom, we have been exploring pets and how to care for them through the lens of the Fueling Brains curriculum! Our Pre-K learners are building essential executive function skills as they discuss what pets need to stay healthy—like food, water, shelter, and love. 
Through hands-on activities and meaningful conversations, students are strengthening empathy, responsibility, and cognitive connections, all while developing the social-emotional skills that support lifelong learning.

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Today, the children explored the work of artist Piet Mondrian and his unique style of art. Through the Fueling Brains approach, students engaged in meaningful, hands-on learning as they discovered his use of bold lines, simple shapes, and primary colors.

Inspired by his work, the children created their own masterpieces using strips of paper, markers, crayons, and pencils. As they experimented with lines, colors, and design, they strengthened creativity, critical thinking, and fine motor skills—bringing their ideas to life in their own special way!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
What would you like the caption or message to say with this photo?  
*
Our preschoolers have been busy little builders! 🏗️ After reading *The Three Little Pigs*, we explored how different materials can be used to construct strong and safe homes.

The students got hands-on with building by using red LEGO blocks for the brick house, Lincoln Logs for the wooden house, and foam blocks designed to look like sticks for the third home. They experimented, problem-solved, and discovered which structures were the strongest—just like in the story!

To bring it all together, each child retold their own version of *The Three Little Pigs*, combining their creative builds with storytelling. Learning through play, imagination, and construction made this experience both fun and meaningful!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Spending time in the garden offers Pre-K children a rich, hands-on way to build essential executive function skills. 

As they plant, water, and care for living things, children practice patience, focus, and self-control while following multi-step directions. Gardening also encourages flexible thinking and problem-solving as they observe changes, make predictions, and adjust their actions.

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Teacher Appreciation Week at Sallie Cone Preschool was truly “over the rainbow” special! 🌈

We are incredibly grateful for the love and support shown to our staff by our amazing administration, families, community members, and district partners. From colorful spirit days celebrating our teachers to the thoughtful meals and treats provided throughout the week, every gesture reminded us how appreciated we are.

A special thank you to Centennial Bank for providing hamburgers and all the fixings, Horace Mann Insurance for providing breakfast, The Tropical Charcuterie  for the adorable and delicious charcuterie cups, Cross Creek Cookies from the district, Sweet House for the yummy sweets and donuts, and everyone else who contributed to the gifts and treats throughout the week.

We are also so thankful for the many parents and families who brought flowers, candy, thoughtful gifts, and helped their children create sweet drawings and pictures for our teachers. Those personal touches meant so much to us and truly made our week extra special.

Thank you all for loving on us, feeding us, and making our teachers feel celebrated in such meaningful ways. We are so thankful to be part of such a caring community! 💛

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
In our Left Brain room at Sallie Cone Preschool, the children have been exploring the fascinating world of artist Pablo Picasso and learning about the many art materials he used to express creativity. This week, we focused on oil pastels and discovered the different textures, patterns, and blending techniques they can create.

Through hands-on exploration, the children strengthened fine motor skills, creative thinking, and self-expression while experimenting with color and texture in their own unique masterpieces. We love watching their imaginations come to life through art!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
Small group instruction is such an important part of learning in Pre-K because it gives teachers the opportunity to connect more closely with each child while gaining a better understanding of what they have learned and mastered. In these smaller settings, children are encouraged to participate, ask questions, practice important skills, and build confidence in a supportive environment.

Even with only a few days of school remaining, learning and growth are still happening every single day! Through small group activities, the children continue strengthening communication, problem-solving, listening, and critical thinking skills while preparing for their next big adventure. We are so proud of how much they have learned and grown this year!

author: Sallie Cone Preschool
text:
In our STEM center in the Right Brain room, the children engaged in a hands-on engineering activity by using screws and tools to build and assemble their own cars. This activity encourages problem-solving, critical thinking, and early engineering skills through play-based learning.

As the children carefully connected each piece, they strengthened fine motor development, hand-eye coordination, patience, and perseverance. Activities like these help foster creativity and confidence while introducing important STEM concepts in a fun and meaningful way!

The letters may not all be perfectly connected yet, but they are recognizing and independently attempting the letters in their names—and that is meaningful growth worth celebrating!

author: Marci Martin
text:
Dear Sallie Cone Preschool Families,

Now that we are getting settled into the school year, we want to share a few important reminders from our Parent Handbook regarding arrival and dismissal procedures. Thank you for helping us keep our school day safe and running smoothly! 💙

🌅 Morning Drop-Off | 7:50–8:10 a.m.
Morning drop-off is 7:50–8:10 a.m.
If you arrive after 8:10, you must check your child in at the parent entrance and breakfast will not be provided.
A picture ID is required before entering the building to check in your child.

⏰ Arrivals After 9:00 a.m.

Students may NOT be checked in after 9:00 a.m. without appropriate documentation for the late arrival.

Acceptable documentation may include a doctor’s note, therapy appointment note, court documentation, or other official documentation.

Students arriving after 9:00 a.m. without documentation will not be permitted to attend school for the remainder of the day.

Late arrivals impact classroom instruction, lunch counts, and the required teacher-to-student ratios for our preschool classrooms. We appreciate your help in minimizing these disruptions.

🚗 Transportation Changes | Before 2:00 p.m.

Need to change how your child is going home? Please message your child’s teacher through Procare before 2:00 p.m.

Transportation changes cannot be made by phone or after 2:00 p.m.

🚫 No Checkouts | 2:40–2:55 p.m.

For student safety and to allow us to complete our dismissal procedures, students may NOT be checked out between 2:40 and 2:55 p.m.

🏠 Afternoon Pickup | 2:55–3:15 p.m.

Dismissal ends at 3:15 p.m.

After 3:15, you will be required to show a picture ID before your child is released. Parents and emergency contacts will be contacted for students who have not been picked up. If no one can be reached, the School Resource Officer will be contacted.

author: Theodore Jones Elementary
text:
Theodore Jones has been recognized by the Office for Education Policy (OEP) as a school that is Beating the Odds, because students demonstrated high growth on the ACT Aspire even though the school serves a high percentage of students who participate in Free and Reduced Lunch.

Awards are based on the 2023 content growth score calculated by the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education. These growth scores reflect how much students at the school improved from 2022 compared to how much they were expected to grow considering prior achievement.

Theodore Jones received the "Beating the Odds" awards for 
High ELA Growth (Statewide)
High ELA Growth (Central region)

#ThisisTJ

❄️Inclement Weather make up day information ❄️

Conway Public Schools will not be in session, as planned, on February 19, 2024 in observance of President's day.  
The District will be seeking waiver approval from the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to transition the remainder of the 2023-2024 school year to serve minutes versus days.  This would allow the current published calendar to remain intact and not add additional days to the end of the school year.  

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
🍎Incoming Kindergarten Students🌟

Conway Public Schools will prepare Kindergarten students to begin their first year in education.  This year, beginning August 19, 2024, all kindergarten students will participate in Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp!  

Week of August 12 - Open House (check your school’s schedule for date/time - link below)
During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

author: Theodore Jones Elementary
text:
We invite you to participate in a special Change Drive on the morning of October 24th, dedicated to supporting Terrence, a Conway high school student who is bravely fighting cancer.

Terrence has shown incredible strength and resilience during this challenging time, and as a community, we have the opportunity to rally around him. Every coin counts, and your contributions can make a significant difference in his journey.

Please consider bringing your spare change to drop off during morning carpool. Together, we can show Terrence that he is not alone in this fight. Let's unite as a school community to support him in his time of need.

Thank you for your generosity and support. Together, we can make a positive impact!

🕕 Time: 5:30 - 7:30

Join us for an action-packed K-12 CPSD STEAM Night—a night of hands-on Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics fun for the whole family!
🚁 See a Helicopter Up Close!
🎈 Marvel at a Hot Air Balloon!

Thank you, Centennial Bank and Conway Area Chamber of Commerce, for your financial support and your investment in our students!

At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. To help keep our classrooms focused and follow state guidelines, students should not use personal electronic devices during the school day. This includes cell phones, AirPods, wireless headphones, and smartwatches. We ask that all devices be turned off and kept in backpacks during school hours.

text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

author: Theodore Jones Elementary
text:
Dear Parents,

We would like to inform you that our school has recently transitioned to a new visitor check-in system.  This will be used to check in for meetings, check in for late arrival and to check your students out. Once fully implemented and populated with information, this system will allow us to process visitors in a more efficient and streamlined manner.

Because this system is not compatible with our previous one, any IDs that were scanned in the past are no longer stored.  As a result, we will need to scan your ID again the next time you visit the school so please make sure you bring the physical drivers license. As always please remember that you will always need your ID to enter the building at any point for student and staff safety. 

With several end-of-year events approaching, we kindly ask that you plan ahead and be sure to bring a valid ID with you whenever you enter the building.

We appreciate your patience and understanding as we make this transition.  We are confident this new system will improve efficiency and enhance safety for our school community moving forward.

author: Theodore Jones Elementary
text:
Dear Parent or Guardian,

It has truly been a pleasure working with your children this year. Can you believe
summer is already here?! Medications and medical devices need to be picked up
by an adult no later than 9:00 am on Friday, May 22. I will send any leftover inhalers
and epinephrine auto-injectors home in backpacks (please be sure to send your child
with their backpack!) on the last day of school, but ANY other medications must be
picked up by an adult. Medications not picked up by the deadline will be
destroyed.
**Please remember that it is the policy of the Conway Public School District to require
yearly updates for all medications, medical needs, allergies, and classroom or cafeteria
modifications. I look forward to the 2026-27 school year and hope you all have a safe
and healthy summer break!**

Thank you and please feel free to call me if you have any questions or concerns!

Alicia Wimberly, BSN RN
School Nurse
Theodore Jones Elementary School
(501) 450-6645

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

author: Theodore Jones Elementary
text:
Please take note of our first-day arrival times:

1st–4th Grade: Classroom doors will open at 7:45 a.m. Teachers will be ready to welcome students and families at that time.

Kindergarten: Classroom doors will open at 9:00 a.m. Teachers will be ready to welcome our kindergarten students and families at that time. If you need to arrive earlier, 7:45 a.m. is available to you as well. 

If you plan to walk your child to class on the first day, please wait until your child’s designated classroom opening time.

Important 🚨: After the first day, students are expected to enter the building independently. If your child is a car rider, please remain in your vehicle, drop your child off in the designated car rider line, and continue moving through the line. This helps us keep morning arrival safe, smooth, and efficient for everyone.

Thank you for helping us have a smooth start to the school year!

Mr. Nail’s class made chemical reaction potions for Halloween on Tuesday. They did this by mixing baking soda, vinegar, and food coloring in a cauldron with cockroaches, bats, and spiders. When the baking soda and vinegar combine, they create a carbon dioxide gas, water, and sodium acetate through a chemical reaction. 

A big thanks to Gabriel’s mom, Tara, for helping supply the materials for this fun seasonal experiment! #wcelions

Any future inclement weather days will be evaluated.  More information will be shared after the waiver has been approved or denied.

text: Health Guidelines

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
We are in the middle of sick season and wanted to give a few gentle reminders about some of the CPSD Health Guidelines, as well as, some other recommendations and requests. 

1. Students are prohibited from carrying  or possessing any form of medication with the exception of inhalers or epi-pens. Medications needing to be administered by the nurse, must be brought into the school by a parent/guardian.  

 2. Students with a temperature of 100.0 or above will be excluded from school.  In order to return to school, students must remain fever free for 24 hours without fever reducing medication. 

3. Any students determined to have had vomiting or diarrhea, will be excluded from school and shall remain home until free of those conditions for 24 hours without the aid of medication. 

4. Please send a seasonally appropriate change of clothing with EVERY student, regardless of age, in his or her backpack. 

Please see the attached graphics for more CPS Health Guidelines.

During Open House, you and your child will meet all of the kindergarten teachers, administrators, tour the school, and Kindergarten classrooms.  Your child will have an opportunity to meet other children, so they recognize some familiar faces on the first day of school!

August 19 - First Day of School
Kindergarten students will begin at 9:00 a.m. on the first day.  We welcome parents and guardians to walk your child into the building and bring them to the designated area.  

August 19-23 - Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp
During the first week of school, Kindergarten students will spend time with each Kindergarten teacher in a classroom.  They will participate in a variety of fun activities, learn their school and classroom procedures, routines, and meet new friends and classmates.  We will learn your child’s strengths and areas where they excel by administering the district Kindergarten Readiness Assessments. 

August 23 - Teacher Reveal!
At the conclusion of Wampus Kitty Kinder Camp, your child will bring home a scratch off card revealing their assigned Kindergarten teacher for the school year!

August 26 - Welcome to Class!
Your child will report to their classroom to begin a wonderful year of learning with their assigned teacher.  We welcome you to walk your child to class the first day!

Teachers look forward to meeting your child and learning their unique needs to ensure their growth and development in the upcoming year!  If you have questions, please reach out to the principal.  We are excited about this opportunity and look forward to seeing you soon!

Open House Dates for Campuses are included here - https://www.conwayschools.org/o/cps/page/back-to-school

Please see the pictures below for a few Poptab collection container ideas!

*All poptabs should be submitted in plastic baggies.  Please do not submit poptabs IN the containers you are using for collections.

text:
Parents/Guardians: 
All students walking from the parking lot in the mornings, MUST be accompanied by an adult and walked to the crosswalk. Please do not pull up to the crosswalk, stop, and let your child out. If you use the parking lot to drop off, you must PARK in a parking space, and walk your child to the crosswalk. This is for your child's safety and to avoid holding up parking lot traffic. 
If you participate in walk-up, pick-up in the afternoons, you must park and walk to the flag pole to meet your child. Students will not be allowed to run to parked vehicles. This is also for your child’s safety. 
Thank you for helping us keep your children safe, and our pick-up/drop-off lines running safely and efficiently.

Tomorrow is the final day of our Read-a-thon!

Our students have done an INCREDIBLE job — I am so impressed with their hard work, dedication, and enthusiasm for both reading and raising funds for our library. They’ve truly gone above and beyond!

We’ll be announcing our top prize winners tomorrow at school — I can’t wait to celebrate all of their efforts and reveal our grand totals for both minutes read and donations raised!

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text: Wow! I am absolutely blown away by the incredible support for our very first Read-A-Thon to raise money for the library! Our students worked so hard, and their dedication truly paid off. The number of minutes they read and the generosity of our community completely exceeded my expectations. Woodrow Cummins is beyond blessed to have such an amazing school family and community. Your support means the world to us, and I hope you’ll take a moment to let your readers know just how PROUD you are of them for their hard work and commitment! Here are our Read-A-Thon grand totals: 📚 TOTAL DONATIONS RECEIVED: $13,027 ⏱️ TOTAL MINUTES RECORDED: 36,907 Students will have 10 days from today to spend their RAT Bucks in the prize store! RAT Buck totals can be found on your reader's Read-A-Thon dashboard. All prizes will be shipped directly to the school and will be distributed to students once they arrive. Thank you again for making this event such a huge success. Together, we are building a stronger community of readers — and that’s something to celebrate!

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
📣 Welcome, Mrs. Lindsey Jones! 🎉

We are excited to welcome Mrs. Lindsey Jones as the new principal of Woodrow Cummins Elementary and into our WCE family!

Mrs. Jones brings a wealth of experience and dedication to this new role. She has been a part of the Conway Public Schools family since 2010. Most recently Mrs. Jones served as the assistant principal for Carolyn Lewis Elementary. She also has previous experience as a third and fourth grade teacher at Theodore Jones and Marguerite Vann Elementary, as well as, taking on various leadership roles along the way. Her peers recognized her commitment to excellence by naming her Teacher of the Year in both 2017 and 2021.

Mrs. Jones is passionate about making a difference and is guided by one clear goal: to be exactly who the students in her care need. She is a tireless advocate for children and truly lives out our district motto—Every Child, Every Day, Whatever It Takes.

Please join us in giving Mrs. Jones a warm WCE welcome! 💙

We are thrilled to welcome Ms. Halle Sligh to the 4th grade team at WCE!

📣Welcome Our New Assistant Principal – Mrs. Siri Briggler! 📣

We are so excited to welcome Mrs. Siri Briggler to the WCE family as our new Assistant Principal! Mrs. Briggler is beginning her 18th year in public education, and she brings with her a wealth of experience and passion for supporting students and teachers alike.

She holds an Education Specialist degree (Ed.S) in Reading and is a proud National Board Certified Teacher. Throughout her career, she has served in a variety of roles including Special Education, Kindergarten, Literacy and Dyslexia Intervention, and Instructional Coaching. Her work has focused on supporting curriculum instruction and promoting inclusive practices to ensure success for all students.

Outside of school, Mrs. Briggler enjoys trail running and spending time with her husband and their three children.

Please join us in giving Mrs. Briggler a warm WCE welcome – we’re so lucky to have her on our team! 💙

text:
CPSD Bell to Bell No Cell
At Conway Public Schools Elementaries, we believe school is a place for students to learn, grow, and build good relationships with others. To help keep our classrooms focused and follow state guidelines, students should not use personal electronic devices during the school day. This includes cell phones, AirPods, wireless headphones, and smartwatches. We ask that all devices be turned off and kept in backpacks during school hours.

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
Bell to Bell, No Cell 🚫
As a reminder, CPSD students are expected to follow our “Bell to Bell, No Cell” expectations during the school day.📌 A student is not considered to be in possession of a personal electronic device if:It’s stored in their bag (and not accessed),It’s stored in a locker (and not accessed), orIt’s stored in their vehicle (and not accessed) — except as permitted by law.📲 Follow-up for Infractions:1️⃣ First Violation: Device Confiscation, Warning, Parent Contact, Student Pick-Up2️⃣ Second Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Contact, Detention, Parent Pick-Up3️⃣ Third Violation: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, Saturday School/In-School Suspension, Parent Pick-Up🚨 Additional Violations: Device Confiscation, Parent Meeting, ISS/OSS, Parent Pick-Up🔗 View the full policy here: https://5il.co/3l9nqLet’s all work together to keep classrooms focused and distraction-free! 💙📚 #CPSD #BellToBellNoCell #StudentSuccess

Dear Parents,

If you do not use the school app:

FREE Dental Care for Students in Need 🦷💙
Conway Regional Interfaith Dental Clinic and the Conway Regional Foundation are partnering with United Way’s Smile Savers grant to offer FREE dental care for eligible CPSD students. Services include an initial evaluation and follow-up care (cleanings, fillings, and extractions). Interfaith does not provide sedation; if it’s needed, we’ll work with families to find alternative care.

text:
Thank you all so much for your patience and grace as we continue working out the details of our arrival and dismissal procedures. Your support helps us make this process as safe and efficient as possible for everyone.

🚗 Morning Drop-Off Reminders:
To help us keep the line moving smoothly, please have your child ready to exit the vehicle before it is your turn to unload by making sure they:
1. Unbuckle their seatbelt
2. Put on their backpack
3. Have their lunchbox and water bottle in hand
4. Are ready to open their own door and exit quickly

🚦 Unloading Zone:

The unloading zone begins at the cone at the front of the line and extends back to the open gate near the safe room. Please pull all the way forward to the first cone, and cars behind you will fill in the line. All vehicles within the unloading zone—from the cone to the gate—should stop and unload together. 
👟 Walking Safely:
Once students exit their vehicle, they should walk directly to the sidewalk that leads into the building. For safety, students should not walk along the row of unloading vehicles.

Thank you again for helping us keep arrival and dismissal safe and efficient—we couldn’t do it without you!

text: We’re excited to announce that the Literati Book Fair kicks off next Monday afternoon and will run through Thursday!Students will have the opportunity to shop during their activity period each dayPLUS during Grands Day 🎉Thank you for supporting our library and school through this fun event!💻 Online shopping and gift card purchases are now open at: Literati.com/storeWhat is a Literati student gift card — and how do we use it?A Literati gift card is like a mini “book voucher” for your child. You can buy it online now or at the fair. After purchase, you’ll get a code via email (you can print it or save it on your phone).During the book fair, your child (or the checkout team) can use that code (or your child’s name, if you connected it to the school) to pay for books in person. Or, if you prefer to shop online, you can use the same code on the Literati website.If there’s money left after shopping, the remaining balance stays on the card for future use — either at another fair or in your school’s Literati Store.Linking the gift card to your child’s school helps the staff find it quickly at checkout and ensures your school gets credit.

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
🎉 October is National Principals Month! 🎉

We are beyond proud to celebrate Mrs. Jones, an absolutely amazing principal who leads with heart, purpose, and dedication every single day. 

Mrs. Jones is truly the best of the best. She arrives early, stays late, and gives her all to ensure our school is a place where students and staff feel seen, supported, and safe.

She encourages and uplifts our staff, builds strong, meaningful relationships with students, and creates a positive, nurturing school culture that feels like family. 

Mrs. Jones leads by example with integrity, compassion, and unmatched energy. She celebrates every win, listens with empathy, and faces every challenge with grace and determination.

Whether she’s greeting students with a smile at the door, supporting a teacher, solving a problem behind the scenes, or cheering on a classroom celebration, she does it all with excellence and love.

We are SO lucky to have her guiding our school. Thank you, Mrs. Jones, for being a remarkable leader, mentor, and champion for all of us.

 Join us in celebrating Mrs. Jones this month! Drop a comment or picture below to share how she’s made a difference in your life! 👇💙 #PrincipalsMonth

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
📣 Help Shape the Future of Conway Public Schools! 🐾

Conway Public Schools, in partnership with the Conway Area Chamber of Commerce and Conway Development Corporation, has launched a Strategic Planning Steering Committee to help guide our district through 2026 and beyond.

We’re working with the Winthrop Rockefeller Institute (WRI) to gather input from parents, students, staff, local employers, and community members. Your feedback will help us understand what’s working well, where we can improve, and how we can best prepare Conway students for lifelong success.

Please note, the survey will close on November 30, so be sure to share your thoughts before then. This is an important opportunity for every parent to have a voice in shaping the future of Conway Public Schools. The feedback collected will inform both our Strategic Readiness Plan for 2025–2026 and the long-range strategic plan being developed by the Steering Committee.

💬 We want to hear from YOU—our community!
 Your perspective as a citizen and taxpayer is vital as we make decisions that impact our schools and our city’s future.

📩 A Parent Survey and Staff Survey has also been emailed to all CPSD families and staff, so if you have a child in or work for Conway Public Schools, please take a few minutes to complete it!

🗳️ CPSD Citizen/Taxpayer Survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/bZLfGmgjWZ 

Together, we can ensure that Conway Public Schools continues to grow, innovate, and serve our students—and our community—with excellence.
#ConwayPublicSchools #WampusCats #CPSDStrategicPlan

text: Dear Conway Public Schools Families,We want to make you aware of an important change coming to third grade promotion in Arkansas.Beginning with the 2025–2026 school year, the Arkansas LEARNS Act will require that third-grade students meet the state’s English Language Arts (ELA) standard — or qualify for a good-cause exemption — in order to be promoted to fourth grade.At Conway Public Schools, we believe every child can become a confident, capable reader. We are committed to working closely with families to support each student’s reading progress throughout the year through:Regular reading assessments and updates through the ATLAS Family PortalTargeted reading interventions and tutoring as neededIndividual Reading Plans (IRPs) for students who need additional support📽️ Please take a few minutes to watch this short video featuring Shanda New, Director of Programs & Accountability, as she explains what the new law means for your child, how it affects your family, and how we’re supporting student success in Conway Public Schools.<span style="font-family: Roboto,sans-serif; color: #0d0d0d; font-size: 11.5pt; background-color: #ffffff; font-weight: 400; font-style

26-27 Kindergarten Registration Information:

In order to begin planning for the 2026–2027 school year, we are asking parents of current students who will have a kindergarten student starting in August of 2026 to please forward us the names of those siblings by completing the Google Form.

With the recent changes to the School Learns Act, we want to be proactive in ensuring that all of our siblings have a spot for the 2026–2027 school year.

Please complete by December 19, 2025.  Just a reminder, they must be 5 years old by August 1, 2026.

Thank you!

Use this link. If you are unable to click the link, please copy and paste into any web browser. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdaOi9t1EccyXOC2P91bIrhk0yfXJfr3N2001mXj0CoSpBj_w/viewform?usp=publish-editor

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
Hi everyone,

I hope you’re having a great week! We just need to share a couple of quick reminders to help keep our afternoon dismissal and morning arrival running smoothly.

Please do NOT crowd the intersection when entering the car rider line. Mrs. Berkemeyer must be able to exit her bus safely, and she has had difficulty doing so each afternoon  because cars have been blocking the area. Your help with keeping that space clear is greatly appreciated.

For morning drop-off, the car line must be used until it closes at 7:55 AM:

If you arrive before 7:55, please continue through the car line to drop off your student.

If you arrive at or after 7:55, and the gate/car rider line is still visibly open, please continue to use the car rider line.

Only park and walk your student into the office if the car line is clearly closed.

Thank you so much for your cooperation and for helping us keep everything safe and efficient for our students and staff!

text:
Weather Update: Monitoring Conditions for FridayGood evening Conway Public Schools,We are continuing to closely monitor the incoming weather system and will evaluate updated conditions tomorrow morning as forecasts continue to change.If weather conditions warrant, we may pivot to a two-hour early release on Friday to ensure the safety of our students, staff and families. Should that occur, the following dismissal times would apply:Elementary Schools: 1:15 p.m.Secondary Schools (Middle Schools, CJHS, & CHS): 1:30 p.m.If an early release is implemented, end-of-day dismissal procedures would remain normal, buses would run their regular routes, and all after-school activities and programs would be canceled.We will communicate any decision as soon as it is made. Please continue to monitor your email, phone messages, and district communication channels for updates. If no additional communication is issued, schools will follow their regular dismissal schedules.Our team will continue monitoring the weather throughout the weekend and will provide updates regarding any additional school closings or delays as needed.Thank you for your patience and understanding as we prioritize safety. Please stay safe and warm. Sincerely,
Conway Public Schools

text:
🔥 National Burn Awareness Week | February 1–6 🔥

Scald burns are one of the most common burn injuries in children, but they’re preventable. Keep kids safe by turning pot handles inward, keeping hot drinks out of reach, setting water heaters no higher than 120°F, and never leaving children unattended near hot water.

If a burn happens: cool with cool (not cold) water, remove clothing from the area, cover with a clean dry cloth, and seek medical care.

Let’s work together to prevent burns and protect our kids.

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
Dear Parents and Guardians,We are excited to share that we are beginning a new reading curriculum called Build: Early Reading Intervention (BUILD Literacy) for our K–2 students.Build is a 100-lesson reading program designed to strengthen the foundational skills students need to become confident, successful, lifelong readers. This structured and systematic program focuses on the five major pillars of reading instruction:• Phonological Awareness
• Phonics
• Vocabulary
• Fluency
• Reading ComprehensionOur goal is to strengthen these essential skills as early as possible. Research shows that gaining proficiency in these areas at a young age plays a key role in long-term reading success.You may notice that reading instruction looks a little different than it has in the past. While the format may vary, please know that we are still teaching the same essential skills—just in a new, engaging, and step-by-step way that builds confidence along the way.We are committed to providing strong reading foundations so every child can thrive. We are excited about the growth we expect to see and look forward to partnering with you throughout this process.If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out. We will also be sharing more information soon about ways you can support your child’s reading at home.Thank you for your continued support!Sincerely,
K–2 Teachers

author: Jenna Havlik
text:
We are writing to clarify information shared in a previous email regarding BUILD: Literacy. We apologize for any confusion it may have caused.
BUILD: Literacy is not a replacement for our current reading curriculum. Instead, it is an intervention program designed to provide additional support for students who may need extra assistance in developing foundational reading skills.This intervention takes place during the school day and is provided in addition to students’ regular classroom reading instruction. Our core reading curriculum remains in place for all students. BUILD: Literacy simply offers targeted, small-group instruction to help ensure every child continues to grow and succeed as a reader.
If you have any questions or would like more information about how this intervention may support your child, please feel free to reach out.Thank you for your continued partnership in your child’s education.

text:
Dear Parents,We are excited to share an amazing summer opportunity for your child — Camp Invention 2026! This nationally recognized, hands-on summer enrichment program is designed to spark creativity, boost confidence, and ignite a lifelong love of learning through exciting STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) challenges.🌟 What Is Camp Invention?
Camp Invention is a week-long, fun-filled day camp for children entering First through 6th grade. Led by caring, qualified local educators, campers dive into collaborative, hands-on activities that encourage curiosity, problem solving, ingenuity, and teamwork;  all while having a blast! Watch this video to see what Camp Invention is all about. Camp Invention Video🚀 What Will Your Child Experience?
This year’s 2026 “Spark” curriculum is packed with inspiring challenges that bring big ideas to life:Space Morphers™: Build and launch a DIY rocket, conduct a rover mission, and explore scientific discoveries that stretch imaginations.Make Waves™: Dive into entrepreneurship and physics as campers experiment with buoyancy and design their own billboard boat prototype.Fur-ensics™: Sharpen detective skills by investigating clues with robotic capybaras and exploring forensic science fundamentals.The Infringers™: Kids unlock their innovation superpowers — inventing, protecting ideas, and learning about real-world intellectual property concepts.🌱 What Your Child Will Gain:
Camp Invention is more than summer fun — it cultivates real skills that support academic growth and confidence. Parents consistently report that campers return with:Increased curiosity and confidenceEnhanced creative problem-solving and collaboration skillsA deeper interest in STEM and learningNew friends and unforgettable memories📅 Program Details & Registration
Location: Ida Burns Elementary School 1201 Donaghey Ave, Conway, AR 72034 Date & Time: June 1 - 5, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 3:30 PM Director: Anita Reynolds | reynoldsa@conwayschools.info👉 Register soon to secure your child’s spot! Register by 3/31 and use Promo Code: SUM25 for $25 off.  Visit Camp Invention Registration to start this amazing experience!Let’s make this summer one your child will never forget — full of discovery, invention, and joyful learning!

text:
🍀 Lucky Charms + Math = A little St. Patrick’s Day magic in 2nd grade! 🍀

Today our 2nd graders practiced their graphing skills using Lucky Charms cereal! First, students sorted the marshmallows by shape and color, then created graphs to show how many of each they found. 📊

We talked about which marshmallow had the most, the least, and compared our data with our friends. The best part? After all that hard work… they got to enjoy their math manipulatives! 😄

Hands-on learning makes math extra sweet. Happy St. Patrick’s Day from our lucky little learners! 🌈✨

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
Mrs. Wilcox’s 2nd graders celebrated St. Patrick’s Day with a fun science experiment! 🍀

Before we began, students made predictions about what would happen to an arrow placed behind a glass of water. Would it bend, change directions, or disappear? Then we tested our ideas by placing the arrow behind a glass filled with water and carefully observing what happened.

Students were amazed to see the arrow appear to change directions! It was a great hands-on way to explore how light travels through water while practicing prediction and observation skills. Science + a little St. Patrick’s Day magic made for a fun day of learning! 🌈

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary

Our 3rd grade students will begin their Summative ATLAS Reading and Writing assessments tomorrow and continue on Wednesday. We are so proud of all the hard work they’ve put in, and we want to set them up for success!

Here are a few ways you can help your child do their best:

✅ Get a good night’s sleep – Rest helps with focus and confidence.
✅ Eat a healthy breakfast – Fuel for the brain is important!
✅ Arrive on time – Being punctual helps students start the day calmly.
✅ Encourage a positive mindset – Remind them to take their time and do their best.
✅ Pack any needed items – Glasses, water bottle, or anything they use daily.

Let’s work together to help our students feel confident and prepared. We believe in them! 💙

author: Conway Public Schools
text:
CPSD Staff & Families, 

We want to provide another follow-up regarding the image circulating on social media last night that contained a threatening message.

The Conway Police Department shared:
“At approximately 10:00 p.m., detectives with the Conway Police Department took a 13-year-old female Conway Student into custody in connection with reported threats made on social media.
The juvenile has been charged with Threatening to Commit an Act of Mass Violence on School Property, a Class C felony, and is currently being held at a juvenile detention center.
At this time, no other suspects are believed to be involved.
This incident remains under active investigation.
We appreciate the public’s cooperation and assistance throughout this investigation.”


School will be in session today. The safety and security of our students and staff remain our top priority.

We want to extend our sincere appreciation to the Conway Police Department and our School Resource Officers for their swift response and dedication in handling this situation. Their ability to act quickly and work thoroughly was instrumental in helping ensure the safety of our students and staff.

Dear Future RDMS Families,
We are excited to invite you to our Rising 5th Grade Parent Information Night on Thursday, May 14th from 6:00–7:00 PM in the RDMS Cafeteria.
This event is designed to provide parents and guardians with an overview of our school, along with important information about what to expect as your child begins their 5th-grade year at Ruth Doyle Middle School.
Our goal is to help make your child's transition to middle school as smooth and successful as possible. We understand that this transition can bring a mix of excitement and uncertainty, and we hope this evening will ease any concerns for both students and families.
The presentation will last approximately 30 minutes, followed by a question-and-answer session where you will have the opportunity to connect with staff and get your questions answered.
We hope you will be able to join us! If you are unable to attend, we will offer another parent meeting during our annual 5th Grade Cat Camp on August 6th. This session will include any updates or additional information shared after the spring meeting. You are welcome to attend both sessions.
We look forward to partnering with you as your child begins this exciting new chapter!

If your student has been receiving K-3 Literacy Tutoring this message is for you!
The Arkansas Department of Education is providing updated guidance regarding Arkansas Literacy Tutoring Grant invoicing deadlines and the proposed program closeout timeline.

Key Updates:
Students must have at least one tutoring invoice submitted by June 30, 2026, to remain active for continued tutoring services beyond June 30, 2026
Tutoring services for active students may continue throughout the summer months
The final program closeout date is September 30, 2026
Eligible invoices for active students and newly approved students may continue being submitted through September 30, 2026

Additional clarification:
Tutoring services must occur before invoices are submitted
Providers should continue submitting invoices regularly throughout the closeout period
Families and providers should not wait until September to submit invoices for completed services

Education Service Cooperatives may continue receiving questions regarding these updated timelines and expectations. We appreciate your assistance in helping reinforce accurate and consistent communication across your service areas.

If you have questions regarding Arkansas Literacy Tutoring Grant guidance, deadlines, or program procedures, please contact the Arkansas Department of Education at ade.tutoring@ade.arkansas.gov.

Thank you, 
Arkansas Department of Education Literacy Tutoring Grant Team

🎉 Please join us in welcoming our new Assistant Principal, Mrs. Tracy Lakey! 🎉

We are thrilled to welcome Mrs. Tracy Lakey back to the WCE family as our new Assistant Principal!

Mrs. Lakey is beginning her 25th year in public education and is excited to serve the students, families, and staff of Woodrow Cummins Elementary in this new role. She is passionate about helping every child succeed, supporting teachers, and building meaningful relationships that create a positive and welcoming school community.

Throughout her career, Mrs. Lakey has had the privilege of teaching 1st, 3rd, 4th, and 5th grades, giving her a broad understanding of elementary education. For the past six years, she has served as an Instructional Coach, partnering with teachers to strengthen instruction, support student learning, and foster continuous growth.

Outside of school, Mrs. Lakey enjoys spending time with her husband and two children, traveling, and curling up with a good book.

Mrs. Lakey is honored to return to Woodrow Cummins Elementary and is looking forward to getting to know each student and family while working alongside our incredible staff. She can't wait to help make this school year one filled with learning, growth, and memorable experiences for everyone.

We are excited to welcome Mrs. Brooke Jones to the Woodrow Cummins Elementary family as our new School Counselor!

Mrs. Jones brings 16 years of experience in education, including five years with Conway Public Schools, where she taught 9th grade English and yearbook. In 2024, she earned her Master's in School Counseling and is excited to begin this new chapter supporting and encouraging our Little Cats.

Mrs. Jones shared:

"I'm so excited to be joining the WCE team as the school counselor this year! I'm thrilled to begin this new adventure supporting and encouraging our Little Cats!"

We know she will make a positive impact on our students, staff, and families, and we are thrilled to have her as part of our Little Cat family.

💙 Welcome to WCE, Mrs. Jones! We're so glad you're here! 🐾

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
🍎 Help us welcome Andrew Wright to the Woodrow Cummins Elementary 4th Grade team! 💙

We are thrilled to welcome Andrew Wright to our Little Cat Family this school year!

Mr. Wright brings 10 years of experience in education, including six years serving students in Conway. Throughout his career, he has taught 5th, 6th, and 7th grade math and is excited to begin this new chapter with our 4th graders at WCE.

A proud graduate of UCA, Mr. Wright earned both his undergraduate and master's degrees there before completing his Building Level Administration degree at Arkansas State University. He believes in being a lifelong learner and looks forward to helping every student develop a love of learning.

When he's not in the classroom, you'll likely find him spending time with his family—his wife, Hannah, and their children, Lee and Johnnie Gwenn. During the summer, he enjoys cheering at the baseball field, relaxing at the swimming pool, and embracing his passions for both sports and all things nerdy.

Please join us in giving Mr. Andrew Wright a warm Little Cat welcome! We can't wait to see the positive impact he'll make on our students this year. 💙🐾

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
📣 ARRIVAL & DISMISSAL PROCEDURES | PLEASE READ, LITTLE CAT FAMILIES! 🐾💙

We know the first few weeks of school come with a learning curve for everyone! Our goal is to keep arrival and dismissal safe, smooth, and as quick as possible. Please review these procedures with your family before the first day.

 🌅MORNING CAR RIDER DROP-OFF

🚗 All car riders will use the north campus entrance and drop off at the south end of the building.

*Only exception to this is for kindergarten parents the first week of school

➡️ Traveling north on Padgett: Turn right into the north campus entrance and proceed to the south end of the building.

⬅️ Traveling south on Padgett: Turn left into the north campus entrance and proceed to the south end of the building.

🚌 Only buses, daycare vehicles, and special education students will be allowed to drop off in the front parking lot.

⏩ To keep the line moving:
• Pull all the way forward.
• Remain in your vehicle.
• Have your student ready to exit quickly  backpack on their back and lunchbox in hand!

 🌟 AFTERNOON DISMISSAL

 Bikers • Walkers • Walk Up, Pick Up (WUPU) | 3:15–3:20 PM

• No tag = No child.
• Line up under your child's grade-level sign.
• Walkers and bikers will exit through the front door with WUPU students.
• Please do not arrive for WUPU after 3:20 p.m. At that point, you will need to use the car line.

🚗CAR RIDER DISMISSAL | Begins at 3:15 PM
 
All car riders will be dismissed using our Driveline system.

• No tag = No child.
• All car riders will be picked up in the car line outside the cafeteria, the same location used for morning drop-off.
• Pull all the way forward and remain in your vehicle.  DO NOT EXIT YOUR VEHICLE. All students should be loaded on the passenger side of the car. 
• If your student needs help buckling up, please pull into a parking spot after exiting the car line to assist them.

See the following video for a Dismissal video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=undLVtC1ytQ

🚌 BUS & DAYCARE RIDERS

Students riding buses or daycare vans will be loaded outside the library as their vehicle arrives.

💙 A LITTLE PATIENCE GOES A LONG WAY! 💙

The first few weeks are a learning process as our students, families, and staff learn and practice these procedures. We appreciate your patience, cooperation, and grace as we work together to make arrival and dismissal safe and efficient for all of our Little Cats!

🐾 Thank you for helping us start and end each day safely!

author: Conway Public Schools
text: Welcome Back!As students and staff return to school for another year, let’s all do our part in keeping safety at the forefront of our minds at school, at home, and on the road.·       Watch for school buses.  Slow down and never pass a stopped school bus with its lights flashing.·       Drive safely in school zones.  Slow down, pay attention, and watch carefully for students, parents, crossing guards, and school staff.·       Stay alert.  It only takes a few seconds of distraction to change a life forever.·       School safety starts when we leave our homes. It doesn’t just depend on what happens inside our school buildings.Let’s work together to ensure every student and staff member arrives at school and returns home Safe and Sound.The volume of traffic will increase this week. Please be patient as we work together getting back in the routine of drop off and pick up.Welcome back, Wampus Cats!

text:
🐾 FIRST WEEK OF SCHOOL REMINDERS! 🐾

We are SO excited to welcome our Little Cats back to Woodrow Cummins Elementary! 💙🤍 As we kick off the first week, please keep these important reminders in mind:

🍎 Lunch Visitors: Students may not have lunch visitors dine with them until  after Labor Day. Thank you for helping us make a smooth transition into the school year!

🎒 Kindergarten Drop-Off: Kindergarten parents should  walk their children into the building each morning this week at 7:45 AM through the front doors.

🚗 All Other Students: All other students must be dropped off through the  car rider line. Please remember that we have ONE lane for drop-off:
➡️ Enter from the north side of the building
➡️ Travel around the building
➡️ Continue to the drop-off zone near the cafeteria on the south side

⏰ Please Be Patient! The first week of school can bring a little extra traffic and congestion as everyone gets back into their routines. We appreciate your patience, kindness, and cooperation as we work to get all of our Little Cats safely to school each morning. 💙

Thank you for helping us make the first week a great one! We are so happy to have our Little Cats back! 🐾📚

author: Woodrow Cummins Elementary
text:
Dear Woodrow Cummins Families,

As we work through our first week of school, we want to share a few important dismissal updates to help make the process as smooth and safe as possible.

🐾 Walk-Up Pick-Up Numbers:
For this week only, walk-up pick-up numbers will begin being entered at 3:00 PM. This will provide some additional time for our staff and students to work through dismissal procedures. This will be for THIS WEEK ONLY.  Next week students will not be dismissed until 3:15. 

🚶 Walk-Up Pick-Up Reminder:
Anyone picking up a student through walk-up pick-up must pull into and park in a designated parking spot before walking up to the front of the building.

For the safety of everyone, please:

Do not stop in the middle of the parking aisle.
Do not park in the bus loop.
Please use a designated parking space before walking to the front of the building.

We greatly appreciate your patience and understanding as we work out all of the beginning-of-year kinks and help our students learn and practice their dismissal procedures. The first week can be a learning curve for everyone, and your cooperation makes a big difference!

Thank you for helping us keep dismissal safe, organized, and efficient for all of our Little Cats! 💙🤍🐾

Sincerely,
Woodrow Cummins Elementary
